# The PDF reader's interface: design

2026-09-25, moved here from the experiment on 2026-10-08 as it stood at its freeze (the tag `exp-freeze-2026-10-07`).
Agreed with the maintainer over nine rounds of a variants harness (local, never committed, deleted once the interface was
built) between 2026-09-24 and 09-25; the maintainer's words are quoted where a decision rests on them. This document is
what the implementation was argued from. Where it and the harness disagreed, this document won.

How the reader meets the rest of the extension is DESIGN §16; the identities its rules are versioned by are §18; the gates
and measurements of its engine are `lab/pdf/README.md`. The experiment's running record and its plans are no longer in the tree
(`git show exp-freeze-2026-10-07:experiments/pdf-bilingual/REPORT.md`). §3 (the displays) and §8 (the states) describe the
reader as it was built, with a final compile; they are rewritten for the instant layer in a later change of the reader's
rebuild. The original's §16, the stage's open items, is not kept: its first item is the next stage's work, and its second
(a service changed while a paper is translating) was decided and never built.

## 1. Goal, scope, principles

The bilingual PDF reader gets its real interface, built where it will stay: an extension page under
`src/entrypoints/pdf-reader/`, React and TypeScript. The engine (the `poc-reader` modules that fetch, translate,
compile, anchor and synchronise) moves behind a typed controller **unchanged**, except for the three measured changes
and the small ones in §10. The next stage, before the reader leaves the experiment, ports the engine to TypeScript
and pays #299's debt.

Not in this stage: the engine's TypeScript port and #299; jumping back after a jump (#300); a draggable splitter (the
maintainer: 「可拖动的分栏不做」); typesetting by writing system (#295); anything paid (「暂时不用收费」).

The maintainer's standards, which every section below answers to:

- **Experience first**: 「优雅、简洁但富含细节、且克制」. Each control, state and motion answers "what does the reader
  gain"; nothing is there for looks.
- **Performance first**: 「性能极佳……避免中看不中用」. Every visual detail that runs while reading (blur, shadow,
  filter, animation) is measured on the heaviest paper before it ships (§12).
- **No technical path is ever shown to a reader**: 「过去和将来都不应该出现这种纯技术性的、非用户可感知的纯开发者提示」.
  LaTeX, compiling, typesetting services, engines, providers never appear in the interface; when a technical reason makes
  a function unavailable, its control is greyed out, without an explanation. (A paper that cannot be had says that much,
  and never why: §8, the maintainer, 2026-09-26.)
- **Its own visual language**: the reader does not inherit the extension's design system (「不用继承我们之前的系统」);
  the extension's interaction rules (one kind of control, one popover; settings apply at once) and copy rules still do.

## 2. Where the reader is reached

What changes on the extension's side is §9; here, the ways in.

- **An arXiv PDF** (`arxiv.org/pdf/<id>`) opens straight into the reader when `pdfReader.enabled` is on (the default).
  `pdf.content.ts` lays the reader's page over the browser's viewer in a full-window frame, as it does today, so the
  address stays arXiv's. Off, the browser's viewer shows the PDF with the floating button.
  - A PDF address carrying `#readarxiv` opens the reader whatever the setting says: it is an explicit request, and the
    abstract page's entry and the floating button use it (the HTML version's link carries the same hash today).
  - A PDF address carrying `#axt-viewer` opens no reader whatever the setting says: the browser's own viewer asked for,
    with the floating button (the reader's original download opens arXiv's PDF so: `core/pdf/entry.ts` `VIEWER_HASH`).
- **The abstract page's popup**: the entry view's one button becomes two, side by side, **HTML 翻译** and **PDF 翻译**
  (the maintainer, 2026-09-25: as few words as stay clear), where `reading.openIn` says (a new tab by default). The
  reader chooses; we do not choose for them (the maintainer: 「在PDF入口和HTML入口中自选——我们不替用户做决定」). PDF 翻译 opens the paper's PDF address with
  `#readarxiv`, which asks for a translation: the reader opens translating, in 对照 or 译文 as last chosen (§3), and
  leaves 原文 if it was last left there.
  - HTML 翻译 is disabled with the existing note when the paper has no HTML version (a thing a reader can see on
    arXiv).
  - PDF 翻译 is disabled **without words** when the paper cannot be had as a bilingual PDF (§1's rule).
  - How that is known (checked 2026-09-25 on 1706.03762, which has a source, and 2608.07562, one of the corpus's 11
    PDF-only submissions):
    - on the abstract page, arXiv's own source link in the Access Paper list, `a.download-eprint` (TeX Source, to
      `/src/<id>`), read as the HTML link is now, with no request; a PDF-only submission has no such link. The selector
      goes into `src/core/rules/abstract.ts`;
    - on a PDF page with the reader closed, a HEAD on `arxiv.org/src/<id>`, as the HTML version is checked there now: a
      source answers `application/gzip` (a `.tar.gz` or a gzipped file), a PDF-only submission `application/pdf`.
- **The floating button**: on the abstract page, and on a PDF page with the reader closed, the logo opens the panel —
  the popup in its frame, with the two entries — and the column's separate control-panel segment goes on those pages,
  since the logo now does what it did (the maintainer's ruling, 2026-09-24). The settings segment stays. On the HTML page
  nothing changes. **Inside the reader there is no floating button** (the maintainer: 「不出现」), as today.
- **A browser the reader cannot run on**: PDF.js's modern build calls built-ins newer than the extension's floor
  without a guard (Chrome 131 has none of them: measured 2026-09-25, Part 1's final review). There the reader is not
  offered: arXiv's PDF stays in the browser's viewer with the floating button, and the popup's PDF entry is disabled without words,
  as for a paper that cannot be had. `src/pdf-reader/support.ts` (`readerRuns`) decides; the modern build is kept for
  every browser that has them.
- **Leaving**: 在默认查看器中打开 closes the frame (the `axt-pdf-reader-close` message, its origin checked, as today); the
  browser's viewer is underneath, and the floating button comes with it.

## 3. Displays and what they share

Three displays: **原文** (the original alone), **对照** (the two side by side), **译文** (the translation alone). The words
appear in tooltips, menus and to screen readers; the toolbar shows icons (§6.2).

- **The display is the extension's**, shared with the HTML page (the maintainer approved, 2026-09-24): 对照 is the HTML
  page's side-by-side mode and 译文 its translation-only mode; the HTML page's stacked mode opens the reader in 对照.
  原文 is "translation off", as the popup's 显示原文 is. Whatever was last chosen, on either page, is what opens next.
- **Swap sides** (对照 only): the translation on the left, the original on the right. Remembered.
- **Sync scrolling** (对照 only): the two sides keep their tops aligned — one mode, no choices (the maintainer checked
  the patent question: no conflict). On by default; remembered; the same value as the settings page's switch.
- **Single display**: the scroller spans the window, so the margins scroll too and the scroll indicator sits on the
  window's edge; the page is centred, and *fit width* fits it to the pane but never beyond a reading width of 1060 CSS px
  (the width the old 1100 px column gave).

## 4. Visual language: "paper"

The direction the maintainer chose (「选"纸"」) after rejecting a first round as 「不够PDF工具场景化」, with PDFSlick's
restraint as the floor (「只是一个及格线」) and alphaXiv's natural transitions as the model for motion.

### 4.1 Tokens

One cool neutral ramp at hue 255 and one status hue, all oklch; light and dark values. The dark ramp is used when the
appearance is dark, or is the system's and the system is dark.

**Shared since 2026-09-27** (the extension's redesign, its design §2.1): these tokens are the extension's now, held as
data in `packages/ui/src/tokens.ts`, from which `pnpm tokens` writes `packages/ui/src/tokens.css`; the reader's sheet imports it,
with the controls it shares (`packages/ui/src/controls.css`, `packages/ui/src/controls/`). The values below are unchanged, and the
reader was held to its pixels before and after the move (`lab/pdf/spikes/reader-pixels.mjs`). The
extension adds roles the reader has no use for — the brand, success, the search mark, the page's and the popup's
grounds — in the redesign's §2.1.

| Token | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|
| `--n-0` | `oklch(1 0 0)` | `oklch(0.255 0.006 255)` |
| `--n-1` | `oklch(0.985 0.002 255)` | `oklch(0.215 0.006 255)` |
| `--n-2` | `oklch(0.962 0.004 255)` | `oklch(0.185 0.006 255)` |
| `--n-3` | `oklch(0.935 0.006 255)` | `oklch(0.275 0.007 255)` |
| `--n-4` | `oklch(0.905 0.007 255)` | `oklch(0.31 0.008 255)` |
| `--n-5` | `oklch(0.86 0.008 255)` | `oklch(0.36 0.009 255)` |
| `--n-7` | `oklch(0.62 0.012 255)` | `oklch(0.56 0.01 255)` |
| `--n-8` | `oklch(0.505 0.014 255)` | `oklch(0.71 0.01 255)` |
| `--n-10` | `oklch(0.235 0.012 255)` | `oklch(0.935 0.005 255)` |
| `--danger` | `oklch(0.545 0.17 28)` | `oklch(0.69 0.15 28)` |
| `--focus` | `--n-10`, the ink (a blue until 2026-09-26) | `--n-10` |

Roles: `--canvas` n-3 (behind the pages), `--chrome` n-0 (toolbar, sidebar, popovers), `--chrome-line` n-4 (0.5 px
hairlines), `--line-strong` n-7 (an edge that marks a choice, a chosen swatch's: a step lighter than the focus's ink,
3.64:1 and 3.39:1 on the chrome; 2026-09-26), `--ink` n-10, `--ink-2` n-8, `--ink-3` n-7, `--fill` n-3 (hover and
pressed), `--well` n-3 (the display switch's track), `--lift` n-0 (its thumb). Floating surfaces: `--float-bg` n-0 at 90 %, with a hairline and a soft
shadow. Pages carry a hairline and a 1–2 px shadow; 14 px between pages.

Contrast, measured (WCAG 2.2, OKLCH → sRGB): ink on chrome 16.7:1 (dark 13.0:1); ink-2 on chrome 5.9:1 (6.1:1), on the
well 4.9:1 (5.8:1); ink-3 on chrome 3.6:1 (3.4:1). So **ink-3 is for icons and hairline-weight marks only** (3:1 for
non-text), never for text: the harness's page numbers in the contents set in ink-3 fail and use ink-2 here; the switch's
off-state track, n-5 in the harness (1.5:1 against chrome), uses ink-3 here.

### 4.2 Type, icons, motion

- Type: the system stack, the platform's Latin face and then the CJK face of the element's language (`FONT_STACKS` in
  `packages/ui/src/tokens.ts`: PingFang SC / TC / HK, Hiragino Sans, Apple SD Gothic Neo on macOS, and their Windows and Linux
  counterparts; UI.md §1, fonts; 2026-11-04, the one Simplified stack before), 13 px base; 12.5 px for controls, 12 px for secondary text, 11 px only for page numbers; 500 for control
  labels, 600 for the title and the current section; tabular figures wherever numbers change.
- Icons: Lucide, 16 px, stroke 1.5 on the 24 grid (1 CSS px), `currentColor`; the display switch's own three (§6.2).
- Motion: one easing, `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`; 120–260 ms; enter heavier than exit; press scales to 0.96. Under
  `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` every movement becomes a fade or nothing.

### 4.3 Appearance and dark pages

- **Appearance**: 浅色 / 深色 / 跟随系统, default 跟随系统 (「深色模式跟随系统」). A change is one crossfade of the whole
  page (the View Transitions API, 260 ms), not element by element (the maintainer: 「要学alpharxiv的方式，过渡自然」).
- **深色时调暗页面**, a switch in the reading options, **default on** (「默认是开启这个功能的」): in the dark appearance the
  pages' canvases take `filter: invert(88.8%) hue-rotate(180deg)` and an undrawn page's background is `rgb(29 29 29)`,
  so nothing flashes white while scrolling. Only the page's own drawing is filtered: the canvas, and over a laid page the
  overlay's text and its crops by the same filter (the reader's sheet), so that every run comes out as the canvas's ink does,
  whatever fill it names — the layer's black, a CJK run's `#141414` (§11.8), a colour of a run's own — which no rule on a
  text's fill would reach. The crops' blend is mirrored with the filter, as the highlight's is: darkened into a white page,
  lightened into a dimmed one (styles.ts). The filter makes a crop's paper the dimmed page's own ground (29, the canvas's white
  through the same filter) and its ink light, so darken kept the ground over the ink: on the website's v2 page on staging
  (2026-11-12) every inline formula of a translated paragraph was a blank gap, the display equations, the canvas's own, still
  there. Lightened, a crop's ink comes out as the canvas's own does (`#c00000`: rgb(255 163 163) both) and its paper lies on
  its equal, no box; only a channel the filter takes under the ground's 29 is lifted to it (`#00ffff`: rgb(0 113 113) on the
  canvas, rgb(29 113 113) in a crop, luma 89 and 95). The highlight's bands keep their colours, screened over the dark page
  as they are multiplied over a white one. Off, the pages stay white in the dark chrome.
- **Where the marks are read** (the website's v2 page on staging, 2026-11-12: the translation drawn black on the dimmed
  page): the appearance is the page's, written by the chrome on `<html>` (`data-theme`, `data-axt-dim`:
  chrome/appearance.ts); the reader's root, the element that carries `.axt-reader`, is the element a host gives `openReader`
  (both hosts: `<body>`; the package's harness: an element of its own). The reader's sheet reads `data-axt-dim` on its root
  or on any element above it (styles.ts `DIMMED`), as the tokens read `data-theme`, so that the look cannot depend on
  which element a host chose and no host copies the mark; the reader's own marks are written on its root by the reader and
  read there (`data-axt-pdf-mode`, `data-axt-narrow`, `data-axt-swapped`, `data-axt-layer-text`), and those it writes inside
  it under it (`data-axt-scaling`, `data-axt-turn`). Before, the sheet read the mark on the root alone, and on both hosts
  the overlay's text, the link rings, the skeleton's colours and the translating marks' light stayed light-page values; the
  canvas's and the crops' filter and the highlight's blend were right by the chrome's own sheet (the crops' blend was never
  right: above). Held by the package e2e's `dim:` checks, in four shapes: the class and the mark on one element (an element of the
  host's; `<html>`), the class on `<body>` under a marked `<html>`, and both hosts' page (the chrome over the reader); each
  reads a crop's pixels too, dimmed and not (its lightest pixel 185 on a ground of 29 dimmed, 29 before the mirror; its
  paper's pixels the page's ground, 29 and 255).
- The night-reading switch of the earlier rounds is gone; the two items above replace it (the maintainer's point 3,
  2026-09-24).

## 5. Layout

- **Toolbar**, 44 px, fixed, a three-zone grid (`minmax(0, 1fr) auto minmax(0, 1fr)`): lead, centre, trail (§6.1). A
  0.5 px hairline below it.
- **Document area** below it; in 对照 two panes with an 8 px gutter of canvas between them (so that zoomed pages never run
  into each other, the maintainer's point 7).
- **Contents sidebar**, 236 px, slides in from the left over 200 ms and moves the document area with it.
- **Floating over the document**: one page pill per pane at its bottom centre (16 px up); the status capsule at the
  document area's bottom centre, 58 px up, above the pills; the scroll indicator on each pane's right edge.
- **Narrow windows**: the title yields first (it truncates, and leaves when the lead has too little room for it —
  the lead's own width, which the trail's menus narrow; the title stays in the id's tooltip), then the id, when the
  lead cannot hold it; the service's and the language's names are cut short at 11 em, whole in their tooltips; below
  900 px the language and service menus move into the reading options, as their first two rows; below 500 px the
  download, the settings and the way back move there too, before them, and the zoom keeps its value's menu (− and +
  give way; ⌘± and the pinch stay), so that the bar holds at 320 px (the interface review; the maintainer,
  2026-09-26). When the
  document area is narrower than 840 px, two pages side by side are too small to read: 对照 stays chosen, the translation
  is shown alone, and the capsule says so once, 窗口较窄，暂只显示译文 — the HTML page's rule and wording (S-P-74, 窗口较窄，
  暂按上下显示). The words stay 5 s of being read: the time stands while the pointer is over the capsule or it holds the
  focus, and the rest of it runs once neither does (the maintainer, 2026-10-01); holding no action, the capsule is a
  stop of its own for the keyboard while it is shown (Codex and Devin on #307). That is the extension's rule; the rule is
  the host's (`Parts.narrow` of the reader package's chrome), so that each host keeps the behaviour its readers have today
  (the coordinator's ruling for the website's cut-over: nothing a reader sees changes): `told`, the default and the
  extension's, as above; `shown`, the website's (its owner's rule of 2026-11-03), where the display switch shows the
  translation chosen and side by side greyed, the stored choice kept for a wider window, and the capsule says so only
  where a window that showed the paper side by side was narrowed while reading (a page opened narrow, or widened again,
  says nothing); while the paper is made there (prepared, translated after its prepare this visit, or refused for now
  with nothing laid), `shown` holds the original on screen, the switch at the original, until the reader chooses a
  display (the website's `displayFor`), a hold never written. The widths are to be checked by reading at them while
  building.

## 6. Components

### 6.1 The toolbar

**Lead**

- 目录 (Lucide `panel-left`, pressed while open).
- The title: 600 13 px, one line, truncating first; the whole title in the tooltip. It is the page's heading (`h1`) at every width: below the lead's 320 px it is hidden to the eye, not removed, so that it stays in the accessibility tree; until it is known the heading is the product's name, said and not drawn (UI.md S-R-03). The title carries the paper's language, `lang="en"`, as a contents heading not yet translated does (S-R-02a): a screen reader reads it in that voice, not the interface's (WCAG 3.1.2; the interface review of 2026-11-03).
- The arXiv id: `arXiv:2608.02163` in ink-2 12 px tabular figures, a link to the abstract page in a new tab (the
  maintainer: 「改成可以点，点击打开abs页」); on hover or focus it takes the fill and a small `arrow-up-right` slides in
  beside it. Tooltip 在 arXiv 打开摘要页, which the link's name carries too, after what is on it (UI.md S-R-03).

**Centre**: the display switch (§6.2).

**Trail**, in this order, a hairline divider between the groups:

1. 左右互换 (`arrow-left-right`, pressed when swapped) and 同步滚动 (`link-2`, pressed when on). Both act in 对照 only;
   in the single displays they stay in place, greyed, so the bar never reflows.
2. Zoom: − · the value with a chevron · +. The value keeps the width of its widest, 000 %, in tabular figures, its
   figures at the trailing edge, so that nothing on the bar moves as it changes (at 99 % → 100 % the button grew 3 px and
   shifted everything beside it: better-typography, 2026-09-26). The value opens a menu: 适合宽度, 适合页面, 实际大小, then 50 %–200 %; the
   current one checked. Shortcuts ⌘− and ⌘+ (Ctrl on other systems).
3. The target language (its name and a chevron, **no icon**: the translation mark belongs to the display switch alone,
   and the name says what the menu is) and the service (its name and a chevron). Their menus are §6.7's.
4. 阅读选项 (`sliders-horizontal`), a popover: 对照高亮 (switch), 高亮颜色 (a swatch for each highlight profile: the
   three built-in, 浅绿, 浅黄, 浅蓝, and any added in the settings), a separator, what to translate (UI.md S-R-27, §9.1:
   a heading row in the second ink naming the five switches under it, the website's group in its words and order, the
   owner's of 2026-10-25; until v21 the HTML page's image switch, S-P-85, the maintainer's ruling of 2026-09-25), a
   separator, 外观 (a small segmented control of three icons, equal whatever
   the language — 跟随系统 a monitor, 浅色 a sun, 深色 a moon, in that order — their words in tooltips and to screen
   readers; the maintainer, 2026-09-26: words ran off the thumb in English),
   深色时调暗页面 (switch). All are settings (§9.1), the same values the popup and the settings page change; a change
   applies at once.
5. 下载 (`download`), a menu of two items, text only: 译文 PDF, 原文 PDF (the maintainer: 「只要译文 PDF / 原文 PDF」).
   The translation's file is named `<id>.<target>.pdf`. Free. 译文 PDF is the final translation: while the translation is
   still coming in (previews), the item is greyed. The original's item opens arXiv's own PDF in a tab of its own, with no
   opener and no referrer, at `#axt-viewer` (§2: no reader laid over it): the browser streams it and its viewer saves it
   (`<id>.pdf` as arXiv names it). The reader never reads the whole
   original to save it: that is 46 MB through the page for every reader, in case one asks (ruled 2026-10-17, for the web
   too); a true download from the reader would need the `downloads` permission, a store-listing item not taken.
6. 设置 (`settings`): opens the settings page at its PDF reader section.
7. 在默认查看器中打开 (`log-out`): leaves the reader for the browser's own viewer (the maintainer's wording, 2026-09-25).

Buttons are 30 × 30 with a 7 px radius and a hit area grown to the bar's height; hover, open and pressed take the fill,
and a hover's look only where a pointer hovers (`@media (hover: hover)`: on a touch screen it latched after a tap).
The interface review proposed a 1 px ring for pressed, since the fill is the hover's too and stands 1.2:1 against the
bar; the maintainer kept the design without it (「这个不要 我们保留之前的设计」, 2026-09-26). Every button has a tooltip:
after 500 ms of hover, at once on keyboard focus; one line always (a tooltip wrapped when it was measured at its last
place near the window's edge); the shortcut, or the value the button shows, in a lighter `kbd` after the words. The
zoom's value, the language and the service are labelled by what is on them — the value first, then their words, hidden
(83% 缩放比例, 简体中文 译为: WCAG 2.5.3, by `aria-labelledby`). 设置 is a link, opened in a new tab. The bar is the page's banner: each control a Tab stop of its own (an
ARIA toolbar would have promised arrow keys between them). In forced colours the chosen display, a pressed button and
a switch that is on take the system's Highlight (the interface review, 2026-09-26).

### 6.2 The display switch

A well (the `--well` track, 30 px high, 9 px radius, 2 px padding) of three equal segments, **40 px each whatever the
interface's language** (the maintainer's reason for icons: 「不同语言界面下文字长度不一样，字宽导致按钮变来变去会很难看」).
The chosen one sits on a lifted thumb that slides between segments in 220 ms; chosen icons take ink, the others ink-2,
a disabled one ink-3 at 55 %.

The icons, each on a 24 × 18 canvas, 1 unit = 1 CSS px, stroke 1 with round caps and joins — as the toolbar's Lucide
icons render beside them — the frame's edges on the pixel grid (the maintainer's round 11, 2026-09-25; stroke 1.2 and
`x 2.25 w 19.5` before):

- **原文**: a pane (`rect x 2.5 y 2.5 w 19 h 13 rx 3`) with an **A** in its middle.
- **对照**: the same pane split by a vertical rule at x 12, drawn `crispEdges` so that a 1x screen keeps it one pixel.
- **译文**: the same pane with **文** in its middle.

The letters are Noto Sans SC (SIL OFL 1.1) at weight 350, the face's DemiLight — its Latin and CJK designed together —
turned into outlines so that every system draws the same shapes (system faces were tried first: headless Chromium gave
PingFang's heaviest weight at that size, and Windows and Linux would draw other faces). Each is centred on the pane by
its ink, not its em box: A 8 px high, 文 8.8 px (a CJK glyph looks smaller than a Latin capital of its height). 文 is
narrowed across to 0.76 of its width (to 6.74 px, beside A's 6.47; the maintainer asked for it to come near A's width),
and the weight that takes from its verticals and diagonals is given back by a 0.18 px stroke round its outline (round
11: 9 px, 0.8 and 0.16 before; its measurements are with the round's files). The
outlines are produced by a script from the font (kept with the reader's code) and committed as path data; the font's
licence goes into `docs/THIRD_PARTY.md`. These are the final glyphs: the hand refinement once left for later was dropped
by the maintainer (2026-09-26).

Rejected on the way, so that nobody tries them again: words (their width changes with the language); letter pairs and
panes marked by drawn letters (「文字的都设计太差了」); left half / right half for the single displays (which side is
which is a convention, 「解释有点牵强」); a translation badge on the pane's corner, outline or solid (right idea, 「不够简洁」,
then replaced by the maintainer's letters in the middle).

It is a single choice, so it is a radio group to assistive technology: `role="radiogroup"` named 显示, three
`role="radio"` with `aria-checked` and the words as their names, arrow keys moving the choice. No single key chooses a
display anywhere on the page: 1, 2 and 3 did, which a stray keystroke or a spoken word could set off (WCAG 2.1.4; the
maintainer removed them, 2026-09-26). A display that cannot be had (§8) is `aria-disabled` and skipped by the arrows.
A host can grey a display its window cannot show the same way: `DisplaySwitch`'s `off` (`readonly Display[]`, none by
default), which the website gives side by side on a phone, where its translation alone is shown (the interface review
of 2026-11-03, v-phone-mode b). Greyed by either, a segment stays a focusable radio, named, its press doing nothing;
the extension's reader passes none (its narrow window keeps §5's rule).

### 6.3 The contents sidebar

- A header 目录 (11.5 px, 600, ink-2), then the paper's own headings as a **folding tree** of up to three levels, one
  28 px row each: level 1 at 12.5 px 500 in ink, levels 2 and 3 at 12 px 400 in ink-2, indented 14 px per level. A fold
  chevron (12 px, rotating 90° in 150 ms) before every entry that has children; a leaf keeps the chevron's slot, so every
  title starts on one edge. Compact, after PDFSlick's folding outline and alphaXiv's hierarchy (the maintainer:
  「空间占用有点太大……两者都更紧凑简洁」).
- Each row: the **translated title**, one line, truncating, in the language it is in (`lang`); the original title in its tooltip; the page number at the end
  (11 px, tabular, ink-2 — §4.1). A fold's tooltip says 展开 or 收起, to its right; the fold is named by the section (UI.md S-R-02a).
  Both titles are text, never TeX: each element of the heading (a paper's macro, a formula, a reference, a citation) is its
  copy text as its part states it (`El.text`, the glyphs TeX set, else `El.copy`, the source's plain text: a formula as linear
  text, "τ_V"), a forced break a space, and an element no part has stated, or one that states neither, nothing, as today's
  reader drops every element (`packages/reader` session/contents.ts `copyTextOf`). The rebuilt reader showed the element's
  source there, "\sys" and the translated words for "Overview of BLIP" (2608.25210v2; 177 contents entries of 38 papers at
  B15).
- The section being read is marked (the fill, 600) and its branch expanded; the mark follows the reading as it scrolls.
  A row jumps both sides to the heading.
- The headings and their levels come from the paper's source as the engine reads it: the source parser
  (`latex-front`) knows which sectioning command each heading unit comes from (`section`, `subsection`,
  `subsubsection`, …) and keeps it on the unit as its level (§10.4); a copy stored before that has no levels and its
  outline is flat. A heading's page is the translation's.
- **Each heading is one entry.** The headings are those of the layer's units as its head names them (`head.units`, each
  object read by its digest from the catalog's directory, as the parts are: `packages/reader` session/machine.ts
  `layerUnitsOf`), the units the head's outline and its parts' members are of. Our server's document names more in
  `layer.units`: every Units object the prepare told, the source's units (handed out before the marked compile, so that a
  translation can start) ahead of the bundle's, the same units under the same ids in another object. The document's list
  stays our server's word for what its run was given (`needsOf`); nothing the reader shows is read from it. The rebuilt
  reader read it as the layer's and listed every heading twice, from its first deploy (2026-11-07) to round RB1: on staging,
  2026-11-13, 2608.25210v2's 25 headings were 50 entries, the view counted 600 units where the head's count 336 (§6.6), and
  the source's object was fetched with the head's. The view's count, the units the paper keeps, the rows made here and their context
  (the paper's abstract) read the same units, each once.

### 6.4 The page pills

One per pane at its bottom centre (EmbedPDF's idea, the maintainer: 「把页码直接放在PDF显示区中间会更好」), a 30 px
capsule on the floating surface: ‹ · the page number (an input, 3.2 ch, select-all on focus) · / total · ›.

- Shown while its pane scrolls and for 2.5 s after, and while hovered or focused; otherwise transparent and not in the
  way of the pointer. Updated from PDF.js's `pagechanging`, never read ahead of it (the harness's first pill lagged a
  page behind for that reason).
- Typing a number and Enter goes there; the arrows step a page.
- Named 原文页码 and 译文页码; the buttons 上一页 and 下一页, whose tooltips stand above them (the pill is at the pane's foot).

### 6.5 The scroll indicators

The panes' native scrollbars are off. Each pane shows its own indicator on its **right edge** — both panes, where every
scroll area keeps it (the maintainer turned down mirroring the left one to the outer edge: 「当handle靠右显示时……会破坏
用户原有的习惯」 — the handle belongs on the right).

- A 14 px track, a 4 px round thumb in ink at 30 %; its length is the pane's visible share (at least 32 px).
- Hidden at rest; shown while the pane scrolls and for 0.9 s after, and while the pointer is on it; the thumb widens to
  7 px and darkens to 45 % under the pointer.
- **Hidden through a zoom**, until the reader next scrolls (the owner's decision of 2026-11-01: 「缩放时让它直接消失行不行？因为在缩放的行为路径中，用户本来就不能上下滑动，这时候手柄消失、等滑动时再出现也是可以的…我们完全可以用这种更直接的解法」).
  A zoom moves each pane's scroll to keep its point under the pointer, but that is not the reader scrolling. Both handles go
  at once, with no fade, from the zoom's first Ctrl-wheel over the pages or its first change of scale, whatever asked
  it: a pinch, a key, the menu or a fit. A scroll shows its pane's handle again once the reader's own input has come since
  the zoom's last change of scale: a wheel without Ctrl, a key other than the zoom's, a touch, a press anywhere (a
  link, the contents, the page pill). The zoom's own scrolls come with none (each step's anchoring, a commit's, and the
  panes' level once the zoom settles, a glide's end 150 ms or more on) and leave them hidden; a scroll begun at once after a
  step shows from its first frame. The handle comes back already at its length and place, on the auto-hide timing above; a
  press on it shows it too, so its drag always works, and so does the pointer resting on it.
- The thumb drags (the pane follows; the other side follows through sync as for any scroll); a press on the track turns a
  screen towards it. A press on an indicator makes its pane the leading side, as a press in the pane does.
- The thumb's position is a CSS scroll-driven animation on the pane's scroll timeline (`scroll-timeline` on the
  scroller, `timeline-scope` on the pane): it moves on the compositor, and no script runs while scrolling. Script sets
  only its length, in the frame the pane's size or its pages' height changes: a ResizeObserver over the pane and over the
  pages' stack, whose callback runs after that frame's layout and before its paint. The place is the scroll's share of the
  track the length leaves, so the two must change in one frame: set a frame later (a React effect on the zoom's state, then
  a frame), every step of a pinch drew the thumb at the new share of the old length and moved it again the next frame, up
  and down through the whole gesture (measured 2026-11-01, `tests/e2e/probes/pinch-jitter.mjs`). A pinch shown by transform
  (§6.8) leaves the scroll and its range alone: the thumb, hidden, holds still until the commit, and then takes its new
  place and length in one frame.

### 6.6 The status capsule and the card

One anatomy for every state: an icon, one sentence, at most one action. Its place is the document area's bottom centre,
above the page pills, clear of the header (the maintainer: 「放在文字切换的上方、页数切换条的上方……不让它占用HEADER的地
方」). It is `role="status"`, present and empty from the first paint, so that what it says later is announced.

- A 34 px capsule on the floating surface. It enters by rising 10 px and fading in with a slight scale (240 ms) and
  leaves lighter (160 ms); a new state of the same kind changes its words in place instead of leaving and coming again,
  its words moving with its box as one motion (the web's round 4, approved 2026-10-04; `Capsule.tsx`,
  `capsule-motion.ts`, the one capsule of the extension and the website):
  - **Growing, the box leads**: its width moves at once, 300 ms on `--ease-soft` (`cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1)`); the
    old words stay, and old and new cross-fade once, at the later of 60 % of the way (161 ms) and the new words fitting
    — clear of what follows them, which is pinned to the box's end and travels with it.
  - **Shrinking, the words lead**: they cross-fade at once while the box closes, 250 ms on `--ease-in-out`
    (`cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1)`), whose slow start keeps it behind them.
  - **The cross-fade**, both ways, on `--ease-out` (`cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)`): the old words 150 ms, 1 → 0, 4 px
    up, blurred to 2 px; the new 200 ms from 4 px below, 2 px → 0, starting with the old; the blur masks the overlap.
    While the box resizes, its moving end fades into the capsule's ground over 16 px, never a cut.
  - **A count** (`withCount`) changes in place: tabular figures, each digit over a hidden 0 that holds its width; a
    changed digit cross-fades, 150 ms on `--ease-out`, shown at most once per 300 ms, a burst landing on its latest. A
    digit gained opens a cell from nothing with the box, 300 ms on the soft curve, the whole number cross-fading at
    161 ms — never a lone 0. It is the one width change between two changes of words.
  - **A chip that comes** opens the box as growing words do and fades in once it fits; until its entrance begins it is
    inert — not focusable, not pressed, not in the accessibility tree — and under reduced motion, with no wait, it is
    reachable at once (Codex on #317). One that goes is inert as it starts to leave.
  - **A change mid-way** retargets from where things stand: the width from its current value, a fade from its current
    opacity; words not yet shown are dropped unseen.
  - **One line, 34 px, in every frame**, and no ink past the border; a sentence too long for one line at the window's
    width wraps and balances (`data-wrap`), and then only its words cross-fade. Nothing is fitted to one language's
    widths. Measured frame by frame in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit (`tests/e2e/probes/capsule.mjs`).
  - **Reduced motion**: opacity with the 2 px blur, at once; nothing slides; the width snaps, growing at once and
    shrinking once the old words have gone (150 ms); the spinner stands (the maintainer, 2026-10-04).
  - **A run's capsule enters once its wait has lasted 400 ms** (`WAIT_SHOWN_MS`, `StatusCapsule.tsx`; the coordinator's
    decision 3, 2026-11-11): a wait the reader cannot perceive is not announced. A wait that ends sooner shows nothing
    and says nothing to a screen reader; once in, the capsule stays through every change of its stage and words (a count
    that pauses and moves again, our server heard again) and leaves at once when no run's capsule is wanted. It is the
    family of the page's mark, which PDF.js draws after 400 ms (`--loading-icon-delay`), and of the translating marks'
    0.3 s. A refusal, an error, a notice and a toast are not delayed. The case it was made for: a stored translation's
    first page and a settled paper's reopening, under a second each on staging, said a run's word every time. The grace is
    for a wait that begins with nothing on screen: where a capsule is (another's words, or a run's capsule still leaving, its
    160 ms), the run's capsule takes its place at once, in place, never a gap after a capsule that was showing (the
    coordinator's R4, 2026-11-12).
  - **What a screen reader is told**: the words' cell is `aria-hidden`; the sentence is told whole (or `spoken`, other
    words, where it holds a count said once a stage) in a line of its own, once per change of that text. A language's
    own name (S-R-13) is a part drawn in its own `lang` (`withPart`; Devin on #313).
- **Progress** is a line along the toolbar's foot, not the capsule's: 2 px of quiet ink (`--ink-3` at 80 %, 2.67:1 on the chrome — the maintainer kept it over a graphic's 3:1 after trying both, 2026-10-02), its length
  the share done of one process: the PDF's download its first stretch (all of it when the original alone is shown), the
  paragraphs translated after it, the final's compile its last stretch (the maintainer asked why it ran twice,
  2026-10-02: the download's line and the translation's were two). It grows by a transform, never runs back within a
  process, and fades out at the length it reached; a process begun after it left — a translation asked for once the
  original was read — is a line of its own, from its start. It is all that shows a load or a translation
  under way: no capsule does, and the words (正在加载, 正在翻译, 正在按当前设置重新翻译) are said to screen readers in
  the status region. (The harness's fifth round moved the progress into a fill of the capsule, ink at 8 %, with the
  status words; the maintainer asked for the line back, 2026-09-25 — the status words were what had to leave the
  header, not the line — and then for no capsule while it runs: the line says it.)
- **The prepare on the line** (the coordinator's decision 4, 2026-11-11): where a paper's layer is made in the process,
  the half of the line after the download is the prepare's, and the line moves by the stage our server's record names
  (`prepare.stage`, `events.ts` `PREPARE_PLACES`): each stage at a fixed place on that stretch, where it starts in the time
  a prepare takes, the mean of the two staging timelines of 2026-11-11 (a new paper's, 2610.20266v1, 87.9 s; a paper
  prepared again after a deploy, 2610.21924v1, 95.6 s). No stage names on screen and no time-based creeping; it never
  runs back. The translation after it takes what remains, from the prepare's end to the whole line; a process without a
  prepare keeps the download's base (the translation from 15 %). Until then the reader read a place in a queue and a
  progress the record does not carry, so the line stood at 15 % for a new paper's whole prepare (88 s on staging), and
  the early units' run ending while the layer was made filled it at 36 s.

  | Stage | Its start in the two timelines | Its place on the prepare's stretch | On the line |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | (told, none yet) | 0 % | 0 | 15 % |
  | fetching | 2.4 %, 1.4 % | 0.02 | 15.9 % |
  | compiling | 12.9 %, 11.2 % | 0.12 | 20.1 % |
  | units | 71.5 %, 33.2 % | 0.52 | 37.1 % |
  | laying-out | 79.7 %, 55.9 % | 0.68 | 43.9 % |
  | bundle | 95.1 %, 99.0 % | 0.97 | 56.2 % |
  | the layer shown, its count not known | | the stretch's end | 57.5 % |
  | the translation | | | 57.5 % to 100 % by the share translated |

- The paragraphs that failed are told once the run has ended, not while it runs.
- **A translation under way is what the view shown waits for**, not our server's record of its runs (`session/rows.ts`
  `viewOf`, told as the reader state's `rows.waits`). One of the units of the layer shown that the paper does not keep
  and the toggles show translated has no translation held, while a run that may bring it is under way: our server's
  run of the target running or still to start, our server still working for the view, or the host's translate. Our
  server still works for the view, without the reader's acting, while the document read for the target says so
  (`rows.ts` `runOf`, `aheadOf`; the coordinator's R3 of 2026-11-12, from the record's fields alone, never a time): its
  prepare running (`prepare.state`: a layer lands at its end, and the target's run over its units follows, our server's
  own start of a run on units it has not run, or this session's open), or a need of the visit (`needsOf`) that the session
  asks, its open under way or not yet asked with no wait named for it: the prepare of a stale `layer`, the target `done` on
  other `units` than the layer's (an attempt covers the layer where its units are the layer's own, by digest). That work, and
  the target's own run, are waited for only while the system still works for this reader by itself (§8.1, `goesOn`). Rows that ended meanwhile are told as arriving (`rowsTold`), and the one
  wait goes on: on staging 2026-11-12, 2010.11929v2 (a stale layer, no translation under the chain) counted 356 of 435,
  left the moment attempt 1 was done while the prepare still ran, and came back 6.8 s later at the new layer's attempt 2.
  Its count is one statement over that set: those
  units with a translation held, of those units. Those units are the layer's as its head names them, each once (§6.3), read
  once its head is read: never the document's `layer.units`, which names the source's units too (2608.25210v2 counted 600
  where the head's units count 336, staging 2026-11-13). It never passes its total, and never falls while the layer shown and
  the toggles stay, since rows held are only added to. Its total changes only with the layer shown or the toggles, and
  then it is a new statement; while a new layer's units are not read yet, the count is the layer's before it (the pages on
  screen), never 0 of 0 for a moment. On a first open the count is 0 of 0 until the head's units are read, then their
  total, once. Some cases are told by their end alone, so the line and the capsule say nothing of them:
  rows read of a run done with nothing more to come (a stored translation); a run that restates rows the view holds; a run on
  units of a layer not shown yet that leaves every unit shown held. Before this rule, on staging 2026-11-11,
  2610.21924v1 opened after a deploy said "translating" three times over a paper already on screen. Its count went from
  476 of 393 to 0 of 0 to 320 of 476: the rows the tab held, over each attempt's total. The view's wait is over once
  every unit shown holds its translation, though a run that restates them may go on. The end held for the layer's
  first page (`laying`) translates nothing, so no capsule says it, in any host's words: a stored translation's first
  page is a load, which the progress line and the page's marks show as they show the original's, and the status region
  says the load there (`R.status.loading`), never the translation (the coordinator's decision 2 of 2026-11-11 and R2 of
  2026-11-12; until then the website's capsule said the paper was being prepared there, 0.7 s on every reopen of a settled
  paper, and then its screen-reader line said `R.status.translating` for 0.6 s, which the staging recorder of 2026-11-12 read
  as a capsule). The layer's units not read yet, the target's run under way or to start waits while nothing is laid (a first
  open's: its count comes with the head); our server's work ahead alone does not, and the rows' end is not told meanwhile, so
  the wait and the end (with the line's whole length) come once the count is known: a stale layer whose every passage is held
  stays silent with staging's objects a second late, and one missing passages never shows the whole line before them.
- **A notice** carries a chip action and a close button, whose tooltip stands above it; closing it is remembered for this paper's visit, each notice apart — the partial one's close does not close the count of failed passages it stood before (#314).
- **Two notes that are not a notice**: settings that cannot be read stand for as long as it is so, with a link to the settings page and no close (UI.md S-R-21); a write storage refused is told with the settings page's sentence until it is closed or a later write of this page goes through (S-R-22).
- **When the translation's pane has nothing to show**, the same anatomy is a card centred in that pane (300 px, 14 px
  radius, the popover shadow), with a filled action; the capsule is not shown as well.
- **The host's look of the states.** The reader package's chrome draws both hosts' readers, and the coordinator's ruling
  for the website's cut-over is that nothing its readers see changes: where the website's page drew a state otherwise,
  the difference is a host's rule or word (`Parts`, `StateWords` of `packages/reader`), which the extension gives none
  of, so that its reader is as above. The website's, each as its page drew it before the package:
  - `signs: 'by-state'` (its interface review of 2026-11-03): a refusal for now's capsule a clock while its time is to
    come, the information sign once it has come (the chrome drawn again at the time); a run stopped by a fault the alert
    in the danger's red (`data-tone="alert"`); a card that waits (our server or the service out of reach, a limit) a
    clock in quiet ink (`data-tone="wait"`), a fault's card the alert. The extension's: the information sign, the alert
    on every card.
  - `retry: 'when-due'`: a retry whose time is named is offered at that time: the capsule's chip absent until then (its
    words alone, asked again at the time so that they drop it), the card's retry greyed and still a stop of the
    keyboard's, pressing it doing nothing, its lines under the reason the host's (`cardLines`: the time, the limit's
    note). The extension's offers it at once, a press before the time asking nothing.
  - `refusal: 'original'`: a refusal for now with nothing laid holds the original on screen, the two translated displays
    greyed (swap and sync with them), until it passes. The extension's keeps the display chosen, arXiv's pages where the
    translation would be.
  - `sync: 'located'`: the sync greyed until the sides can scroll together (both sides' pages laid out).
  - `openOriginal`: the original that could not be read is the original's pane's card (the file sign in quiet ink, a
    link to arXiv's PDF of the version), the translation's pane left as it is. Where the original's pane is not shown
    (the translation alone, side by side in a narrow window) the translation's pane carries it: the package composes the
    translation over the original's bytes, so that pane has nothing else to show (today's page drew the translation from
    its own files and left the card to the original's pane). The translation's card, the service's, is due at the
    service's time. Without the word, the translation's pane's card with its retry.
  - **One word for the wait** (the coordinator's decision 1, 2026-11-11, after the owner found the staging prompts
    confusing): a status says what the reader waits for, never what the system is doing. The paper's first making (its
    layer being made, the first time anyone opens it, until the count of its translation is known: `status.ts`
    `firstOf`) is the stage `translating`, its words the host's `translating(got, total, chip, first)` with `first`: the
    website says the translation with the time a first one takes, and then the count as before. No stage says the
    paper is being prepared; a screen reader is told the stage once, the first making's words, since the count that
    follows is the same stage. The capsule has no quieter part for the hint (its cells are the count and a part in
    another language, both in the words' ink), so the hint is one sentence with the stage's word.
  - **Waiting in line** (`queued`; the coordinator's decision 5, 2026-11-11): our server at capacity refuses the open
    `busy` in its answer, with a time (30 s); the reader asks again by itself at that time for as long as it is answered
    so, never counted with the limit's 429s (`REFUSED_ASKS`). Where the host words the queue (the website), it is a run's
    capsule, `causeOf(state) === 'busy'` the stage `queued`: the spinner, no retry, the 400 ms of every run's, and the
    first making's words follow it in the same capsule once the open is taken. The extension gives no words for it, so its
    capsule is the refusal's as before (S-R-26's words and retry). The visitor's rate of asks (a 429 that says so) is never
    the queue. Before this, our server named no place in a queue and the reader read one the record does not carry, so
    the queue's words could not show; a busy refusal said the translation was unavailable for now, and stopped asking
    after three.
  - `showTranslation`: the run's capsule carries a chip that shows the translation where it is not on screen and some of
    it is there (the original's display, or the original held for the narrow window), pressing it the reader's own
    choice.
  - `htmlLink`: the link beside a bilingual version not to be had in the host's address and words (the extension's store
    page, where the extension is not on the page), or none (a phone). The HTML version itself is our server's word first
    (its prepare's `html`, after a prepare that cannot be made), arXiv asked only where it says nothing. Every link the
    chrome draws from a host or a document (this one, the settings page's, the lost original's, the title's) is parsed
    and drawn only to the page's own origin, or by https to arXiv's or an origin the host names (`linkOrigins`: the
    website's store page); a `javascript:` or `data:` address, a foreign origin, draws none (`chrome/links.ts`).
  - A face the translation is set in that cannot be had is the reader's state (`ReaderState.faces`), for the host to
    say.
  - `bar: 'bare'`: where neither side has anything to show (the original could not be read, nothing of the translation
    there, none to be had now: its layer refused), the bar is its page's for a paper arXiv does not have: the lead's slot
    (its way home) and the reading options alone, without a paper's rows (the appearance, the dimming and its own last
    rows), no progress line (the interface review of 2026-11-03, v-modes-disabled). The extension's keeps its whole bar
    over the card.
  - With `openOriginal`, the capsule tells the translation's state beside the original's own card (a refusal for now with
    its retry, the paper's own refusal, a run's stage where the host words it), as its page did; not where the service
    failed too, whose card is the pane's answer.
  The hold of the original (`refusal`, `narrow: 'shown'`) is the reader's `hold` command: never written and not a
  choice, so the run the chosen display engages goes on, and the reader's own choice of a display ends it. While it holds
  the original as the paper is made, the progress line is the original's load, whole once read, as the website's page
  drew it (the maintainer's ruling that nothing a website reader sees changes at the cut-over).

The states are §8's.

### 6.7 Popovers and menus

- Anchored under their button, 6 px below it, kept within the window; they grow from the button (scale 0.97 → 1 and
  4 px, 150 ms). Escape and a press outside close them; focus returns to the button.
- Items are 30 px rows with an 8 px radius, their words 10 px in, on the search field's words; the chosen one's check
  at the row's end, 10 px in, in a 14 px slot every row of the menu keeps, after anything else the row holds (UI.md §4).
  Until 2026-10-25 it led the row (the maintainer: 「对勾都在前方…我们应该把它放在字的后边」).
- 译为 (the target language): a search field, then the languages the reader supports (the engine's rules TARGETS), each in its own language,
  by script: CJK in the design's order, 日本語, 简体中文, 繁體中文, 한국어; then the Latin ones and the Cyrillic ones, each in
  the order of their own names: Bahasa Indonesia, Bahasa Melayu, Čeština, Deutsch, Español, Français, Italiano, Nederlands,
  Polski, Português, Svenska, Türkçe; Български, Русский, Українська. The ten after the first nine are the languages of a
  script the engine already set (the owner's ruling of 2026-10-29): each has babel's names, TeX's hyphenation patterns and
  minimums (rules/layout.mjs, tests/fixtures/hyph/README.md) and the letters every served face draws a translation in.
  The list shows eight rows and a half, the half saying there is more, and scrolls in a box of its own under the field,
  which stays in view; it opens with the chosen language in view and keeps the active one there as the arrows walk it
  (`MenuList`'s reveal). Uncapped while the languages were nine, the nineteen ran to the window's foot, on a phone past
  it (the owner, 2026-11-03: a shorter list, the search kept). The field takes the focus as the menu opens, so that
  typing filters at once, but not where the primary pointer is a finger (`(pointer: coarse)`): there the list takes it,
  as the service menu's does, and no on-screen keyboard covers the list until the field is tapped; a letter typed on the
  list (a tablet with a keyboard attached) moves into the field and goes on the end of the search. The primary pointer
  and not `any-hover`/`any-pointer`, which answer for every input a device has: a phone with a stylus that hovers would
  read as able to hover and get the keyboard, and a laptop with a touch screen would lose the focus its keyboard types
  into. The extension's popup and settings page draw the same menu (UI.md S-P-22, S-O-23), at five rows and a half.
- 翻译服务: the same list and labels as the popup's service menu.
- They are built on the shared `Menu` once it has the fixes in §9.4.

### 6.8 Pinch zoom

A trackpad pinch (or Ctrl with the wheel) over the pages zooms both panes together around the pointer, as EmbedPDF
does (「直接双指捏合滑动就可以放大缩小」): a trackpad's small deltas zoom continuously, a mouse notch steps a tenth. While
the fingers move the pinch is shown by transform; `PINCH_COMMIT_MS` (200 ms) after its last step it is committed: the scale
written once (`updateScale({ scaleFactor, drawingDelay: 0 })`), both panes put, the pages drawn once. The browser's own zoom
is taken only over the pages. The overlays follow the pinch exactly (§10.1).

- **Only Ctrl makes a wheel a zoom.** A trackpad pinch arrives in Chrome as a wheel event with Ctrl held, and Ctrl with the
  wheel is a mouse's zoom; ⌘ with the wheel is no zoom gesture on macOS. A wheel with ⌘ held is a scroll like any other,
  never a zoom, in the chrome's pinch, the panes' inputs and the scroll indicator alike. **Why** (the owner's report,
  2026-11-10): the page sometimes zoomed when he pressed ⌘⇧ — macOS's screenshot keys (⌘⇧4, ⌘⇧5), which he uses all the
  time, hold ⌘ while a trackpad's scroll or its momentum is still running, and every wheel with ⌘ was then taken as a
  zoom. The keys are unchanged: ⌘ or Ctrl with − and + zoom by a tenth (§7).
- **No step lays anything out.** From the page boxes read at the gesture's first step, a step works out the layout the
  commit will make at its scale — each page box scaled, the gaps between them not, a page narrower than the view centred,
  the scroll put so that the point under the gesture stays under it, then held within the scroll's ends — and shows it by
  transform: the view scaled about the page that holds the point (growing, the scroller, which the pane clips; shrinking,
  the pages' stack, so that the pages around the view show), each other page near the view moved by what is left over,
  and a box of the scroll's size at the gesture's start holding its range. Nothing scrolls, nothing is clamped, the handles
  hold still, and the commit lands on the layout the last step showed. A step shows the scale PDF.js will set (its
  hundredth), so that the commit does not snap.
- **Nothing is made or drawn meanwhile.** The scaled view is a layer of its own (`will-change: transform` while the
  gesture lasts), drawn at the gesture's first scale and scaled on the compositor: growing, the pages show soft until the
  commit draws them sharp (a step had drawn the original's canvas soft too, and the translation's text sharp, at the cost
  below). The places' near window is held until the commit, so that no place is made, laid or drawn at a scale the commit
  replaces; a pinch out of up to three times shows only places the window held already (it reaches a pane's height above
  and below).
- **Both panes about the gesture's point.** Each pane shown keeps the point at the pointer's place in its view (on the
  other pane, the same place in its view: the same point of the same page while the pair is level), wherever it lies — on a
  page, in the gap between two, beside one: a share of the page box it is level with, or px from its edge where it is
  outside (the gaps and margins do not scale). The pair stays level through the gesture, and its rest finds nothing to level.
- **The follower stands aside.** A wheel with Ctrl is no scroll input; the pinch's first step ends whatever the
  follower moves, calls its rest off (and a zoom's before it still to be levelled: this one's end levels the pair) and holds
  it from binding until the commit; the commit's scrolls are the view's own puts, and the pair is levelled only once the
  zoom settles.
- **Anything else commits first.** Another input on a pane (a wheel without Ctrl, a key, a press, a touch), a scroll the view
  did not make, and every command that reads or moves the panes (a zoom from the menu or the keys, a jump, a page, a
  heading, a display, a click's level, the original let go) commit the pinch before they run; a pane another has scrolled
  (the find bar, a script) keeps the place that scroll took it to, the pinch committed about the point it shows there at
  the gesture's place. The pointer's highlight finds the page under it through the preview's transform, looked at again
  at each step as a scroll had it.
- **The scroll's ends are the paper's.** The range the preview keeps the point within is the one the commit lays: the paper
  at the step's scale and its margin below the last page, never the empty foot of a pane the paper does not fill.
- **Small steps add up.** PDF.js rounds each scale to a hundredth; the fingers' factor is carried whole through the gesture,
  and what the commit's rounding leaves is carried to the next pinch while it keeps its direction, as PDF.js's own viewer
  carries it.
- **Why a transform** (measured 2026-11-02 offline on 2501.14787v1, 101 pages, its layer laid; the reader as `pnpm e2e:reader`
  opens it, staging's recorded layer served by the stand-in; next against this, two runs each, in a slot of its own): each
  step had written the scale, and PDF.js's `update()` then read every page box of both panes, laying them out again — 25–52
  ms a step on staging, 85 % of a pinch's layout, the zoom moving in lumps 106 ms apart at 1x and 300 ms at 4x. On the
  owner's gestures (1093×892, the pointer at 21.5 % across and 61 % down the right pane, out by 0.5 then in by 2.1), the
  layout during the gesture fell from 298–357 to 103–107 ms at 1x and from 1442–1813 to 492–577 ms at 4x, forced layout from
  349–389 to 42–64 ms (1x), tasks over 50 ms from 27–31 to 2–17 (4x) and the longest from 130–158 to 66–79 ms; frames
  dropped zooming in 8 → 1–2 (1x) and 55–63 → 1–35 (4x), zooming out 49–57 → 29 (4x). Zooming out at 1x it drops 7 single
  frames where next dropped 1–2 (the GPU scales the larger view it shows: 155 against 125–130 ms). With 60 Ctrl-wheels to
  three times at 4x (hjfy-compare's gesture, 1440×900), 84–91 frames dropped against 1. The commit costs one step's layout
  (a 15 ms task at 1x, up to 185 ms at 4x for a threefold zoom, against next's redraw of 139–150 ms). Shown as a layer at its
  first scale, the pages are soft while the fingers grow them and sharp from the commit; drawn again at every step's scale
  instead, the GPU spent three times next's and a pinch out dropped frames for it (0 → 14 % at 1x). The owner watched the
  same gestures side by side at 1x and 4x and accepted both costs, the softness while the pages grow and the frames a pinch
  out drops at 1x (2026-11-02: 「能接受」).
- **Why** (the owner's recording on 1706.03762v7, 2026-11-01, the handles jittering through a pinch; the probe's frames): the right pane was kept
  only where a page lay under the pointer, and a pointer beside a page at a small zoom kept nothing, so that the pane stood
  still while its pages grew about its top — its thumb jumping 10–14 px a step, the pair drifting two pages apart, levelled
  by a glide of more than a page after the gesture; the left was kept about its top quarter whatever the pointer's height,
  so that the pair drifted even where both were kept; the thumb's length came a frame after its place (§6.5); and at 26 %
  a step under 1.9 % rounded to no change and was lost, a slow pinch not zooming at all.

## 7. Interaction details

- A press on a toolbar button scales it to 0.96; hover and open take the fill in 150 ms.
- The display switch's thumb slides; the sidebar slides; the pills and indicators fade; the capsule rises; the appearance
  crossfades. Nothing jumps.
- Escape closes the open popover, and a Tab out of it closes it too, the focus going on; ⌘± zoom.

## 8. States

The mechanism is §6.6; the words come from the locale packs, and failure reasons reuse the ones the popup already shows.
No state that tells the reader nothing is shown (no "done").

| State | When | Shown |
|---|---|---|
| Reading | 原文; a translation ready; a stored translation shown, offline included | nothing |
| Loading | a large PDF is loading; the translation there, its first page being laid (a stored one read, or a run's last rows in) | the progress line by the share downloaded, its first stretch; 正在加载 said to screen readers |
| Preparing | the paper's bilingual files are being made (our server's prepare, a paper no reader opened before) | the original; the progress line's first half after the download, by the prepare's stage (§6.6); 正在准备 said to screen readers (S-R-23); the website's capsule says the translation the reader waits for, with the time a first one takes (§6.6) |
| Translating | the paper's paragraphs being translated by the service chosen | the same line on, by the share of paragraphs done; 正在翻译 said to screen readers; each page laid on the right as its paragraphs come, the original's page until then. The paragraphs counted are those of the layer on screen that "What to translate" shows translated; one whose translation is already held is done, and a run that only restates them is not shown |
| Not to be had now | Read arXiv's website out of reach, at its limit, or the network itself down (§8.1: each cause its own words) | the original readable, the displays as they are; capsule: PDF 对照暂时无法加载 · 重试 · 改用 HTML 翻译 where arXiv has an HTML version (S-R-24), the retry only where the session does not ask again by itself (§8.1); passing, not remembered; a paper whose files this machine keeps opens without it |
| Some paragraphs failed | a translation with gaps: rows that are none, or a run that ended failed and is not asked again at once (§8.1) | capsule: {n} 处翻译失败 · 重试 (where nothing asks again by itself) · close |
| Language not supported | the shared target language is not one of the reader's | 原文, with the capsule: PDF 对照暂不支持{语言} · 选择语言 (opens the language menu in place); choosing one of the reader's translates |
| Nothing translated | a service failure with no paragraph done | card in the translation's pane: the reason (网络连接失败, API Key 无效或已过期, 尚未配置 API Key, 请求过于频繁, …) · 重试, or 设置 when the reason is a key (opening the settings page at the services). The reason is the unit's `Why` read by format's one reading of it (`kindOfWhy`, which the extension's `errorOf` and so the HTML page's words read too): a reply no translator gave back whole an invalid response; a translator out of reach the network, a rate limit where it named a wait; a key refused the key's; no model or no translator for the target a bad request; any other unconfigured code a missing key's. Our server's run of the target failed is the network's |
| Cannot be had | no bilingual version can be made of the paper (no source, no PDF, a prepare that cannot succeed, one this version of the reader cannot read) | 对照 and 译文 greyed in the switch; the reader shows 原文, with the capsule: 这篇论文暂不支持 PDF 翻译, and 改用 HTML 翻译 where arXiv has an HTML version (opened where `reading.openIn` says); no close |
| No paper | the address names none (a hand-typed one) | the phase is ready, not loading; 对照 and 译文 greyed and 原文 selected whatever the saved display; a card in the document area: 找不到这篇论文 · 前往 arXiv (a link, opened where `reading.openIn` says) |
| Settings cannot be read | storage did not answer in a page's first 1,500 ms, or its value cannot be used | the defaults in use and the PDF opened on them, not held for the storage; capsule: 设置读取失败，当前使用默认设置 · 设置, for as long as it is so, beside an address with no paper's card too; the controls that write the settings greyed, with the reason in their tooltips; the menus keep their places |
| Narrow window | 对照 chosen, the document area under 840 px (§5) | the translation alone; capsule, once: 窗口较窄，暂只显示译文 |

- **The website's words** (`readarxiv-web` `web/src/reader/web-words.ts`, given to the chrome as `StateWords` by its
  v2 page; zh-TW, ja and ko in the same table). The extension gives none and keeps the catalogue's above. A run's
  capsule enters once its wait has lasted 400 ms (§6.6); every other capsule at once.

  | State | When | zh-CN | en |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | The first making | the paper's layer being made (no layer to show yet: the first time anyone opens it), until the count of its translation is known | 正在翻译 · 首次约需 1–2 分钟 | Translating · the first time takes 1–2 minutes |
  | Translating, counted | the view waits for paragraphs of the layer shown (Translating above) | 正在翻译 · {n} / {N} 段 | Translating · {n} of {N} passages (under 400 px: Translating {n} of {N}) |
  | Translating, bare | the same, the layer's count not known yet (a layer shown before this visit), or the count beside the chip in a window under 400 px where the short count does not fit | 正在翻译 | Translating |
  | Waiting in line | our server at capacity: the open refused `busy`, asked again by itself | 排队中 | Waiting in line |
  | Reconnecting | our server's document not heard while a run is under way | 正在重新连接 | Reconnecting |
  | The run's chip | beside a run's words, the translation not on screen and some of it there | 查看译文 | Show translation |
  | Cannot be had | no bilingual version can be made of the paper | 这篇论文暂时无法翻译 | This paper can't be translated yet |
  | Too large | the paper too large to prepare | 这篇论文篇幅过大，暂时无法翻译 | This paper is too long to translate |
  | Not now, our server | out of reach or at fault; the time while it is to come | 翻译暂时不可用，{time} 后可以重试 | Translation is unavailable for now; you can retry at {time} |
  | Not now, the limit | the visitor's new papers spent; the time while it is to come; then the note today's card said under it, true of this limit alone (the feature list's I7) | 新论文的翻译次数已达上限，{time} 后可以重试 · 已有译文的论文仍可打开 | You've reached the limit for new papers; you can retry at {time} · Papers already translated still open |
  | The HTML link | beside a paper that cannot be had, where arXiv has an HTML version: the extension on the page, or not (none on a phone) | 改用 HTML 翻译 · 安装扩展翻译 HTML | Translate HTML instead · Get the extension for HTML |

  A time once come drops from its sentence (the title alone). The visitor's rate of asks and the network itself are
  the sibling lane's words (flow-refusals, 2026-11-11). Nothing the website says names the paper being prepared: the
  word 正在准备 is the old page's (`reader/job-view.ts`, production's) and the extension's screen-reader line (S-R-23)
  alone.
- Recovery is automatic where it can be: our server's wait (a 202's, a 429's) is waited, as our server names it, and asked
  again, a 429's three times in a row at most (S-R-26: a visitor's limit lasts up to a day, and a tab left open asked again
  for as long as it stayed open; #88 E5), the visitor's rate of asks, our server at capacity (its queue) and the network's at every time (§8.1); 重试 opens the
  layer again and asks only for the paragraphs that are missing, the rest coming from the cache; rate limiting never shows
  (the chain retries it, and only its final giving-up counts as a failure).
- A failure never takes focus.

### 8.1 Refusals and failures: one source for a time, the causes apart, the passages that failed

A status says what the reader is waiting for and what they can do; every number or time it prints has one source and is
true (the coordinator's flow of 2026-11-11, which the owner delegated after testing staging: with the hour's new papers
spent the page said "20:26 后可以重试" at 20:16 and "20:36" at 20:26, while our server's record said 21:00:00).

- **The retry's time is our server's instant.** A refusal of new work names the instant it ends, on our server's clock: the
  visitor's period's end exactly for a quota (the hour's, or the UTC day's, as the admission knows it), its wait from the
  admission's now for capacity. The paper's record keeps that instant as it is (`retryAt`), and the open's answer names it
  (`refused.retryAt`) beside its distance to the millisecond (`refused.retryAfterMs`: what the session counts on its own clock)
  and in whole seconds, rounded up (`refused.retryAfterS`: all an older reader reads). Never a wait in seconds re-anchored on another clock: the admission's
  `ceil((until - now) / 1000)` added to the paper's clock and the viewer's landed past the minute (staging's record 21:00:00.408)
  and was said 21:01, "tomorrow 0:01" across midnight (flow-fixes F1, 2026-11-12). The session's own next ask waits for the later
  of two: our server's wait measured on the viewer's clock from the answer, and the viewer's clock reading the instant said; so
  it never asks before the time it said nor before our server would take it, whichever way the viewer's clock is off (90 s
  ahead: it asks when our server's hour is over, at 21:01:30 on that clock; 90 s behind: at 21:00:00 on that clock, our server's
  21:01:30); where the two clocks agree, the ask is at the instant itself (a wait counted in whole seconds asked again 0.4 s
  past it). A wait no time is said for (capacity, the rate) is our server's wait alone. Whether a time is said is the chrome's
  (`capsuleOf`), the host's words saying the time they are given: while it is to come, and while the session will ask by itself
  at it, until that ask begins (never the bare sentence between the instant and the ask); one the reader is to retry at drops
  from its sentence once it has come. A refusal's time is the one our server
  names, as it names it (a failed run's `retryAt` in its document likewise), never capped: the time printed, the moment the retry is offered
  (the website's `retry: 'when-due'`; a press before it asks nothing) and the session's own next ask are that one time. A
  bound remains only where it paces polling (a stream's reconnection time, `WAIT_MAX_MS`). The fourth refusal in a row keeps
  the time and only stops the session asking by itself. A refusal told again with another time is told again, and the
  capsule follows it. The session's own next ask has a floor and a pace of its own, never printed (integration, round B10):
  never sooner than a second after the answer (`WAIT_MIN_MS`), and a refusal of our server's capacity or of the visitor's
  rate answered again and again backs off, its wait doubled each time, at most thirty seconds (`BACKOFF_MAX_MS`) or the time
  our server names, the larger; an answer that moves the paper on ends the run. A 429 naming 0 s was otherwise asked again
  at once, without end.
- **Printed rounded up.** The time is printed in the viewer's zone, rounded up to its minute only where it is not on one, so
  that at the minute printed a press works (15:19:45 is said 15:20; 21:00:00 is said 21:00). The hour is two digits where the
  language writes it so (zh-CN, zh-TW, ja, ko: 00:00, 09:05, 21:00, each in its own hour cycle), English unpadded (9:05 AM): one
  formatter for every such time, the website's `home/card.ts` `clockOf`. On the visitor's next day (their zone) the sentence says tomorrow (明天 {time} 后可以重试); on a
  later day it gives the date and the time, as the website's home card writes a date.
- **The causes apart** (`causeOf`: quota, busy, rate, network, server), each with a sentence of its own:
  - the visitor's new papers spent (`quota`): 新论文的翻译次数已达上限，{time} 后可以重试, its time our server's (the website's adds its note, 已有译文的论文仍可打开);
  - our server at capacity (`busy`): its own state (the wait's words, §6.6);
  - the visitor's rate of asks (`rate`: a 429 whose body says `rate-limited`): 请求过于频繁，请稍后再试, no time; the reader
    asks again by itself once our server's wait has passed, never counted among the three refusals in a row;
  - the network itself (`network`: a fetch that rejected twice, or the browser offline): 网络连接失败，请检查网络, no time; the
    reader asks again by itself at once when the browser says it is online again (the `online` event), and, while it says it
    is online, at a growing pace (a second, doubled to thirty);
  - our server at fault (`server`: a 5xx twice, a prepare that failed by its fault): 翻译暂时不可用, with its time where its
    record names one; a retry asks again. A prepare's failure is our server's when its record says `internal`, `deadline`,
    `translation-down` or `unavailable`: each named in the session's table (`session/machine.ts PREPARE_WHY`, the layer
    refused `unreachable` with the record's `retryAt`, the time of our server's next attempt), never the paper's own. They
    had fallen to the same by being in no table; today's page told `internal` as a failure (the feature list's R08). The
    website's tests hold its server's words and the table equal, so a word its server adds fails them until it is named.
  The extension's capsules keep the catalogue's sentences (PDF 对照暂时无法加载 for our server and the network, its limit's
  sentence for a limit and the rate).
- **An action is offered only where the system will not take it by itself; a failure is told only where the system is not
  already trying again** (the coordinator's principle, 2026-11-12; flow-fixes F2, F4). At a refusal's time the retry chip came
  and, the same instant, the session asked again by itself: the chip stood a quarter of a second. The session states, for each
  thing that stopped, whether it asks again by itself (`againOf`): the original the network failed to bring (opened again a
  second on, at once when the browser is online); the look a 429 stopped that it waits out (the rate, capacity, the limit's
  first three) or the network stopped; a prepare or a run of the target whose record names a time and whose open this visit has
  not asked; a translator's wait. The reader's state carries it (`self`), and no retry is drawn for it: not the capsule's chip
  (`retryOffered`), not the notice's, not the failure card's button, not the original's card's (the extension's v2 build). A
  retry is offered where nothing asks again but the reader: our server out of reach, the limit past its three asks (at its
  time on the website), a key, a run this visit asked already. A session that does not say (the extension's today session)
  keeps every retry as it was.
- **The network down while a counted translation is waited for** (flow-fixes F3): where the view waits on our server for a
  translation it counts, the browser offline, or an ask's fetch rejected with nothing heard since (the look stopped for the
  network, or asked again and not heard yet) is the network's (`linkSaid`, the reader's state's `network`): its words over the
  count, whatever is on screen, with no retry (the session asks again once it is back), the count again once a document is
  heard. A stream that broke while the browser is online and is opened again is reconnecting (the system acting, nothing for the
  reader to do). A reader only reading a finished translation is told neither: nothing is waited for. With no layer shown, the
  network's stop is the layer's refusal for now, as before.
- **One definition of the system still working for this reader** (the coordinator's R6 of 2026-11-12; integration's B11 F1,
  F2): our server's look on, or stopped for a cause the session goes on from by itself, with no period to end and nothing of the
  reader's (`GOES_ON`: our server at capacity, the visitor's rate of asks, the network; `goesOn`). The one table is the
  session's (`machine.ts`): the view's wait reads it (`rows.ts` `runOf` `live`), the session's own next ask (a cause in it is
  always asked again: `refusedFor`'s wake), what it asks again by itself (`againOf`) and the chrome's display and words
  (`model.ts`, `status.ts` `GOES_ON`, made from it). Before it, the view's wait read a narrower test (the look on, or stopped for
  the network), so a queue over a shown layer flipped the wait to done and back at every one of the session's re-asks, 1, 2, 4,
  8 s apart, the progress line flashing each time; and a prepare running by the last document kept a wait whose look had stopped
  for good (our server out of reach), its count still, nothing offered.
- **A wait the session carries on by itself is one wait** (R7): its cause is said as round B10 words it (the website's
  `queued`, `rate` and `network` words, §8's table), over the run it pauses (the queue a run's stage, the rate and the network over its
  count), the run's phase kept (`model.ts`: an `unavailable` of a cause in `GOES_ON` the session asks again by itself), so its
  line goes on, nothing reads as done, and the cause stays said from one of the session's asks to the next until an answer
  moves the paper on (`lookSaid`: the refusal's cause kept, `pacing`; the network until a document is heard). Over a layer
  shown it is said as where none is (the reader's `layer.stopped`, while the view lacks what the work would bring).
- **Where the session will not go on by itself, the wait is over** (R8): the limit of new papers (with its time; its first
  asks the session's own, at that time, asking nothing of the reader: no retry, §8.1's first bullet), our server out of reach
  (a retry at once), past the limit's asks (a retry at its time): the notice as round B10 words it, over a layer shown too,
  never a count that does not move with nothing offered.
- **The display the reader chose is kept while the session goes on by itself** (flow-fixes F5 and (b), the coordinator,
  2026-11-12): with no period to end and nothing of the reader's (our server at capacity, the visitor's rate of asks, the network:
  `goesOnNow`), the page stands as it does in the first-time wait, the display chosen kept and the translated displays to be
  chosen, so nothing jumps when the session goes on. The original is held alone, the translated displays greyed (the website's
  `refusal: 'original'`), where the translation cannot come before a period ends or at all (the limit of new papers, a lasting
  refusal) and for our server's fault with its time. A narrow window holds the original, as before, whatever the cause.
