- **A capsule showing that turns into a run changes its words in place** ((c)): the 400 ms gate (§6.6) is for a wait that
  begins with nothing shown; after the network's words or the failed passages' notice, the count takes the capsule's place at
  once, never a hole of 0.4 s; so does a run's capsule wanted again while it is still leaving (R4, 2026-11-12).
- **Which refusals last** is one table, the session's (`LASTING`: no source, not found, cannot be prepared, too large, a
  version this reader cannot read); the chrome's is made from it. A layer the reader could not use (an object not its bytes,
  a layer refused by the side) is passing: a retry asks again.
- **Failed passages on the website.** A failed passage is a unit of the layer shown that the toggles show translated and
  that holds no translation once the target's run has failed: a row that is none, or no row at all (our server writes no
  row for what a failed attempt did not translate, and an attempt our server ends itself writes none). They are counted over
  the same set as the run's count (§6.6), told whenever the count changes (a toggle, the units read, passages a later run
  brings), and said as the extension's are: after a page is laid, the capsule {n} 处翻译失败 with its retry at our server's
  time; before, the card (翻译暂时不可用 · 重试, its time under it). A run that ends done tells none, whatever rows are missing
  for kept or toggled-off units. 重试 asks only for the passages that failed: our server's next run reuses every row it holds.
  When the session's own next ask runs, the wait's own words replace the notice, and the passages it brings leave the count.
  Told only where the session is not already asking for them again (flow-fixes F4): a failed run whose open is under way or due
  at once (a run the visit did not open, found failed with no time to wait) is the run the reader waits for, its count, never
  the notice (it stood 150 ms); one asked again at our server's time is the notice for that wait, with no retry, giving way to
  the count when the ask begins; one nothing asks again but the reader is the notice with its retry.
  The notice closed stays closed for the visit unless more passages fail.
- **A page laid is a lay over the rows as they stand** (2026-11-13). A page laid, committed or laid with nothing of its own
  (every member without a translation: the original's by the rule), keeps every row its lay read and what it saw of it (a
  translation, a refusal, none in yet); a row that lands otherwise than it saw (one come, a refusal translated after all by
  another service or a retry, a row stated again otherwise) lays that page again, alone, its drawing kept and muted until the
  new one commits (`packages/reader/src/compose/composer.ts` `moved`). One condition in place of three: a row stated again
  otherwise laid every page again in a generation of its own; a row missing at the rows' end, come since, did too; a page laid
  with nothing kept only the units it read missing once the rows had ended. A page laid with nothing BEFORE the end, every
  unit refused while the run went on (a refusing service, the extension's `src/pdf-reader/host/translate.ts`), kept nothing,
  and the translations another service brought later laid it again never (the V5 lane's e2e: 3 runs of 5, `laidPages: 0`).
  A row read and waited for by no page (the paper's own names, §19.14) lays its page again when it comes, once. The law test:
  `packages/reader/tests/composer.test.ts` "the toggles turned and turned back", each sequence of landings, the run's end and
  each option turned, every drawing a fresh lay's.

## 9. The extension around the reader

### 9.1 Settings: one set, shared

The reader keeps no settings of its own apart from the extension's: the popup, the settings page and the reader change
the same values, and each follows the others through the shared configuration's subscription at once
(`useSurfaceConfig`). There is no new message for it.

**Read, as they are**: `targetLanguage` (the reader's languages, §6.7; §8 for the others), `provider` and `services`,
`reading.sentenceHighlight` (对照高亮), `appearance.activeHighlight` among `appearance.highlights` (高亮颜色: the swatches are
the configured highlight profiles, the three built-in and any added), `uiLanguage` (the reader's words), `mode` (the
display, §3). The image switch (`image.enabled`, S-P-85) is the HTML page's alone since v21: the reader's figure text is
its own toggle, below; until then the switch showed or hid it too.

- **Writing the display**: 对照 writes `mode: 'side'`, unless it is `'stack'` (a side-by-side choice already for the
  reader); 译文 writes `'only'`; both clear `pdfReader.original`. 原文 sets `pdfReader.original` and leaves `mode` alone.
- **Another target language**, once a translation has started (chosen here or elsewhere): the translation in it in place, the
  page never loaded again (`settings.ts` `followOf` `retarget`, the run's `retarget`, §11.8). The left, both documents, the zoom,
  the sync and the reading place stay; each laid page shows the language before until the new one's page is laid, and the
  original's page where the new one's service fails or stops short with nothing translated. The line and the phase are an open's (Translating, §8). A hold
  for the language before (one the layer does not set) is lifted and the translated display shown again; a hold for the
  paper's own reason stays.
- **Another service** (`provider` or `services` changed, here or elsewhere; most often the key the card sent the reader to
  set, §8): a translation that stopped short, failed or ended with passages lost, is asked again of it at once, whatever wait
  the service before named, and only for the passages with no translation (`settings.ts` `followOf` `retry`). The rebuilt
  reader (`packages/reader`) reads the services as the preferences' `translator`, the chain's revision (`host/prefs.ts`): a
  landing that names another one is the session's `cmd.translator` (`session/machine.ts` `askedAgain`). The website's
  preferences name none (its rows are our server's), so nothing there asks again.

**New**, a `pdfReader` group; `CONFIG_VERSION` 18 → 19, with a migration that adds it with its defaults:

| Key | Type | Default | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pdfReader.enabled` | boolean | true | 在 arXiv 的 PDF 上使用对照阅读器 |
| `pdfReader.original` | boolean | false | the reader was last left in 原文 (the HTML page's "translation on" is the tab's session, not a setting) |
| `pdfReader.sync` | boolean | true | 同步滚动: the engine's `same` mode on, `off` off |
| `pdfReader.swapped` | boolean | false | 左右互换 |
| `pdfReader.appearance` | `'light' \| 'dark' \| 'system'` | `'system'` | 外观 (the extension has no appearance setting; its pages follow the system) — moved to the extension's theme at configuration v20 (the redesign's §3): one appearance for every surface, set here or on the settings page |
| `pdfReader.dimPages` | boolean | true | 深色时调暗页面 |

The experiment's own `axtPdfReader` storage key goes, without a migration: it was never released (rule 7 is about what a
released version left on a machine).

**What to translate** (UI.md S-R-27, S-O-56; `CONFIG_VERSION` 20 → 21, the owner's rulings of 2026-10-25, 2026-10-28 and 2026-10-30): `pdfReader.classes`,
five booleans whose keys are the engine's toggles (`rules/content-classes.mjs` `TOGGLES`, `always` and `never` aside) and
whose value is the layer's `classes` option as it is (§19.10, §19.13).

| Key | Default | Row (§15) | What it shows translated |
|---|---|---|---|
| `figures` | true | Text in figures | the text inside a paper's drawn figures (§19.12) |
| `tables` | true | Text in tables | the table cells |
| `heads` | true | Headers and footers | the running heads and feet |
| `references` | false | References | the bibliography, each entry whole, the names inside it included |
| `names` | false | Authors and affiliations | the whole author block under the title: its names, affiliations, institutions, addresses and e-mail line (the owner, 2026-10-30; from 2026-10-28 to then the names alone, "Author names", the rest always translated), and the notes its source ties to it wherever they stand: a `\thanks` written in `\author{…}`, acmart's `\authornote`, ICML's footnote of the places its class stores (the owner, 2026-11-13; §18.71). The key and its default are as they were: no migration, and by default the whole block is the original's |

- **A toggle shows or hides; it never translates.** Every class is translated once whatever the toggles say (the run sends
  every unit `toTranslate` names, the hidden classes' among them), and a change is the layer side's `setClasses`: the door
  opened again over the same documents, parts and rows, each laid page kept until the new door's commits, nothing fetched
  from our server and nothing sent to the service (`session/host.ts` follows the setting as it lands, from the reading
  options or the settings page: `sameClasses`, `run.setClasses`). The cache key does not move: no toggle is an input of a
  translation (hard rule 4).
- **Figure text is its own setting**, no longer the image switch: the HTML page's switch (S-P-85) decides whether a figure is read
  and translated at all, which spends the reader's service, and a toggle here only shows or hides what was made. One row,
  one setting, one name. The migration writes each toggle as the reader had it in effect at v20: `figures` the image
  switch's value (the reader gave the layer its figures from it), the rest the engine's defaults then (heads and tables
  shown, references and names not), written as literals so that a later default does not move what v21 wrote.
- **The rows' order** (`CLASS_ROWS`, `pdf-reader/settings.ts`): the text in figures and in tables first, then the heads and
  feet, the references and the author names (the owner's, 2026-10-25), in the reading options (S-R-27) and on the settings
  page (S-O-56) alike. The defaults are restated in `config/schema.ts` (`DEFAULT_PDF_CLASSES`), the configuration free of the
  engine, and held equal to `TOGGLE_DEFAULTS` by `tests/config/storage.test.ts`.

### 9.2 The popup while the reader is open

The entry message's answer (`EntryStatus`) gains the page's kind, `'abs' | 'pdf'`, and on a PDF page whether the reader
is open. With the reader open, the popup acts on it, by the settings (the maintainer: general functions stay; what the
reader cannot do is greyed or hidden):

- 翻译服务: all, as elsewhere.
- 译为: the reader's languages only (§6.7).
- The prompt row: as elsewhere.
- The mode bar: 左右 and 仅译文 usable; 上下 disabled, its title PDF 对照不支持上下排列 (a layout the reader can see, not
  a technical reason). A `mode` of `'stack'` shows as 左右 chosen, since that is what the reader shows.
- The primary button: 翻译本页 / 显示原文, clearing or setting `pdfReader.original`.
- 对照高亮: as elsewhere. The image switch greyed in its place, as the style menu is (it is the HTML page's since v21, and
  changes nothing in the reader, whose figure text is its own toggle, §9.1); its value the stored one.
- The style menu: greyed, in its place (it has no effect on a typeset PDF; greyed, not explained — the maintainer, 2026-09-28: the foot stays the same on every page).

With the reader closed, a PDF page gets the abstract page's entry view: the two buttons.

### 9.3 The settings page

- A new section **PDF 阅读器** (`#pdf-reader`, after 阅读): 在 arXiv 的 PDF 上使用对照阅读器, 同步滚动, 外观, 深色时调暗页面
  (since the redesign: the PDF group of the Reading section at `#reading/pdf`, the appearance and the dimming under
  Appearance; `#pdf-reader` still leads there). The reader's 设置 button opens the settings page there.
- **What to translate** (v21, `#reading/classes`, UI.md S-O-56): a group of its own after the PDF group, its heading's aside
  saying it is the bilingual PDF's alone (the HTML page translates every part, and its figure text is the Reading card's
  image switch), its five switches the reading options' (S-R-27) in their words and order. Shown whether the reader opens
  arXiv's PDFs or not: `#readarxiv` opens it either way.
- **数据** gains a line for the PDF translations kept on this machine, `{n} 篇 · {size}`, and 清除 through the existing
  `Confirm` (two presses; it disarms after 4 s), beside the HTML translations' line (the maintainer: 「其他暂时这样」 on
  the proposal). The settings page is on the extension's origin and calls the store's `usage()` and `clear()` directly: the
  store of the reader the build runs (`AXT_READER`), never the other's.
- **The papers this machine keeps** (the rebuilt reader, `packages/reader` behind the extension's host): the owner's rule of
  2026-10-08, offline nothing new is drawn and a paper kept still opens. The store is the reader's network seen through this
  machine (`host/stored-fetch.ts` over `cache/paper-store.ts`, at the Host's one seam, its `fetch`): what never changes at its
  address (an object of a layer or a range of one, our copy of arXiv's PDF where it was read, a face's file) is read there
  first and kept as it is read; what may change (the faces' tables, a language's patterns) and the paper's document (the
  open's answer, the follow's documents) are asked of our server first, the last document with a layer kept for each paper
  version, and answered from the store where our server is out of reach (a fetch that rejects and is no abort of the reader's,
  or a 5xx). arXiv's own bytes are never kept, as the old reader's store kept none. Each answer is checked against the digest
  of its bytes as kept, every time it is read (and a whole object against the digest its address names before it is kept);
  past 200 MB the paper versions opened least recently go first, with all they hold, the faces' files last; every failure of
  the store is a miss. What a reader sees, our server out of reach (the existing words only):
  - **a paper kept**: the Reading state: the original, and the translation laid from the store and from the passages the
    background keeps (the rows, DESIGN §9), no capsule; a passage never translated before is asked of the service, which may
    itself be out of reach: the passages that failed, with their retry and close (S-R-15), once the run has ended;
  - **none kept**: the original, the translated displays as they are, and the capsule of Not to be had now (§8, §8.1): our
    server answering with a failure (a 5xx), the bilingual version not to be had now, with its retry (S-R-24); no answer at
    all (the browser offline, a connection reset), the network's sentence with no retry, the session asking again by itself
    (`tests/e2e/reader-v2-layer.mjs`, the states section, both with nothing kept).
  The database is the old reader's (`axt-layer`) at version 5. **The version step** deletes the old reader's three tables
  (objects by digest, catalogs, who held what), which no address of the rebuilt reader reaches, on the first open by this
  build. **The way back**, measured (`tests/cache/paper-store.test.ts`, Dexie 4.4): a build of version 4 meets the database
  of version 5 and works, Dexie opening it at 5.1 with the old tables made again beside the new; its papers kept from then
  on are its own, and this build, back again, works on its own rows. Nothing breaks either way; what a return leaves is the
  old tables beside the new (at most the old store's 200 MB), until a later version step names them null again: the
  rollback recipe is that step in the release that comes forward after a rollback (`axt-layer` version 6, `objects`,
  `papers`, `refs` null). The background's `axt-translation-cache` at version 3 (cache/translate-store.ts, the per-text
  table dropped) goes back the same way, measured (`tests/cache/translate-store.test.ts`): a build of version 2 works at
  3.1 with its `entries` made again, this build again on its own rows; its recipe the same, `entries` null in version 4.

### 9.4 The shared `Menu`, made accessible

The reader's menus are built on `Menu`, the shared component of `src/ui/` at the time, and its gaps are closed for every user of it (the popup, the
settings page's drawers): the active item announced as the arrows move; Home and End; typing a letter jumps to it; focus
back on the trigger when it closes; no buttons inside a listbox. (Retired with the redesign: the reader's menus are
`MenuList`, `packages/ui/src/controls/`, and `Menu` is gone.)

## 10. Engine changes, each measured

### 10.1 Overlays follow a pinch by transform

The highlight bands and the figure overlays are positioned in CSS pixels of the page as it was drawn. While a pinch lasts
PDF.js scales the page by CSS alone, so they drifted off their figures: 54 → 108 → 209 px from 83 % to 114 %. Each keeps
its pixel geometry and gains `transform-origin: <−left>px <−top>px` and `scale: calc(var(--total-scale-factor) / s0)`, `s0`
the viewport scale it was drawn at: it scales about the page's origin with the page, on the compositor, with no layout
and no script. Mid-pinch it stays within 0.7 px of its place.

Measured on 2608.02163, a pinch 83 % → 245 % in 36 steps, three runs each, in a real window; the method is in the report's nineteenth addendum
(`git show exp-freeze-2026-10-07:experiments/pdf-bilingual/REPORT.md`), and the implementation commits the probe, driving PDF.js's `updateScale` itself so
that it needs no harness:

| Way | Layout per pinch, 1 figure / 220 labels | Main thread | Frames over 1.5× |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pixels (before) | 29 / 86 ms | 303 / 528 ms | 1–3 |
| Percent of the page box | 4–9× the layout | 2–4× | 7–56 |
| Transform (this) | 30 / 84 ms | 335 / 476 ms | 1–2 |
| Hidden while pinching | 29 / 91 ms | 295 / 431 ms | 0–2 |

Percent positioning — proposed first, and the reason the maintainer asked for certainty (「一定要确定……不是贪小便宜吃大
亏的，它不能影响性能」) — costs the whole page's layout on every frame as soon as one child of a page is sized in percent,
whatever the number of labels (2.5× with the labels removed). PDF.js itself hides its text layer during a pinch for the
same reason. Freezing the overlays into a layer (`will-change: transform`) during a pinch gained nothing and cost more
under load; hiding them costs the same as the transform but loses them for the pinch. Neither is used.

### 10.2 Overlays kept across a redraw

PDF.js's page `reset()` removes every node it does not own when it redraws a page after a zoom; the overlays were put
back only after the figure pipeline ran again, so a figure showed its original text for 40–300 ms. A `MutationObserver`
on the pages puts a removed overlay back in the same task, before the frame is painted, except the ones the reader
removes itself (marked as it removes them). Measured: 0 ms bare (no figure was without its overlay after a redraw); what the observer itself costs while
reading was not measured apart. The transform keeps the overlays right at the new scale, and nothing is recomputed unless
their content changes.

### 10.3 Stopping early when the service fails

When a batch fails because of the service itself (network, key, quota), the rest are not sent: they would fail the same
way. With no paragraph translated nothing is compiled and the card shows the reason; with some, what there is is
compiled and the notice counts the rest. (Before: every batch retried for 24–48 s, and after 215 s an English "translation"
was compiled.)

Measured on the fake compiler (`parked/lab/spikes/cache-cases.mjs`): a failure in the second of three batches sends no third, and
the final is compiled with the first; nothing translated compiles nothing, not even the marked original. A key refused
midway stops the run the same way, and the run resolves (the unhandled rejection it left on the page is gone). The
figures' text goes through the same service: once a run has stopped, none is sent until it runs again. The notice's
{n} is the paragraphs left in the source language: a paragraph a stored copy had translated keeps it when its new try
fails, and is not counted.

A stop the service makes by withdrawing the reader's scope (the background retiring its chain when a service is deleted, a
translator that gives up with an abort) is a stop like the others (the owner's ruling, 2026-11-11): its kind, `aborted`, is
told as `unknown` (UI.md §3.4), since `aborted` is the reader's own cancel and shows nothing; the card or the notice says it
with its retry, and the units never asked are counted with the rest (`runRows` counts them unless the run's own signal
stopped it). The run's own abort (a retry, another target, the page's end) returns before any of this and tells nothing.
Before, the run read the service's `aborted` as its own: the translation told done, our page laid with nothing translated
on it, and a notice with no retry counting the last batch alone.

Texts that did not come back for a reason that is not theirs (the service's own: a network down, a timeout, a rate limit
the background's queue has already retried) are not sent again piece by piece, since they would only fail again, once for
each piece. They stay in the source language, counted, and the failure is kept (`EngineError.lost`, `mt.mjs`
`translateUnits`).

### 10.4 Small ones

- A heading unit keeps the level of its sectioning command, for the contents (§6.3).
- A figure's bitmap is read by the extension's recogniser through the background (`axt:ocr`), as the HTML page's
  are: the package carries one recogniser (its build check allows one runtime), and results are cached by the image's
  hash.
- A replaced viewer lets go of its pages: `setDocument(null)` on it and on its link service cancels its page views, their
  text layers and its annotation editor's manager. Before, each swap of the right side kept the whole old viewer alive
  (measured on the demo paper, the heap by CDP: 26 pages and 2 text layers a swap, 234 pages after nine; one more
  document `selectionchange` listener each time); after, none. PDF.js's `abortSignal` is not used: nothing is left
  for it after the teardown, and the document-level selection listener all text layers share is bound to the signal
  of whichever viewer's text layer came first, so aborting that viewer would take text selection from the viewers
  still on screen.
- The translation scope the reader binds in the background is withdrawn when the page goes (`pagehide`), and that handler
  is set before the status call that binds the scope: an extension page is no tab the background watches, so nothing else
  withdraws it, and a page closed while that call was out left its scope bound. A reader that finds no engine able to
  translate withdraws the scope it just bound at once (`session/translate.mjs` `openEngine`).
- A test pins the PDF.js internals the engine reads (`_pages`, the page views' `pdfPage.view`, `renderingState`), so an
  upgrade that changes them fails at once.

## 11. Architecture

### 11.1 The page

- `src/entrypoints/pdf-reader/` (`index.html`, `main.tsx`, `App.tsx`), built by WXT with React and TypeScript.
  `pdf.content.ts` opens it in its frame with `?paper=<id>`; `web_accessible_resources` names it, at the browser session's
  dynamic address (`use_dynamic_url`, DESIGN §4.0c).
- It frames nothing: the translation is the layer's, drawn in the page (§11.7–§11.9); the compile page it framed until
  Stage 5 is parked (`parked/README.md`).
- **The reader's address is not trusted.** The reader is a page that arXiv's pages may frame, so its URL is not its own to
  trust: a page that frames it must not point its requests anywhere else. It fetches the paper from arXiv and its layer
  from our server, or either from a server on this machine when a probe says so; the build, never a paper, a service or a
  framing page, chooses which server it reads the layer from (`src/pdf-reader/addresses.ts` `READER_API`).
- **Framed, the reader acts only for the content script that made its frame** (`shared/frame-owner.ts`, DESIGN §4.0c):
  with no such content script to vouch for it, it draws nothing and does nothing — no paper fetched, no run started, no
  setting written, whatever its address asks (`ask=translate` included). **Nor does a release build's reader that is no
  frame**: the PDF page only ever frames it, while an arXiv page that learnt its address could send its own tab there
  (Chrome 153 lets that navigation through; Chrome 131 refuses it: measured 2026-10-24), and there the settings alone
  would start a run (`?paper=` and a translated display). A development build, and the
  harness's copy of a release build (the manifest key `axt_top_level_reader`, which `scripts/check-output.mjs` holds no
  build carries; `tests/e2e/lib/extension.mjs`), open it as its address says, for the browser checks and the probes.
- **`?paper=` is an arXiv id or none** (`core/paper-id.ts`, read once by `addresses.ts` `paperOf`): anything else is an
  address with no paper, its card shown, and never a request or a link.
- The demo papers stay reachable by address for the probes and the e2e checks (`?paper=<id>` without `live=1`, the
  probes' form since the prototype), never from the interface.

### 11.2 The engine, moved

- The modules move to `src/pdf-reader/engine/` with their import paths changed and nothing else: `anchors`, `sync`,
  `figures`, `engine`, `mt`, `live`, `latex-front`, `paper-meta`, `scripts`, `tar`, `cache`, `names`, `ocr-worker`.
  They import the extension's source directly; the `lib/axt` shared build goes.
- PDF.js from npm at the version vendored now (6.3.289), pinned, bundled by Vite; its cmaps, standard fonts and wasm as
  static files. Text recognition in figures uses the extension's own.
- `reader.js` is cut along its seams: the viewers, anchoring, sync, overlays and the live pipeline become the engine's
  session module behind the controller; its toolbar, hidden controls, status text and link box go, replaced by the
  React interface. Behaviour changes only where §10 says.

### 11.3 The controller

One typed boundary between the engine and the interface (pdfslick's per-viewer store, adopted): the engine reports a
state the interface subscribes to (`useSyncExternalStore`), and takes commands.

```ts
type Display = 'original' | 'bilingual' | 'translation'
type Side = 'left' | 'right'
interface ReaderState {
  paper: { id: string; title: string }
  display: Display
  available: { bilingual: boolean; translation: boolean } // false: cannot be had (§8), greyed
  phase: 'loading' | 'translating' | 'retranslating' | 'ready' | 'failed'
  progress: number                                         // 0–1, the share of paragraphs done
  failedUnits: number                                      // the notice's {n}
  failure: ProviderErrorKind | null                        // the card's reason, through REASON
  languageSupported: boolean
  finalReady: boolean                                      // 译文 PDF can be downloaded
  scale: number
  sides: Record<Side, { page: number; pages: number }>
  outline: Array<{ id: string; title: string; original: string; level: 1 | 2 | 3; page: number }>
  currentHeading: string | null
}
interface ReaderController {
  getState(): ReaderState
  subscribe(listener: () => void): () => void
  setDisplay(display: Display): void
  zoomTo(to: number | 'page-width' | 'page-fit' | 'page-actual'): void
  pinch(factor: number, origin: { x: number; y: number }): void
  goToPage(side: Side, page: number): void
  goToHeading(id: string): void
  setSync(on: boolean): void
  setSwapped(on: boolean): void
  lead(side: Side): void                                   // a press on a side's indicator makes it the leading side
  retry(): void
  download(which: 'translation' | 'original'): Promise<Blob>
  dispose(): void
}
```

The engine's failure classes (`EngineError`: permanent, isolatable, the service's) map to `ProviderErrorKind` here, so
that the reasons are the popup's. The exact shapes are the plan's to fix; the boundary is this one.

`retry()` on a reader whose session could not open loads the page again, as it first was: there is no session to resume.

### 11.4 Components

`App` · `Toolbar` (`SidebarToggle`, `PaperTitle`, `ArxivLink`; `DisplaySwitch`; `SwapToggle`, `SyncToggle`, `Zoom`,
`LanguageMenu`, `ServiceMenu`, `ReadingOptions`, `DownloadMenu`, `SettingsButton`, `LeaveButton`) · `Outline` · per
pane `PagePill` and `ScrollIndicator` (the engine owns the pane's scroller) · `StatusCapsule` · `FailureCard` ·
`Tooltip`. Popovers and tooltips use the native popover API and CSS anchor positioning (Chrome 131+, as the figure
viewer's control does).

### 11.5 Styling

Tailwind v4, as the popup and the settings page use it, with **the extension's token sheet** (`packages/ui/src/tokens.css`
since the redesign; §4.1) through `@theme inline`, not `ui.css`. PDF.js's viewer sheet with a `box-sizing` reset inside
the viewers (pdfslick's lesson; the highlight offset of 2026-09-22 was ours for want of it).

The panes are laid out by the view's marks (`data-axt-pdf-mode`, `-narrow`, `-swapped`) wherever they are written around
them: the reader package writes them on its root (any element a host opens it on: `<body>` on both hosts' v2 pages), today's
engine on `<html>`; read on `<html>` alone, a host that opened the package's reader on `<body>` showed both panes in every
display (2026-11-07). The original's pane out of the display (the translation's display, side by side in a narrow window) is
laid out at no width and out of sight, as the package's own sheet takes it out (`styles.ts`): it is PDF.js's viewer, which the
reader still fits and scrolls there, and under `display: none` PDF.js had no `offsetParent` to scroll ("offsetParent is not
set -- cannot scroll"); at no width it draws no page. The translation's pane in the original's display stays `display: none`.

A page shown from the back-forward cache: the reader meets a persisted `pagehide` and `pageshow` itself, as it meets the
document's visibility and the browser's online state: away, our server is neither followed nor asked and no timer runs; back,
the document is followed anew, the panes as they were (today's web `session/job.ts putAway`). A `pagehide` that is not
persisted closes the reader, and only that one: the package's one glue of a reader and the chrome's session
(`chrome/open.ts` `openSession`, both hosts; the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-13: a page the browser may restore is never
closed for good). The glue tells the reader's state as the chrome's events (`eventsOf`), runs the chrome's commands, and
takes from a host only what differs: its telling of some events (the website's arXiv HTML link, the extension's crash as a
failure), what it watches, whether the chrome may hold the original, what goes at the page's end.

A settled paper is asked nothing until something says it moved: once the document says nothing runs, the follow waits for the
reader's wake instead of asking again a minute later (design-performance-2026-11-13 Q9; the page shown again, the network back
and the back-forward cache start a new follow by themselves). The wake is an object of the layer answered gone (a 404: our
server replaced the layer and deleted the old one's objects): its head, or a part, which is read as its page comes near, long
after the head (#640 review). Either lets the layer go (`object.refused`) and wakes the follow, once a catalog: the document is
asked again and the layer our server serves now read and laid, no reload; on the extension, whose rows are made here, no follow
lives once its layer is final, and the layer let go is what asks again. A document that still names the catalog gone asks
nothing more. The add-on is not among them yet: read by ranges, a range answered 404 once bytes of it came is the network's
(`bytes/source.ts`), and the layer is refused `broken`, which a retry asks again.

The extension's reader never comes back from the back-forward cache: it is shown only in a frame over arXiv's PDF page
(`entrypoints/pdf.content.ts`), and Chrome does not cache a page that embeds an extension's frame. Its reasons, read through
the DevTools protocol (`Page.backForwardCacheNotUsed`; the page's own `notRestoredReasons` says only `masked` for the frame,
another origin's), measured on Chrome for Testing 153 in 2026-11 by `tests/e2e/reader-v2.mjs`: `SupportPending:EmbedderExtensionFrame`,
`SupportPending:ContainsPlugins`, `Circumstantial:BrowsingInstanceNotSwapped`. The page comes back loaded again, its reader
opened anew. The check keeps the restored branch: a Chrome that caches such a page sends it to the reader's own resume.

Where its host gives no engine, the reader lays with lane L3's typesetter (`packages/reader/src/compose/typeset.ts`):
`layPage` under the rule set's rules for the target the rows are of, the reader's "What to translate" as the rules' `leave`
(a toggle lays the pages again under them), the hyphenation patterns the rules read (our site's `/hyph/<lang>.json`), and the
reader's own Metrics over our site's served faces (`served.ts`: `/static-fonts/index.json`, its groups'
`/static-fonts/<group>.json?fonts=<fonts>`, each slice `/static-fonts/<16 hex>.woff2` fetched as data through the host's
fetch and made a FontFace with its code points as its unicode-range), measured as lane L7's spec says (runs cut where the
slice changes, a CJK run unkerned and cut between two punctuation marks, never in small capitals; held in a browser by
`lab/typeset/metrics-browser.mjs`). The website serves those files from its origin; the extension reads them from our
server's, as today's reader does.

### 11.6 Words

The reader's words go into the locale packs (`zh-CN`, `en`; `zh-TW`, `ja` and `ko` since 2026-11-04) under a new surface in `docs/UI.md`, **R** (`S-R-01` …),
with the popup's where they are the same (§15). Nothing in the reader is hard-coded any more; its status text, English
today, goes.

### 11.7 The reading view: one view for both readers

The engine holds one reading view, `createReaderView(host)` in `engine/view/reader-view.mjs` (exported by `view.mjs`), which
the web's reader and the extension's both run. It imports engine modules only: no extension module and no `pdfjs-dist`.
PDF.js is the host's kit, so every PDF.js type the view names is structural.

- **The host seam** (`ReaderHost`): the two panes' scrollers, PDF.js's kit (its library, `EventBus`, `PDFViewer`,
  `PDFPageView`, `PDFLinkService`, `LinkTarget`, and the `getDocument` options its data files are found by), the words a page
  is named by, the look (`ViewPrefs`: the view reads the highlight's on or off; the panes swapped, dimmed pages and the theme
  are the host's sheet), a link out of the paper, a clock, whether `scrollend` comes, a title where the PDF's metadata has
  none, and one channel for the view's events (`ViewEvent`). The view writes no preference: the display, the sync, a narrow
  window, the zoom and the pinch are commands.
- **The original takes no bytes.** `showOriginal(open)` calls the host's opener once, with the view's own `getDocument`
  options, and owns the task it returns: a newer call supersedes one still loading (its task destroyed, its call
  `'superseded'`), an opener that throws or a task that rejects is `'failed'`, and the call answers `'opened'` once the pages
  are laid out. `dropOriginal(task)` lets go only of the task shown: the places' page views first, then the viewer emptied,
  then the task. `originalData()` reads the bytes through the document.
- **The right pane opens no document.** It holds the places (`places.mjs`): a page box for each of the original's pages,
  sized by the left page box's own style under the left viewer's `--scale-factor`, so that both panes hold the same pages at
  the same places at every zoom with nothing measured. A place near the view (one pane's height above and below) shows the
  best version of its page there is: the layer's content once the layer side has laid it, else the original's page, else,
  with no original, the skeleton. A far place is an empty box: its page goes, canvas and all. The places borrow the left's
  document and never clean its pages up.
  The original's page, while it waits for its layer, is **the left's own drawing of it**: where the two panes scroll together
  (the sync on, both shown), the left draws every page the right shows at the same viewport, so the place takes a copy of the
  left's canvas as the left's page view finishes it (one `drawImage` at its size: the same pixels, shown as PDF.js shows its own
  canvas in a page box of the same size; the host sheet dims it as it dims the left's), and shows PDF.js's loading mark meanwhile,
  as the left's page shows it (its classes mirrored). No second render of the page is made, nor a second text layer or annotation
  layer. A zoom keeps the copy by CSS, as PDF.js keeps its own canvas through a zoom's steps, until the left has drawn the page at
  the new scale, then takes it again; a far place lets it go; one bitmap a place, as its page view held. A page that stays the
  original's (the layer side's word, `places.settle`: it failed, stalled or is arXiv's by the rule, it was laid with nothing of its
  own, the layer was refused, the attempt's rows will not come) and a pane whose pages the left does not show (the sync off, the
  right alone) are drawn by PDF.js's own page view in the place (canvas, text layer, links through the view's jump): there the
  right's page is selected, found and followed as the left's is. Its copy, where it showed one, stays over the page view until
  that is drawn. While a page waits, its text is the left's alone: selection, find, links and a screen reader meet one copy of it.
  On the audit's replays (the rules audit of 2026-11-04, seven prepared papers), the places showing the skeleton instead of a page
  view of their own put page 1 in place 59 ms sooner at 1x and 138 ms at 4x on a returning reader (the second render 48 of those
  59 ms at 1x); the copy is that, with the original's page shown. A paper's form fields, which the right's page view drew into its
  canvas (its annotation mode `ENABLE`) and the left's draws in its annotation layer (`ENABLE_FORMS`), are not on the right while
  it waits.
  A place near the view but not in it that draws its own page view waits to draw it until the layer lets the pages ahead go, or until
  `AHEAD_HOLD_MS` (15 s) after the places are made. The layer lets them go once it puts its first page in place, shows a
  near page as the original's (by the rule, a failure, a stall), is refused or is let go (`letAheadGo`). Its page view is made
  all the same, and a place that comes into view is drawn at once: only when a page is drawn changes, never what. On
  2610.31506v1 in two panes (staging, 2026-10-30), the right's page 3 is near and holds eleven images, 5.5 MB to draw. Drawn
  at once, it read the original 56 times (3.6 MB) from the layer's open to page 1 drawn, on the line page 1's 3.7 MB of font
  slices were waiting on. The web holds PDF.js's own pages ahead on the left alike (its `holdAhead`).
- **The sync is the identity follower** (`sync.mjs` `createFollower`). Both panes hold the same pages, so the other pane moves
  by the reader's own steps (on the compositor, by a ScrollTimeline, where the browser has one) and is levelled at rest by
  the same point of the same page; a click levels the same point at the click's height. It is available once the places
  exist. The web reader's fixes are plain behaviour: the scroll's end by a timer where no `scrollend` comes, no rest while
  a finger is held, a rest an input called off armed again, a glide baked on input, a click's level calling off the rest
  and the timer's end, the pair levelled once a zoom settles.
- **The right zoomed through the left.** A zoom, a fit or a pinch over either pane scales the left's viewer, which the
  places follow; the right shown alone is fitted to its own pane. A step is drawn 400 ms after the last one (one redraw a
  burst), the places' page views with them (a place showing the left's drawing takes it again once the left has drawn it); a pinch is shown by transform and drawn once it is committed (§6.8). A zoom
  and a display's change keep the reading place (the page and
  the point at the reading line); a pinch keeps the point under the gesture on both panes (§6.8).
- **The highlight** (`lighting.mjs`) reads a pane through its shapes alone (`Shapes`, the seam the shapes' PR builds); a
  pointer over a page of either pane is a want of that page. The highlight's layer follows a pinch by transform and is kept
  through PDF.js's redraws (§10.1–§10.2).
- **The layer side's handle** is internal: `internalsOf(view)` (not exported by `view.mjs`) gives the right pane, its places
  and their content swaps, the left's pages, the shapes' seam, the units, and the page-drawn, want, near and original
  listeners. Disposing the view disposes its layer side first, then leaves no listener, observer, animation, document, task,
  place or page view.

The extension's host is `src/pdf-reader/session/host.ts` (`openReader`): the reader on the view since Stage 5 (the compiled
session it replaced is parked, `parked/extension-compile/`), arXiv's PDF shown at the open, always, and the paper's layer
the run's (`session/run.ts`, §11.10). `scripts/check-output.mjs` checks that every build holds the view. A link the view opens
out of the paper is a web page or a mail address, never a script, data or a page of the browser's.
The view's rows are `tests/pdf-reader/reader-view.test.ts` (V1–V14, on PDF.js stand-ins and a clock moved by hand) and
`tests/pdf-reader/reader-view-bundle.test.ts` (a browser build of the view and layer entries reads nothing outside the engine,
no `pdfjs-dist`, and nothing of the server's).

### 11.8 The layer side: one sink for a paper's layer

`createLayerSide(view, options)` (`engine/view/layer-side.mjs`, exported by `view.mjs`) is the reading view's one layer
side. The host tells it what it hears of the paper's layer — refs, rows and their end, from any source, in any order — and
gives it a transport (`fetchObject`, an object by its ref), the base's check (`bind`) and the composed document's opener
(`composed`: the base page, our compile's wrapped by optional content, §19.7, §19.9; parts carry no tails, so it is opened once
for a head, and `composed(null, options)` is the one call). No host calls the door.

- **The feed** (`feed.mjs`) merges what is told, deduplicated by digest, fetches each object once while it is wanted and
  reads it with the format's own readers (cap, digest against its ref, values, shape, chain): the units chunks and the head
  into the index, then the parts in page order against the chain they make. An object's bytes go once it is read (the door
  holds what it reads); a part that waits is not fetched before it joins. A part extends the chain where it begins after
  the last one and names its digest as `prev` (a catalog's part, which names none, by its pages). One beginning at or
  before the last told, under another digest, is a fork, and the chain is reset from its page, where it joins and is heard
  later than every part it lets go (a source that comes late, a 202 made before a job's fork, does not undo it) or those
  are refused. A tell with the parts' end whose parts reach it (the catalog; one of no part at an end of page 0) names the chain
  whole: a part waiting from before it is let go (the same catalog told again keeps those heard since), and no later part
  forks it; one may extend it. A part that does not follow yet waits; one refused stops the chain at the part before it, and is fetched and read
  again when it is told again (an abort of the host's transport is a refusal too). A second head is passed over with one
  warning.
- **The order** (the reader view's contract §2.2): the index read; the base bound, once (false is no layer); the original
  open; the composed document opened with the view's assets, `PDF_OPTIONS` and `disableAutoFetch`, and its one
  optional-content configuration read (`visibilityOf`, below); the door opened over it with the parts read so far; each later
  part added in page order; the rows held until the door opens, then taken; the parts ended once the
  catalog's `through` is added. A fork, a later attempt (`again()`), or parts past the end the door was told (a later
  build's) dispose the door before it is opened again (one open layer a page): `again()` carries no row (the host takes
  its rows again), the others every row so far (the units are the head's). Only the first open waits for the original: a
  dropped original stops no later part, no `again()`. A part the door refuses stops the parts added to that door there,
  with one warning; the side stays open. A refusal of the whole side carries a code (`head`, `units`, `index`, `base`,
  `composed`, `open`).
- **The link layer under a delta.** The delta keeps the original's `/Annots` on a replaced page (about 91 % of its link rectangles
  match ours); the layer draws its own links from the layout (the door's `links`, one wrapper). The composed document's annotation
  layer is rendered nowhere: the side draws the copy canvas, the SVG and that wrapper, never a viewer's annotation layer, and the
  copy is rendered with `AnnotationMode.DISABLE` on a replaced page so that none of the original's appearances are drawn into it.
  `layer-side.test.ts` L18 pins it: no annotation element on a laid page, each link once, all in the wrapper.
- **A page of a part with no layout** (over our base: the engine's check refused the part, or its producer recorded none, a
  part's `layout` null) draws nothing and erases nothing, so its pages would show our base page in other line breaks beside
  arXiv's. What TeX's positions do not draw is arXiv's PDF: such a page (some part holds it and every part that holds it has no
  layout, `noLayoutPage`, a unit running on from the page before can put a page in two parts) is not asked of the door and not
  committed, one the door laid before its parts were all told is not committed, and its place keeps, or returns to after a
  fork, the original's page view. Such a page asked near the view is told the host as settled, never as laid: the `layer`
  events' `original` (and `coverage()`'s), once a page a door, so that a host holding the run's end for the layer's first page
  where the translation shows (the controller's `laying`, the web's) holds it for none of them. 2610.30854v1 (staging, 2026-10-29):
  our compile set its pages 1 to 9 a line apart from arXiv's, the page check drew none of them, and with `laid` alone told the
  end was held while the reader looked at page 1, the progress line on until a page past 9 was laid. Any other head is laid as
  before (it draws nothing: `layerDraws`).
- **The document** is the side's: one composed document a head, destroyed once, at a refusal of the side (its feed's fetches
  with it, and the right's shapes the original's again) or at dispose, once no door reads it (the door's `onRetired`, told at
  the door's dispose). `again()` disposes the door and opens the next over the same document.
- **Each place shows the best version there is** (§11.7): its pre-layer content until the door has laid its page and the
  place is near the view, then the layer's copy (the door's `copyOf(page, { k, width, height, context, annotationMode })`:
  the composed document's page rendered at the place's k, device pixels a PDF unit within 2^24 pixels, on a canvas of the
  place's box at that k, the groups of the units drawn there hidden, below; never a canvas the left or a page view drew,
  at the commit or at a zoom's recopy: one page render a laid page, 10 to 25 ms on the sample; a page of a delta over
  arXiv's PDF, §19.8, is drawn with annotations off where the delta replaces it) and its SVG, put in one task, in place: the place's size and the pane's
  scroll unchanged, its page view destroyed first, no viewer document set. A zoom draws the copies again at the new k
  600 ms after it, nothing laid again; a copy is kept while it is at the scale a copy drawn then would be at. A page this
  door laid that leaves the view takes its drawing out of the document and holds an empty element (retired: the place shows
  no page, and no page view is made of it); a page the door makes ready while it is far is retired at once, and committed
  directly when it comes near. The one exception: a page that holds the focus (a link, or the place a jump gave it to) is
  kept in place as it goes far, and retired once the focus has left it (read a task after the focus moves, never in a
  microtask: a native Tab clears the focus before it arrives at the next link), so at most one far page stays in the
  document, and the focus never falls to the document.
- **The layer's text, at the page's weight** (the maintainer's ruling of 2026-10-29; `engine.css`, `view/text-rendering.mjs`).
  The SVG's text is drawn as PDF.js draws the page's own on its canvas. Two settings had drawn it lighter on macOS, and both
  had to go: the `-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased` the reader's page sets for its chrome (inherited), and
  `text-rendering: geometricPrecision`, which Chromium on macOS draws without the system's smoothing whatever the smoothing
  says. Measured (Chromium 153, macOS, device pixel ratio 2, the same Chinese line in Source Han Serif SC Regular at 11.96
  px): PDF.js 7,327 units of ink, a canvas's `fillText` 7,326, the SVG with both 5,870 (80 %), with neither 7,326; over a
  page of 2608.16117v1, Chinese and German, 79 and 80 %, and the same in the dark (79 %). WebKit (Playwright's 26.6, macOS)
  draws geometricPrecision at full weight and only the smoothing mattered (77 % with it). So the layer's SVG takes the
  browser's own smoothing everywhere (a no-op where there is none to take), and `text-rendering: auto` where the browser
  lays a line out alike under both: geometricPrecision is there so that a word's glyphs advance as the engine measured them
  on a canvas, and Chromium on Linux (headless, device pixel ratio 1 and 2 alike, fontconfig's hinting ignored for web
  fonts) lays `auto` out on whole-pixel advances, up to 4.5 CSS px off over a page of German (mean 0.59), while there
  geometricPrecision costs no weight (within 4 % of the canvas either way). The test is the browser's, not the platform's, and
  it is the layer's own words that tell, in its own faces: a face the system holds is laid out with fractional advances under
  both on Linux too, where the web fonts the layer draws in are not (a first probe in the system's serif took `auto` there,
  and moved the page's letters by the 4.5 px above). At the commit of the first laid page that offers words drawn from one
  place each (a Latin word: one x, its glyphs advancing as the browser lays them; a CJK run has an x a character, which no
  rendering moves), the layer side lays up to 24 of them out again off the view, at the layer's scale, in their faces, sizes
  and tracking, under each rendering, before the page is painted; `auto` is taken where every glyph's advance within a word
  agrees within 0.05 CSS px (macOS's differ by a 64th of a pixel at two sizes; a whole-pixel advance by up to half a pixel)
  over at least 16 fractional ones, once a document, written on `<html>` as `data-axt-layer-text="auto"`, which `engine.css`
  reads; anything else keeps geometricPrecision, and a page that tells too little (no such words, or a monospaced face whose
  advances are whole) leaves it to the next. It is decided before the page is put in place (its words' faces read with its drawing
  held where nothing is laid out, `display: none`): decided after, the attribute restyled the page the commit's own reads had just
  laid out, and the task that paints page 1 laid it out twice: with the marks' paddings read once (below), page 1's commit task
  and the frame that shows it are 8 to 10 ms shorter at 1x CPU and 36 to 43 ms at 4x (traced replays of seven prepared papers,
  2026-11-04; the task's layout 25-28 to 17-20 ms at 1x, 117 to 75-86 at 4x). Measured (`lab/pdf/spikes/layer-text-check.mjs`, every character of a page
  against geometricPrecision): Chromium on Linux (Docker, device pixel ratio 1 and 2) keeps geometricPrecision, its places
  unchanged; Chromium on macOS takes `auto`, every character of four papers' twelve pages (16,528) within 0.17 CSS px of where
  geometricPrecision put it (mean 0.007; the ends of long words), at zooms of 0.75 to 3 and device pixel ratios of 1 and 2;
  WebKit takes `auto`, its places the same to the pixel. Not yet seen by eye: Chrome on Windows, a Linux desktop, Safari on
  iOS (which has no smoothing to restore).
  The reader package (`packages/reader`) decides by the same test, once a reader and before its first overlay is drawn, from
  a fixed probe rather than a page's words (`compose/text-rendering.ts`): a pangram at 9, 10 and 12 points, laid out again
  under each rendering in a served Latin face loaded for it (Computer Modern's serif, `axt-cmun-serif`; a host's own faces,
  the table's first face read from a file), asked as the pages are first to be laid and awaited by every overlay; written on
  the reader's root (`.axt-reader`, its sheet `styles.ts`); where the face cannot be had, geometricPrecision. Decided by the
  first page that told, a page of few Latin words told nothing (2610.40645v1's page 1 in Japanese: 10 such runs, 12
  advances), so that page was drawn at 80 % of its ink until a later page told and then every page flipped, and the weight a
  page was shot at hung on the order the pages were laid (the owner's question of 2026-11-08).
  It draws a run that names no fill of its own in the layer's ink, the PDF's own black (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-08:
  today's `layer-proto/run.mjs` `SVG_RULES` draws `#141414`, the approved prototype's ink, whose darkest pixel is 92 % of
  black's, so that the translation stood lighter than the original's text on every page; a run's own fill is kept), but a
  CJK run, which it draws in `#141414`, today's ink (the owner's exception of the same day, on the lane's measurement that
  this ink was the one difference between today's CJK text and v2's: the same faces, sizes, smoothing and rendering, 0.922 of
  black's ink a glyph). A CJK run is one whose characters are of the breaker's CJK class (`script.ts` `cjkClassRe`: Han,
  kana, Hangul, Bopomofo, the CJK marks and full-width forms, and the curly quotes, dashes, ellipsis and middle dot where the
  rules set them as CJK's), the class it was set in the CJK face by; typeset's `emit/display.ts` `inkLines` inks every laid
  line of a page (units, names, figure texts) with `CJK_INK`, so the Page states it as the run's fill and the painter writes
  it; the translation's Latin, digits and formulas stay in the PDF's black. Measured against the original's body text (mean
  darkness of glyph pixels, 42 pages of the 21 CJK pairs, macOS Chromium at a device pixel ratio of 2): beside Times-like
  originals the CJK text in `#141414` is 0.911 of the original's darkness (0.978 in black), beside Computer Modern 0.996
  (1.071 in black).
  Without the smoothing and `auto` (the maintainer's report of 2026-11-08, 1706.03762v7 in Chinese, page 1) it drew the
  translation at 80 % of its own `auto` ink, in pure black: 86 % of today's ink on the abstract's first line (4,305 against
  4,982 units at a device pixel ratio of 2), 92 % on the bold title; with them 4,989 and 100 %. Held by the harness's check
  (`packages/reader/e2e/run.mjs`, "at the weight a canvas draws it"): every measured line's ink within 6 % of the same runs
  drawn by a canvas's `fillText`, 0.80 before, 1.00 after.
- **No flash coming back** (the owner's goal of 2026-10-24: a page already seen never shows the original, or an empty place,
  before its translation, coming back to it). A retired page's drawing — its copy, its SVG and its links, detached — is kept off the view,
  and put back in its place in the same task as the page comes near again (`bringBack`), one pane height before it can be
  seen: no ask, no copy drawn, the right's shapes the page's own. The drawings are kept within the device's budget
  (`keepBudget`): a 64th of its memory (`navigator.deviceMemory`, 4 GB where the browser does not say) at 4 bytes a pixel, at
  least two of its screens' pixels, at most `KEEP_PIXELS`, 2^25 pixels (128 MiB), and on iOS and iPadOS at most
  `IOS_KEEP_PIXELS`, 2^23 (32 MiB: its WebKit tells no memory and kills a tab past its process's limit; until Safari 17 it also
  refused a canvas past a page-wide canvas cap of about 200 MB on an iPhone SE, WebKit bug 195325, which WebKit PR 14375 removed;
  32 MiB beside the near pages' copies stays under a third of the lowest cap reported); past it the drawing farthest from the
  view goes first. A copy costs its pixels: an A4 page at 120 % on a 2x screen is 1905 × 2694 pixels, 19.6 MiB of the GPU process's
  memory in Chromium 153 on Metal (an `ImageBitmap` of it no less; the probe of 2026-10-24). So a computer of 8 GB keeps six and
  a half such pages, nine at 100 %, twelve at the reader's fit (two thirds of what the left pane's PDF.js holds of its own at
  that zoom, its ten page views drawn), and a phone of 4 GB 64 MiB, some ten pages of its screen at the fit. A page let go past
  it is laid again from the door's kept markup as before. A drawing kept across a zoom comes back as it was and is drawn again
  at the new k. A later attempt, a fork or another target lets every kept drawing go (they are the door before's), as do
  `dropOthers()`, a refusal and the dispose. A host may give its own budget (`keepPixels`; 0 keeps none). The reader package's
  page stack keeps the drawing in its own slot instead of detached, and out of the layout tree as today's is out of the
  document: the slot marked `data-axt-kept` while its drawing is kept, its holder `display: none` (`packages/reader` stack.ts
  `keep`, styles.ts). Kept in layout, every laid page of a paper was laid out again at each face added to the document (a face
  added re-lays every text node laid out): over a scroll of 2610.20808v1 41 such relayouts of 10k to 41k objects, the longest
  134 ms, most of the reader's long tasks (lane reader-perf, 2026-11-12, `verification/reader-perf.md` §1); out of it, the
  relayouts walk the near pages and the left's (15.6k objects, as today's 16k), and Blink's heap holds 147 MiB less after that
  scroll. `display: none` rather than `content-visibility: hidden`: the same relayouts measured, no layout objects kept, and
  every browser the website serves has it (`content-visibility` only from Safari 18). The slot keeps its box, so the pane's
  height and the sync's places never move; what changed while the drawing was out (a zoom, a face) is laid out as it comes
  back, one pane height before it shows, and a zoom's page view is drawn again then. A jump straight to a kept page (a link,
  the outline, a page number) puts it back in the jump's own frame, in the stack's frame callback on the pane's scroll, before
  that frame is laid out and painted: the near observer tells it only in a task after the frame, which would show the bare page
  box for a frame. A pinch's preview, a transform the near observer is held through, holds every kept drawing in layout while
  it is held, out again at its end where still far. A kept page's words are not found by the
  browser's find while it is far, as today's are not (the coordinator's word, 2026-11-12: equal to production is the bar).
  Held by the harness's check "a far laid page kept out of the layout tree, back pixel for pixel, the scroll height unmoved".
  **A kept page holds one bitmap** (design-performance-2026-11-13 Q7): its page view's. Its crops canvas, page-sized so that the
  compositor draws it as it draws the page view, holds a few formulas' pixels on most pages; kept, it let every laid page hold a
  second page of pixels (2610.20808v1 and 2610.40645v1 after a scroll: 27 and 35 of them, 62.6 and 74.3 MiB; the GPU process
  595-605 and 658 MiB against 420-433 with them let go, lane crops-probe, 2026-11-13). As the page is kept, the smallest box of
  whole device pixels that holds where its crops are drawn (`packages/reader` paint.ts `cropsBox`) is copied one to one into a
  canvas of its own that is never in the document and is read by the CPU (`willReadFrequently`), and the crops canvas's bitmap
  is let go (`cropsAway`); as the page comes back, in the task that puts it back into the layout tree (the jump's own frame or
  the near observer's), the canvas is made page-sized again and the copy drawn at its place, one to one (`cropsBack`): the page
  comes back as it left, the same canvas and the same pixels, alpha included, no crop render made. A canvas cut to the box and
  shown so (lane reader-perf's C) is not taken: Chromium composites a layer of another size differently, 14 of the harness's 37
  shots unlike though the canvas's own pixels were identical (lane crops-probe). Where no copy fits (the scale moved while the
  page was far) the crops are drawn anew (`cropsAgain`) and the page goes back into the layout tree once they are in: never
  shown without them, nor with the old scale's. The budget counts what a kept page holds: its page view and its copy.
  Held by the same check (the crops canvas 0 × 0 while far, the budget, the canvas in the jump's frame equal to what it held,
  no crop drawn again; after a zoom while far, the crops at the new grid as the page goes back) and paint.test.ts.
- **The faces, in one wave** (`layer-proto/warm.mjs`). v0 checks and loads the faces of a unit as it lays it, one unit after
  another (E2), so a page whose units brought new characters waited a round trip a unit: 2602.23285v2 in Chinese asked 38
  font files in 12 waves before its first page, 4.3 to 9.2 s of a cold visit (production, 2026-10-24). The side asks the
  slices of what v0 will draw of the near pages at once, the page in the middle of the view first (page 1 alone until a page
  is shown, the others after it), as soon as the index, their rows and the parts that locate them are in (before the
  composed document is open): each unit's translation in the style its lines are set in on the page (their most common font
  by width, formulas aside, as v0 takes its original's most common class; a heading the layout tells no font of in the
  bold), an author's unit never (v0 never draws one; on 2602.23285v2's page 1 its names alone took 16 slices, 1.7 MB, where
  the units drawn take 1.4 MB), the page's babel names in the target's words, the alphabet slice of each text font the page
  is set in, and on page 1 the faces v0 warms there (`warmFaces`). CJK characters go by the rules' class to the CJK face,
  the rest to the style's Latin face; the paper's family is read from the parts' layouts (each font weighted by the lines
  set in it; the same family page 1's characters give on the seven papers of the gate pack). The slices are loaded
  `WAVE_SLOTS` (4) at a time: the edge answers a connection's streams side by side whatever their priority (staging,
  2026-10-24: a High fetch beside 28 slices loaded as fonts, VeryHigh, ended in 175 to 470 ms, as beside 28 asked Low or
  High), so a wave of 28 slices in flight held each read of the original the composed document makes, one after another,
  to a share of the line in 29. v0's checks are unchanged: they find the slices loaded or loading, and a run the wave did
  not foresee (a bold word in a paragraph, a character only the original's text holds) asks its own as before. A slice is
  asked once. The reader package's served faces (`packages/reader` served.ts `addIn`) add the slices one ask needs to the
  document together, in one stretch once every one of them is in, and a slice counts as loaded for the typesetter's measure
  only from then on: Chromium re-lays every text node laid out at each change of the document's fonts ("Fonts changed"), and
  a slice added as it came made 41 and 48 such whole-document relayouts a scroll of 2610.20808v1 and 2610.40645v1, today's
  reader 22 and 25 (it adds a wave's faces in one task; lane reader-perf, 2026-11-12, `verification/reader-perf.md` §3f). An
  ask is one page's (the composer asks each page's faces apart, the page in the middle first), so a page still never waits for
  another page's slices, and none is measured or drawn with a fallback face. A slice that comes in for an ask whose page went
  meanwhile is added all the same, ready for the next ask.
  Before any part, the first page's CJK slices are asked early (`firstPageUnits`, `warmEarly`). On a first open the rows come
  while the box runs and its head and parts at the end, so the page's wave began only with part 1 and its slices were the
  page's last wait: on staging (2e627695, 2026-10-30) the door made page 1 ready 40 to 110 ms after its last slice came in all
  twelve visits probed, 10 to 77 slices, 0.4 to 4.4 MB at about 1.6 MB/s. Now the units' kinds are read from the units chunks
  told at the compile (the feed's `kinds`), and the rows the host reads before any part (its deltas, `warmEarly`, or rows taken
  between the head and part 1) give the units' texts. The estimate is the units in id order, an author's aside, up to
  `FIRST_PAGE_CHARS` (800) CJK characters, and the author block's places whatever their ids. Their CJK characters are asked
  alone (`cjkOnly`), in the target's CJK face, which is the same whatever the paper's family, and each with no style (a
  heading's in the bold). On seven papers in Chinese the estimate's slices held 100 % of page 1's CJK bytes on four, 90 and
  92 % on two, and 55 % on the seventh, whose abstract is set in bold. It asked 0 to 1.07 MB (median 0.39) of slices page 1
  does not draw. Nothing is asked early once a part is read, or where a catalog tells the parts' end with its parts (a cached
  translation's first page has its own wave at once).
- **Translating** (the owner's "Field", 2026-10-25, in his "Glint", 2026-11-01). While a near page is not laid, its place
  shows the original's page, and each paragraph the parts read so far locate on it carries a mark over its box, showing its
  own share of one diagonal light that crosses the whole page. The light is one picture three pages wide in the page's frame
  (the page's overlay is a size container), and each mark clips its own slice of it: one page wide, the picture's middle third,
  where the band lies on any page up to about twice as tall as it is wide, and as high as the mark, set in the page's frame by
  the mark's place, so the light is one surface whatever the paragraphs. A transform moves each slice across the page, so the
  compositor runs the pass: nothing is restyled, laid out or painted on the page's thread while it runs. Each mark's pass
  starts when its page's indicator did (its `startTime` set, Web Animations, in the frame after its marks came, before it paints:
  the marks stand in a size container, whose style waits on its layout, so `markPage` reads none of it, and reads the card's
  padding once a document on `<html>`), so a mark a later
  batch of rows brings shows its share of the same light, not a pass of its own. The light passes through the glyphs and
  leaves the paper untouched: a band at 100° of the paper's own colour, 78 % at its middle (80 % on a dimmed page), fading to
  nothing over a tenth of the three-page picture on either side, over no ground, so that the letters it crosses fade toward
  the paper and nothing else changes. A mark shows after 300 ms (a fast page shows none) and fades in over 0.4 s; a pass
  takes 3.4 s, its last 20 % a pause. A mark stands out from its paragraph by 4 CSS pixels inline and 2 block, with 4-pixel
  corners, at the reader's 100 %, scaled with the page so a zoom keeps it in proportion; each side's padding is at most half
  the gap to the nearest mark beside it, so no two marks meet. The Field's first look was Graphite (2026-10-25: a faint graphite card, 14 by 4
  pixels out from its paragraph, which the light cleared); the owner chose Glint on 2026-11-01, having seen both on the
  reader's own pages, a Glint with no margin and its still state lighter: 「不带边距的 glint」，「用 Glint，减少动态那一态调淡一些」.
  The band is laid as it is, with no blend mode. The overlay is a stacking context (its z-index), an isolated group, so a
  mark's own blend mode mixes with nothing but the overlay's empty ground: in the reader on 2026-11-01 a white mark with
  `difference` drew the same pixels as a plain white one, and the same blend on the overlay inverted the page. A band of the
  paper's colour laid normally gives the pixels that Glint's first sketch blended for, `screen` with white on a white page and
  `darken` with the paper's colour on a dimmed one, within one level of luminance, with no blend to composite. Its cost is
  Graphite's (the reader on the sample's waiting page, Chromium 153 on an Apple M4 Pro at 2x, three 5-second traces each):
  1.36 ms of the main thread a frame against Graphite's 1.39 with 10 marks, 7.4 against 7.7 ms with 16 marks under a CPU
  four times slower, no frame dropped in any run; a blend on the overlay would have doubled the frame's draw (0.13 ms against
  0.07), the only difference it made.
  Until 2026-11-01 the pass was a registered property animated on the page's overlay, and the main thread restyled and
  repainted every mark at every frame, while the same thread lays the page the reader waits on. In the reader at 4x, on the
  sample's first page (10 marks; nine interleaved runs each, medians and the middle half), page 1 went in place 363 ms (355
  to 367) after its rows were let go with the light moving, against 297 (290 to 307) with the marks still and 294 (285 to 298)
  with none: 66 ms later, a tenth of it in the lay and the rest before the rows reached the layer, on the same thread. On the
  compositor, with the look the same pixel for pixel (within one level in light and dark at three points of the pass, the
  still marks identical), a frame's work on the main thread with the light moving is 0.79 ms at 4x where it was 4.71 (its
  style 0.37 where it was 2.81, no paint where it was 0.75), the main thread busy 81 ms a second where it was 318, and the
  GPU 3.6 where it was 37; at 1x, 0.25 ms a frame where it was 1.39. Each slice is a layer of the compositor's: the reader's
  tiles hold 10 MB more than the marks painted with the page did (48.7 MB against 38.3 at 2x), where slices three pages wide
  and a page high had held 67 MB more. The light moving no longer delays page 1: over 22 rounds alternating the two builds on
  a busy machine, it had put page 1 in place a median 24 ms later than still marks (later in 14 rounds of 22), and now 10 ms
  sooner (later in 9). The compositor draws a frame only where the light changes something on screen, at the display's
  rate: none while the band is off the page at either end of its pass, where the registered property's light had drawn
  every frame.
  Every value of the look is a custom property of `engine.css` (`--axt-tr-*`: the ground, the light and its shoulders and
  where they stand, the angle, the blend, a filter, the mark's padding and corner, the still mark, the pass and its easing,
  the delay and the fade; a light of another shape sets `--axt-tr-image` and `-size`), so that a look is a change of values,
  no code. The light lies over the mark's ground (a light that cleared its ground, as Graphite's did, would be a picture of
  its own). With reduced motion asked, and where the browser cannot size a container (before Firefox 110 and Safari 16), the
  mark is still: a veil of the paper over
  the paragraph, 10 % (14 % on a dimmed page), `--axt-tr-still`, which a look with no ground needs (the ground alone would show
  no mark at all). It lightens the letters by 26 levels of luminance at most (28 dimmed), where Graphite's still ground moved
  them by 10 (11): a page that waits, calmly; the 30 % of Glint's sketch moved them by 76 (59), and the owner asked for less.
  The marks sit at the paragraph's box in shares of the page, so no zoom moves them, above the page and
  under the pointer (no pointer events, hidden from assistive technology). A page is laid whole, through its page pass, the
  moment its rows and slices are in (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-10-24: pages, never a unit drawn on a provisional fit
  that later moves), and all its marks go in the same task its drawing is put in place. An author's unit has none (it is
  never drawn), nor has a paragraph whose rows ended with no row of it, nor has a page that failed (the original's).
- **The pages ahead** (the prefetch on the layer). Once the rows of the attempt have ended (a host that translates as it shows
  is asked for nothing it has not translated), the door is open, the right pane is shown and the document visible, the side
  lays the `AHEAD_PAGES` (2) pages past the near ones the way the reader moves, while the reader scrolls as at rest, and draws
  each at its place's k into a drawing kept off the view: the reader reaching it finds it put back at once, never arXiv's page
  first. The way the reader moves is read from the near places alone (an IntersectionObserver's run, no layout read in the
  scroll's path): the edge of the run that moved past where it was, down by default; a run that shares no page with the one
  before (a jump) reads on forward. The window is read again once its pages are laid, so a reader who moves on moves it, and a
  run whose pages are no longer ahead, or that lays the other way, is given up. It is background work, by the lesson of
  `WAVE_SLOTS` above (work the reader is not waiting on must not take the line or the thread from a page the reader is waiting
  on). The window is begun once the near places have stayed where they are `AHEAD_SETTLE_MS` (150 ms: a page of a steady
  scroll comes near every half second or so, a fling's every tenth), in a turn of the main thread at background priority
  (`scheduler.postTask`'s `background`, run once nothing of a higher priority waits; a task where the browser has no
  scheduler), and only while the view's own pages hold nothing: no near page asked of the door or being put in place, and none
  PDF.js is drawing, on the left or as the original's in its place. Its pages' faces are asked in one wave and its pages of
  the door at once, the nearest laid first, as the near pages are; each copy is drawn in a background turn of its own. A page
  of the view asked gives the run up at once (its wave's slices not begun, its asks, its copy under way), and the run begins
  again once the view's pages are in place or drawn. A page the
  door had begun to lay for the run is laid all the same, once (a page told `laying` never goes back; the view's ask overtakes
  it, the door's `OVERTAKEN`), and a wave stopped before its end asks its page's faces again next time. A scroll gives nothing
  up. A page come near as the door answers it is left to the view's own ask, which puts it in place under the door's hold as
  any near page; one whose lay or copy fails, that draws nothing of the layer, or whose drawing the keep budget cannot hold (a
  page past it, or a window wider than it), is not laid ahead again by the same door, so a window that stays is not drawn
  again and again. A host may lay none (`ahead: 0`).
  Until 2026-11-01 the pages ahead were laid only once the view had rested 600 ms (`AHEAD_IDLE_MS`: no scroll, nothing asked,
  the last near page committed), and a scroll gave the window up: a reader who kept scrolling never had them. On staging
  (2026-11-01, the comparison with hjfy.top's reader on 1706.03762v7 and 2501.14787v1), 2 of the 10 right pages of a steady
  10-page scroll first showed arXiv's page, the translation 49 to 1,052 ms after it came into view, and up to 4.2 s (p95) with
  the CPU four times slower. Three things were measured on the way, offline: the web's reader at next (5d1a5dcf) against the
  same with this change, the web's played-run stand-in serving a staged layer and the font slices, the comparison's own probe
  and scroll (Playwright's Chromium, 1440 × 900 at a pixel ratio of 2, a fresh profile a run, a steady scroll of 10 pages at
  1,500 px/s, its rest, then a fling of 2,600 px), the link shaped by the browser, every run begun with the machine's load
  under 20. An idle callback is no turn for it: Chromium gives a page no idle period while the reader scrolls, and
  `requestIdleCallback`, asked as the scroll began, fired only once it had ended (6 s), so the window laid nothing while it was
  needed. One page at a time, each after its whole faces' wave, a page took its round trips in a row, longer than a page of the
  scroll on a slow link. And a window laid while the left drew the pages a fling brought into view kept the left's page 14 of
  1706.03762v7 blank 392 and 489 ms, against 158 and 163 with none laid; a page PDF.js is drawing holding the window, 232 to 312
  ms against 100 to 174 (the window begun as the fling's pages came near, its lay beside the left's drawing of the page the
  fling stopped on); the settle as well, 158 to 192 against 159 to 226: as before. Until the window also waited for a near
  place drawing the original's page (the places' own drawing, `places.drawing`: the slot `view(n)` the side first read holds
  no page view, so that check held nothing), it cost the fast link at 1x, where nothing is gained, some 8 ms at p95 on every
  frame of the scroll and 1.4 to 1.6 % of the compositor's frames dropped; with it, nothing measurable.
  With all of it (2026-11-02, 1706.03762v7 in Chinese, 15 pages; the before 5d1a5dcf, the after 2c506199 and 5cec45df, which
  differ by the retry a task after a page is drawn alone; four runs each, interleaved, at loads of 6 to 20): on a slow link
  (150 ms, 10 Mbit/s) at 1x, 3 of the 10 right pages first showed arXiv's page before in every run, for 53 to 502 ms, and none
  after; with the CPU four times slower on a fast link (40 ms, 40 Mbit/s), 6 of 10 before in every run (415 to 1,390 ms) and
  4 or 5 after (294 to 1,252 ms), the main thread then too short for the view's own pages to leave a turn; on the fast link at
  1x none either way. On 2602.23285v2 (19 pages, figures of several MB) on the slow link, 3 of the 7 pages the layer lays
  showed arXiv's page for 684 to 1,128 ms before, 2 for 76 and 119 ms after (one run each, an earlier build). No cost was
  measured on what is in view: during the scroll's gesture the main thread's frames took 34 to 37 ms at p95 after, 34 to 46
  before, on the fast link at 1x (the frames over 50 ms 1 to 8 of some 310 after, 4 to 11 before; the longest task 56 to 64
  ms after, 61 to 68 before; the compositor's dropped frames 0 to 0.6 % either way); 34 to 47 after and 34 to 35 before on the
  slow link; at 4x 146 to 231 after and 167 to 262 before, the thread full either way. A left page blank on the fling: 49 to
  568 ms after and 50 to 541 before at 1x, 214 to 784 after and 167 to 709 before at 4x. The bytes fetched during the gesture
  and during the rest are the same as before at both links (1.56 MB and 1.34 MB over 1706.03762v7's scroll): the pages ahead
  move what is fetched no earlier than the near pages did, and the two pages past the stop are fetched in the rest, as the
  window waits while the view's last pages are drawn. Three pages ahead (`ahead: 3`, an earlier build) left 1 and 5 of 10 at
  4x, the same none on the slow link, for 0.45 MB more at the stop and as much more kept: not taken.
  On a delta head the composed document reads the original's own source, so a page laid ahead reads the original's bytes of
  that page into the store the left reads: on 2602.23285v2 the left's pages 5 to 7 were no longer blank as they came into view
  (an earlier build, which did not wait for the places' drawing).
