## 17. The highlight

The hover highlight (the reading options' switch, S-P-80) as built on `exp/pdf-highlight` (its plan, with its record at the end:
`git show exp-freeze-2026-10-07:experiments/pdf-bilingual/plans/2026-10-01-pdf-highlight.md`): what lights and how it looks, where its shapes come from, and
what it costs. Every number is from the ten papers of the highlight's investigation (`data/runs/highlight-ten`: arXiv's
PDF on the left, our Chinese typesetting on the right), investigator B's four papers of the ground truth
(`data/runs/highlight-gt`) and the demo papers. The counts are one run of the Node gate, `lab/pdf/spikes/highlight-gate.mjs`, on
2026-10-02 at the head of the final review's fix round, and the costs one run of the browser gate's,
`lab/pdf/spikes/highlight-gate-browser.mjs costs`, that day (§17.6); what another probe measured carries its own date.

### 17.1 What lights

- **The pointer lights; nothing else does.** Hovering a sentence lights it and its translation on both sides; hovering
  a unit that lights whole lights it whole on both. A click holds nothing — the pin drawn in the draft round was
  dropped by the maintainer on 2026-10-01 after a test build; a click only levels the two panes by what lies under it
  (anywhere inside what the highlight paints is its unit's; a float's body levels by what is around it).
- **Sentences**, where a unit's sentences are known on both sides; else **the whole unit** (paragraph, theorem,
  footnote, list item, caption), decided for both sides together — a unit never lights by sentence on one side and whole
  on the other. A unit of one sentence lights as a sentence shape (its first row from where its text begins).
- **One light map for both panes** (the owner, 2026-10-30: 「请确保我们一定要从最底层、最长期、最通用的方式去解决」): every block
  TeX sets as text or math lights, the same block on both panes; graphics, and a figure's own labels, never. A block's members are
  the maker's own boxes of it on our page, which the parts' layouts carry already (each unit's `lines`, its placeholders' segments
  `ph`, its `labels`: `layout/file.mjs`, TeX's ownership by its marks, `layout/own.mjs`), and each pane resolves them to its own
  tokens. The right (our page) lights what the door drew of the block and what it kept of our page's ink there
  (`layer-proto/hide.mjs` `unitHiding`'s `shown`, written into the page's word table by `words.mjs` `addUnitWords`; a unit the layer
  shows as the original's by its own boxes, `addBoxWords`, no longer by copies of the left's tokens, which it had none of where
  the left did not locate it). The left (arXiv's page) lights what its left part locates and, where the page is *in place* (90 % of
  our page's lines hold a token of arXiv's at their middle row: our compile set it as arXiv's), the tokens under the block's boxes
  (`view/shapes.mjs` `createShapes`: only tokens no span holds, which is where the left part and TeX's marks disagree for 86
  tokens of 800 000 on the 54 papers below; a label or a kept piece that has no text token, a bullet TeX draws as a mark, widens
  its unit's row instead, `highlight.mjs` unitRuns). So:
  - **A display formula is a block of its own**, paired on both panes, its equation numbers included: one display placeholder of
    a unit (an equation, an align of several lines, every segment of it) one block, lit whole, under an id of its own
    (`units.mjs` `displayBlockId`: the unit's id and the display's place among its unit's, so that the door and the view number it
    alike). Its tokens are never its unit's, on either pane (a kept line on its rows is its ink, `words.mjs`; on the left it takes
    its own unit's tokens and the free ones in its segments, never another unit's: an array's cells set in a display keep theirs;
    and those of its unit's between two of its own in the page's stream whose box meets one of its segments, as TeX sets a
    display's glyphs together (never one in the room between them: a paragraph's word there, an align's \intertext, stays). arXiv's text layer draws a token's box from its font's ascent and descent, and a math extension
    font's (cmex10's, txexs's) hang under the baseline: a wide accent's box stands under its ink, a big delimiter's reaches far past
    it, its middle out of the segments. 2610.35877v1 p5's hat on the w of display (4)'s denominator, 1.9 pt under the display,
    had lit with the sentence before it, a band in the formula, the owner's report of 2026-10-31. On the 70 papers of #524's
    measure, 3 648 displays: 10 such glyphs in 7 displays of 5 papers, now 0). Our page's drawing meets the same glyph as a kept
    line: the layer reads a unit's lines as bands about their baselines (`tex.mjs` texRects), and the file sets a math extension
    glyph's baseline at the top of its ink, so a line of a display's ∑ had its band 12 to 24 pt over the display and stayed its
    paragraph's, lit with the sentence before it (2610.42112v1 p34's display (54)-(55), p4's LSE, the owner's report of
    2026-11-03). The word table tells a kept line on a display's rows by the file's own box of the line (`layer2.mjs` keptLines'
    `fileTop`, `fileBottom`), the boxes the left's inventory reads (`shapes.mjs` takeInventory): over the release sweep's 53
    papers, 210 such lines in 194 of 3 016 displays (26 papers), now 0.
    Its unit lights around it, and a sentence across it lights whole, every piece of it, as across a column or a page break (the
    owner: 「第 1 条就用这个，推进吧」). Inline math stays in its sentence.
  - **A display at its unit's edge is a block of its own too** (the owner's report of 2026-11-02 on 2501.14787v1 p24: the display
    before "In order to understand why …" lit with that sentence on arXiv's pane and with nothing on ours). A paragraph that opens
    with `\[ … \]` after a blank line gets no point before its start mark (`layout/marks.mjs` `headEnd`: a mark there, in vertical
    mode, would begin a paragraph of its own), so the maker left the display LOST and OUTSIDE, no box of it in the light map: the
    left part, which locates the unit by its text and its lead, kept the display's tokens in the unit's span, lit with its first
    sentence, the stop after its matrix too; our page's ink of it, in no group, lit nothing but the kept blocks the ink units had cut
    of its lines with letters (three there, each lit alone on both panes). TeX ships such a display right before the start mark,
    in the paragraph it begins: what the start's region holds from that paragraph's point (`q<n>`) or the mark before to the start
    mark is its ink, but the line before that point, the start's own line and a label of a name above it all ("Theorem 5.",
    "Proof.", which `\everypar` sets on the paragraph's first line), and none where no point stands before the start mark on its
    page (a display TeX broke over the page) (`layout/stream.mjs` `headInk`, asked by the unit's start mark: `marks.mjs`
    `headsOf`; a babel name inside the display is the display's). The maker reads it as
    any display's (its segments), and the wrap gives it to its unit for the ledger alone (`own.mjs` `leads`), so that no ink unit
    nor kept block is made of it; its glyphs stay in no group, never erased, as before. A display past its unit's end mark that runs
    to a later unit's opening the maker now finds as the erasure did (2610.20595v1 p19u153, hidden with its unit's placeholders
    and LOST in the layout before). Over 66 local papers (the gate pack's 7 among them, the production pass on both engines over the
    same compiles, `readarxiv-lab-data/hl-display-14787`): 22 of the 24 such displays found, on 9 papers, every other placeholder row
    of every unit as it was; 19 ink units gone, 17 kept blocks and 2 orphans translated over a display (2610.22299v1 p1's
    `\text{any two adjacent vertices …}` inside its equation, drawn translated over the formula), none made. On the left, as the
    reader makes it, a point at the middle of each of the 22 displays' 44 segments lit its unit 36 times, a kept block 7 and an
    orphan once, and now the display's own block 44 times; on ours the door shows each found display under its hover id, as any
    display. The text after one that opens its unit still opens the unit's first line, as after one drawn as nothing: a mark the
    reply sets after the display's marker that no line may start with is drawn without it, unless the original's line there opens
    with one (`layer2.mjs` `finishUnit`, `inPlace`: a display whose segments hold none of its unit's lines' characters; the
    drawing's rule for the text after a display, the maintainer's fix 4 of 2026-10-15). The source sets no mark there
    (`\end{equation}` and "which will now be …", "where …", "with …"); Microsoft's Chinese writes a full-width comma (U+FF0C) after the marker, as its
    clause after a formula. Between #550 and this rule the release sweep of 5e519d69 found four texts drawn opening with it
    (2610.20595v1 u24, u25, u47; 2307.16209v1 u459): of the 23 paragraph-head displays of the 66 papers (21 found, 2 still
    OUTSIDE), those four are every one whose zh reply sets a mark after the display's marker, each now drawn without it, and
    every other unit on their papers' pages drawn as before. Left as they were: two edge displays whose ink the stream cannot tell (2610.19274v1 u110's on the page before its
    unit's start mark; 2610.20595v1 u31's after the display before it, whose opening point alone runs to that start mark), and 7
    displays inside their units the maker finds no ink of (LOST), each unit the original's, lit with it on both panes.
  - **A block's label lights with its first sentence**, on both panes, and hovering the label lights that sentence: a heading's
    number, a list's bullet or number, a caption's "Figure 4:", a theorem's head (the owner's case: 1810.04805v2 A.3/A.4's bullets
    lit on neither pane; its headings 4.2–5 lit the number on the left alone).
  - **A block lights whole, its kept pieces included**: a citation kept where it stands, a reference's numbers-only last line
    (1810.04805v2's Zhu et al., "19–27.").
  - **A unit the left does not locate** lights by its boxes on a page in place, whatever its kind (a cell's lines did since #515).
  - Measured on the release sweep's 53 papers and 2010.11929v2 (1 453 pages, every one laid by the door, both panes' shapes made as
    the reader makes them, the pages in place: `readarxiv-lab-data/unified-light`, 2026-10-30), before and after: displays lit as
    their own block on both panes 0 → 2 995 of 3 016 (20 more in part on the left; before, 2 553 lit with their unit on both and
    428 with it on the left alone); labels unlit on a pane 2 678 of 4 805 → 5; kept pieces unlit on a pane 958 of 43 068 → 18;
    text lines unlit on a pane 336 of 60 516 → 18 (ink our page shows under an item's box that the unit's lit area meets counts as
    lit: a crop the door drew a little aside, a label drawn anew in a centred line); units dark on both panes 35 → 21, on the right
    alone 20 → 1 (the nine dark on the left alone after were dark on both before); arXiv's text of a unit that no block lit 305
    lines → 9. The sentences the sweep's invariant checks keep their faults (2 units, as before); 4 456 → 4 461
    units lit by sentence.
  - **Text no unit owns is a kept block** (the owner's ruling of 2026-10-30: at the same place on both panes, a listing one block):
    a page number, a listing, an e-mail line, a note that is an address alone, a bibliography the front end did not cut into
    entries, a display no unit holds — what no unit owns once the ink units have claimed theirs — is a unit the bundle keeps
    (`layout/ink-units.mjs` rule 10, PIPELINE 42): an ink unit of the KEPT flag, never translated nor awaited, its rows its lines'
    boxes, on the left the tokens on its lines, so that the rule above lights it as any block. A block is a run of such lines in
    TeX's stream with nothing a unit owns between them, in one column and one class (a listing's brace in it). A float's text is
    none (a figure's labels light nothing), nor a line beside a unit's text on its baseline (its label or its number, lit with
    the unit). Its glyphs are in no group: our page and its ledger are as they were. Over the 54 papers: 1 920 blocks of
    5 871 lines on 49 papers, every one lit on the left; arXiv's lines in the frame no block lit 5 399 → 1 357, every other
    count of the probe as it was; the bundle +0.6 % (a paper's median +0.22 %, 2610.19159v1's agent logs +3.9 %), a paper's
    left made 8.7 → 8.5 ms (median of 7), a page's geometry 0.070 → 0.079 ms; 2610.19159v1 44 → 58 ms and 0.047 → 0.094 ms.
    The 1 357 left: 2610.19159v1's framed transcripts, which the figures' text takes (1 016), algorithms inside floats, arXiv's
    stamp, lines our compile sets elsewhere. A page
    moved (our lines elsewhere than arXiv's) lights as a page in place since BUNDLE 12 (below). On the rebuilt reader a display
    TeX set that no unit owns is one block whatever its lines' baselines, its number with it, as a unit's display is (§18.58).
  - **A block lights on both panes or on neither** (the owner, 2026-10-30: 「为什么修改后还有一边不亮的情况？我们可以从根本上解决吗？
    …如果实在分不出来，我们就两边统一亮，或者划成一整块亮」): on a page in place a block's area on each pane is its boxes. On the left
    each box lights the tokens of arXiv's page under it where they are and itself where none is (a display or a formula drawn as
    paths, a bullet drawn as a mark: `highlight.mjs` pageGeometry's box lines, the floats' walk never reading them); a box on one of
    its unit's token lines widens that line, up and down as ink, and gives its row what the tokens leave of it, in the sentence of the
    token beside it (a label the first's); a box on no token line of its unit is a row of its own, in the sentence the unit's text is
    in there. A unit's line on its display's rows is the display's; a unit the left part locates on another page than ours lights
    on ours too; a label or a head hanging before the first row, and a block's own box past the column's edge (an overfull line), are
    never clamped; a laid page's tokens are the door's own ink and never clamped. On the right, a placeholder whose ink the wrap could
    not part (its group missing from the document) stays shown, lit with its unit. Measured on the same 54 papers, before and after:
    units dark on both panes 21 → 0, on one 1 → 1; labels lit on one pane alone 5 → 0, pieces 5 → 0 (and 2 dark on both → 0), text
    lines 17 → 1, displays lit in part 21 → 0; units lit by sentence 4 461 → 4 461, their faults 2 units → 0. What stays one-sided:
    one paragraph whose translation ends on the page before, so that nothing of it is drawn on the page its original's last line is
    on (2610.19159v1 p119: lighting it there would light blank paper); six lines of a display with a word before it on its baseline,
    where only the blank between the word and the formula is unlit, every token of the line lit.
  - **A page our compile set otherwise lights as a page in place** (the owner's ruling of 2026-10-30; `PIPELINE_VERSION` 41,
    `BUNDLE5` 12). Another TeX Live's glue moves our lines a point or a few, a line goes over a column's or a page's break
    (1810.04805v2's page 16, every line 3 to 27 pt above arXiv's): the maker's boxes stand beside arXiv's ink, and the left lit only
    what its left part located (Table 8's header cells "RND", "Mask", "Same" lit on the right alone). The page pass's line check
    pairs each of our lines with arXiv's already (`layout/carry.mjs` `lineCheckOf`: the partner's page and the median offset of the
    words matched), and the producer ships the pairs: the left part of each page a line leaves or lands on holds them (`lines`,
    `pipeline/moved-lines.mjs`: a line's page of ours, its box, arXiv's page and the offset), every line of a page with one moved
    past half a point (a line with no partner takes the offset of its column's nearest line that has one, never of a line given
    one so; one in place carries nothing), and an empty list on every other page the check placed. Only a page the check placed
    has a list: 90 % of its lines found a partner (`MAP_FOUND`, the reader's own share), the page read whole and drawn; a page
    whose words are arXiv's but whose lines our compile rebroke has none, and is judged by its tokens (#524's review: an empty list
    there had lit blank paper at our lines' places). The reader carries each box by the line it stands on onto arXiv's page,
    another page's too; a box beside its line's words, which the line's tokens do not reach (a heading's number drawn as a mark, a
    piece drawn as paths), by its own block's line on its row; and tells the page by its boxes as a page in place
    (`view/shapes.mjs`), a block told from its boxes there by its carried rectangles too, so that a click finds the line under it.
    A page with a list, an empty one too, is in place whatever its tokens give: 2610.16663v1's page 15, its displays leaving
    arXiv's text layer few tokens, was read as moved by them though 41 of its 43 lines stand in place. A left part of 11 has none,
    and its page is judged by its tokens as before.
    Measured over 70 papers (the release sweep's 63 cached papers and the gate pack's 7, the production pass on both engines over
    the same compiles, next 44c3a36d before, `readarxiv-lab-data/moved-lines`, 2026-10-30, after #524's review), every item of the
    maker's inventory judged lit on the left at its place on arXiv's page (a box beside its line's words at its block's line's):
    - 1 873 left parts: 1 550 carry entries (9 667, 8 of them a line over a page break, on both its pages), 301 an empty list, 22
      none (a page the check did not read whole or draw: 2307.16209v1's 71–76, whose lines our compile set across its pages).
      Every page found 90 % of its lines' partners (the least 87 of 95, 2610.37668v1 p21): `MAP_FOUND` takes no page's list on
      these papers, and guards the rebroken one. Our lines holding a token of arXiv's at their middle row, as they stand and
      carried: on the moved pages below 222 → 296 of 299, on every page 85 101 → 85 180 of 85 302.
    - The pages moved by the in-place test (under 90 %, or under 3 lines: the unified-light probe's rule): 21 on 9 papers, 542
      items. Lit on the left 439 → 541; one-sided 103 → 1 (lines 27 → 0, kept pieces 25 → 0, labels 2 → 0, displays 40 → 0,
      display lines 9 → 1). 1810.04805v2 p16 lights 92 of 92, its Table 8 cells with them. On every page one-sided
      items 123 → 7 of 152 266, each a display line with a word before the formula on its baseline, the word and the formula
      lit and only the blank between them not (the case above; 2610.16663v1 p15's joins it now that the page is in place); 400
      boxes beside their line's words go with their block's line (the first round, by the map's line alone, left 3 labels and a
      display of them one-sided).
    - The producer's units, cut and laid, are 40's: 18 383 units located on the left on both, the laid sets equal, every units
      chunk equal but its version (33 068 units). The bundles grow 0.28 % (0.54 % gzipped; the left parts 0.71 %; a paper's
      median 0.53 %, its largest 1.13 %, 1810.04805v2).
    - The reader, every part and page made as it makes them, best of 3, both orders: a paper's left 6.8–6.9 → 6.9–7.1 ms median
      (all 70: 550–553 → 552–567 ms), a page's geometry 0.074–0.075 → 0.077–0.078 ms median, a hit 0.102–0.103 → 0.104 µs. A
      moved page's rectangles are told again without the document made again (quiet rectangles are no part of its columns,
      edges or leadings: highlight.mjs retellQuiet, only their units' pages and anchors), its carried inventory kept until the
      inventory or a map changes, the map read by our page; told whole each time, they cost 552 → 697 ms.
    The unified-light probe's 20 moved pages were staging's layers of 2026-10-30 (PIPELINE 38, BUNDLE 11), which hold no line
    map: its 8 papers give 12 here (2610.20030v1 falls back to arXiv's PDF in this pass), and the 21 above are this pass's.
- **Whole, whatever their sentences**: headings, table cells and displays. A drawing's text lights nothing (below).
- **Every drawn thing lights its original, whatever its kind, but a figure's text** (below; the owner's report of
  2026-10-29 on 2010.11929v2 p9: its References' Chinese lit nothing on either side, its Conclusion's and
  Acknowledgements' did). A source unit and an ink unit (its
  left anchor arXiv's tokens on its lines, `ink-pass.mjs` `inkAnchors`) light as units. A figure's level label is anchored by
  arXiv's tokens in its run's band (`figureAnchors`, PIPELINE 31) and its translation's words are under its unit's id
  (`run.mjs` `paintFigures`); its part holds its left anchor beside its figure row, never a layout row of it (`format.mjs`
  `partShape`; the chain tells its row once, apart from its left unit, `figured`), and the layer's units leave it to its row (the
  web's re-pin at 3b2aa271: every part with a figure unit was refused its layout, `figures[0][0]: a unit of the left or of the
  layout`, until the check took the left anchor). Since 2026-10-30 it lights nothing (below): the server's anchoring and the
  layer's drawing of it stay, so that lighting it later needs no paper prepared again. A babel name (Abstract,
  References, Contents, …) is no unit of the bundle's: each occurrence lights as a heading under a hover id of its own
  (`units.mjs` `nameOccurrenceId`: from `NAME_ID_FROM`, 2^22, past every id a bundle holds, a late chunk's too, and below the
  view's Int32 owners), on the left by the tokens of its page in its box, which the parts' layouts give (`view/shapes.mjs`
  `createShapes`, with no change to the wire), on the right by the words the layer drew of it (`paintNames`), and where the
  layer left it the original's (no word of the target's, unfit, a face refused) by the left's geometry of it, the page's units
  shown as the original holding its id (`layerShapes`); one that leads a unit (RUN_IN) lights with that unit.
- **Figures and tables light by what they hold, never whole** (the owner, 2026-10-30, on 2610.35877v1's Figure 4 and
  Table 2: captions and a table's notes 「按正常的正文单元去按句子对应」; the picture 「悬停图片处不用高亮（因为左右其实已经对照了）」;
  a figure's text labels not now, 「除非对性能开销是免费的」). This replaces the maintainer's decision of 2026-10-01, a float lit
  whole with its caption (a table washed over to its rules, a figure outlined and its caption washed):
  - **A caption** lights as a body unit does, by sentence where both sides have its sentences, and its float never with it;
    a subcaption so too. On every engine: the tags path (Google, an LLM) cuts a caption into sentences as it cuts a
    paragraph (`mt.mjs` `translateUnits` by `highlight.mjs` `bySentence`), where before it sent a caption whole, lit whole
    on Google and on an LLM whatever the view did; the markers wire (Microsoft, whose own sentence lengths always covered
    captions) is byte for byte what it was, every unit's (3 358 units of twelve papers, 2026-10-30, where the tags wire's
    cuts changed for their 135 captions and nothing else). `TRANSLATE_VERSION` 9 and `PIPELINE_VERSION` 38 come with it
    (§18.2): every paper prepared and translated again once, in the release that re-keys anyway. **A table's notes** are body
    units already (a paragraph or a footnote under the table): they stop the caption's walk and light by sentence.
  - **A figure's picture** lights nothing, nor its panels: the two panes stand side by side already. No outline is drawn.
  - **A table** lights cell by cell, and a gap between two cells or a rule nothing. A cell the front end made a unit lights
    alone; so does one it did not — a cell of numbers, of a formula, of one letter (a unit has two letters at least): the
    table's words no unit holds, one cell while they stand on one line within 0.6 of their height of each other, and
    within 0.4 where those words leave a column free between them on every row of the table (`floats.mjs` `cellsOf`: a
    word space is a third of the height, two columns' `\tabcolsep` more than one; columns set tight, a decimal point or a ±
    every row sets alike stays in its cell). On the ten papers, two numbers more than 0.4 apart stay one cell twice, both
    on our typesetting's side (2026-10-30, the rule as Codex's review left it). Lit whole at the same
    place on both panes under a hover id of its own (`units.mjs` `tableCellId`: from `CELL_ID_FROM`, 2^30, 2^16 a page,
    below the view's Int32 owners and past every name's), the right's run a copy of the left's (§17.8). A cell unit the
    left part does not locate is told by where the layout lays it (§17.8), so that a cell pairs with its translation.
  - **A figure's text lights nothing** (TikZ's words, a figure's labels the wrap made units): no layout holds it, its words
    free as a table's rows are, and only where it stands is kept, which makes its float a figure (`highlight.mjs`
    `DRAWING`). Pairing it was measured, and it is not free: the production pass in Docker, its parts and left parts read
    back, and the reader's shapes made of them with the figure units and without, medians of 9 rounds, a hit over a 4 pt
    grid of each figure page (2026-10-30):

    | Paper | Figure units (anchored) | Shapes built, with / without | A figure page's geometry | A hit | Heap |
    |---|---|---|---|---|---|
    | 2610.35877v1 | 101 (85), pages 3, 8, 9, 15, 18 | 1.39 / 1.07 ms | 0.79 / 0.19 ms | 0.14 / 0.07 µs | 760 / 620 KiB |
    | 2010.11929v2 | 87 (69), pages 6–9, 16–20 | 1.88 / 1.76 ms | 0.47 / 0.34 ms | 0.12 / 0.09 µs | within the collector's noise |

    A hit costs twice as much, a figure page's geometry up to four times, the shapes a third more: the labels are left
    unlit and unheld, and they cost nothing. A turned label was in no text layer before and is in none now; its translation is in
    the reader package's layer, turned (§11.11).
  - A float is still found on both sides, from a page's first drawing (§17.3): it is where the pointer finds a table's
    cells or nothing, and what a sentence's row keeps out of. A caption's float is a figure on both sides when it is one on
    either, once both pages are drawn.

### 17.2 Where the sentences come from

- **Microsoft** reports its own sentence lengths for the text it was sent (`sentLen`); the extension's service
  verifies them, its translation cache keeps them, and the reader's engine passes them on (`session/translate.mjs`). Nothing is
  added to the request, and the wording is Microsoft's own.
- **Google and an LLM** take the tags path's markers (DESIGN §8.6): the reader cuts each unit's wire text into
  sentences (`mt.mjs cutsOf`: the shared splitter, with a split context that reads the LaTeX placeholders — a citation
  or a footnote annotates the sentence before it, `\citet` is its sentence's subject, a reference a number, an inline
  formula a word), the service puts a marker at each cut and reads where they come back. Units that light whole are
  sent without cuts. Google, zh (2026-10-01): on investigator B's sample 267 of 267 markers back once and in order, 83
  of 83 running units aligned; on the four full papers 1 239 of 1 239 and 507 of 507. With markers Google translates
  each sentence apart: its wording changed in 77 of 83 units (median 4.6 % of characters); of eight pairs read, two
  better, three about even, three worse. The maintainer kept Google by sentence (2026-10-01). An LLM's path is unit
  tested with a fake model (merged, split or reordered sentences fall back to the paragraph) and was measured with the
  maintainer's key on 2026-10-02 (OpenRouter, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, Chinese; `lab/pdf/spikes/highlight-sentences-tags.mjs`,
  ENGINE=llm): on the four full papers, units marked directly, 1 227 of 1 233 markers back once and 482 of 502 units
  of more than one sentence aligned (4 lost a marker, 16 a placeholder); on B's sample 75 of 81 marked directly, and as
  the reader sends them 68 of 81 — the service left unmarked the 10 whose marked text was over the LLM's 1 000-character
  batch cap (32 of the full papers' 502). Marked all the same since (`2ae0d235`, DESIGN §8.6): 79 of 81, those over the
  cap 9 of 10 on their first marked request (one lost a placeholder). Against the same units sent unmarked the text was
  the same in 3 of 81, a median edit of 10.2 % of its characters — though an LLM's two answers differ without markers
  too.
- **Cleaning** (`mt.mjs sentencesOf`): the lengths must partition both texts; a boundary inside a marker, a tag or an
  entity goes to its end; a boundary that begins no sentence on either side (a trailing marker, a formula alone) is
  dropped on both together. Each sentence after the first is kept as the offset of its first word in the unit's plain
  source and in its plain translation — the texts each side is anchored by.
- **Found on each side** (`anchors.mjs sentenceStarts`, report-B's option X: no new TeX mark): the page token of each
  sentence's first word, as the unit's own text match inside its marks found it; its second or third word where the
  first was not found; past that, the unit lights whole. arXiv's PDF has marks only once our marked original is compiled
  — in a live run right after the first preview (the typesetting rule plans every later compile from it, 2026-10-02) — so a unit there found by its text alone takes its
  starts where its match covers 80 % of its words or more (B3c): on the ten papers 625 of 738 units of more than one
  sentence, 1 702 starts, all on the token the marks give; on the ground truth's arXiv PDFs on the mark's line as often
  as with marks (98.6–100 % against 98.9–100 %). In a live open with Microsoft and nothing cached, the first sentence
  lit 155 ms after the first preview on 2608.02785 (12.6 s before) and 173 ms on 2608.06701 (20.1 s before; B3c,
  2026-10-01).
- **Held to a ground truth**: investigator B's compiles with a mark at every sentence's start — starts on the mark's
  line on our original 98.9–100 %, our translation 100 %, arXiv's PDF 98.9–100 % with the marks and 98.6–100 % by text
  alone. The ten papers: 965 running-text units lit by sentence on both sides, 707 of more than one sentence; B's four
  papers 451 of 466 units of more than one sentence with every start found on arXiv's PDF and our translation.
- **The splitter's abbreviations** (shared with the HTML page, DESIGN §8.6): no cut after a place's or a title's
  (`Mt.`, `Mr.`) or a Latin one; after a case's `v.` only behind a capitalised name (`Oregon v. Mitchell`, not `a vertex
  v.`), after the label of a numbered part (`Ch.`, `Sect.`, `Eqn.`, `Tab.`, `App.`) or a month only before its number,
  after any short capitalised label only before a number that is no enumerator (`2)`, `2.`); and never after a
  placeholder's own letter — a sentence ending on a formula keeps its boundary. On the reader's units of twelve papers,
  against the splitter before 2026-10-01: 6 cuts removed (`Oregon v.` ×5, `Mt.`), each false, none added
  (2026-10-02); the reader's split context gives a formula as `x`, so the placeholder rule changes nothing there.

### 17.3 The shapes

- **Runs and rows** (`highlight.mjs`): a unit's tokens on a page, in its lines, by column → its runs, one page and one
  column each, cut where another unit's line stands between two of its rows (a float set inside a paragraph) and, on a
  page of two columns, where a full-width line does (revtex's widetext); its rows are its lines' union, never part of one:
  lines that overlap up and down are one row there, so that a display's numerator, denominator, limits, scripts and number
  are every one lit (today's merges them into one row, their extent across; the rebuilt reader cuts the union into bands at
  every line's head and foot, §17.9). What stands between two of a unit's words
  and is no unit's is its own (an inline formula's pieces), in running text only and never across another unit's line;
  the words before its first one on its line (a theorem's head, a list's label) too, but a cell's: the words before a
  cell on its row are cells of their own (2026-10-30; before, a cell took its row's cells of numbers before it, unseen
  while a cell lit its whole table).
- **The column's text edges** come from every page's long lines, per page size, parity and column, so a page of
  displays takes the document's measure and a landscape page keeps its own; a run reaches up to 6 units past an edge
  (an overfull display) and snaps to it within 3. A float's cells keep their ink past the edge.
- **The ink**: a token's ink is its text item's share by a proportional face's widths (Times-Roman's for ASCII, a full
  em for CJK — and for dashes and quotation marks in an item mostly CJK — half an em otherwise; an even share in a
  monospaced face), widened over the marks it sets against itself (an opening bracket, a closing stop; a CJK stop inks
  half its em) and to the end of an item of marks alone after it. English sentence boundaries through a letter on the
  canvas: 3 of 166 (61 with an even share; B3's probe, 2026-10-01).
- **One outline a shape, 3 px corners**, padded 3 px beside the column's text and half the leading above and below —
  the lower quartile of the space between a kind's lines on that page (a footnote by a footnote's), and over what hangs
  past the first and last lines (a script, a denominator).
- **The sentence shape**: its first row from its start, the rows between across its unit's text in the column, its last
  row to its end with its punctuation; two sentences on one row meet halfway through the space between them. Over a
  column or a page break the rows reach the unit's text edge there — the column's edge less the unit's least indent, so a
  list's item keeps to its own — but not over another unit's words on that row, nor under a float's painted shape; an
  overfull line sticks out alone, by up to 6 units. Across the unit's own display they do not: TeX ends the line before a
  display where its text ends and begins the one after it at the column's start, so the rows either side reach no further
  than their ink (`highlight.mjs` `interrupted`'s DISPLAY; before, a sentence that went on past its display lit the row before
  it to the margin, over the blank TeX left there: 2610.40645v1 p14's "partition functions²" in Japanese, its verb after display (3.5),
  the owner's report of 2026-11-01; the same on either pane, wherever a sentence goes on past a display). Where a unit's shapes cannot hold its words (two lines of text made
  one row by a tall formula, a glyph hanging into another sentence's row) it lights whole: 12 of the 977 units whose
  starts both sides found, on the ten papers.
- **A token's sentence is the text's** (`highlight.mjs withSentences`, `segsOf`): on the left a token paired with a word
  of the unit's source is in that word's sentence; on a laid page a word is in its word's, and any other token — a formula's
  crop, a display's kept line, a lead — in the sentence its place in the translation falls in (the word table's `at`). A
  sentence's place begins at the opening marks (Unicode's Ps, Pi) set right against its first word (`shapes.mjs` openedAt): the
  row names the word, and the door draws a full-width bracket as a token of its own, which by its place was the sentence
  before's, where the left's token of the word holds its bracket (`anchors.mjs` inkEdges: 2610.42112v1's Figure 7 caption,
  "(a)–(e):" and "(f):", the owner's report of 2026-11-03). The stored offsets are read so, and none is made again. A placeholder
  that opens a sentence ("Figure 6(c) isolates …") is still the sentence before's on both panes: the row's offset names the
  word after it, and the left has no glyph of its own to place it by.
  Token order still makes the rows and the runs, and decides only a left glyph no word is paired with (a formula's, a
  script the text layer gives late), with the floor: no such glyph on a row below one where a later sentence began is an
  earlier one's. Until 2026-10-19 every token went by order, and the page's word table wrote a unit's displays after all
  of its text: each display joined the page's last sentence, the floor gave it every row below, and nothing fell back —
  on 54 papers of the sweep 527 of 3 796 units lit by sentence (40 papers) lit a sentence short, empty or over others.
- **Never another sentence's words**: a unit lights whole on both panes where a later sentence begins above an earlier
  one's last row (the drawing did not keep the text's order where the fit ran the text on above a display, its `flow` step,
  which RULES_SCHEMA 10 took out, §18.2), or
  where a sentence of one of its runs paints over a word of another sentence in another run on the page (a display wider
  than its column beside the column's text, a label read apart from its line; `runsApart`). On the 54 papers
  (2026-10-19), against the layer pinned for each paper: by sentence 3 779 units (3 796 before), of them 3 on the right
  with a word their shapes miss (none lit as another sentence; below) and none on the left (5 before); the 24 that now
  light whole all lit wrongly before — 16 a display's line made one row with the text line where the next sentence
  begins (§17.7), 5 runs over each other, 3 the left's pairs putting a later sentence's word above an earlier one's row.
- **The hit test is the paint**: the same shapes, the smaller unit winning where two overlap (a heading run into its
  paragraph). Inside a float's body (§17.1) the pointer finds its caption where the caption's block reaches in, a table's
  cell, or a smaller unit's block; else nothing — never the float. On the ten papers 0 holes in
  37.3 M points of painted blocks (7–16 % of points lit nothing or a neighbour before), in 25.3 M of sentence shapes and
  in 6.2 M of floats' shapes, 0 points lit as another sentence of the unit, 0 points of running text taken by a float,
  and every anchored unit lit (1 829 of 2 553 on both sides). Under the rule of 2026-10-30 (the gate that day): 999 units
  aligned by sentence, 83 more than before (the captions), with 0 holes and 0 points of another sentence in 24.6 M
  points of sentence shapes and no unit more lit whole for its shapes (11, as before); of 5.26 M points of floats' bodies
  4.18 M light nothing (a figure's picture, a table's gaps and rules), 0.79 M a cell no unit holds, 0.29 M a cell unit,
  5 878 a caption and 250 a smaller unit; every cell lights itself at its middle (408 cell units, 4 512 cells no unit
  holds), and no unit's point is taken by a float. A drawing's text, 28 units of two papers, lights on neither side by
  rule. The blocks that moved are those: the drawings' (gone), the 124 cells that had taken a head (58 on the left, 66 on
  the right; four fewer pads overlapping another block), and one heading's pad on one page of 2608.12502's right, 0.38
  units taller on each side, a drawing's lines no longer counting toward its page's leading.
- **Floats** (`floats.mjs`), made on a page's first drawing from the operator list it was drawn by (its figures, its
  rules, its other marks): each figure to its nearest caption only, the one just below first; from each caption a walk
  away from it over what lies across it — lines no running text owns, figures, marks, rules — stopping at another unit's
  line, another caption's figure or a gap, and at its own last rule. A float that holds a figure or a drawing (3 % of it
  marked outside its text, or a drawing's text standing in it) is a figure; one of text and rules a table, whose words no
  unit holds are its cells (`cellsOf`), each a run of one row. Found on the ten papers: figures 46 of 47, tables
  52 of 52, algorithms 2 of 2.
- **The wash** (`engine.css`): the band's colour at its strength over the page, multiplied into it (screened over a
  dimmed page, `reader.css`), so the paper takes the wash and the letters keep their own colour, as a band behind the text
  looks on an HTML page. The highlight layer blends, not its bands: its z-index, which keeps it over the text layer and the
  figures, makes it a stacking context, an isolated group, and a band's own blend mode mixed with nothing but the layer's
  empty ground, the wash lying over the letters (the owner's report, 2026-10-31: the letters looked grey under it). Measured
  on staging that day, 1810.04805v2 p1's abstract, the mean of the ink under a band: black (9, 9, 9) read (8, 44, 32) and
  reads (8, 9, 8) blended by the layer; on a dimmed page the light letters (216, 216, 216) read (174, 210, 198) and read
  (216, 222, 220); the paper's wash the same either way, (208, 242, 231) and (29, 59, 49). Scrolling a pane a frame at a time
  with a block lit and the layers of all 16 pages made, every frame 16.7 ms with the bands blending, the layer blending, or
  only a lit layer blending, the main thread's time alike (521–565 ms a run of 145 frames).

### 17.4 The pointer's path

- One hit test and one paint per animation frame (`pointer.mjs`); the pointer read before anything is written; no layout
  read — each pane's and page's place kept when the layout changes (a ResizeObserver, the contents panel's slide, a
  zoom) and the scroll as its event gives it. A miss keeps what is lit 120 ms (the HTML page's value), so crossing the
  space between two paragraphs does not blink; a scroll under a still pointer lights what comes under it.
- A side's layout is made in the idle time once no side is being anchored (or at once in its own task when the pointer
  needs it first), a page's geometry and its sentences on the page's first drawing, a side's sentences in an idle period
  of their own after its layout, the left's again after the right's; nothing of a sentence's fit is made in the
  pointer's frame. A unit whose sentences are known but not yet found, or whose fit is not yet worked out, is a miss
  meanwhile (25–125 ms after the pointer comes to rest on an open, 2026-10-01), then lights its sentence — never the
  paragraph first.
- What is lit is drawn again by what replaces it — a new compile's right side, the left anchored again by our marked
  original's marks — and the pointer resting on it is carried to the new side. While its unit's sentences or their fit
  are on their way there, what was drawn for it stays, never its paragraph; when they land it is drawn anew and the
  pointer is asked again. A sentence lit at a swap is drawn on the new side at the swap itself: where the idle time has
  not made the new side's layout and sentences yet they are made before the swap, each in a task of its own and only
  while a sentence is lit, and the lit unit's fit in the swap's task (under 1 ms) — on 2608.02459 and 2608.06701, a
  pointer resting on either pane through a swap or a re-anchor, the sentence painted on both sides in every frame,
  where the new side had been blank for 40–200 ms; the swap 15–40 ms later at the median (2026-10-02).
- What a run's sentence was drawn as is kept and put back when it is lit again at the same scale (at most 512), and
  let go when a page's floats come.

### 17.5 What a copy keeps

- The record keeps each unit's sentences beside its translation (`CachedUnit.sentences`, `{ src, tr }`: the offsets
  above), additive and optional — no pipeline change; on 2608.02459 +20.7 KB (2.7 %, B3, 2026-10-01). A copy made
  before keeps working and lights by paragraph until its paper is translated again. A copy's sentences are used only
  where they are of their shape and the translation made again from its pieces is the text they were counted in; what
  the offsets mean rests on `plainSource`, `plainTranslated` and `anchors.mjs tokens` — a change to any is a change of
  the record. A run again (a retry, the network back) seeds itself with what the visit's last run made, sentences and
  all (`cache.mjs seedAgain`).
- A translation's `inSource` mark (a final set it in the source: the author block under CJKutf8) belongs to the copy's PDF,
  not to the run. A run that sets no final writes the units' provenance over the copy's PDF, which still sets that
  translation in the source, so the mark goes with the translation from the record to the seed, to the run again's seed
  and to the run's results, and only a final that sets the unit again says anew whether it set it there
  (`cache.mjs inSourceOf`).
- Units that share a source hash (table cells, often) each take the best translation of that source, whole before partial
  (`cache.mjs seedFrom`); whether a run changed anything a stored copy holds is judged on the units as a whole, never by
  hash (`decideWrite`).
- A table group kept whole is shown in the source (`state: 'kept'`), and the record keeps beside it what the translator
  gave its cells (`translation`: whole, partial, none or lost) and their sentence cuts, so that a cell given in part is
  asked for again rather than taken as whole, and a retry that makes it whole with the same pieces is written. A cell
  left partial in the copy was asked for on every run (`cache.mjs translationOf`).

### 17.6 What it costs (2026-10-02, interleaved against a base build)

One run of the browser gate's `costs` (three rounds, pooled) at the head of the final review's fix round against
`174b5896` — the paragraph blocks of B1, before sentences and floats. B1 against the reader before it (`5957a4be`,
2026-10-01): per light p50 script 0.15–0.17 ms against 0.14–0.19, style and layout 0.28–0.34 against 0.22–0.33, the open
within noise.

- Per light (a sweep on 08350, 29181, 06701), p50 script 0.152–0.243 ms against the base's 0.159–0.179, p95
  0.319–0.427 against 0.291–2.403; style and layout after it p50 0.259–0.393 ms against 0.279–0.366; no layout forced
  where the highlight is written; no long task in a sweep. 2608.06701 sits near its limit (0.243 against 0.159, the
  limit 0.26): a sweep there lights 44 times, sentences, against the base's 14 blocks.
- The open: time to ready and anchoring within noise of the base — 02459 873 and 607 ms against 909 and 615 (p50),
  04322 537 and 419 against 540 and 429 (on a loaded machine paired rounds have differed by −395 to +336 ms; in Node,
  anchoring 90.5 ms cold on 02459's translation, B3c, 2026-10-01).
- In idle time after the open, 02459's layouts 15.1–17.0 ms on the left and 10.1–11.1 ms on the right, each in an
  idle period of its own with its drawn pages' geometry (the base's paragraph blocks 8.7–9.3 and 7.8–8.3), and its
  sentences 2.3–2.9 ms a side; a page's geometry at its first drawing 0.03–0.17 ms in the browser (B1, 2026-10-01), the
  rows' reach adding 6–12 % since; a page's floats 0.3–0.8 ms p50 (up to about 4 ms on a side's first pages; B4,
  2026-10-01), from the operator list it was drawn by — asking the worker for it again had made pages 7–8 of 06701
  take 326–387 ms to draw, against 198–224.
- Memory: a side's layout keeps what a page's geometry needs of its tokens, not the tokens — on 2608.02459, both
  layouts and sentences made and the garbage collected, the heap 10.5 MB; 31.8 MB while an arrow the layout kept held
  the anchoring's scope and both sides' tokens with it (the final review; the browser gate checks the tokens are let
  go).

### 17.7 Known limits

- A grid of panels in several rows with the subcaptions over their panels pairs them wrongly (each subcaption is read
  with the panel under it).
- A table the left's floats miss lights its cell units alone, and its cells of numbers on neither pane (the right's floats
  are the left's); a plain-word inline diagram marked under 3 % is taken for a table, its words lit as cells; a caption
  between two tables takes the one below.
- A cell of numbers is the words no unit holds on one line within 0.6 of their height (0.4 across a column the table leaves
  free): one set over two lines lights as two cells, and two columns set closer than 0.4 of their height, or than 0.6 where
  a cell no unit holds runs across the column between them on another row, light as one.
- An equation number set on its own line below its display (2608.09746 #27) is no unit's and is not lit, but where the maker holds
  it among its display's segments, which light it with the display (§17.1).
- A page our compile set otherwise than arXiv's lights as a page in place by its line map (§17.1); one whose
  lines the line check did not find (90 %), did not read whole, or whose layer stands over arXiv's PDF, has none, and lights on
  the left what its left part locates.
- A table at a page's head whose first row is single letters over numbers, after a display that closed the page before,
  is taken by that display's walk: no distance tells them apart (A1, measured: lead walks' first gaps up to 19.6 pt).
- Two lines of text made one row by a tall formula, with a sentence beginning on the second, light their unit whole (12
  units on the ten papers, with those a hanging glyph makes whole); so does a display's kept line made one row with the
  translation's line under it, where the next sentence begins (their boxes overlap by more than half a unit: 16 units on
  the 54 papers of the sweep, 2026-10-19).
- A formula or a citation that begins a sentence lights with the sentence before it, on both panes alike: a sentence
  starts at its first word (`mt.mjs sentencesOf`), and the record keeps no more. Starting it at its first piece changes what
  the record means (§18.2's `TRANSLATE_VERSION`).
- A word the layer draws past the column's edge by more than the overhang, or on a page the unit's rectangles are not on,
  is in no shape and lights with nothing (3 units on the 54 papers).
- Before our marked original is compiled, units of arXiv's PDF matched under 80 % by their text alone light whole (113
  of 738 on the ten papers; 29181 38 of 90).
- A copy made before the highlight lights by paragraph until it is translated again; an LLM's sentences are measured
  on one model (above); with Google the markers change the wording (above).

### 17.8 On the layer path: the shapes made page by page

- **Made for the pointer, and only while the highlight is on** (`layer-side.mjs` `catchUp`, `pauseShapes`). The highlight lights on
  the pointer alone (§17.1), so its shapes are made on the pointer's first want of a page, which comes only while the switch
  (S-P-80) is on, in a task of their own after the pointer's frame, and are told nothing while the switch is off. Until then, and
  while it is off, the side keeps what they would have been told (the parts read, by the batches they came in; each laid page's
  words, the first its door gave; the pages shown, hidden and muted as last told; whether the right was reset), and tells them, in
  that order, on the next want: the shapes made late are the shapes made as things came (`layer-side-door.test.ts` H3: every
  unit's runs and starts on both panes, made at the start and told as things came, made at the end, and told nothing while the
  switch was off between, are equal). Before, both panes' shapes were made at the index, for each part and at each commit, the
  switch on or off: 7 to 10 ms of the main thread before page 1 at 1x, 31 to 42 at 4x (the rules audit of 2026-11-04); page 1
  in place 12 ms sooner at 1x and 22 ms at 4x on a returning reader with it (the audit's replays, seven papers, paired medians).
  The first light waits for the making: on the same replays the first hover's light came 0 to 18 ms later at 1x and 17 to 49 ms
  at 4x, the making a task of up to 56 ms at 4x on a new reader, once a visit. A page shown or hidden makes again the starts of
  its own units alone (`layerShapes` `unitsOn`), not every unit's.
- **One layout, made page by page** (`highlight.mjs` `pageLayout`, `layoutParts`, `layoutPage`; `shapes.mjs`
  `createShapes`). On the layer path the left's tokens come a page at a time (the door's `leftPageOf`, on the first want
  of the page) and its units' rectangles a part at a time. The document part — each page's columns, the columns' text
  edges, the half leadings — is made again of every unit told whenever a part comes, and each page's geometry made before
  is let go and made again from it (a part that tells no view or unit not told before changes nothing); a page's part
  is its left part's tokens and spans when it lands. Built so, in any
  order, it is the layout made whole: on the ten papers, both sides cut as the wire carries them and made again with the
  pages shuffled among the parts, every page's geometry (4 049 runs on 483 pages) and every sentence shape (7 669, of
  2 340 units' starts read from their pairs) equal the whole layout's (the highlight gate, 2026-10-15).
- **Token ids are the side's stream**, from the left part's `first`, as the parts' units name their streams: they rise
  page by page whatever order the pages come in, a unit's first token is known before its page comes (its head on the
  page, whether a sentence began before a run), and they equal the whole layout's. Each page's tokens are a table of its
  own; a layout made whole reads its arrays through views of them.
- **A unit's sentences wait for all its pages** (`tokensIn`): a run's sentence shapes read the unit's tokens beyond the
  run — whether a sentence began before it or goes on after it — so a unit over a page break lights whole on the pages
  that have come until the others have, then by sentence. A page's left part comes on its first want, so the side asks
  for the left parts of the other pages its running units are on in the task after its own (`layer-side.mjs spreadFrom`;
  the nearest `SPREAD_MAX`, 8; a page so fetched spreads no further, or a paper's paragraphs would fetch every page): before, a paragraph that ran on
  to the next page lit whole until the pointer had been there. On the 54 papers, 0.78 more left parts a page wanted (none
  on 43 % of pages, two on 21 %), 43 KB at the mean, 25 KB at the median, 121 KB at the 90th percentile (2026-10-19).
- **The right, mirrored** (`mirror`): until the layer's pages bring words of their own, the right's shapes are a layout of
  the right's own over copies of the left's tokens and rectangles, following the left as it is told. Its blocks equal
  the left's from run objects of its own: the paint keeps what it drew by the run, and a run shared would move the left's
  element into the right's pane. The right's floats are the left's, and the right's sentence shapes keep from under them as
  the left's do; a table's cell no unit holds is the left's run of it copied, on a page the layer laid as well (its numbers
  are our page's ink there) where it stands on no unit's row of ours and the page's lines did not move across its break, as
  a unit shown as the original's is copied (`layerShapes` `make`); elsewhere it lights on the left alone. On a laid page
  whose lines moved within it (its line map, §17.1) the left's floats and those copies stand where our page sets them, the
  map read back (`backOf`): a float moved whole, as TeX sets it, as most of its cells' lines moved (one of no cell as its
  caption's line), its cells with it (`floatBack`), a copy as its token's line; none of a float whose lines are another
  page's of ours. Before, 1810.04805v2 p16's Table 8, set 30 pt higher on ours, lit a cell three rows off on the right (the
  staging check of 2026-10-31). Where its place shows the original, the mirror's starts are the left's (the
  same tokens), so a unit lights by sentence on both panes as it does on the left.
- **The left's starts** are its units' pairs (the left part's runs of words to tokens) read as `sentenceStarts` reads an
  anchor's, once every page the unit is on has come. The reader takes every pair shipped, so the producer ships them only
  for a unit `sentenceStarts` would read (located by its marks, or by its text over 80 % of it): on the ten papers, one
  unit's pairs read where the whole layout's anchor refused them.
- **An empty or refused left part** (a page past the left part's caps ships none, M8): no shapes on that page and
  nothing thrown; a refusal warns once a page, and a later left part for it is taken. A left part whose token ids reach
  into a page already in is refused, and the first of the two keeps its place: a bogus page that comes first leaves its
  true neighbour refused, since nothing in the two tells which is wrong.
- **The right on a laid page** (`layerShapes`): where its place shows the layer, the right's shapes are a layout of its own
  over the page's words (the door's `LaidPage.words`: the tokens it drew and what it kept of our page's ink, in the page's PDF
  units, each unit's spans in paint order, then each display's under its own id, then each unit shown as the original's by its
  own boxes), its token ids the page's (page · 2^16 + its index); a unit shown as the original's that the door gave no boxes over
  copies of the left's tokens of it, made once the page's left part is in too; elsewhere the left's mirrored. A unit's stream on
  the right is its first token on its first page, told when that page lays. The right's starts of a unit all on laid
  pages are the tokens carrying its sentences' first words (`words.word` against the row's `sentences.tr`), each token's
  sentence its word's or its place's (`words.at`, §17.3); of a unit on no laid page, the left's; of one on both, none, and
  it lights whole. The page's word table is in the order of its units' text (`words.mjs addUnitWords`): a display's kept
  lines where the line walk passed its region (`breakLines`' `past`), a kept line no placeholder holds before the block that
  follows it in the unit's rectangles.
- **Every block told by its boxes** (`createShapes` takeInventory, tellBoxes; the owner's rule of 2026-10-30, §17.1): the parts'
  layouts give each unit's lines, labels and placeholders' segments on our page. Every display, and every unit the left part does
  not locate, is told from them on every page (`quiet`, as below), so that the right, which lights it by its own table, holds it;
  on a page in place, once both its left part and its boxes are in, whichever first, a display takes the tokens of its segments
  (its own unit's span gives them up) and every unit the free tokens in its boxes, its spans changed in the page's kept input
  before it is laid and in the layout and the mirrors after; a unit told so begins at its first token on its first page. A located
  telling that comes after a quiet one takes its place; a quiet telling of a located unit's boxes on a page it is not located on
  adds that page, its rectangles there quiet. On a page with a line map (§17.1) the boxes are carried first: our page's and those of
  the pages beside it that the map brings there (`invAt`), the layout's boxes of the page the carried ones, and the rectangles
  there of every block told from its boxes (`carryPage`: a part `carried`, highlight.mjs layoutParts, in their place among the
  block's pages; a block brought from another page of ours told there, one whose boxes all left the page no longer on it; a unit
  the left part locates there keeps arXiv's), whichever of the page's left part and the parts comes first, in any order the same
  (`tests/pdf-reader/moved-lines.test.ts`: every order of two parts and two pages, the mirror alike); such a page is in place. This made the cells' telling below a case of it, now on pages in place alone. The
  layout keeps every block's boxes (`boxes`) and the pages in place (`inPlace`), which the mirror reads too; a laid page's layout
  keeps none of them (its table holds every token the page shows of a unit) and clamps none of its tokens (`unclamped`).
- **A cell unit the left part does not locate** (`createShapes`): the producer locates few cells on arXiv's PDF (on the
  sweep's 64 cached papers, 1 113 of 5 094; 7 of 2010.11929v2's 165, 2 of 2610.35877v1's 71), since a cell carries no unit
  mark of its own (`latex-front.mjs`: a heading, a cell or a figure has none), so it is found by its text alone between its
  located neighbours (`anchors.mjs`: one or two words only where they stand in a row once in that gap, more by 3-grams there). Each one the parts' layouts lay (`lines`, arXiv's page's)
  is told on the left, as a babel name is, by the tokens of its page whose middle stands in one of its lines' boxes and that
  no unit told there holds, its part `quiet`: on its pages, no part of their columns, edges or leadings (`layoutParts`). The
  right tells what the left tells, the laid page's words of it its own. Before, the left's words of it were a cell of the
  page's and the right had none: the two panes never shared its id (the release sweep of ba433da8, Table 2 of 2610.35877v1,
  Table 1 of 2010.11929v2), hidden until 2026-10-30 by the table lit whole. On the 64 papers' 1 644 pages, 3 917 cells are now
  told, and the 24 600 units the parts locate keep their runs on both panes, every one (2026-10-30).
- **Floats and the view's window**: a page's floats are made of what its drawing gives (its figures and paths,
  `floats`), and again on the page's first use after a part moves the document part — never in the part's task, which
  would make every such page's geometry again at once. A page leaving the window (`forget`) lets its geometry, its
  floats and their inputs go; its drawing gives them again. Inputs that throw are let go with one warning, and the page
  has no floats.

### 17.9 On the rebuilt reader (`packages/`): the starts stated by the prepare

- **What pairs the sentences** is the row's starts (Row.sentences: the translator's own, offsets in the unit's projection and
  its translation's) found on each pane, as on the layer path: on arXiv's page at the sentence's first word or element, its
  second or third where the first is not found, else the unit lights whole on both (`packages/typeset` lay/lit.ts
  `startsOnA`); as drawn, the laid token of that word or element. **Which sentence a piece is in is decided once, for both
  panes** (lit.ts `sentenceMap`, the owner's rules of 2026-10-30: both panes always light the same thing; a sentence lights
  all its pieces, text, elements, labels): the unit cut at the row's starts into half-open ranges, each piece in the one its
  start falls in. A token of the translation's text by its first character's place (a sentence's start at its first word, from
  the opening brackets and quotes set against it: "(Vier" begins its sentence at the bracket); an element, one piece in both
  texts, by where its ink begins on A, wherever the translation sets it: its crop or its text as drawn, its ink on A and the
  row it stands on there, widened over its ink (one TeX set past its line's text, an equation's number at the margin, stands in
  no line's box), all in that sentence; a label in the first (a babel name's too, the number TeX set before it: 2610.20967v1
  p5's "9." was in no box on A). A sentence's box on a line takes the line's band, whatever it holds there (an element's crop
  alone took its ink's height, short of the line's: 2602.23285v2-ja p13 t219). A translator counts a mark at a cut with either sentence:
  Microsoft set "…的方向。[P²-MOPD]沿该方向…" with its cut past the element, the source's at it, and the left lit
  "P²-MOPD" with its sentence, the right with the sentence before (2611.03953v2 p2, the owner's report of 2026-11-10); the
  translation's places alone had put 425 elements of the corpus's laid pages in another sentence than A's (today's rows over
  stage 1a's parts at 95529b6f9). Where a translation sets an element inside another sentence than its own on A, the element
  is an island of its own sentence there, a run of its own on its row. **I10, the sentence cover** holds it
  (`packages/typeset/tests/replay/cover.ts`, counted by `lab/typeset/gate-l1.mjs --entry --reading=part` over a run's parts,
  the release check's `sentence-cover`, and by the parity's lay of its pairs, its `display`; with today's reading the runner
  lays no entry): on both panes every piece drawn of a lit member (each word of its text on A
  at its first glyph, each character as drawn, each crop, each element's ink, its label, its held lines) is in exactly one of
  its sentences, an element and the label in the same one on both, and every sentence drawn on one pane is drawn on the other
  (a full-width mark's ink read in its own em: one at a line's head, its blank half cut, is drawn half an em left of the line's
  start with its ink at it; the corpus runner gives the entry no row of a stored reply that says nothing, the chain's `empty`,
  as the chain makes none: given it, the entry hid a cell's text and drew nothing, three cells of two pack pairs).
  A sentence that begins with an element (a reference, a citation that is its subject, a paper's name
  macro: "\method{} trains this model …") begins at it on both panes: moved on to the first letter past it, as both panes did
  until 2026-11-10, the element lit with the sentence before (2611.03953v2 p5, the owner's report: "Three details of Equation
  (6) matter." came back with the reference first, and "(6)" lit with the sentence before; on staging's rows of five papers,
  591 of 2,148 translated starts and 556 source starts stood before an element, 350 and 320 units, the paper's `\method{}`,
  `\citet` subjects, `\cref`s, formulas, a bibliography's `\newblock`s). A forced
  break (TeX's `\\`, El.brk) ends the sentence it stands in on both panes, as the line TeX ended there: the text after it is
  a block of its own on the page (1810.04805v2 p8: "… as BERT_BASE:" `\\` "No NSP: …", one TeX paragraph and one sentence of
  Microsoft's across the break, lit as one; the owner's staging review). On a row a sentence's box runs on to the next one's
  start, the last to the row's end, so that the space after a full stop lights the sentence before it, as today's shapes tile a
  row (the full parity of round 3: 23 rows of 21 pages with 2.9 to 10.3 pt lit by neither). `Laid.lit` holds an entry a
  sentence, numbered alike on every page of the unit; the reader paints and hits the entry under the pointer on both panes
  (`{id, s}`), nothing on a page that holds none of it.
- **The prepare states where each word stands on A** (format's `Placed.words`: each word of the projection, its line and its
  first glyph's x0, from the opening brackets and quotes set against it, as the text layer runs them in its token;
  `packages/engine` locate/words.ts: the projection's letters and the unit's glyphs' matched in order, Myers', each side's word
  breaks kept; and each element where its ink's first box stands on A, its line and x0, but a display, a block of its own, and
  an element TeX set outside the unit's text; locate.ts), and marks the units a translator is to cut (`Unit.sentences`: every kind but a heading,
  a cell, a figure's text and a babel name, the layer path's NOT_RUNNING). Every word, not the shared cutter's starts alone:
  of Microsoft's 40,409 stored starts over the corpus (13,149 units, 96 paper-targets, 2026-11-08), 82.4 % are among the
  shared cutter's cuts and 82.9 % among Unicode's sentence boundaries, and what precedes the rest is no closed set ("." 73 %,
  an element 16 %, ";" 6 %, "(" 1 %, a comma, a letter). Placed: 8,608 of 8,610 words on 1810.04805v2, 8,293 of 8,299 on
  2010.11929v2; a part states them only for the members with ink on its page.
- Until 2026-11-08 the rebuilt reader lit every unit whole: the prepare marked no unit for sentences (no translator was
  asked to cut, no row carried any) and placed no start on A (the maintainer's staging review of converge-7, 225f0959f).
- **A display is a block of its own, and no shape fills one** (the owner's reports of 2026-11-09 on staging: 2602.23285v2 p15,
  "… processed as: [display (11)] and a sequence …" lit as one shape over the line before, the display across the column and
  the line after, on both panes, where today lights a bar on each line and the display not at all: 「这里我们主站是分开的」;
  2609.33403v1 §4.2, a paragraph lit as one region over both of its displays, their own shape drawn inside it). The highlight
  shows which words correspond, and a display is the same ink on both panes: lighting it with its text adds nothing. So
  `Laid.lit`'s `own` holds a member's displays alone, each by its piece, the same boxes on both panes, and no row of its text
  is on one (on A a KEPT line on a display is the display's, a member lit from A too); the reader lights a display alone where
  the pointer is over it (`{id, s: -2 - piece}`, the same on every page: today's `displayBlockId`, one hover id a display),
  never with its member, whole or by sentence. The rest of a member's kept ink (a piece or a label kept where it stands, a
  character) lights with it, the row it stands on widened over it, by sentence with its sentence (an element, the sentence its
  ink begins in on A, as every element's). The painter's outline (today's `shapePath`) joins two rows where they
  meet across and paints the room between them, from the upper row's left to the lower one's right; v2 hands it every row of a
  sentence on a page, so it bridged whatever stood between them, a room no box holds and the hit test never found. A shape's
  rows are one outline now only where no other block stands between two of them (a box lit on the pane, another member's or a
  display, whose middle is between them and that stands in their column, the two a row's height apart at least: today's runs,
  cut there, `highlight.mjs interrupted`); a gap with nothing in it stays the unit's, as today's. The column is the one the
  member spans on the page (`columnOf`: the extent across of its every box there, its sentences' and its displays'), never the
  two rows' own width: a sentence whose translation ends a line short before its display and goes on short after it had the
  two short rows, both left of the display's ink, joined by a strip down the column's edge over the display's row, while the
  rows on arXiv's page, longer, met the display and were cut (the owner's report of 2026-11-10 on staging, 2610.17024v1 p9,
  display (43)). Judged by the parity's highlight measure as the reader paints it (`lab/typeset/parity/paint.mjs`, the
  reader's own cut): over round 6's drawing, the shapes' fills of another block (a display; on arXiv's page another unit's
  line) were worse than today's on 181 units of 103 pages (2602.23285v2-ja p15 t127: 2 against 0), and are on none. The
  measure counts a bridge too (a room the outline paints between two rows room for a line apart, across a block's row in the
  column, which holds none of its ink): over round 8 part A's drawing (5c83a7faf), with the rows' own width the cut was worse
  than today's on 34 units of 31 pages, default and every toggle on alike (2610.17024v1 p9 t129 among them), and is on none.
- **A shape paints the union of its boxes, never part of one** (the owner's report of 2026-11-13 on staging, 2111.09276v1 p5:
  display (4), two rows and its number set at the right between them, lit on both panes as a band over its first row and a
  strip from under that row's end to the number, its second row on neither: 「我发现这里的对照高亮有瑕疵」). The display is no
  unit's ink (its paragraph opens with it, set before the paragraph's start: §17.1's display at its unit's edge), so it is a kept
  block lit whole (§18.58), its lines on A cut by the text line rule (`packages/engine` locate/geometry.ts, lines.ts): the
  number's "(", its ink 13.7 pt over the second row's baseline, under that rule's one and a half sizes, stayed on the row's line
  as a script, its "4)" a line of its own. The painter met every two of a shape's rows next to each other from the top where
  their pads overlapped, as if one stood over the other: the second row's line and "4)", their tops alike, were met at the
  middle of the band they share, the row's foot raised over all of its ink; the hit test read the same rows, so the pointer on
  the second row or on the number found nothing. Now a shape's rows are `compose/highlight.ts` `paintRows`': two rows one over
  the other meet at the middle of their pads' overlap and one outline joins them where they meet across, the room between them
  painted, unless another block stands between (as before); boxes on one band (their own extents overlapping up and down) are
  never met: the union is cut into bands at every box's head and foot, each band's boxes one row where they meet across (a row
  and the number beside it, two lines whose fonts' boxes overlap) and a row each where they stand apart (a sentence's runs either
  side of another sentence's element, a line of the next column), each row joined to the outline whose last row stands on the
  band right above it and meets it across. A shape of no two boxes on one band paints as before, row for row. So the pointer
  on any row of a display or on its number lights the whole display on both panes, and on a sentence of its paragraph that
  sentence alone (above). A unit's display states its number inside its row's box (the display rule, `rows.ts`): its row's band
  reaches the number, the blank between lit, as today's lights a display whole as one rectangle (over the parity's 24 pairs, 448
  numbers set on a row, every one so on both readers); the painter now lights every box it is given, whatever the lines' cut.
  Measured over the 92 pairs' laid pages (the reader gate's entry, Google's rows, every shape lit alone by the reader's own code,
  b06a95ba6 against this change): of 4,439 displays (judged by arXiv's text items inside them, painted and hit on both panes),
  the 4,365 of units painted whole before and after, and 25 of the 74 no unit owns (12 papers; 10 of their 19 of several rows)
  lit wrongly, now none; over every shape, boxes not painted whole 387 on the left (in the shapes of 30 kept blocks, 52
  sentences, 20 members lit whole) and 862 on the right (30, 377, 55), now 0; 611 shapes paint otherwise (on the left and the right: kept blocks 30
  and 30, sentences 63 and 410, members lit whole 21 and 57), every one with two boxes on one band, none holding another

- **A figure text lights its own lines' band alone** (Laid.lit `band`, every member the part states of kind `figure`, laid or

  A level one of one line is cut to its container where the part states one (Room.over, the closed shape's edge over its

- **The half leading is read between a member's rows, whatever sentence each row is of** (2026-11-12, lane parity-small;

- **The band chosen paints it** (the reading options' highlight colour, §6.1 item 4): the host gives the bands its store keeps (`Prefs.bands`, each its

- **The right's page told reads no layout either** (design-performance-2026-11-13 Q8): the page number the chrome shows for
  the right pane (`panes.ts` tellRightPage) is the page at its shown top, told in every scroll and each time the stack puts a
