- **What it does not settle**: a display the part states no ink of (LOST) leaves a gap with nothing in it, filled as today's;
  a display set on a text line beside a word (TeX's display after a word on its baseline) is on that line's row, lit with it;
  a sentence whose only text is a display lights nothing but the display; and a sentence that runs on past a display with no
  stop of its own is one sentence to the translator (the markers wire writes nothing after the display's marker, and Microsoft
  cuts at neither a marker nor a colon; the tags wire's cutter reads a display as a word), lit as one in pieces around it, as
  today's (2609.33403v1).

## 18. Rules and their versions

Three kinds of rule decide what the reader shows, and they change at three different costs. Each has its own identity,
and no identity names another kind's change: a tuning of how a page is drawn must not make a paper compile again, and a
fix to a unit's cutting must not wait for the store. This section is the contract the engine, the web and the extension
read their versions by (the rules-as-data plan of 2026-10-08, agreed with the maintainer the same day); a test holds the
table of §18.2 to the identities the engine exports and the table of §18.5 to the fields of the rule set.

### 18.1 The three kinds

**The test that classifies a rule.** Ask what the change alters:

- **the units, their geometry, the layout file, its cell rules or the wrap** (what our server makes per paper): **extraction**;
- **what is sent to a translator, or how a reply becomes a row** (what a language's translation holds): **translation**;
- **only the pixels and text a reader draws from the same bundle and the same rows**: **layout**.

A rule that does two of these is split, or classed by the more expensive.

| Kind | Where it runs | Where it lives | Its identity | A change reaches readers by | Cost of a change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Extraction | the server, when a paper's bundle is made | engine code: `latex-front.mjs`, `arg-roles.mjs`, `latexml-args.mjs`, `groups.mjs` `groupOf`, the layout maker, the ownership and the wrap. HTML: `src/core/rules/latexml.ts`, in the extension | `PIPELINE_VERSION`, `LAYOUT`, `REMOVAL`: the bundle's content versions, in its key (HTML: none since stage 4b; a block's wire is in its key, DESIGN §5.5) | the web's deploy. Each paper's bundle is made again on its next open (§18.4). HTML: an extension release | one compile per opened paper. Rows are rebuilt; the extension's store of answers answers every unit whose wire the change left alone, the web's journal of answers is its output's and asks them all again (`worker/src/mt/journal.ts`) |
| Layout | each reader, at draw time | the rule set, `rules/layout-rules.json` (§18.5) | `RULES_SCHEMA` (the shape and how the engine reads it) and the set's `version` (the values) | publishing: both readers take it on their next load | none |
| Translation | each reader (the extension), the translation workflow (the web) | engine code: `translate/mt.mjs` (`serialize`, `rehydrate`, the wires, `translateUnits`), `toTranslate` (the KEPT flag, the structural names the target's packages answer), `translate/groups.mjs` `decideGroups` and `NAMES_SHARE`, `batchesOf`; and, held by each reader, the paper's context sent with every batch (`paperContext`) | `TRANSLATE_VERSION` (`translate/version.mjs`) | the next release of each reader's engine. Rows of the old version are translated again on open | the rows. The extension's per-text cache holds the translator's raw answers, so there the translator is asked again only for texts that changed; the web's journal is its output's, and a raise asks a reopened paper's every text again |

The edge cases, decided:

- **`NAMES_SHARE` (a table's groups)** is a translation rule. The workflow decides groups, and the rows a reader gets hold the decision (`state: 'kept'`), not the cells' translations. Making it a layout rule would mean rows that carry every kept cell's translation, for a threshold measured once.
- **`authorsTranslated`** decides which units a target sends, so it is a translation rule and lives in `translate/kept.mjs`, apart from the TeX path's strategies (`scripts.mjs`, taken out of the engine with the compiled translation on 2026-11-04).
- **Float labels and babel's names** (the names a language gives a figure, a table and each generated heading: Abstract, References, Contents, …, and whether to use them) are layout: one language's choice at draw time. Where each name stands is extraction: the layout marks wrap the name macros' text and the layout file locates each occurrence (D1a). The layer draws the target's word wherever TeX identified the heading: by its macro, by a style's literal through the definition it sits in, and after the paper's own `\selectlanguage`; the captions (which float labels are the target's: the reader's `CAPTIONS`, `layer-proto/reader.mjs`; a compile of the translation once read them, `captionsOf`, taken out with it on 2026-11-04) decide float labels alone (the ruling on D1a). A name TeX sets right before a unit on its first line (IEEEtran's run-in "Abstract—") is that unit's lead, flowed with its translation whatever its width, the original's joint and glue after it. A name's word is drawn in runs by script as a unit's words are: its CJK characters in the target's CJK face, every other (a Latin word, a digit, a space) in the Latin one (`layer2.mjs` `nameScriptRuns`): the CJK faces served hold no ASCII, so that one face for a word of two scripts was refused by the face check and the name left the original's (the figure labels' finding, #490). **The parked final's requirement:** if the TeX page program returns, it must name the same headings: rewrite a literal the marks wrap to its macro (`\abstractname`), and apply the target's captions again after the paper's own language switch. **Hyphenation** (which patterns a target uses, and their minimums) is layout; the pattern files are assets the host serves, and the algorithms are code.
- **The font roles** (which CJK family and weights a script takes) are layout. The face catalog (files, licences, size corrections, coverage) and the Latin design table are facts about files and stay code. **A CJK script is drawn at Regular, and Bold for bold, beside every English family** (the maintainer's ruling of 2026-10-29, on crops of four papers, `research/babeldoc-typography-2026-10-29/weight/`): Light, and SemiBold for bold, beside Computer Modern and Garamond read lighter than the page they sit in and than BabelDOC's Source Han Serif Regular, by 9 % of the original's stroke on 2608.16117v1's six blocks (0.86 of it against Regular's 0.95, at the canvas's weight); the rule (`cjkFaces.light`) and the eight Light and SemiBold faces went (`RULES_SCHEMA` 6, §18.2; engines of schema 5 keep the last set published for it, §18.3). **A CJK italic run is the body's own face slanted** (the owner's ruling of 2026-10-19, Q17's row 3), in zh, zh-Hant, ja and ko alike: the same face, size correction and weight as the upright, sheared 13° about its baseline as it is drawn (an SVG skew, `layer-proto/fonts.mjs` `CJK_SLANT_DEG`, the one number; 10° was the other the owner saw). A bold italic run is the bold face sheared, no longer the bold upright. No file is fetched for it and no face is made: the run is measured in the upright's own font string, so its advance and every character's place are the upright's. **A CJK run's family list ends with the Latin face of its weight**, upright (`fonts.mjs` `roleFaceOf`, #47.14): the copy space the drawing appends to a run (`layer2.mjs` `lineRuns`, for copy and find) is Basic Latin, which every CJK slice leaves to the Latin faces (the web's font slices), so with the CJK face alone the device drew it and the canvas measured it in the device's own face (the web's `layer-fonts` e2e, rows 3 and 4, marked known); the CJK faces stay first, so every CJK character is theirs, and the CJK class holds no other character the Latin faces serve. The rule set's `cjkFaces.kai`, which no engine read after this ruling, went with the light designs at schema 6 (§18.2): the engines readers held before it, which draw emphasis in it, read schema 5 and keep their schema-5 set (§18.3), so no set of schema 6 names it.
  - **Measured** (Chromium, dpr 2, 44 px): the shear against the outlines sheared in the file, the Oblique 13 faces the owner judged, overlap 98.1 to 99.4 % of their ink (IoU), 0.1 to 0.8 % of the ink pixels more than a quarter apart, all at glyph edges (zh regular and bold, ja, ko).
  - **Row 2, kept for later versions** (no code): the Kai matched to the body by measurement. FandolKai (zh): its ideographs' mean ink box 0.828 × 0.848 em against the body's 0.890 × 0.910, a size factor of 1.074; ink per em² 0.135 against 0.183 (−26 %), made up by an SVG stroke at drawing time. AR PL KaitiM Big5 (bkai00mp, zh-Hant): 0.821 × 0.823 against Source Han Serif TC's 0.891 × 0.913, a factor of 1.098; ink 0.155 against 0.200 (−22 %). Its limits: Chinese only (ja and ko still get no italic); the factors are per font; the stroke only emulates weight; there is no bold Kai, so bold italic stays bold upright. The comparison page as the owner saw it, rows 1 to 4 in all four languages with their measures and licences, and its README: `~/Downloads/readarxiv-test/archive/cjk-italic-2026-10-19/` (`index.html`, `README.md`), on the maintainer's machine.
- **`textless`** is extraction, but v0 also applies it at draw time to a unit's source (only the alignment fallback reads it). A reader applying an extraction rule to a bundle's content is a defect class; it is listed for the debt pass.
- **Cell membership** (`groupOf`, from `tableGrid`) is extraction: the bundle carries each cell's place.
- **A unit's alignment** (whether its lines are centred, flush left or flush right) is extraction, and TeX's own: the marked original writes, for a unit's or a heading's end mark, the stretch of `\leftskip`, `\rightskip` and `\parfillskip` its paragraph was broken with, read once the paragraph ended (`AXT-ALIGN`, `layout/marks.mjs` `readAlign`: centred, flush left, flush right or justified; `{\centering text}` and a blank line is justified, its group closed before its paragraph ended), and the layout maker sets `UNIT_FLAG.CENTRED`, `FLUSH_LEFT` or `FLUSH_RIGHT` from it (the last two by TeX's word alone, LAYOUT 26, never read off arXiv's lines). A unit whose paragraphs TeX set in two alignments (its text set again elsewhere, a class's footnote or reference block) tells none, as a piece set in two colours tells no colour (PIPELINE 43, §19.6's guard). A paragraph a box's close ends (a `\vbox`, `\vtop`, `\insert` or `\vcenter` closed in horizontal mode) is read by its own skips: TeX ends it there with no `\par` where LaTeX sets no `\partokencontext` (TeX Live 2023's LaTeX; 2025's sets 2, and inserts one), so no `para/after` hook runs for it, and the probe watches the box it is set in and, where the box closes before a `\par` told its skips, writes the skips at the end mark, nothing of the unit set after it; each end mark's reading is written once, so the hook that runs later at another paragraph's `\par` writes nothing. Before it, 2608.16117v1's elsarticle abstract (`\global\setbox\absbox=\vbox\bgroup … \egroup`, TeX Live 2023) was read as its keywords' `\raggedright` (`lab/pdf/spikes/layout-align-cases.mjs`: 15 documents in pdfLaTeX, XeLaTeX and LuaLaTeX under both years read as TeX set them, each PDF byte for byte the one before). A unit TeX set in a box (a one-line caption `\@makecaption` centres, `\centerline`) or whose line the log lacks is read from arXiv's lines instead: every line's centre on its column's (the text block's for a full-width row), one line short of it by more than an em; and a one-line paragraph TeX set justified that its own glue centres (`\noindent\hfill X\hfill\null`) is centred where its line is on its column's middle and more than two ems off both edges. The layer draws by the flag. A table cell, which the probe does not read for the layout file (the rebuilt engine reads its column's class: §18.12), it decides by the cell's own lines (several centred: a makecell's) or its table's column on the page (a single line: centred where the column's cells' middles are all within 2 pt of each other and their widths are not, so a column whose cells share a start or an end never is; a cell its column cannot decide, alone in it, a header's or of widths alike, as the layout file's flag says); a unit of a part with no layout by its lines and the page's column, as before the file had a flag (2026-10-19: the layer's own guess had centred 1810.04805's "C.1" and "5.3" headings and missed IEEEtran's centred ones). **The file tells a unit's alignment in four flags or none** (LAYOUT 37): `CENTRED`, `FLUSH_LEFT`, `FLUSH_RIGHT` and `JUSTIFIED` (neither centred nor flush), and the door takes a unit of none as one whose alignment nothing tells, reading its lines itself (`layout/file.mjs` gives `centred` true, false or undefined; `layer2.mjs` `blocksOf2`). A source unit always has one: TeX's word, or the maker's reading of a unit TeX does not tell (centred, else `JUSTIFIED`: a source unit's lines are never the door's to read, so a two-line reference whose hanging indent puts its lines' centres a point apart stays justified). **An ink unit's alignment is TeX's too** (2307.16209v1's title pages, 2026-11-05: its title, author, place and date and its examining board, text no source unit owns, were drawn from each English line's start): the marked original sets a point at every paragraph's end with the alignment TeX broke it by (`marks.mjs` POINTS_TEX `qe<n><code>`, at LaTeX's `para/end`), right after the paragraph's last character, rule, mark, insertion or formula, before its kerns and penalties and the one last glue TeX takes away, which are put back after it — none where the paragraph ends in a box (its end would be read as the end of the box's own last paragraph, where that one has none: 90 justified source units of the 87, under a centred paragraph's end), a whatsit (a unit's own end mark, which `AXT-ALIGN` reads), an adjustment, a glue before its last or a discretionary, none while the gate is off: a point after `\\`'s break made a last line of its own and re-broke its paragraph, one after amsart's caption kern stopped the class's `\unkern`, one in a contents list left hyperref's links unstable, one after an end mark moved a microtype line by 0.04 pt; and an ink unit whose last glyph its paragraph's end follows takes that code (`ink-units.mjs` `alignOf`), as does a unit inside a paragraph whose start stands before it with nothing ended between (the lines of a paragraph TeX broke with `\\`): either way with nothing between its last glyph and the end, no paragraph begun, no unit's end or start mark and no bracket. An ink paragraph ended at a source unit's end mark has no end of its own, and the paragraph after it may begin with no start, so the end after both is not the unit's; a table's first cell ends a paragraph right after the cell's start (2610.21084v1's captions, whose own paragraphs are justified, would have read its centred end); a unit that is not its paragraph's last line (a paragraph the ink cutter made several units of, 2610.11256v1's hypotheses) takes the code of the first end after it in its body — past a column's or a page's end to the next body, a float passed over — where that code is not centred, and nothing where it is (it may be a line TeX set between two paragraphs). A running head takes only its own paragraph's end, else is centred where it stands on its page's middle, as before. Where nothing tells, the door reads the unit's lines (several whose centres agree and widths differ, or one on its page's middle). Over the 87 papers of the release sweep's list (the gate pack's 7 among them) every glyph and box of the marked original and of our final pass stays where it was, page by page.
- **A placeholder's colour** (its glyphs' fill: hyperref's coloured links and citations, a coloured formula) is extraction: the layout file's placeholder row ends with the colour more than half its inked glyphs are filled with, where that is not black (`0xRRGGBB`; `MIXED_FILL`, -1, where no one colour holds more than half), read from arXiv's operator list (`layout/ink.mjs`, every colour space as PDF.js turns it to RGB; a pattern's fill counts as none).
- **A character's colour** is an attribute of the original's glyphs, as its font is (E1 of the residuals' batch R2, 2026-10-19). Each text item of a page's draw carries its characters' fills (`layout/fills.mjs` `itemFills`: the glyphs of the page's ink on the item's baseline within its extent, read in order as the item's own text; an item they do not spell exactly — turned, a glyph too many or too few, a combined accent set as two glyphs, a right-to-left run — tells none, nor does a Type 3 glyph whose procedure paints its own colours), and a page read live tells the same from the list PDF.js drew it by, its render's or its early pixel read's, with no second parse: a walk of the glyphs alone, `LIVE_FILLS_MS` at most, past which the page tells none (`run.mjs` `liveFillsOf`, with the host's `OPS`). That budget is a clock: on a loaded or slow machine a page may tell none where it tells them on another. The lab's gates walk with none (`openProto`'s and `openLayer`'s `fillsMs: Infinity`, the layer gate's run and every door gate's), so that a gate's run draws and counts alike at any load. The reader's character holds it as `st.fill`. The drawing reads it three ways. A unit's base weight, slant, small capitals, family and colour are those most of its matched glyphs hold outside every piece that may set that attribute (a style pair or switch in any spelling, `{\bf …}` too; a colour piece, a link, a paper's own macro), and of all its glyphs only where none lies outside; a tie goes to regular, upright, serif and black, else to the unit's first glyph (`layer2.mjs` `measuredStyle`). A glyph's slant is read as it would be without the `\emph` and `\em` toggles around it, so that a unit wholly inside one is drawn as the original. A piece that may set colour and that no `colours` row tells takes its own glyphs' colour; a row (TeX's, PR-C) wins. A unit read without its source pieces (a lab record, not a reader's) keeps the reading before: the majority, its groups' share taken off (`baseOf`), and a colour only where every glyph whose fill is told holds the same one. A rendering of the page's own characters (a citation, a reference, an equation's number) is drawn in runs of its characters' fills: `[16]` keeps its black brackets and blue digits. The placeholder's row fill above stays only for a character whose fill is not told. Word-level colour inside a sentence stays a limit: no majority paints a unit. On the wire, a styled pair whose two ends stand where the wire is cut anyway (a forced break, a display or an item beside it, never an inline formula, which the translator moves as a word; a kept pair's edge; the unit's end) keeps its markers (`translate/mt.mjs` `classOf`, the boundary rule). The draw's item rows carry the fills as their tenth value (`BUNDLE5` `'7'`); the boundary rule raises `TRANSLATE_VERSION` to `'4'` and `PIPELINE_VERSION` to `'22'`, whose copies carry every unit whose wire it leaves alone (`mt.mjs` `boundaryChanges`): over 137 papers' sources 126 of 36,136 units, in 29 papers, are asked again.
- **A unit's size and its small capitals, where NFSS fakes them** (the owner's report of 2026-10-24 on staging: 2602.23285v2's appendix headings, page 15, drawn far smaller than the original in zh, es and de, and in es and de with no small capitals) are read from the original's glyphs as its other attributes are. The Times family has no small capitals of its own, nor have PSNFSS's other base-35 families: NFSS sets `\scshape` in a virtual face (`ptmrc8t` and its kind) that draws each lowercase letter as the upright face's capital at 0.8 of the size, in the same PDF font as the capitals, so that no font name says small capitals, and the `\sc` of a class's heading (ICLR's and ICML's subsections, IEEEtran's sections and table captions) is in no piece of the unit's source. The alignment pairs each page letter with the source letter it spells (case-blind): a capital paired with a lowercase source letter, set at most `SMALL_CAPS_SHARE` (0.9) of the median size of the unit's letters and digits whose case TeX kept, is a faked small capital (`layer2.mjs` `smallCapsOf`), and their median size over the capitals' is the share the unit sets them at (`capsRatio`, to the hundredth: 0.80 on 1711 of the 1747 faked capitals of the 32 papers of the corpus that set any, 0.71 on the other 36, one table's at 7 pt in 2608.27181; a unit's own, never a paper's). The unit's size is the median of its glyphs with those set aside: its capitals', the size TeX was asked for (2602.23285v2's "A.2 DYNAMIC SPECTRAL GRAPH STRUCTURE", 21 of its 25 letters at 7.97 pt, is read at 9.96 where it was read at 7.97, the median its small capitals made). It is set in small capitals where most of its glyphs that can tell say so (`capsVote`: a faked small capital says so, a lowercase source letter drawn as itself says not, and where the unit has faked ones a capital or a digit of a face that names no small capitals says nothing, since NFSS draws it alike in either shape), of the glyphs outside every piece that may set them as `measuredStyle` reads every attribute; a unit read without its source pieces (the gate's, the lab's) of all its letters, its `\textsc` groups' share taken off as `baseOf` takes off its other groups'. A capital paired with a lowercase source letter at the others' size is a capital of the text's: a class's `\MakeTextUppercase` (REVTeX's section titles, 2610.21288v1's "I. INTRODUCTION", drawn "I. INTRODUCCIÓN" in Spanish where it was "Introducción"), the unit set in them (`upper`) where most of its letters that can tell are, and its translation drawn in the target's capitals at its size. A face of real small capitals (cmcsc10, LM Roman Caps, a face with an SC name) draws its lowercase letters as themselves, and a unit with no letter of the source's own case to read the sizes against reads as before. In a CJK target, which has no case, a unit set in small capitals is laid at its nominal size × `CJK_CAPS_SIZE` (`layer2.mjs` `unitSizeOf`; 1, the owner's of 2026-10-24). **Every drawn thing is read so, whatever its kind** (the owner's report of 2026-10-29 on 2010.11929v2 p9: ICLR's `\sc` "REFERENCES" drawn in Chinese smaller than the Conclusion's and Acknowledgements' headings beside it). A babel name's size is its characters' with its faked small capitals set aside, where the class changed its case (the file's `CAPITALS`: a capital at `SMALL_CAPS_SHARE` of its largest letter or less), and it is drawn in small capitals as such a unit is, its word in its own case, never as a case change's capitals (`layer2.mjs` `nameStyleOf`; it was drawn at the file's size, the most of its glyphs', 9.6 against its capitals' 12). An ink unit's source is our page's own text, its case as drawn, so no letter of it tells a case change: where every cased glyph of it is a capital, a capital at `SMALL_CAPS_SHARE` or less of its full letters' size is a faked small capital by its size alone (`inkSmallCaps`), and a unit with a lowercase glyph reads as before (a paragraph with a drop cap is none).
- **Small capitals the layer draws itself, and capitals.** A run in small capitals in a face with none of its own (no smcp feature: Nimbus Roman, Nimbus Sans, FreeMono; `rules/font-roles.mjs` `ownSmallCaps`) is drawn as NFSS's virtual faces draw it: each lowercase letter as the face's capital at the unit's `capsRatio` of the size, `SMALL_CAPS_RATIO` (0.8) where its page tells none (a face of real small capitals the target's face has none of), the other characters as they are; each run of one case is a token of its own, glued to the one before and never hyphenated, measured in the face with no small capitals asked of it as it is drawn, a `<tspan>` at its share of the size (`layer2.mjs` `caseRuns`, `selfCaps`; `lineRuns`' `sc`, which `svgOfUnit`, `runEdge`, `lineExtent` and the breaker's cut read). Case is each character's, whatever its script, in the target's own case mapping (`upperOf`, `toLocaleUpperCase` of the target, the root's for a code no locale reads, never the device's: Turkish i to İ and ı to I, German ß to SS measured as the expanded capitals, Greek's tonos dropped, Lithuanian's dot above dropped after i, a mark with its letter): a Latin word inside a CJK translation takes its own small capitals or capitals, a CJK character, Arabic, Devanagari and Thai none, a digit or a mark is drawn as it is. A rendering of the page's own characters keeps the small capitals its page sets (a macro's text in faked small capitals, which the PDF's text gives in capitals: a capital the page sets at most `SMALL_CAPS_SHARE` of the unit's size is drawn as a small one, `smallCapsAt`; 2602.23285v2's `\method`, "ODEBRAIN" in typewriter capitals at the text's size, is drawn as it is), a formula's text takes neither small capitals nor capitals, and a babel name in a face of real small capitals is drawn as a run is (`nameRuns`). No rule asks a browser to synthesize any (`capsRule`): synthesized, they were each browser's, Chromium's at 0.7 of the size (Nimbus Roman's "Discusión: perspectivas clave" at 20 px, 237.31 px), Firefox's at 0.8 (266.93), WebKit's at two widths (its SVG 241.57, its canvas 237.30), where the layer's own are 266.91 in all three. A face's smcp feature draws its own (Libertine, CMU, XCharter and the other faces `METRICS` says have one), and Latin Modern's caps face, whose letters are its small capitals, is asked none (`capsLetters`, `fonts.mjs`), so that it is measured as it is drawn: asked them, the canvas measured capitals it synthesized, 1125 against the 1187 px it drew. `tests/e2e/layer-small-caps.mjs` (`pnpm e2e:small-caps`) lays and draws ICLR's heading in Spanish, German and Russian, a paragraph's `\textsc` run and a REVTeX heading in capitals in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit: each run's glyphs are drawn as wide as they were measured (within 0.02 px and a sixtieth of a pixel a glyph, Firefox's unit; WebKit's `getComputedTextLength` gives a run unkerned though it draws it kerned, so the test reads `getSubStringLength`), and every item is laid at the same place in the three (within 0.00002 PDF units in the role table's faces). Measured on the gate pack (13785c79, 32 outputs, the model tier in the rules gate's configuration, base `next` 3713cf45, and 5e723185 before it alike): no measure worse and no page moved; the units' own records (`--dump`) move in 2608.04322v1 alone, against `next` its section headings at 7.97 to 9.96 pt and its table captions at 6.38 to 7.97 (84 units on 63 pages of its 7 outputs), against the first step of this change, which left the browser to synthesize them, 60 of those, their small capitals at 0.8 where Chromium set 0.7, two captions a line longer (de, fr); over those 7 outputs the pixel tier's translated share rises from 82.7 % to 83.3 % and its lost-ink regions fall from 29 to 28, as at the first step. No unit of the other 25 outputs moved (none in Latin Modern's caps face, none in capitals of the text's). A limit, the front end's: an explicit `\MakeUppercase{…}` (`\MakeTextUppercase`, `\uppercase`) in a unit's source is one placeholder of `source/latex-front.mjs`, its words left the original's, and `\section{\MakeUppercase{Related Work}}` makes no unit at all; none of the 37 930 units of the 158 local sources holds one.
- **A translator's stutter** (a word written twice in a row: Microsoft's "konformen konformen" in 2608.16117's German abstract, the M1 survey) is drawn as the translator wrote it. `layer-proto/stutter.mjs` drew such a word once, where the unit's source set no word twice; it went with the rules audit of 2026-11-04 (T-D4, the owner's ruling: the format is ours, the translator's wording is not): on the gate pack it changed 3 of 6,397 units, one word each, at the cost of a scan of every source and piece, a tuned five-letter minimum, and a drawn text that differed from the rows, the cache and the plain text the word table maps back to.

The store holds the translator's raw answer, judged again on every read, and the background's rows answer a paper opened again with nothing sent.
- **A file is refused by its schema, never by its maker.** `parseLayout` refuses a layout file whose `schema` is not 5 (4 before a found placeholder's row ended with its glyphs' fill, 2026-10-19; 3 before a display group's later displays were written `JOINED`, their ink the group's first display's, and a LOST piece outside its unit's lines `OUTSIDE`, the LOST survey of 2026-10-15; 2 before the paper's `\lineskip` and `\lineskiplimit`, 1 before the babel names, D1a) (the add-on's manifest, refused by its own `schema` the same way, went with REMOVAL 8); the file's `layout` is read for its shape (a version token) and never compared, so a reader opens what a newer maker wrote. A change of the file's fields, bounds or meaning raises its `schema` and `BUNDLE`, not `LAYOUT` or `REMOVAL` — but the layout file's schemas 4 and 5 did not raise `BUNDLE` (the controller's ruling of 2026-10-15: the next `BUNDLE`, 4, is the pipeline lane's new wire). This breaks the contract's promise for `b3`: a released reader of schema 3 asking `b3` of content this engine makes would refuse it whole, as `parseLayout` refuses any schema but its own. It holds only because no released reader asks for such content: the web's pin does not move before `BUNDLE` 4 lands, and moves with it (M1).

### 18.3 Bump rules

- **A change of a value in the rule set** raises `version` by one. Nothing else moves.
- **A field added, removed or renamed, a range or enumeration changed, or the engine reading a field differently** raises `RULES_SCHEMA`.
  - The new schema publishes under `s<n+1>`, and `s<n>`'s pointer stays at its last set.
  - A newer engine's built-in carries the new field, and the published set gains it in the same pull request.
- **Adding a language:** the published set gains its entry first. Engines that do not offer it ignore it. The engine that offers it follows.
- **A drawing code change that keeps every field's meaning** bumps nothing. The layer gate measures it, and the live-engines check guards each published set on the engines that read it.
- **Extraction and translation changes** bump their identity as §18.2 says. A change that touches two kinds bumps both.
- **A unit cut that moves raises `PIPELINE_VERSION`**, whatever else it leaves alone: a stored translation is found again by an
  identity naming the pipeline, and one made for the old cut given to the new one names pieces it does not have (#435 re-cut
  2610.19860's `\url{…}` from seven pieces to five under PIPELINE 25; staging gave unit 176 its old row, which the door dropped,
  and the unit stayed English). `tests/pdf-reader/unit-cut.test.ts` holds it mechanically: each unit's kind and its pieces'
  types over a few sources the repository keeps (the sample paper; 2610.19860's llncs `\url`), recorded with the
  `PIPELINE_VERSION` they were recorded under (`golden/unit-cut.json`). The cut moving under the same version fails, and so does
  the version moving with the cut not recorded again; `WRITE_UNIT_CUT=1` records it, and refuses while the cut moved and the
  version did not.
- **A bump of `PIPELINE_VERSION` or `REMOVAL` writes its line in §18.10** and its identity's row in §18.2; `pipeline/versions.mjs`
  holds the constant alone.
- **The classification test of §18.1 decides which kind a change is.** When it is unclear, the change takes the more expensive kind and the pull request says why.

### 18.4 Bundles: the reader names its contract, the server names the content

Were a reader to ask for a bundle by all of its own versions, every extraction fix would strand each released extension for new papers until the store shipped its update. So the reader names only what it can verify, its contract, and the server names the content:

```
ctag (the reader's contract) = b<BUNDLE>-j<PDFJS>
vtag (the content)           = <ctag>-p<PIPELINE>-l<LAYOUT>-r<REMOVAL>      // the R2 key
GET /api/v1/layer/<id>v<n>/<ctag>   302 to /api/v1/layer/<id>v<n>/<vtag>, the newest made under that ctag (max-age=300)
                                    and, when that vtag is not the server's own, the server's own prepare begun in the background
                                    | 202 Preparing | 404 | 429
GET /api/v1/layer/<id>v<n>/<vtag>   200 immutable
```

- **The engine's half:** `CTAG` and `VTAG` are `layer-proto/bundle.mjs`'s. `readBundle` compares the contract's two versions (`bundle`, `pdfjs`) with the reader's and names the maker's three and the image's, never comparing them; the layout file and the manifest it holds are refused by their schemas (§18.2).
- **What it buys:** an extraction fix reaches every reader on its next open, at one compile a paper, with no release.
- **What it costs:** one redirect, and the first open after a bump reads the previous bundle while the new one is made.
- The routes are the web's (its layer API v1); this section is the contract they are built to.

### 18.5 The rule set's fields

The rule set is one schema-validated file, `rules/layout-rules.json`: configuration in a closed vocabulary (numbers, booleans, enumerations and short lists of characters), never a pattern, a selector or code. It has three scopes. A **script's** fields (`Hans`, `Hant`, `Jpan`, `Kore`, `Latn`, `Cyrl`) are v0's own `Params`; a **language** (a target) may override any of them field by field, and has its own `labels`; the **set** holds the hyphenation minimums. `resolveRules(set, target)` gives one target's rules, and a set that fails any bound is refused whole, naming the field. **A set holds a `languages` entry for every one of `TARGETS`**, the targets either reader offers: the web's eight (`zh`, `zh-TW`, `ja`, `ko`, `de`, `fr`, `es`, `ru`) and the extension's Portuguese (`pt`). A set that omits one is refused when it is read, not when that language's run opens; other languages (`pt-BR`, the language wave's) may be added beside them. `TARGETS` must cover every language of `VERIFIED` (`session/verified.mjs`, compared by language and script: `zh-Hant` there is `zh-TW` here), which a test holds, so a language added to `VERIFIED` is added to `TARGETS` and to the built-in file with it. The engine's built-in copy is the fallback. The words are `RULES_FIELDS`', the lab's rows.

| Field | Scope | Group | Range or values | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | script | fit | an ordering of track, borrow, lead, shrink | The order in which the fit turns its knobs when a translation does not fit: tracking, borrowing free space below, the leading, the size. |
| `leadBase` | script | fit | 0.8 to 2, step 0.05 | The translation's line pitch, × the original's line pitch. |
| `leadFloor` | script | fit | 0.8 to 2, step 0.05 | The tightest line pitch the fit falls back to, × the original's. |
| `trackMin` | script | fit | -0.3 to 0, step 0.005 | The tightest letter spacing the fit uses, in em (zero or less). |
| `compressMax` | script | fit | `0`, `1`, `2` | How far full-width punctuation is compressed: 0 not at all, 1 at a line's start and between two marks, 2 every mark. |
| `centredPunct` | script | fit | yes or no | Whether punctuation is centred in its em box (Traditional Chinese): no mark is then compressed or hung. |
| `borrow` | script | fit | `0`, `1` | Whether a unit may borrow the free space below its last line (1) or not (0). |
| `borrowGap` | script | fit | 0 to 2, step 0.05 | The gap kept clear under borrowed space, × the original's line pitch. |
| `floor` | script | fit | 0.4 to 1, step 0.05 | The smallest size the fit sets a unit at, × the original's size. |
| `step` | script | fit | 0.01 to 0.1, step 0.005 | The size step between the fit's tries, × the original's size. |
| `further` | script | fit | some of widen, shrink, in that order | The steps tried, in order, for a unit the fit leaves clipped: widen its lines, shrink below the floor. |
| `floorMin` | script | fit | 0.3 to 1, step 0.05 | The smallest size the last of those steps reaches, × the original's size. |
| `cjkJust` | script | fit | 0 to 1, step 0.01 | The most a line may open between CJK characters to justify, in em a gap. |
| `spaceMin` | script | fit | 0.3 to 1, step 0.05 | The least a word space shrinks to, × its natural width. |
| `spaceMax` | script | fit | 0 to 3, step 0.05 | The most a word space opens to justify a line, × its natural width. |
| `autospace` | script | fit | 0 to 1, step 0.05 | The space set between CJK text and Latin letters or digits, in em. |
| `adaptiveFill` | script | fit | band, track, size; or none | Spreading each unit's lines over its original's space, the page's body units to one leading and one size, the leading within a band of the page's own paragraphs' (D6, page by page); empty keeps the script's leading on the original's pitch alone (B). |
| `fillLead` | script | fit | 1 to 3, step 0.05, or none | The loosest line pitch the fill spreads a unit's lines to, in em of the size it is drawn at; empty: the original's own pitch. |
| `fillLeadRel` | script | fit | 1 to 3, step 0.05, or none | The loosest line pitch the fill spreads a unit's lines to, as a multiple of the original's own pitch, where that is looser than the pitch above; empty: the pitch above alone. |
| `keepAll` | script | breaking | yes or no | Whether lines break only at spaces (Korean and the alphabets) rather than between any two CJK characters. |
| `cjkQuotes` | script | breaking | yes or no | Whether curly quotes, dashes, the ellipsis and the middle dot are set as CJK characters. |
| `noStart` | script | breaking | a list of characters | The characters no line starts with. |
| `noEnd` | script | breaking | a list of characters | The characters no line ends with. |
| `hyphen` | script | breaking | `0`, `1` | Whether a Latin word is hyphenated at a line's end (1) or not (0). |
| `latinPatterns` | script | breaking | `en`, `de`, `fr`, `es`, `pt`, `it`, `nl`, `pl`, `tr`, `id`, `cs`, `sv` | The hyphenation patterns a Latin word uses. |
| `cyrillicPatterns` | script | breaking | `ru`, `uk`, `bg` | The hyphenation a Cyrillic word uses: Russian's rules (ru), or a language's own patterns. |
| `cellClear` | script | cells | 0 to 5, step 0.1 | The room kept between a table cell's text and a rule over or under it, in PDF units. |
| `cellCapMin` | script | cells | 0.3 to 1, step 0.05 | The smallest share of the size a cell's text may be capped to between its rules. |
| `cjkFaces` | script | faces | group; or none | The CJK family the script is drawn in, at Regular and Bold; empty for an alphabet. |
| `labels` | language | labels | figure, table, abstract, ref, bib, contents, listfigure, listtable, appendix, index, proof, preface, glossary; or none | A float's label and each generated heading babel names (Abstract, References, Contents, …) in this language's words; an empty word, or none, keeps the original's. |
| `hyphenation.minWord` | set | hyphenation | 2 to 20 | The shortest word, in letters, that is hyphenated. |
| `hyphenation.en.left` | set | hyphenation | 1 to 6 | The fewest letters English leaves before a hyphen. |
| `hyphenation.en.right` | set | hyphenation | 1 to 6 | The fewest letters English leaves after a hyphen. |
| `hyphenation.de.left` | set | hyphenation | 1 to 6 | The fewest letters German leaves before a hyphen. |
| `hyphenation.de.right` | set | hyphenation | 1 to 6 | The fewest letters German leaves after a hyphen. |
| `hyphenation.fr.left` | set | hyphenation | 1 to 6 | The fewest letters French leaves before a hyphen. |

| `hyphenation.uk.right` | set | hyphenation | 1 to 6 | The fewest letters Ukrainian leaves after a hyphen. |
| `hyphenation.bg.left` | set | hyphenation | 1 to 6 | The fewest letters Bulgarian leaves before a hyphen. |
| `hyphenation.bg.right` | set | hyphenation | 1 to 6 | The fewest letters Bulgarian leaves after a hyphen. |

### 18.6 Hosts: opening a layer with a rule set

What a host (the web's door, the extension's session, the gate, the lab) calls. Each host owns its fetch and its cache; the engine owns the reading.

- **`openLayer({ …, rules? })`** (`layer-proto/reader.mjs`) and **`openProto({ …, rules? })`** (`layer-proto/run.mjs`, v0's open, which the gate and the lab call) take the set that every choice made for the target is read from, resolved once at the open. Absent: `BUILTIN_RULES`, the engine's copy of the published file. Neither takes a single rule as an argument.
- **`firstFaceOf(target, rules?)`** is the host's early face request, made before the paper's family is known: the CJK body face the set names for the target, else `null`. Pass it the set the layer will be opened with (absent: the built-in).
- **`stats().rules`** is `{ schema, version }` of the set the layer was opened with (`ProtoRun.rules` likewise). While no set was passed it is the built-in's. A host records it.
- **`readRules(bytes, { etag })`** (`rules/layout.mjs`) reads an answer's body as a set and returns `{ set, sha256 }`. It refuses, naming the field, a body of more than `RULES_CAP` (65,536) bytes, a body of malformed UTF-8, more JSON values than `RULES_VALUES`, text that is not JSON, and a set that fails the schema or a cross-check; a refused set is never partly used.
  - **`etag`** is the answer's `ETag` header, given where there is one. It is compared with the SHA-256 of the bytes given to `readRules`, the body decoded of any content coding, and a different one is refused with the field `etag`. Two forms are read: the strong `"<sha256>"` and the weak `W/"<sha256>"`, which a CDN may put in the strong one's place when it recodes the body. Any other form is refused. A host passes the header as it came, or `null`.
- **The reader's choice** is the same in both readers: the server's answer, when one comes and is read; else the last read answer the reader cached; else the built-in. The server is the authority, so a lower version is taken like any other. A refused answer is ignored and counted, and the reader keeps what it had. The set is chosen when the composed document is ready, and an answer that has not come by then serves the next open: a rule-set fetch never delays a page.
- **A `rules` must come from `readRules` or `parseRules`**, or be `BUILTIN_RULES`. The door checks only a set's shape (an object holding `scripts` and `languages`, else a `TypeError`), not its values; a set built by hand can fail to resolve a target, or draw badly. `BUILTIN_RULES` is frozen to every depth and typed read-only, so a set to edit is `structuredClone(BUILTIN_RULES)`.

### 18.7 Layout decisions of 2026-10-23

Decisions made by the maintainer by looking at crops, and what they changed. The drawing code reads them at read time: none moves a version token (§18.1), and `RULES_SCHEMA` rises only for the field the fill rule adds.

**A Chinese or Japanese line breaks before an inline formula (PR #438).** After a CJK character or mark a formula crop no longer glues to it: a script that breaks between CJK characters (`keepAll` false) may end the line before the crop, as xeCJK's `\CJKecglue` allows. A mark no line ends with (an opening bracket), a lead's end and a kern stay glued.

**A letter-spaced line squeezes (PR #438).** A line takes the group it misses only when, without it, it would stretch more than `STRETCH_MIN` = 0.05 em a gap, the overflow is at most what it can give, and that squeeze a gap is less than the stretch. What it can give: the blank halves of comma-, full-stop- and bracket-type marks, spaces down to `spaceMin`, then `SQUEEZE` = 0.02 em a gap, never past the tracking floor (`trackMin`) and never below the tracking the page fill raised (`fitTrack`). Only marks whose ink sits in one half of the em in every face the layer draws are cut: comma, full stop, enumeration comma, brackets and quotes. Never the colon, the semicolon, `!` or `?`: the CJK face centres them, and a question mark cut by half ran 0.22 em into the next character. Measured on the 53 papers of the release route's sweep: lines more than 0.15 em a gap over their unit's least 403 to 265, ragged CJK lines 625 to 457, the owner's line (2610.10069 page 7, unit 49) 0.194 to 0.022 em a gap. Long formulas stay stretched: no new cap and no new ragged rule.

**The fill's top is relative to the original's pitch for Chinese (`fillLeadRel`).** The fill spreads a unit's lines up to a top; the em top (`fillLead`, 2 em of the size drawn) equals the original's own pitch on a double-spaced original and is below what the frame allows, so the paragraph ended early (2610.11256 page 12, unit 75: 7 lines of 9). The top is now the looser of the em top and `fillLeadRel` = 1.3 times the original's pitch, scaled by the fit's size; 1.3 is the engine's own Chinese `leadBase`, so Chinese reads at the same density as its original. Chosen by the owner by eye on crops, 2026-10-23, over 1.5 and over replacing the em top outright (which tightened 3,035 single-spaced units). Simplified and Traditional Chinese only; Japanese and Korean stay off until measured. Measured on the 53 papers (Chinese): 168 units whose leading shows change by a median of 0.20 pitch (0.36 em), none tighter, none past its frame, no new collision, and a page of single-spaced originals is unchanged. It acts only where the em cap binds: a single-spaced original keeps its top, and the band, tracking, size and the leftover below the paragraph are unchanged. For the same two scripts the halving that finds the loosest leading now tries the top itself (it was left untried when the fraction of a step was under a half, so the unit took neither tracking nor the page's size). With that step more pages grow, and a unit of one line keeps its own size in these scripts: it has no frame to spread over, and a larger size only carries its ink past the original's line (a note under a table's rule, 2610.21924 page 18, whose formulas touched the rule at x1.1).

**A unit split by its displays is laid a run at a time (2026-10-24).** The text between two displays is set on the slots between them alone, so each run of a unit is a text block of its own (the rubric below), and each takes its own state: the first of the fit's states at which its own text fits its own slots (`layer2.mjs` `runsOf`, `layoutRuns`), its size and leading its own, and the page fill fills each run as a unit of the page the unit begins on, the page's target reading the unit once, as one, at its fit as one, so that its neighbours keep the rhythm they had (`run.mjs` `fillUnitsOf`, `fillPass`; voting a run at a time moved 55 of 158 such pages' targets and 64 single-run neighbours); its runs grow with the page's size together, read by the unit's line count (`fillPage`; a run of one line had stayed at 1.0 beside its unit's others at 1.1); filling each run on its own first page was measured and declined ( on 7 Chinese papers, link colours lost 2 to 9 and paragraph ends letter-spaced 4 to 14). A run opens at a display alone: a forced break that opens another frame (tokensOf2's `brk`) keeps its frames in the run, as the unit's own walk sets them. Where a run set larger would carry a token to a later page than the unit's fit set it, the unit is laid as one. The owner's ruling of 2026-10-09 (sizes per unit where some must shrink) is carried to its natural unit: only a cramped run shrinks. Every run fits at the state the unit's fit found, so each comes out there or more naturally. One tracking a paragraph: the walk tightens a run's tracking (and its CJK punctuation's compression) before it shrinks it, so a cramped run came out tighter than a roomy one, and the page fill tracked a roomy run further still; the paragraph read at two letter spacings, its roomy part's last line looser than its own tightest lines (the sweep's (j), paragraph end letter-spaced: 967 rows over 53 papers in Chinese where `next` has 12). Each run is laid again from the tightest tracking any of them needs (`P.runTrack`, the walk's first state), and the page fill gives a unit's runs the least fill tracking any of them takes (`fillPage`); size and leading stay each run's own. The page fill keeps a unit's text on the pages its fit set it (`layer2.mjs` `keepsPages`, read for a unit's runs; read for every unit, it moves 34 more pages of 19 Chinese papers, a change of its own left for later): a looser leading holds fewer lines on a page's frame, and the page cuts (`pageCutsOf`) keep text only from the page before; 2610.21884v1's unit 10 in Chinese, a paragraph over pages 1 and 2, had its last run filled to a leading of 1.61 and a sentence of page 1 drawn at the top of page 2 (the sweep's (i), sentence drawn on another page). 2602.23285v2's unit 35 in Japanese (seven lines, then two after each of two displays) was set at 0.85 throughout because the two lines after eq. 5 held their text from 0.85 alone, its first run five tight lines over two empty ones; it is now 1.0, 1.0 and 0.85, its first run six lines at a leading of 1.1. A unit of one run (no display, or a paragraph over a page break, one run), a table's cell, a unit the fit's further steps set (widened, run past its display, below the floor) and one whose runs do not each fit alone are laid as before, byte for byte, and filled as before: measured over the Chinese sweep set (19 papers traced, 2026-10-24), every page with no line of a unit laid in runs is drawn byte for byte as `next` draws it; the 3 that differ each hold the lines of such a unit begun on the page before (2610.21201v1 page 23, 2610.21026v1 pages 18 and 33). Running the text on past the display was rejected as the way to lay a unit's runs: it moves text across the display, breaking where the paragraph meets its equation. It stays the walk's last resort, and only that (`fit/walk.ts` layoutUnit2 with the breaker's `strict` off, the unit's layout `spilled`: the approved prototype's iteration 3 of 2026-10-06, laid at its most natural state since 2026-10-17, 2608.16117's German page 10): where in order nothing fits at any state, a run whose text fits its own slots at no state, the floor and the further steps included, the text runs on past the display. The cause is capacity: the display's place on the page is TeX's, and the reply's text between two displays may be longer than the original's, most of all where the translator moves a display's placeholder or merges the words around it (2610.21106v1's Remark 1.3 in Chinese: Google and Microsoft alike dropped "where" and set the second display after "under conditions …", so that the one line TeX left for "where", ended 2 em before the display it set with its short skip, was asked to hold a clause). What it costs: the display stands inside the run's text, not where the reply put it. **The line before a run's boundary is a last line (2026-11-13, the coordinator's ruling on that remark).** Where a display begins TeX breaks the paragraph so far as a paragraph (tex.web §1145, ⟨Go into display math mode⟩: `line_break(display_widow_penalty)`, which appends `\parfillskip`, §816), so the line before a display ends where its text ends, ragged, and never in a discretionary hyphen. One rule on both paths: on the in-order walk the region's break ends that line (the breaker's `blockTo`, a run's forced break in `runsOf`); on the run past, the line before a kept region the next slot lies after (a slot's `after`: whatever TeX set between the partial paragraphs, by the run boundary, no list of kinds) ends at a legal break that is no hyphenation point and is set ragged (`break.mjs` beforeBoundary, advance). The remark with Google's text had "Hes-" (after two Chinese characters) on the line before its second display and "sian" after it; the line now ends after the two characters, and "Hessian" stands whole after the display. A CJK phrase the run past cuts between two of its characters (Microsoft's text of the same remark: its word for "Hessian quotient equation" cut after its third character) is a legal break, drawn as production draws it (LATER). Measured over the 90 pairs (round B14's bundles, the reader gate's entry, both stores): a unit runs past a boundary in 4 units on the door's rows (Microsoft) and 8 on Google's; the line before the boundary ended inside a word in 1 and 4 of them before the rule, in none after. What moves: 3 units on the door's rows and 5 on Google's, each its line before the boundary (ragged, or its word whole after the boundary), and one of them its size: 2608.16117v1-de's unit 28, a paragraph of nine displays that fitted at 0.875 of its size (Google's text: 0.85) only by cutting "Periodizitätsbeziehung" with display (33), is laid one state smaller (0.85; 0.825), where the text before that display lies on its own lines and the display stands after the colon, as the reply sets it. One state of the fit on one paragraph of the 90 pairs is the law's price (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-13: the cut word is the fault, and a size step a reader does not see is none, the owner's words of 2026-11-12 on the page's fill, §18.57). The tap's replay against today's restates today's line before a boundary as a last line (`packages/typeset/tests/replay/tap.ts` lastBeforeRegion, lastLineIn); over the tap's 123 ledgers the walk replays 32,396 of 32,589 rounds as today did (32,401 before): the five are the rule's, four lines' mode and that paragraph's state. A run's lines carry its size, scale and state (`seg`), which the drawing, the word table, the links and the checker read a line by; the even pass, which sets a page's units at one size, lays a unit as one again. The lab's reader dump states a unit's size as its layout's, its first run's, as the baseline's harness does; where a later run is drawn at another size it states each line's too (`DumpUnit.sizes`, `packages/typeset/tests/replay/display.ts`), and the check that each page's lay lays a unit alike (I6: `gate.ts`, `gate-l1.ts`, `selfDiffer`) compares them, so that every run is checked at the size it is drawn at (2026-11-12: a theorem of 2610.40645v1 in Japanese, its line before a display at 10.64 pt and its lines after it at 10.91 on the next page, read as 10.64 on both).

**Judging a block (the rubric for samples and rulings).** The owner, 2026-10-23: judge per block, not per line. A block is better, the same or worse than its base on three questions. (i) Uniformity inside the block: no line stretched or squeezed out of step with the others. (ii) The block lands in place: each sentence at the right place in its paragraph, paragraph boundaries where the original has them. (iii) Rhythm against its neighbours: leading and density consistent with the page's other blocks. A shift under one pitch counts as the same. Line-level shifts and per-line offsets are normal and are not a verdict.

### 18.8 Layout decisions of 2026-10-29

Two of lane B's five typesetting rules, B1 and B2, adopted by the maintainer on its crops the same day
(`research/babeldoc-typography-2026-10-29/rules/`). Both were fields of the rule set, on in every script (`RULES_SCHEMA` 7, the set's version 7), and are the engine's own since `RULES_SCHEMA` 10; B2's
flags are the layout file's (LAYOUT 26).

**One pitch inside a block at the leading of 1 (`evenPitch`, B1).** At the original's leading a block's lines stood on the
original's baselines, so a gap TeX's `\lineskip` rule opened around a tall line of the original (a fraction, a radical, a
superscript over a capital) stayed under whatever line of the translation landed there, a formula on it or not (the
block-level audit's finding 1: 32 of 520 multi-line body units at leading 1 a point or more off their median pitch, up to
6.7 pt). The grid now closes each gap that rule set to the block's own pitch (`layer2.mjs` `evenGridOf`): a gap is the rule's
where it is no wider than the two lines' boxes in the file and `\lineskip` (blocks2's `opened`, the test `through` already
made between two blocks, the file's hundredths within 0.025); any other gap keeps its room, one that holds another block's
line or a `\vadjust` among them, and with no `\lineskip` told nothing is closed. The first line never moves (B′: a
paragraph's start stays), every line under a closed gap moves up by it, none stands lower than the original's own, and what
the closed gaps free stays at the block's foot. TeX's rule reopens a pair where the translation's own line is tall
(breakLines' `settle`, on the drawn ink, which stands in for TeX's boxes). Where the pair holds a formula TeX set in the
original, TeX measured that formula's room itself: the distance it set between the formula's line and the next (the formula
on the upper line) or the one before (on the lower), `texRoomOf`; where that distance already keeps the two lines' ink
`\lineskiplimit` apart, TeX's rule holds at it, and the pair is set no farther apart. So a formula that stays on its line
keeps the room TeX gave it, and one the translation sets on another line takes that room there. The experiment's rule (the
ink alone) reopened 1706.03762v7's Spanish unit 33 (page 4) by 2.35 under the fraction TeX had opened 2.26 under: the ink of
the fraction's radical passes its box, and the Spanish line under it is 0.04 taller by ink than the English one, so its last
line stood 0.09 past the original's last baseline and the whole unit was set a size smaller (0.975); with TeX's own room it
is at full size, its lines on TeX's baselines.

Measured on the gate pack (`d541e4c9`, 32 outputs, 5,403 laid units; the rule on against off, one engine): 9 units move, every
line up or still, none changes size (1706.03762 unit 33 in de, fr and ru by 0.83, 0.83 and 2.26; 1810.04805 unit 81 in de, es,
fr and ru by 1.0, in ja by 1.78; 2608.16117's German unit 76 by 2.61). The rules gate against `next` (a30a53ba): every target
pooled the same, one page moved (1706.03762v7-ru page 4, a blank line more at unit 33's foot: the room its formula no longer
needs, B′'s). A limit: a block's pitch is the median of its gaps (`pitch0`), so a block of three lines whose one gap TeX opened
has that gap for its pitch and keeps it.

**A unit TeX set flush left or flush right keeps that alignment (`keepAlign`, B2).** A unit TeX set `\raggedright`
(`flushleft`, ragged2e's `\RaggedRight`, a class's ragged heading) was justified, and one set `\raggedleft` (`flushright`) set
flush left. The layout file says how TeX set each paragraph, by TeX's word alone (§18.1, `UNIT_FLAG.FLUSH_LEFT`, `FLUSH_RIGHT`),
and the layer keeps it (`run.mjs` gives the unit's blocks `flush`, `placeItems` sets a flush-left line at its natural spacing,
ragged, and every line of a flush-right unit at the right edge, its last too); a centred unit follows `CENTRED` as before, and a
table's cell its own lines. On the gate pack: FLUSH_LEFT on 63 units of a target (1706.03762's 23 headings, 1810.04805's 29,
2609.26457's 7 title and author lines, 2608.16117's keywords), FLUSH_RIGHT on one (2307.16209's quote); on the pages the gate draws, the quote's lines are the ones that change (both now end at the right edge, the closing mark's blank half hung past it as a justified line's), the headings and the title lines being one line each in translation (1810.04805's two-line headings stand on its pages 14 and 16, past the gate's twelve). The
experiment vetoed a flag where arXiv's lines contradicted it (a unit told flush left whose lines all reach its column's edge:
2608.16117's abstract); the cause was the probe's, which read a boxed paragraph by the next one's `\par` under TeX Live 2023
(§18.1), and it reads the paragraph's own skips now: no flag is read off arXiv's lines.

### 18.9 Layout decisions of 2026-10-30

**A paragraph over a page break ends the earlier page with a full line.** Since E3c (2026-10-20) a unit over a page break
holds on each page its share of the paragraph. Until the follow-up below, that share was read off the alignment and the
row's sentences (the first source word on page B, `pageStartsOf`, and the share of the sentence the source sets before the
break), and a page-break token at that cut sent the text on to page B (`layoutCut`, laid at the fit's own state, kept where
it fits). The line ended at the cut wherever the share fell in it, so page A's last line stood short with the rest of
its measure empty, and a word could be split over the two pages: 1706.03762v7 in Chinese, §3.2.2, ended page 4 half a line
short and opened page 5 with the second half of the word for "output"; §6.2 ended page 8 a few characters into its second
line, the language pair split over pages 8 and 9. The owner, 2026-10-30: 「明明有空间，但我们却强行把内容挤到了下一行，导致这个地方直接空着。按空间预估来说下一行大概只显示"..图2所示"的几个字，其他文字填满上一行。」
("There was room, yet we forced the text onto the next line and left the place empty. By the room, the next line should
show only the few characters of '…as depicted in Figure 2', and the rest should fill the line above.")

The rule, as TeX never leaves a short line before a page break: the line that holds the cut ends where the breaker ends it
(full, set as any line: justified where it is full enough), and page B opens at the next line's start. A page's text begins
up to a line from where its source's does, and no further; a cut that falls on a line's first token breaks there. It lives in
the breaker (`breakLines`: a page-break token reached on an earlier page is held by the line in hand and sends the next line
to its page's first slot when that line closes), not in a token index fixed from the fit's lines, because every later lay of
the unit's tokens moves the line ends: the page fill's leading, tracking and the page's one size, and a unit's runs laid
apart. Where the line that holds the cut is its run's last (the run's text ends on it, or on the empty line a forced break
leaves after it, at a display or at the unit's end), page B would get none of the run though the source sets some there
(the sweep's invariant (i)): the breaker lays that line again on page B's first slot, whole, and the line before it ends page
A, full (`breakLines` `strand`, the one place a held break's fate is decided, so in every lay of the unit, the page fill's
included). Where that line is also the first of its run on page A, moving it would leave page A none of the run: the line is
laid again with the break at its token, as before, the one place a short line still stands before a page break (a run of one
line split over two pages). Two cuts in one line (a unit over three pages whose middle page holds less than a line of it):
the first sends the next line to its page, and that line holds the second; where no text is left after it, the third page
gets none. Every guard stays: no break before a display the text has not passed, none at a unit's
first token, and a cut never costs the unit its fit (laid at the fit's state, else as without it). The page fill's guard,
`keepsPages`, which refuses a state of a unit's run that sets text on a later page than its fit, lets a line after a page
break stand on the break's page: the tail of the line that holds it goes there at a looser state, and it is that page's text
in the source.

**By the paragraph's height, not its sentences (the owner's follow-up, 2026-10-30).** The owner, looking at the result:
「整个段落级语块在高度上覆盖得自不自然、有没有填满…位置对应上…不是追求做到 100% 精确匹配…最后一行有没有 100% 占满…其实并不重要」, and then 「好，就按这个做」
("What matters is whether the paragraph-level block covers its height naturally and fills it, and whether the positions
correspond; it is not about a 100 % exact match, nor whether the last line is 100 % full. OK, do it this way."): blocks stay
aligned, sentences need not, and the page changes at a natural line end, as LaTeX sets it. He holds a column break to the
same (1810.04805v2-zh, Appendix B's MRPC paragraph, unit 251 on page 15: three dense lines at the left column's foot, and
the right column only its last few characters, the room under them empty). So the cut is the paragraph's height alone
(`pageCutsOf`, from the fit's own lay), at every frame break: a frame is a column of a page (the unit's consecutive blocks
of one run on one page whose columns meet). Each run of the unit (its blocks between two displays) whose source lines
(`originalLines`: a line its rectangles cut in two is one) stand in more than one frame keeps in the frames before each
later frame k of its n laid lines, k = n × the source's lines before that frame over all of them, at the line end nearest
it that a token opens (a line a long token's cut opens, a URL's or a hyphenated word's tail, begins inside a token; ties the
later, the earlier frame the fuller), one line at least on each side; the break token (`frame`: the unit's block the frame
begins with) then stands at that line's first token; where the fit sets that line in that frame or later, the page fill alone
reads it, and only where the share holds within the page's band (§18.11, 2026-11-10). A run laid in one line is cut in it at each frame's share of its tokens, the
one short line. The breaker reaches a frame by its block (`blockBase` for a run laid alone), so a column break is laid,
held and stranded as a page break is. The breaker's held break, `strand` and `keepsPages` are as above. Nothing of the
alignment or the row's sentences is read for it any more: `pageStartsOf`, the sentence share and the row's sentences on the
unit the layer lays (`rows.mjs` `unitOf`) are gone. On the gate pack against `next` (`f98fa527`, the rule above): 55 units
are drawn otherwise, 25 over a page break, the column breaks' and those on the pages that hold them through the page fill's
reads; the owner's two paragraphs are as above (1706.03762v7-zh unit 40, three full lines on page 4 and the last characters
on page 5; unit 128, two full lines on page 8, one on page 9), and the MRPC paragraph (all of the paper's pages laid) is two
justified lines in the left column and two in the right, at the one state of the unit. The rules gate: de, es, fr and ru
unmoved; worse, zh frames with a blank line 23.3 % to 23.6 % and paragraph gaps tighter than the lines beside them 45 to 46
(0.17 to 0.174 a thousand cells), ko frames with a blank line 6.3 % to 6.8 % and paragraph gaps tighter 12 to 13 (0.17 to
0.18); better, paragraph gaps a pitch or more wider in zh (22.7 % to 22.0 %), ko (4.3 % to 2.4 %) and ja (2.9 % to 2.4 %).
The MRPC paragraph stays dense in both parts: its state is the fit's (leading 1.0, the original's pitch, where its
neighbours are filled to 1.6; tracking -0.03 em, punctuation compressed), because its two frames are its source's own five
lines, which hold its four lines only at the original's pitch, and the fit walks tracking and compression to their floors
before the leading, and keeps them once the leading fits, whether or not the leading alone would. That is the walk's order, not the split,
and is left to its own change. The zh measures that the rule above made worse
than before it (frames with a blank line 0.22, paragraph gaps 0.22, pitch spread 0.433 at `8fcdca28`) do not come back: they
follow from the page change at a line end, which this keeps, not from the sentence share. The sweep's invariant (i) cannot hold
a sentence to its source's page under this rule: the first k lines stay on page A whatever sentences they hold. Its smallest
tolerance that matches is the break itself: for a unit drawn over a page break, a sentence drawn on either page of the break
is not a violation; a sentence drawn two pages or more from its source, or in a unit on one page, is as before.

Measured for the rule above (pull request 517) on the gate pack (`608b7e87`, 32 outputs) against `next` (`8fcdca28`): 142 units reach a cut (their fit sets page
B's text on page A). 106 end page A at the end of the line that holds the cut, each checked against the fit's own lines (page
A's lines are the fit's through that line, page B opens at the fit's next line, or at the cut where it is a line's first
token); 19 more now keep their cut, where the old one cost them their fit and was dropped, page B's text drawn on page A
(1810.04805v2-ko unit 47); 11 lay their run's last line on page B, 3 keep the short line (a run of one line on page A), and 3
are laid as without the cut in both. 93 of them are drawn otherwise, and 31 units on 9 pages that hold one, through the
page fill's reads of it: the page's target leading (1810.04805v2-ko page 4, 8 units from 1.11 to 1.05, unit 47's cut kept;
2608.16117v1-zh pages 24, 25 and 27, 15 units looser by 0.08 to 0.12, their cut units' page B parts a line shorter) and the
page's one size (2307.16209v1-zh, 4 pages, 3 of them where a line went whole). The rules gate: de, es, fr and ru unmoved; ja,
ko and zh worse on the measures of the room the rule frees, which is the rule's own outcome, accepted by the owner's ruling
(`lab/pdf/rulings/2026-10-30-page-cut-line.json`): a paragraph's page B part up to a line shorter (zh frames with a blank
line 0.22 to 0.233, paragraph gaps a pitch or more wider 0.22 to 0.227; ko 0.055 to 0.063 and 0.038 to 0.043; ja's gaps 0.024
to 0.029), a page A a line shorter where a line went whole, and the fill's leadings that follow (zh pitch spread 0.433 to
0.483). The sweep's
invariant (i) reads a sentence as drawn on another page only where none of its drawn pages is among its source's: the rule
moves no sentence so but one the source sets wholly on page B that ends inside the rest of the line that holds the cut, and,
where a line goes whole, one wholly inside that line that the source sets wholly on page A.

**A cell left the original's keeps its place from its neighbours.** A unit's line grows over what no other unit holds
(`run.mjs` `growOn`, `layer2.mjs` `extendRects`: within 1.2 em, over characters that read the unit's own words), and what
another unit holds is the page's rectangles of every unit (`rectsByPage`). A unit the left locates stands there by its
left's rectangles from the moment it is added, laid or not; one the left does not locate, the layout file's alone (most of a
table's cells: §17.1), stood there only once it was placed, so a cell left the original's (its row kept, or skipped) stood in
none and its ink was free to a neighbour. 1810.04805v2's Table 8 (the owner, 2026-10-30: 「在 MNLI fine-tune 的地方，文字出现了重叠」,
"where MNLI's fine-tune is, the text overlaps"): MNLI's "Fine-tune" kept, NER's "Fine-tune" beside it 6.5 pt away grew over
the same words to MNLI's start, and its translation was laid from there over MNLI's original, its own place left erased and
empty. Such a unit now stands there by its file lines from the moment it is added, laid or not; one placed adds the
rectangles its growth moves as before. Measured on the pack's 32 outputs, every page (647, the layer gate's model tier with
v0's records): of 5,962 unit records one moves, that cell in each language; in Spanish, French, Korean and Chinese it is laid
on its own line, and in German, Japanese and Russian its translation does not fit its own cell, so it is the original's (it
fitted only by taking MNLI's room).
