### 18.64 A size tie caps a member from the passes up to its own first page (the coordinator's ruling, 2026-11-12)

**The rule.** A size tie (one paragraph of TeX's the front end cut, a figure's set: `layPagePrepared`) caps each member at the
least scale of its tie-mates as the fill passes up to that member's own first page leave them:

- a tie-mate begun on that page or before counts as laid and filled, in this round;
- **a tie-mate begun on a later page counts at its own fit from that page's FIRST lay, before any fill and any cap**
  (`PreparedPage.unfilled` of the first `layPageTied`, read in every round);
- never as a later page's fill set it, nor through a cap that fill set in an earlier round.

A later page's fill (its shrink, the evening of §18.57, the foot step) may cap, through a tie, the members that begin on that
page or after it; it never reaches back over the page break. `packages/typeset/src/lay/page.ts` `tieCaps`;
`packages/typeset/tests/unit/tie-cap.test.ts`.

**Why.** I6 (each unit laid alike by every page's lay that lays it, §18.54's check) holds because a page's lay runs the fill
of its own page and of the first page of every member on it: every lay that draws a unit runs the pass of the page it begins
on, and a later page's pass runs in some of them alone. A tie capped from the scales after every pass the lay ran, so a
member begun on page 1 was capped by its tie-mate's page-2 fill in page 2's lay and not in page 1's: drawn at two sizes across
the break (2610.21098v1 in Chinese, ord 12: one paragraph of TeX's cut at its inline list's items, its first member on pages
1 and 2, its items on page 2; with Google's text the reader gate's runner evened the last item a size step, 0.975, page 2's
lay then capped ord 12 there, page 1's laid it at 1; the entry given the same members' rows named it, "p1 ord 12 by p1/p2:
scale 1 / 0.975"). Accepted with it: a tie may stand one fill step apart across a page break, the member begun earlier keeping
its size; I6 outranks the tie's evenness, and one step is the grain the owner's eye passes (§18.57). Not capping before the
fill (it would break ties inside one page), nor freezing every tied member (it would take a page's fill knob for a
neighbour's sake). One definition for every fill step, whatever knob set the scale.

**Two simpler cuts failed; do not go back to either.**

- *Later tie-mates not read at all* (each member capped by those begun on its first page or before only). A later tie-mate's
  own fit is the same in every lay (its flow is whole in every part that lays it), so it may cap; leaving it out let page 38's
  fill grow 2608.16117v1's ord 115 (Chinese, the door's rows) a step to 1.05 past its tie-mate ord 119's own 1.0, and split
  115's runs, its first ones at 1.05 and its last, the one running on to page 39, at 1.0: one paragraph at two sizes on one
  page, where the tie had held it at 1.
- *Later tie-mates read at their scale before the fill, round by round* (each round's lay, not the first). From the second
  round on, a later member's own lay is set under the cap the first round gave it from its page's fill: on 2610.21098v1 the
  items begun on page 2, capped at 0.975 in round 1 by page 2's evening, were laid at 0.975 in round 2 "before the fill", and
  capped ord 12, begun on page 1, through them: the reach-back came back by the tie's own rounds, and the like-for-like run's
  I6 failed again. Hence the first lay's.

**Measured** (the reader gate, `lab/typeset/gate-l1.mjs --entry --reading=part`, over the 90 pairs with r21's bundles, the
lane google-lay's gate; before = this tree with `lay/page.ts` of a681cf7ab): the door's rows, Google's rows (the store of
round B14, `refactor-2026-11/google-rows`), and Google's rows given to the entry for the runner's members alone. I6 across
the lays: 11 laid otherwise, all the head pass's, on each, before and after; but the like-for-like run, 12 before (this unit)
and 11 after. The runner's own I6 ("laid otherwise from another page's part"): this unit with Google's rows before, none
after. Nothing else moves: the runner's dumps differ in this unit alone, and the entry's lines against the runner's (ENTRY)
in it alone (Google 836 -> 835, door 244 and like for like 281 unchanged). The 7 size ties over the 88 papers whose members
begin on two pages or more (28 members: 2608.16117v1 57/59 and 115/119, 2610.10492v1 19/21, 2610.20716v1 95/97, 2610.21098v1
12-16, 2610.21827v1 47-59, 2610.22197v1 72/74): what the entry draws of each, page by page, is the same before and after on
the door's rows and on Google's; given the runner's members' rows alone, ord 12 on page 2 at 10.91 pt, its page-1 size, where it
was 10.64. No PIPELINE, TRANSLATE or CHAIN_RULES: the lay is the reader's, and no stored byte moves.

**What the page states of it** (2026-11-13, round B16, the coordinator's ruling). A member laid at its tie's cap states `tie:
{ scale, by }` (`types.ts` Laid, `lay/page.ts` tieStated): the cap, a scale of its own size, and the member whose own need set
it, in the round that set it (`tieCaps`' TieOrigin, followed back through a cap that member was itself laid at). That member
states the tie too, by itself; where its own page's fill set it there (the evening's size step, §18.57) and its final lines
stand that step under its own size, its `evened` names the size step among the knobs its final lines carry, with its line
count on the page at its fitted layout of the final round. The statement is of the final lay, never a merged history: a knob of
an earlier round's is named only where the final lines carry it. 2608.25210v2-zh page 11, traced over the rounds: in the first,
unit 200 (today's t212) was evened by its tracking and a size step, 0.975, and unit 199 (t211), one paragraph of TeX's with
it, capped there; in the second, 200 laid again at its own size took its tracking alone; in the third it was capped in turn
through 199, whose cap is 200's own step, and the final page stated `{ track }` on 200 and nothing on 199, so that the display
gate read the tie one step small with no reason. Both at 0.975 is no fault of the drawing: one paragraph has one size, and the
step is the only size both fit at (200 at its own size needs it while 199 stands at its own). Now 199 states `tie { 0.975, by
200 }` and 200 `tie { 0.975, by 200 }`, `evened { track, size }`. The display gate's TRS reads a tie's members' statements
(the measure's `tie t211, t212`, which it could not read before): a member stating `tie` is covered where the member that set
it is (`lab/typeset/parity/rulings.mjs`). Nothing drawn moves. `packages/typeset/tests/unit/tie-cap.test.ts`,
`tight-paragraph.test.ts`.

### 18.66 A paragraph TeX opened inside a unit is read by the same facts on both sides of its end (2026-11-13)

The owner's report on staging (round B14, 2111.09276v1, pages 5 and 6): a paragraph that opens with a bold run-in title and
follows another was drawn from the last line of the paragraph before it, right after its last character (the paragraph's
footnote mark 12, then "Howto-GEN" on one line), one line above the original's first line of it, and "COIN" early too. The
source writes no blank line between them, `…editing.~\footnote{…} \medbreak \noindent \textbf{Howto-GEN} To evaluate …`, so the
front end ends no unit there: one unit holds four of TeX's paragraphs (§19.10's "A group TeX set as a paragraph of its own").
TeX ends a paragraph at each `\medbreak` (`\par`, then `\medskip`), and the marked compile states each end; the facts pass found
no group to state it on, so the part held no `SpanAt.opens` and the reader laid the unit as one paragraph, its fill spreading
it. Not this round's: staging drew the same at round B10's engine; the lay follows §18.11 on what the part states.

- **The rule** (`locate/facts-pass.ts`): the source side and B's side of a paragraph end are read by the same facts. What bounds
  a text window is a piece TeX set ink for in this compile: its glyphs on B, the unit's, of an element's role (an element's own,
  or a nested unit's mark, which `pipeline/instrument.mjs` owns as its piece's), whatever its class; B's run of the unit's text
  stops at such a glyph, so the source's window stops at such a piece. `\medbreak`, `\noindent`, any command that set no ink
  here bounds nothing (the class list `VISIBLE` had made `\medbreak`, an unknown macro, a bound: its window held only the white
  space after it, and no group was met). Each side of the end is met by what stands there, one rule both ways (`sideB` and
  `sideOf`): where the unit's glyph next to the end is a piece's and no letter or digit stands between, by that piece itself (a
  footnote's mark ending the paragraph before: no text to compare stood there); else by its text, spelled, `WANT` characters,
  as before. TeX opened the paragraph at the group so met on both sides (one group alone, the outermost of those opened
  together), else at the element B's next glyph opens where its side before is met too (`El.opens`).
- **The gate.** A paragraph end of B inside a unit (the unit's glyphs on both sides of it) that states no point is counted, by
  what stands where the next paragraph begins in the source (`Located.stats.opensUnstated`, the dump's `counts`): an open or
  an element (`anchored`, this report's class, which must count none) or plain text (`plain`: no anchor exists for it today).
- **Measured** (stage 1a over the 88 papers and 2111.09276v1, cb10a1f7d against this rule): points stated 7 more, in 2 papers
  (2111.09276v1 ords 60 (two), 63, 87 at "Youcook2", 99 at "Step Aggregation Model", 127 at "IER"; 2610.21924v1 ord 17), none
  lost; bundle objects move in those 2 papers alone. `opensUnstated` anchored 7 -> 3, plain 57 -> 57 (30 papers). The 3 left are
  2608.25210v2 page 3's prompt frames (ords 55 to 57): an end before `\mypython{…}` whose glyphs the instrument owns by an inner
  piece the unit's content holds inside its element 14, stated a display, a block of its own; before the rule those ends found
  no piece either and went uncounted. The reader gate over the 90 pairs: no invariant moves on either store.
- **The end itself, in the marked compile.** A paragraph end the marked compile does not state is no fact of this pass:
  2111.09276v1's "Howto-GEN" and "COIN" follow paragraphs that end in a footnote, and B's paragraph ends held none at either.
  LaTeX's para/end point (`layout/marks.mjs` `\axt@peat`) was set only where the list ended in a character, a rule, an
  insertion, a mark, a ligature or a formula; these lists end in whatsits (the element's own end point after the footnote, and
  under hyperref's colour links the link's end and the colour stack's pop after its mark: `\showlists` at para/end), as every
  paragraph that ends in an element or in a unit's own end mark does. A paragraph's end is a fact of TeX's mode, not of its
  last node: the point is now set whatever node ends the list, but on an empty list (TeX builds no line for it, the point would
  build one) and on one that still ends in a glue after its last space, kerns and penalties are taken off (`\\`'s
  `\hfil\break`, after which the point would be a line of its own; a leaders' glue, which `\hskip` cannot put back). A list
  that ends in a box states none yet, a debt with a stated end and no rule: with points after boxes as well as after whatsits,
  pdfTeX 1.40.28 segfaults on 2610.30769v1 (a link of the paper's own ending in another nesting level than it starts; the crash
  follows the node list's memory, no single point causes it; its reproduction in the lab's lane note para-start), and a paper
  production serves is not refused. Its cost: five members of two papers keep B14's "justified" where the page centres them
  (2610.21313v1's affiliation 7, 2610.42112v1's author 1 and affiliations 486 to 488: an end after the box they are set in is
  what tells their alignment, `marks/channels.ts` boxedAlignOf, right wherever it was read), and one paragraph TeX opens inside
  2307.16209v1's centred two-line title (its second line a `\resizebox`) is not stated. It goes when the marked compile is
  robust to such a paper. Three opens the ends after boxes gave went with them, all false: each at a member's first line after
  a column or a page break, mid-sentence (2610.20716v1 84, 2610.20848v1 80, 2610.19159v1 513), read from another paragraph's end
  set between the member's lines on B (a float's image, the outer paragraph of a box split across the page). That the pass can
  read such an end as the unit's own is a debt of its own; at the final rule no point of the 89 stands at a break but a run-in
  title's, its paragraph opening on the next page (2111.09276v1 ord 60, "Object Replacement").
- **Measured at the final rule** (stage 1a over the 89 at the marked compile's final rule, its compiles made anew): B states
  26,124 paragraph ends (10,412 before), none lost; points 3 more than the facts pass alone gave (2111.09276v1 ord 87 at
  "Howto-GEN" and "COIN", 2610.21765v1 ord 42), none lost; the alignment of 4 members moves against B14, each now as the page
  sets it (2307.16209v1 424 and 2608.25210v2 270 centred; 2609.20976v1 112 and 2610.37668v1 434 flush left); no join of the
  flows lost or new; `opensUnstated` anchored 3 (the frames above), plain 63. 2610.30769v1 compiles, its bundle as before the rule.
- **A running head reads no body paragraph's end as its own.** With more ends stated, a paragraph's end at the foot of B's page
  was read as the next page's running head's (2610.30854v1 p8, p9: flush right read as justified). An end is carried onto A before
  the partner of B's next glyph, so where A breaks the page later than B, it lands right after the next A page's head. The end
  right after a unit's last glyph is the unit's own only where, on B, it stood right after that glyph's partner, on its page
  (`locate/ink.ts` carry keeps each end's place on B and each A glyph's place after its partner; `today/ink-units.mjs`
  alignOf); and the points between are read by their glyphs, A's list of points not being in glyph order (the points carried
  from B's page before come first).
- **The end's gate**, `lab/pdf/spikes/para-end-cases.mjs`: a paragraph after a hyperref'd footnote, after a plain `\href`,
  after a citation and after a full stop, with microtype, each end stated before the next paragraph's first glyph and no glyph
  moved by the points (four ends missing before). The facts pass reads two ends at one glyph position as one.

### 18.67 Two elements the source sets side by side are one word, at TeX's distance (the coordinator's ruling, 2026-11-13)

The owner's report on staging (round B12, 2111.09276v1 p1, a caption): `the tokens that have been edited are
\hlyellow{high}\hlblue{lighted}`, one word in two highlights, was drawn with white between the two colours. The row set the two
elements with nothing between them and the breaker made no space token; the gap was the typesetter's: each crop advanced by its
padded box (`unit/crops.ts` cropOfBox, 0.4 pt each side) where TeX set the second's ink 0.25 pt over the first's, and the CJK
line's justification put its slack between the two (`break.mjs` inWord read only `brk` and `cont`): 0.97 pt of white. On Google's
wire a reply also set a space there (3,122 of 3,290 such pairs over the lab's 90 pairs), which the reading now takes back (DESIGN
§6.2's glue rule, one rule for every pair of pieces): spacing and places are restored from the source on reading, and the row
carries the adjacency.

The rule (`breaker/tokens.ts` sideBySide): two elements consecutive in the source (their pieces' index `k`, one after the other,
nothing between) and in the row (no token between them), each drawn (a crop or a text; never a forced break's newline or a kept
region's blockTo, control tokens), are one word as TeX set it, whatever their kinds: the later one's first token is glued and
`tight`, inside the word for `inWord` (no slack of a justified line and no squeeze between them), and two crops TeX set on one
line (one page, one baseline) keep TeX's distance between their starts: a kern after the first, that distance less its box, which
a line's end drops. A tie between them is TeX's own space (the tie's rule holds them across it); a forced break, its line end.

Measured over the 90 pairs (r21's bundles, the reader gate's runner, base = the round's typesetter, Google's rows read with the
glue rule): with the door rows 6 of 23,006 units move, with Google's 5 of 22,939, each holding such a pair (2501.14787v1 ord
404, a typewriter symbol and its superscript; 2610.21098v1 ord 13, a minus sign and a macro's number, its paragraph one character

typewriter word and a formula): the
crops' places by at most 2.5 pt, one line's end by 0.8 pt; I3 (3), I4 (0), I5 (2) and I6 (11, the head pass's) as before on both, a closing mark's blank half past
its slot 3,537 -> 3,536 on the door's rows (2610.21098v1's re-broken lines, the one unit whose lines moved there), 3,121 on Google's. The owner's caption: the two highlights
16.26 pt apart, TeX's distance, where they stood 17.48. The display gate's lay (its 22 pairs, the door's rows, default and every switch on): one page
of 344 moves, 2608.25210v2-zh p9, a formula and the element right after it on one line, the line's other items 0.01 pt at most. A first build glued the control token after such an element (2608.06701v1
p1: a page's fill threw, I6 caught it) and was corrected before it was committed: both sides must draw.

The migration's differential (the lab's `baseline/tools/diff.mjs`) counts units by their id, the hash of a unit's kind and
pieces: a unit the rebuilt engine reads otherwise is another id, and today's counts as lost unless stage 1a's statement
(`lab/pdf/prepare-back/stated.mjs`) finds what stands for it. Eleven lines stayed lost round after round; traced one by one
(the lab's lane lost-11), eight are drawn by the rebuilt engine on every line, and three are real, kept as the original where
today's erased ink it never drew again (a class's "Funding:", a table note's mark): those are the facts round's.

- The dump's element keys. Stage 1a's dump (`lab/pdf/prepare-back/run.mjs`) numbered a unit's pieces by place and wrote each
  element's `k` as the instrument's content id, which numbers a piece by the front end's own index and skips the groups it

  by its piece's k read another piece, or none. Round B15's r22: 8,225 of 73,121 elements keyed otherwise than by their piece,
  7,261 of them naming no piece of their unit. `lab/pdf/prepare-back/pieces.mjs` flattens a unit's content once and keys each

- (t) "held whole by the drawn units on its lines, read as arXiv prints them": today's unit whose every line one or more drawn

### 18.69 A paragraph TeX opened in plain text opens where the row's sentence start pairs with its first word (2026-11-13)

§18.66 states a paragraph TeX opened inside a unit where a group or an element stands at its start. Two cases remain (the
display design of 2026-11-13, 2a): a paragraph that opens in plain text (`A. \smallbreak\noindent B.`, a class's separator, a
plain new paragraph the source writes no blank line before), and a point stated at a group the translator's reply dropped (with
Microsoft's rows the bold markers of 2111.09276v1's run-in titles come back at the unit's end, and the reading places a lost group
only where its text stands once in the source: "COIN", three times there, runs on). The fact for both is the paragraph's first
word: its offset in the unit's source projection (what `Row.sentences.src` counts in) and the line TeX opened it on, the part's
`paras`. A paragraph point is a fact of the source, and a group or an element is one carrier of it that a reply can drop: the
part states the first word of EVERY point, whatever stronger anchor it also has, and the lay reads the strongest carrier the row
kept (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-13, in place of the design's "stated once, by the strongest fact"). The engine's half
states it, in a later round; until then no part holds it and nothing drawn moves.

- **The lay** (`unit/breaks.ts` `paraPieces`, `pairing`). A point on a line no stronger fact the row holds opens (a group's open
  or an element between the row's texts, a forced break: `statedBreaks`; one opening a line) is paired with the row's
  sentence whose start on A is that word: the row's cuts each holding a word of A (`lay/lit.ts` `worded`), the first of
  `Placed.words` at or after the start (`firstWordAt`, the highlight's own start rule) being the point's word on the point's
  line. Its place in the translation is the highlight's too (`startsInProjection`: the start's first letter, digit or element,
  back over the opening marks set against it). A piece of the typesetter's own (`par`, never in a Row, never on a wire) stands
  there, before the groups opened right there, a text piece cut in two; it stands for no character, so the row's projection,
  its sentences and the highlight's places do not move. `statedBreaks` reads it as a group's open with `opens` its line, under
  the same guards; one it does not open is taken out. The blocks, the tokens' `blockTo` and the breaker run unchanged; the white
  space at the cut is dropped as at any block's edge. A named variant pairs after `lay/named.ts` has given its sentences back in
  the unit's own projection.
- **No pair, no guess.** Where the row carries no sentences (they did not reconstruct; Chrome's translator) or no start of it is
  the point's word (an end inside a sentence: a float TeX set in the middle of one), no block opens and the text flows on through
  the member's lines, as before: no nearest start and no proportional place is taken, which would set half a sentence on a line
  of its own.
- **Stated** (`Laid.paras`, where the part states a point and the member is laid): `[opened, noStart, noSentences]`: the points
  opened on their line (by their own pair, or by a stronger fact the row holds there), those that flowed on for want of a start
  the lay can open at their word, those for want of the row's sentences.
- **The gate** (the reader gate, `lab/typeset/gate-l1.mjs --entry`, `packages/typeset/tests/replay/paras-gate.ts`): each point a
  part states (a group's open, an element, a first word) whose row carries its anchor (the group or the element between the
  row's texts, else the sentence start paired with its first word) is laid with its first word starting a line of the member: a
  laid line of the member on the page of TeX's line begins with the paragraph's first thing. The defect a reader sees is a
  paragraph that starts on the last line of the one before; one that starts a line of its member has none, whether that line
  stands on TeX's baseline or not (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-13: the baseline is the spacing design's). A point run on
  fails the run; those on TeX's baseline are counted beside, never failed; a point with no anchor flows on and is counted by why.
  In the lab the first word of a point stated at a group or an element is read from the unit's source, so the gate holds today's
  group points to the fallback the part will state. Of several facts that state one line, the point is the first in the source
  (2609.36054v2's author block states each line at its name's group and at its affiliation's after it). The release check's
  `sentence-cover` reads the counts and fails on a point run on once `PARAS_HELD` (`lab/release-check/gates.mjs`) is on: the
  engine half's lane turns it on in the round it lands in; until then a point a reply's dropped group leaves has no first word
  to fall back to.
- **Measured** (the base c331582c6 against this lay, round B15's parts, no part stating a first word): the reader's own lay
  (`lab/typeset/parity/v2.mjs`) over the 90 pairs and the two added ones (2111.09276v1-zh, 2611.03953v2-zh), on the door rows
  and on the lab's Google store, default and every switch on: 368 of 368 files identical. The reader gate at this lay: every
  number it read before as at the base (90 pairs, door: entry 24,056 alike / 244, I3 3, I4 0, I5 2, I10 0 over 3,145,577
  pieces, I6 0 other; Google: 23,544 / 827, I3 3, I10 0 over 3,569,346, I6 0 other). The points: 27 stated over the 90 (all at
  a group), 3 not on TeX's line on both stores, each beginning a line of its own at the member's own pitch (2608.25210v2 p1 ord
  8, 2610.21924v1 p2 ord 17, 2610.30151v1 p1 ord 0: CJK leading, a title's); on the door rows 24 belong to members with no
  door row. 2111.09276v1-zh: Google's rows 8 of 8 open; the door rows (Microsoft's replies in today's reading) 6 not, 5 of them
  run on (COIN, Youcook2, Howto-GEN, "Token Replacement", "Step Aggregation Model", "IER": run-in titles whose groups the reply
  dropped). A copy of its parts stating COIN's and Youcook2's first words (the lab's simulation) opens those two on TeX's lines
  (179.84, 585.36) on the door rows; one stating every such point's first word, and its words in every part that holds the
  member, opens all six (the gate 0) and moves no other unit across the pages' lays (I6 0 other).

### 18.70 A stop the source ties to a word or a number ends no sentence on the tags wire (the coordinator's ruling, 2026-11-13)

A tie after a stop is TeX's own statement that the space there is a word space and not a sentence's end: `~` is
`\penalty10000\ `, and no end-of-sentence space is ever set at it. So where the source ties a word or a number to a stop, the tags
wire (Google's, Chrome's built-in translator's, the LLM services') marks no sentence end there: no boundary marker, no cut of the
row's sentences (`wire/tags.ts` planTags `tied`). A word or a number is text that begins with a letter or a digit, or an element
the sentence cutter reads as one (a number, a reference, a formula, a paper's macro); a tie and then a mark, which annotates the
sentence before it (a note's mark, a footnote's call, a citation), keeps the end, the mark glued to the sentence that ended
(2111.09276v1's `search.~\footnote{…}`). No word list and no language's case decide it: the tie is the source's.

Why: on round B15's wire the boundary marker stands right after a sentence's stop, before the elements the source glues after it
(DESIGN §6.2), and the cutter ended sentences at abbreviations' dots a tie follows. After "vol." Google then completed the
"sentence" with a volume, an issue and pages the paper does not print ("…Systems, vol.~36, pp.~…" read as "vol. 10, no. 1, pp.
1-10" in Chinese) in 42 bibliography units of 7 papers over the lab's Google store at round RB1, 39 of their rows read; on round
B14's wire (the marker after the elements) none. Every such marker over the store's 92 pairs (lane glued-mark, 2026-11-13): 533,
532 in bibliographies (after a one-letter initial 366, "M.~Casals"; "vol." 99, "no." 51, "p." 6 before a number; a lower-case
initial 3, "J. a.~P. Cavalcante"; journal abbreviations 7, "Amer.~Math.~Soc.", "Math.~Ann.", "Ch.~Pommerenke") and 1 in prose
("…an ingredient in Definition.~\ref{…}.", a stop the author typed inside the sentence): every one read, none a sentence's end.
The wires of 479 bibliography units and 1 prose unit change; they are asked again. Reading a `number` element as a digit
instead was measured and withdrawn: the cutter's own merge of a short capitalised word before a number (`Exer. 5`) then joins
262 author blocks to their year ("…Llion Jones. 2018. Character-level…"), true ends lost.

### 18.71 A note the source ties to the author block follows the names option (the owner's ruling, 2026-11-13)

The owner's ruling: text the paper's code ties to the author block follows the names option both ways (off: the original; on:
translated); text in a region of its own is body text. What ties a note to the block is the source's, read as LaTeXML's bindings
read it, never a word list or a share:

- **A note written inside an author command's argument** is the block's: a `\thanks` or a `\footnote` anywhere in the argument of
  a command the role table names `author` (`FRONT_ROLES`: `\author`, `\affil`, `\icmlauthor` …), the innermost such argument
  deciding (`latex-front.mjs` `tieNotes`, the walk's `within`). A note of `\title`'s argument is the title's: body. LaTeXML reads
  the first so (a `\thanks` in a creator's text annotates the creator, `Base_Utility.pool.ltxml` 331-332).
- **A note written on its own** is the block's where the paper's bindings attach it to an author: the generator keeps, per
  binding, where a note command's text goes (`scripts/latexml-args.mjs` `NOTE_POOLS`, `NOTE_PACKAGES`): `creator`, the author
  before it (REVTeX's `\thanks` after `\author{…}`, acmart's `\authornote`); `label:<prefix>`, the authors whose text requests the
  label (`REQUEST_*`: elsarticle's `\cortext[key]{…}` and `\corref{key}` in an `\author`, read once the whole source is); or the
  document's (the kernel's `\thanks`, amsart's), body. A label no author's text requests is an orphan LaTeXML drops: body.
- **An author command's argument a macro stores** keeps its role's kinds (`frontBlock`): ICML's `\icmlaffiliation`, which its
  class stores with `\gdef` for the footnote `\printAffiliationsAndNotice` sets, is the block's places, held and unmarked as
  before (a mark there could be set twice or never: 2608.16117 lost a page), no longer a paragraph's.
- **The ink TeX sets of the block's own text** (locate, `today/ink-units.mjs` rule 8): a block of notes or orphans that holds
  whole the letters of an author or affiliation unit with no place of its own on A (it owns no glyph of A, or its only place is
  a paragraph that sets a unit again: 2610.22065v1's names its own `\@mkauthors` types out) is the names', and opens the block's
  stretch; outside the stretch it is turned back, the text it is (`nameBlock`: acmart's reference format, amsart's addresses at
  the paper's end, a running head, which is never a note's or an orphan's line). One that holds whole a stored argument's text
  (ICML's footnote of its places) is the names' wherever it stands. "Holds whole": the unit's letters a run of the line's words'
  letters from a word's start to a word's end, a class's separator ("and", a comma) no part of it. Today's named a block where 60 %
  of its letters were an author unit's words (`NAMES_SHARE`), which is gone.

A note so tied carries `of: 'author'` on its unit and on each of its members (format's `Unit.of`, `Placed.of`: optional, not in
the id; a reader of before reads none and translates the note, as before), and every reading of a class reads a unit's or a
member's kind through format's `toggleKind` (`of`, else its kind): the reader's classes, its composer and its count, the
typesetter's `leave`, and so every gate that lays a page (a test holds every such site to it). ICML's footnote is `inknames`, a
kind of the names already. Its variant (§19.15) stays: with the names on, the note is drawn from its variant, the block's names in
it (one person, one translation); with them off it is left the original's and neither its row nor its variant's is read. So off,
on, off, on draws two drawings, the original and the variant, never the note's own row beside the variant (the coordinator's
ruling of 2026-11-13: the owner saw 2611.03953v2-zh p1's footnote drawn from its own row off and from its variant on, two
translations of one sentence across the switch).

Measured over round RB1's 89 papers and 2611.03953v2 (stage 1a against its own run, lane f2-author): every unit and member as
before but `of` on 32 units (36 notes, equal texts one unit) in 20 papers, 29 of them drawn on a first page; the two ICML papers'
stored places (2 and 5) of kind `affiliation`, no longer `para`, and their footnotes `inknames`, no longer `inknotes` (the
footnotes' ids move with their kind; their rows are made again from the stored replies, the wire unchanged, nothing asked; their
variants keep their ids); rule 8's tie leaves every ink unit's final kind and the block's stretch as the share left them,
2610.22065v1's two names lines among them (its eight `\author` units' only place a paragraph that sets them again); the lines the
share named and the tie does not all stood outside the stretch, turned back either way; the glyphs' ownership as before. By default 31
notes in 20 papers are now the original's on their first page: 28 `\thanks` inside `\author` (17 papers), acmart's `\authornote`
(2402.10294v1) and the two ICML footnotes. `\title`'s six notes, the five `\thanks` amsart and acmart attach to the document and
2608.16117v1's `\cortext`, whose label only a commented-out `\author` requests, stay translated. PIPELINE moves (the units gain
`of`, and the stored places and ICML's footnotes their kinds); no LAYOUT (no mark moves), no TRANSLATE (no wire moves); FORMAT
stays 1. The display gate's ruling AN (`lab/typeset/parity/rulings.mjs`) covers the `shown` readings these notes make with the
names off.

## 19. The engine's contract

**Today's engine and the rebuild's.** This chapter describes today's engine, `src/pdf-reader/engine/`, which our server
and the shipped extension's reader (`AXT_READER=today`, DESIGN §16) run until the rebuild's cut-over. Its successor is the
workspace packages (`packages/README.md`): the prepare in `@readarxiv/engine`, where our marked compile is an instrument
no reader sees, its ownership of each glyph is carried onto arXiv's own glyphs by aligning the two, and arXiv's PDF itself
is wrapped in optional content groups by unit, so that both panes show arXiv's page (DESIGN §16, the prepare's two halves);
the typesetter in `@readarxiv/typeset`, two pure functions of a page's part and the translated text; and the reader in
`@readarxiv/reader`, `openReader` with a host, whose interface is this document's §1 to §17, unchanged. What this chapter
calls the maker — the page pass (§19.6), our compile as the base page with its final pass (§19.7), the delta over arXiv's
PDF (§19.8) and the layout file's geometric ownership — has no counterpart in the packages. The chapter goes with today's
engine when the cut-over deletes it.

`src/pdf-reader/engine/` is what the web imports, and nothing else of the reader is. The directory is the boundary: a gate
holds what may be imported into it (`scripts/check-boundary.mjs`, run by `pnpm lint`), a snapshot holds what it exports
(`tests/pdf-reader/engine-contract.json`), and a test holds that it loads where it is meant to
(`tests/pdf-reader/engine-contract.test.ts`).

### 19.1 The tree

```
src/pdf-reader/engine/
  pipeline.mjs translate.mjs rules.mjs layer.mjs view.mjs      the five entries: re-exports only
  source/       latex-front, tar, paper-meta, node-files                          a paper's source: the server
  pipeline/     live, anchors, versions, record.ts, tex-errors, and the compile path's cache, scripts, typeset/   the server
  layout/       file, json, marks, make, paper, ink, carry, match, stream, own, wrap, delta, cell-rules, remove   the layout file, the wrap and the delta (file, json and cell-rules also the readers'; remove the content walk the wrap reads)
  translate/    mt, groups, kept, mixed, version                                    the wires and the units a target keeps: both
  rules/        layout (the rule set and its reader), font-roles, font-coverage, script, arg-roles, latexml-args   both
  layer-proto/  run, reader (the reader's door), bundle, rows, fonts, hyph, visibility, hide, tex, check, layer1, layer2   the drawn layer: the browser
  layer/        pieces, and check (the pixel checker the layer gate's instrument loads)                             the browser
  view/         reader-view, places, layer-side, feed, contents, lighting, highlight, shapes, floats, figures, pointer, sync, overlay, outline, engine.css   the browser
```

What the engine does not hold: the extension's session (`src/pdf-reader/session/`: its host of the view, its run on the
layer, its client of our server, the served faces, its translation client `session/translate.mjs`) and the addresses
(`src/pdf-reader/addresses.ts`); and, parked (`parked/README.md`), the first instant layer (`parked/engine/`) and the
extension's compile client (`parked/extension-compile/`).

### 19.2 The five entries

| Entry | Loads in | What it gives |
|---|---|---|
| `pipeline` | Node (the server) | A paper's source to its units (`openPaper`, `loadProject`, `unpackSource`, `analyze`); the marked original and the probes (`originalFiles`, `probeFiles`, `readingsOf`, `stoppedShort`); the left geometry (`anchors`); the layout marks, the layout maker and its cell rules (`layoutMarksOfPaper`, `makeLayout`, `pageRules`, `checkBoxes`), the wrap (`wrapFinal`); the TeX Live year arXiv's PDF says it was built on, from its pdfTeX banner and before any compile (`texLiveOfPdf(doc)`: the `PTEX.Fullbanner` of the Info dictionary PDF.js resolves from the trailer, never a scan of the bytes, else null); the page pass, a paper's layer told a part at a time (`layerOfPaper`, §19.6), and its cut (`partCutter`, `wholeCutter`, `cutBundle`); the layout file and the add-on's manifest, with their caps; the bundle's writer (`writeBundle`, `bundleUnitsOf`); the faces' coverage; `PIPELINE_VERSION`, `PDFJS`. Not the compile path's typesetting, strategies or cache, and not `runLive`. |
| `translate` | Node and browser | The wires a unit goes out as and the reading back (`serialize`, `rehydrate`, `serializeTags`, `rehydrateTags`, `translateUnits`, the sentences, the batches); the table groups (`decideGroups`, `groupOf`); the units a target keeps (`authorsTranslated`); the rows (`rowOf`, `unitOf`, `layerRows`, `toTranslate`, `batchesOf`, `runRows`); `TRANSLATE_VERSION`. No DOM, no network. |
| `rules` | Node and browser | The layout rule set and its reader (`readRules`, `parseRules`, `resolveRules`, `BUILTIN_RULES`, `RULES_SCHEMA`, `RULES_CAP`, `TARGETS`), the font roles (`FACES`, `rolesFor`, `faceFor`, `familyOfFonts`) and the script of a tag (`scriptOf`). |
| `layer` | browser | The reader's door whole (`layer-proto/reader.mjs`): `openLayer`, `firstFaceOf`, `readBundle` and its caps and refusal, `BUNDLE`, `CTAG`, `VTAG`, `parseLayout`, `indexLayout`, `parseAddonManifest`, the rows' helpers it takes. |
| `view` | browser | The reading view both readers run (`createReaderView`, §11.7, and its types) and its layer side (`createLayerSide`, `PAGE_MS`, §11.8), what is lit under the pointer (`highlight`, `floats`, `figures`, `pointer`), the synchronised scrolling (`sync`), the overlays kept through a zoom (`overlay`) and the outline. |

### 19.3 What holds

- **Imports.** A whitelist, applied to every file of the engine (modules, TypeScript and declaration files) and to every way
  a module is named: a value import or a type one, `export … from`, `import(…)`, `require(…)` and `new URL(…, import.meta.url)`.
  A file of the engine names a module by relative path, to the engine's own files, `src/core/sentences`,
  `src/core/protector/tokens`, `src/core/names` or `src/core/protector/math-runs`; or a `node:` module; or, in `rules/`, the layout rules' validator
  (`zod/mini`). Nothing else: no alias (refused for its spelling), no build setting's name (`#imports`), no root-absolute
  path, no other package, no module of the extension, and no specifier that is computed. A TypeScript file is reached by its
  extension, which Node reads with its own type stripping; the closure behind the four core modules is those four files.
- **Loading.** `pipeline`, `translate` and `rules` load in plain Node with no bundler (a child process in the contract test);
  `layer` and `view` load in a browser's environment. The closures of `translate`, `rules`, `layer` and `view` hold none of the
  server's modules (the front end, the compile path, the layout maker, the marks, the ownership and the wrap). The
  `pipeline` entry's names leave the compile path out, but its closure still loads `cache`, `scripts` and `typeset/*` through
  `live.mjs`; PR 5 splits `live.mjs` into the paper's pipeline and the compile run before that path is parked.
- **Licence.** No file in the closure of the five entries states that it is ported from a reference project or a scoped
  package (the web's R21 detector, `portedInClosure`). The shared interface (the reader's chrome,
  `packages/reader/src/chrome/**`, and `packages/ui/src/**`) reaches no GPL-ported file since the chrome moved into the
  package (stage 5a): the language tables, the service menu and the keyed reasons that reached them are the extension's
  host (`src/pdf-reader/host/`), given to the chrome as its slots and words. The test pins that list as empty.
- **Notices.** What the web carries with the engine and the shared interface: the LaTeXML acknowledgement now
  (`rules/latexml-args.mjs` is in the closures of `pipeline` and `layer`; `docs/THIRD_PARTY.md` has its row), and Lucide (ISC)
  and Noto Sans SC (OFL) with the shared interface (the icons of `packages/ui/src/controls/Icon.tsx`, the glyphs of
  `packages/ui/src/controls/display-glyphs.ts`).
- **Reached.** Every module of the engine is reached by an entry, by the checker the layer gate names, or by a file under
  `src/` or `lab/` outside the engine (`unreached`: the shipped extension and every file of the lab, its bench and spikes, not
  only its kept gates); a module only a test or a script reaches is parked with its tests.
- **Versions.** The identities of §18 move with the code that owns them; a change of an entry's names is made on purpose, by
  recording `engine-contract.json` again (`WRITE_CONTRACT=1 pnpm vitest run tests/pdf-reader/engine-contract.test.ts`), and
  the web sees it as a change of the surface it pins.
- **Behaviour.** `tests/pdf-reader/engine-golden.test.ts` holds, as SHA-256 values, what the engine makes of inputs the
  repository wrote itself (units, wires, the files of every compile, the bundle, the layout file, the rows). A move or a refactor leaves every hash as it is.
- **Runtime.** What the server's reads make does not depend on the Node they run on. PDF.js 6.3.289 keeps a glyph's outline,
  which the ink reading takes a glyph's own extent from (`layout/ink.mjs` `outlineBox`), in a Float16Array where the runtime
  has one (Node 24 on; Node 22 has none), and half precision moves a rounded coordinate of the layout (494.89 is 494.9 on
  1706.03762v7). A host that makes the lite worker its PDF.js worker calls `float32Outlines(api, worker)` (`layout/pdf-lite.mjs`)
  before its first document: both sides Float32, whatever the runtime (`tests/pdf-reader/pdf-lite-outlines.test.ts`). The
  extension and the browser layer run stock PDF.js and read no glyph's outline for the layout. A failed allocation is one on
  every Node: from Node 24 on, `Buffer.allocUnsafe` and what is made of it (`Buffer.concat`, zlib's output) throw a RangeError of
  Node's own words, `Failed to allocate memory`, with the code ERR_MEMORY_ALLOCATION_FAILED, where Node 22 threw V8's `Array buffer
  allocation failed`; `pipeline/memory.mjs` `isMemoryError` reads the code first.
  PDF.js's worker recovers from a failure inside it in some twenty places and answers the read as whole (a page's list ended
  where its parse failed, a font read as none): no call of its API fails for it, `stopAtErrors` included (its API settles a
  page's list with what it read). Its warnings are where it says so, each with its reason as text: the engine's `readPdf`
  (the back half's reading of A, the instrument's of B) hears them for the document it reads (`warnings.ts`: PDF.js's level
  raised to its warnings for that document and set back after it, console.warn PDF.js's channel to the watch while it is open
  and put back). A reason that is a failed allocation (`isMemoryText`, V8's words, the same definition as `isMemoryError`'s)
  throws one, so the prepare refuses the paper for its memory (2609.19644v1's page 70, read empty at 880 MiB, committed 77
  objects without it). Any other recovery is stated in the head, optional, as `recovered`: [A or B, its site, its count, its
  first reason]; none fires on the corpus (the census of 2026-11-10: 88 papers and 2609.19644v1, arXiv's PDF and B).

### 19.4 The layer API, as the web defines it

The routes are the web's, `/api/v1/` kept for every released extension; the engine holds the format both readers parse and the
tags they ask by (`layer-proto/bundle.mjs`).

- **One file per paper version.** The bundle is a single JSON file: `{ schema, paper { id, version, pages }, base { bytes,
  sha256, url }, versions { bundle, pipeline, layout, removal, pdfjs, image }, units, left, layout | null, rules | null }` (`rules`: the
  table rules near each page's cells, `{ "<page>": [x0, y0, x1, y1, …] }`, where the layout file is; the add-on it carried
  before REMOVAL 8 is gone). Both readers parse it with `readBundle(json, caps)` after the byte cap (`BUNDLE_CAP`) and the value count
  (`BUNDLE_VALUES`) are checked before `JSON.parse`; a refused bundle draws no layer, a refused unit is dropped and counted, a
  layout of `null` draws nothing (the layer draws only from the layout file: every unit stays the original's). Over arXiv's
  PDF (BUNDLE 3's base) no unit has a group, so every unit stays the original's too (§11.8).
- **Routes by tag.** `GET /api/v1/layer/<id>v<n>/<tag>` answers 200 with the bundle, 202 `Preparing { position, stage,
  progress, retryAfterMs }`, 404 `{ why }` (`not-prepared`, `no-source`, `no-pdf`, `cannot-prepare`, `unknown-versions`) or 429
  `{ retryAfterMs }`; `POST …/<tag>/prepare` (JSON body `{}`) answers 202, 200 `{ ready: true }`, 404 or 429; `GET
  /api/v1/original/<id>v<n>` is `base.url`, our copy of arXiv's bytes; `GET /api/v1/base/<id>v<n>/<sha256>` (no suffix) is our
  base page a head of ours names (§19.7), by its digest, by ranges, a strong `ETag`, any origin, immutable; a head held as a delta (§19.8) names no
  such page: its delta is a bundle object, `GET /api/v1/layer/<id>v<n>/<ctag>/o/<sha256>.delta` as bytes (`application/octet-stream`;
  the suffix the engine's `deltaKey` names it by, the web's `deltaPath`), and its
  composed document reads `/api/v1/original` by ranges. The tag is the engine's `VTAG`, or its contract
  tag `CTAG` where the server redirects to the newest bundle made under it (§18.4). The public GETs answer CORS `*`; the prepare
  POST relies on the extension's host permission.
- **What the reader sends.** A paper's id and version, and the engine's public versions (the tag). Nothing else leaves the machine.
- **The rows.** `runRows` makes a language's rows from the bundle's units; the reader draws them through the door
  (`openLayer(…).take(rows)`). The rows are cached by the bundle's key, the target and the chain.
- **The faces and the patterns.** From the web's `/static-fonts/*` and its `hyph` files, which answer CORS `*`.

### 19.5 The hand-off

The web moves its imports to the five entries, once: its server takes `pipeline` and `translate`, its reader `layer`, `view`,
`translate` and `rules`; its fork-session script and the copies of the session it makes go with the reading view that replaces
them. The extension's own modules are not importable from the web, and a module the web needs that no entry exports is a
request for an entry's change, made here with its test, not an import by path. The shared interface it imports besides
(the reader's chrome and `packages/ui`) stays under the licence rule of section 19.3: it reaches no ported file.

### 19.6 The page pass

`layerOfPaper` (`pipeline/page-pass.mjs`, in the `pipeline` entry) makes a paper's layer (bundle 4) from its marks and arXiv's
PDF and tells it to its host a part at a time: the left (anchored on arXiv's tokens under the unit marks), the layout file
(`makeLayout`'s, each page's operator list read once for the maker and its cell rules) and the cut (`partCutter`, `cutBundle`'s
own), each part carrying its pages' cell rules (`rules`).

- **In.** `paper { id, version }`; `source` (`openPaper`'s); `marks` (`layoutMarksOfPaper`'s: `{ marks, unitMarks }` or
  `{ refused }`), or `marked { doc, log, options }` (the marked original, read by the pass a page at a time); `arxiv { doc,
  text? }` (a PDF.js document of arXiv's PDF, the caller's to open and destroy, and its text as `readArxivText` read it, else
  read here: the left's); `ours` (our base page, §19.7: `{ doc, bytes, sha256, xref, check }`, or the final pass's refusal, or
  null), `orig { bytes, sha256 }` (arXiv's PDF beside it) and `tree` (the TeX Live year it was made on); `base { bytes, sha256,
  xref }` alone is a host of BUNDLE 7's, whose paper falls back (`final`); `OPS`; `pdfjs`; `image`;
  `rules` (`DEFAULT_RULES` where not given: rules 1, 3 and 4, the page stream; `WHOLE_RULES`, next's whole run), `whole`
  (the whole made first, whatever the rules), and `frame`, `columns` (read under the whole run's rules); `verdicts`
  (default on).
- **Out, in order.** `onHead(head, chunks)`, then for each part its left parts (`onLeft`) and the part (`onPart(part, note)`),
  each awaited; `note` is `{ pages, layout: 'kept' | 'none' | { refused, … }, lines: [in place, total] }` (the lines of its
  pages in place on arXiv's PDF: information). It returns
  `{ through, count, stats }`, or `{ refused: 'anchors', why }` before anything is told.
- **Per part.** Each part is judged as it is cut (`verdicts`): its own reader taking it (`readPart` against the head, the
  chunks and the parts before); a part refused is its pages with no layout (C1.4: drawn from the left), never the paper's
  refusal. No share of a part's lines judges it: each unit is judged by its own lines (the page and line check, below). Every bound a part holds is the
  part's (`LINES_ALL`, `PAGE_TEXT_ALL`, `NAMES_MAX`, `FONTS_MAX`, the part's caps): an over-bound part is shortened, a first page
  alone past them has no layout, nothing is truncated. A page whose operator list passes `OPS_CAP` operations, whose walk
  passes `STEPS_MAX` steps, `STACK_MAX` levels or `GLYPHS_PAGE` glyphs (one operation's glyphs and placements counted within
  it), or whose list fails, is dark (its units stay the
  original's), that page alone, whatever the pages before it: no count of pages given up on darkens a later page, and a marked
  page whose carry passes `PAGE_WORK` carries none of its lines, that page alone. A page past `BOXES_PAGE` boxes is not dark:
  its boxes past the budget are merged by cell (`degraded`, its text whole). Each bound is an abuse guard twenty times or more
  above the corpus's heaviest page (`layout/ink.mjs`, the census of 2026-10-16), and none is a fixed number of the paper's:
  each is a page's or a part's (see below for why none is needed).
- **The marked original for a host that reads it itself.** `markedOfPaper` (layout/paper.mjs, in the pipeline entry) is
  `layoutMarksOfPaper` without its reading: the mark probe and the marked compile, and the marked PDF, its last pass's log and
  readMarked's options, which a host passes as `marked: { doc, log, options }` so that the pass reads the marked original a
  page at a time beside arXiv's; its refusals are the same (`{ refused, why }`: 'probe', 'compile', 'texlive', 'engine',
  'marks', below), and `layoutMarksOfPaper` is it followed by one `readMarked`, its marks the same bytes.
- **The marked original must be the paper: the layout guard** (`layout/guard.mjs`, applied by `markedOfPaper`; R1 of
  2026-10-19). Our marks are TeX inserted into the paper's own source, and a construct the front end reads wrongly made three
  of the 50-paper sweep's marked originals another document than arXiv's, so that each paper lost its whole layout through a
  fault of ours (343 rows): 2610.21377's pgffor loop headers written back with their body's brace doubled, 2610.21201's
  etoc depth tag whose end mark TeX wrote into the contents inside a `\csname` (ten errors, 36 pages to arXiv's 34),
  2610.21288's `\appendixname` wrapped by the babel names' marks under revtex4-2 and the appendix package (the job aborted).
  Each check holds for any paper:
  - *Before the compile, in the mark probe* (PIPELINE 43): where a unit of the main file stands in its preamble, the probe sets
    the preamble as the marked original writes it (`live.mjs` `markedPreamble`: the layout marks and their line probes, every
    class, no babel name wrapped, a unit whose writing unbalances its braces as the paper's own; `probeFiles` `preamble`, and
    `\axtlines` a protected macro that sets nothing there), so that TeX reads our marks in the preamble where the marked compile
    will, a compile before it. An error TeX raises on a line of that preamble names the units of the marks of ours it stands
    among (`guard.mjs` `preambleUnits`, `marksAtError`): on the line as the log shows it, those of the brace group TeX closed just
    before the error's place (a command that read its argument whole), else of the group open at it — never another unit's on
    the same line, a title set on the author's line, and none where the place is in no group (the marked compile's guard judges
    what is left) —, and the units so named are left unmarked before the marked compile
    (the record's `failed: ['preamble']`, `extra` 0). A class's command that reads its argument as data raises its errors there:
    2610.37668v1's myarxiv `\author` takes a name's initials, the first token of each word, through a `\csname`, and our start
    mark was that token (nine errors, 36 pages to arXiv's 35, two compiles more; now none, the babel names kept). Then, or where
    that probe stopped before its body wrote a row (TeX stopped in the preamble), the probe is asked again over the paper's own
    preamble, whose answers no error of ours came before; one that stopped in its body, in a sample of its own, stopped where
    the paper's own preamble's stops (2610.21377v1: the same errors and rows; 2610.21884v1's too, at a sample of xy-pic's syntax,
    until PIPELINE 45 kept its diagrams as the paper has them, below), and stands. A paper whose preamble
    holds no unit has the probe it had, byte for byte. Over 72 papers, 34 hold a unit in the preamble: on each, the probe's
    answers over the marked preamble are the paper's own preamble's (switches, macros that set no ink, their texts, the names,
    `\lineskip`, the boxes begun apart), at the same time (37.9 s against 37.8 s locally over the 34), and only 2610.37668v1's
    names a unit.
  - *Before the compile*: each unit's writing in the marked file against its source, by its brace balance outside comments,
    `\verb` and verbatim environments (the innermost unit that changes it); such a unit is written as the paper's own bytes
    (latex-front.mjs `patch` `asSource`: no mark, no span), and a file whose balance our other edits move (a style's literal
    babel name wrapped) has the name marks off. Over the corpus's 124 papers and the sweep's 50 it moves one paper's three
    units (2610.21377), at a median of 2.2 ms a paper (33 ms at most, 2610.19159's 1,813 units; 177 sources).
  - *After it*: it ran through (`ranThrough`); its page count is arXiv's where the host gives it (`pages`: a number or a
    function asked once; with several toplevel sources, at most arXiv's); no auxiliary file it wrote (the files a host
    returns, else its main aux, which holds every list entry LaTeX writes through `\@writefile`) holds a mark of ours where
    no text is set: anywhere but a list entry's text (`\contentsline`'s second argument) and nameref's title (`\newlabel`'s
    third group), where LaTeX writes a caption's or a heading's text by design, unless TeX shows what it did with the mark
    (PIPELINE 43, `guard.mjs` `copiesOutOfPlace`): where the compile is otherwise the paper's (it ran through to arXiv's pages,
    its pages' text read through the host's `textOf` with no mark printed — a host that reads none, or failed to, shows nothing,
    and the marks stay out of place —, no TeX error) and TeX wrote the PDF itself (`tellsTwice`: pdfTeX's and LuaTeX's log names every
    destination set twice, XeTeX's driver and the DVI driver latexmk runs tell no log the host returns), each such mark was set
    once where the paper's TeX sets its unit's text — enotez prints each endnote from its `\enotez@note{…}{text}` line at
    `\printendnotes` (2609.36054v2: 16 notes, unmarked and English before, one compile of 34 s more) —, or never — jmlr's
    `\jmlr@author{…}{…}` discards both arguments (2610.21201v1) —, and its unit is located there. One TeX set twice — a unit's own
    start or end mark the log names: elsarticle's and cas-common's `\emailauthor{…}{name}` set an author's name again in the
    e-mail footnote (2610.21084v1, 2610.20848v1) — is out of place still, its unit unmarked and the marked original compiled
    again (round 8 B2, rebuild/block-residue): the reading would drop every destination the log names (`marks.mjs` `readMarked`
    `dropped`) and lay the unit as an unmarked one anyway, and a class may take the argument it stored apart as data, our marks
    among its words. cas-common's `\parsename` splits the name at its spaces and makes each given name's initial of its head,
    `\tl_head:n`: the first word's head was our `\leavevmode`, so that 2610.21084v1's footnotes read "(. Chung)", "(.M. Solomon)",
    "(. Verma)" where arXiv's read "(M. Chung)", "(J.M. Solomon)", "(D. Verma)", and the ink unit made of them, holding the
    initials arXiv's page sets and ours did not, was refused (a content difference). Unmarked, the three names are the paper's
    to the class: our final pass's text is arXiv's but for arXiv's stamp, at one compile more. In the same compile the guard
    reads a class's verbatim copy of our source (`guard.mjs` `cutCopyUnits`): a line of a file the compile wrote that holds a
    mark as our source writes it (no space after its control word: `\write` writes one) is a copy of our line, and where its
    head is our line cut inside our TeX the copy lost the start of it, the unit out of place, unmarked. cas-common's abstract
    is one: `\RenewDocumentEnvironment{abstract}{o}{…\verbatimwrite{\jobname.abs}}{\endverbatimwrite}`, read back by
    `\file_input:n`; the look-ahead for its optional argument reads the body's first token before moreverb's `\verbatimwrite`
    makes every character other, and the copy loses it where it is a control word (TeX Live 2025, tried: a letter is kept,
    `\relax` lost). Ours was the line probe's name, so that the copy read "{4}\leavevmode\axtmark{4s}…", our page set a "4"
    before the abstract and the unit was refused for that content of ours, left English. Unmarked, the paragraph is the
    paper's own to the class (its first character a letter, kept), and its lines an ink unit's. A copy of whole lines stands:
    comment.sty's, acmart's acks (2608.25210v2, 2610.22065v1), whose marks TeX reads back where it sets the text; so does one
    that begins inside the paper's own text, which arXiv's copy cuts alike. Over the 88 papers' marked compiles, marks stand
    in a copy of ours in these three papers alone; of the classes and packages they load, cas-common writes body text
    verbatim to a file after a look-ahead, acmart (through comment.sty) and memoir (its own `\verbatim@out`, which no paper
