  [ours] /Order [] >>`, or a foreign one's kept, ours appended to its `/OCGs` and `/ON`). A BDC goes only between whole
  operators, and each BDC and its EMC share a stream, a q depth, a text-object state and a depth of marked content: a run is
  one group's operators with only state between them, closed at q, Q, BT, ET, any marked content, an inline image, a shading
  or ink not its group's; a rule's path object is wrapped from its first construction operator to its painting; the `ri`
  points stay. A show two groups share is split as the remover's hide mode splits one (E4's variant (a): a number stays with
  the chunk before it, codes kept): no re-anchoring. Content streams name properties, never OCG objects (the later export
  re-points names, §3.3 of the note).
- **Page refusals** (the page left unwrapped, its units `page`): it does not align with PDF.js's reading (remove.mjs
  `alignPage`; a soft mask's content, an ExtGState's `/SMask` that PDF.js lists as a group, is no painted ink of the page's,
  as an annotation's appearance is not: alignOf counts no path or show of it, pageInk's `indices` give none a place —
  2610.19159v1 p3's figure was refused for it, REMOVAL 9), passes the walk's bounds or the wrap's own (`WRAP_DECODED_PAGE` 32 MiB of its content streams decoded,
  `WRAP_HELD_PAGE` 48 MiB of every operator's heap by remove.mjs COST, about 300,000 operators: each read of the page — the
  wrap's, the proof's of the new stream, the proof's of the unwrapped page — under these bounds of its own, in turn, so that a
  plot of millions of path operators is a refused page and never the process), fails its proof (below), or fails in any
  other way (anything thrown but a failed allocation is the page's, never the paper's),
  its own `/Properties` already name a group of ours (the page's own entries are kept, never dropped), holds a form partly owned, an owned run in a clipping text mode (Tr 4 to 6: hiding
  the only clipping run lifts the clip; Tr 7 glyphs are never ink, so never owned), a split in a vertical font or a Type 3 font
  without widths, or PDF.js read it past its bounds. Past `GROUPS_PAGE` 512 groups or `SEQUENCES_PAGE` 2000 sequences the
  page's `.p` and `.l` groups are merged into the text's (a unit with a placeholder there `bounds`), and refused if still past;
  past `GROUPS_DOC` 8000 groups the later pages are refused.
- **The proof** (in the box, every wrap). Of each page, before it is written (a page that fails is refused, never the
  paper): its new stream lexed again within the page's bounds, every BDC of ours named by its groups, none inside another and
  closed at its depth and state, none left open (the page's own marked content need not balance: our runs lie in none of it);
  its operators, ours taken out and each split show's chunks joined, the unwrapped page's (operators, operands, codes and
  numbers in order); and the deflated bytes written inflated back to that stream. The unwrapped page is read again for the
  proof: each of its content streams decoded and lexed whole, every operator kept, under a budget of its own, so that what it
  compares is read from the bytes by the proof itself. What it takes from the wrap is the list of those streams alone (`provePage`:
  the wrap's walk's pieces, the page's `/Contents` as the object layer parsed them, which nothing changes: the wrap writes its
  objects after the file), as a form the page's figures were wrapped in is read by the stream of the wrap's walk's container: a
  second walk of the page found the same list, at the cost of every form on it walked again (2.7 s of 2610.21924v1's wrap on one
  core, its 15,338 forms; 2026-10-31). Of the paper: the section read back
  (`deltaSection`: each entry at its `n g obj`, `/Prev` our startxref) and the wrapped document read again by the object layer
  (catalog, page dicts and resources ours but `/OCProperties`, `/Contents` and `/Properties`; each page's own `/Properties`
  entries kept as they were and ours beside them; every group listed and ON). A failed wrap is the paper's: `wrapFinal` gives `{ refused: 'wrap-parse' |
  'wrap-proof' | 'wrap-bound', why }`, the host passes `ours: { refused: 'wrap', why }`, the head's base is arXiv's with `why:
  'wrap'` (a LAYOUT_REFUSED code).
- **Both forms** are made of the wrapped bytes: the full base IS them (its head's `bytes`, `sha256`, `xref` theirs); the delta
  copies their streams verbatim and carries their catalog's `/OCProperties` alone (19.8). Every check that judges our compile
  reads the same pass; wrapping changes no glyph. The page pass numbers glyphs on the wrapped streams (one stream a page).
- **The host's contract** (the maker child, before any document of its own is open): `wrapFinal(final, { PL, getDocument,
  documentOptions, OPS, units, deflate, inflate })` → `{ bytes, xref, sha256, stats, unhidden, labelKept, pages, own }`
  (`documentOptions` the box's: the lite worker, `maxImageSize: NO_IMAGE_PIXELS`, so that the ownership's read of every
  page decodes no image: a stock read of the 46 MB pair peaks at 3 GB of native memory); then `deltaOf(orig, bytes)` with
  every page replaced that the wrap wrapped (the default) and `proveDelta` (its `readers` reading the wrapped bytes' document, §19.8); then `layerOfPaper({ …, ours: { doc (of the
  wrapped bytes), bytes, sha256, xref, delta, wrap: { stats, unhidden, labelKept, pages } } })` (a delta that leaves a wrapped
  page arXiv's is refused there, `delta-shape`, beside deltaOf's and the proof's own check on the bytes: a unit's group on it
  could not be hidden); the record notes `own` (`{ units, unhidden: { marks, across, spell, page,
  bounds }, spell: [ids, at most 64], labelKept, leaks: { count, units: [ids, at most 64] } }`: `leaks` the units left the
  original's because ink of theirs lies outside every group, so that the next such case shows without pixels). `units` (required) are the paper's SOURCE units, an array each entry of
  which has a source text or pieces (missing, a hole or an entry with neither a TypeError; `null` said asks for no spell check,
  the lab's alone); `deflate` and `inflate` are required (the written bytes are read back); `pages` is required beside the
  lists, the wrapped pages as ranges within our pages and as many as `stats.wrapped` (`pipeline/live.mjs openPaper`'s,
  the page pass's `source.units`): a translation's (text pieces `tr`) holds neither the text after a placeholder its ink ends
  at nor the source the spell check reads, and is refused (TypeError).
- **The head** (both kinds): `base.stats` gains `{ wrapped, refusedPages, unhidden: { marks, across, spell, page, bounds },
  split, groups, labelKept }` (a delta's own counts beside them; every unit counted); `base.unhidden` `[[unit id, code], …]`
  by rising id and `base.labelKept` rising ids, none in both, of the units with a group in the document alone (a unit with
  none is the original's by construction): so each holds at most `GROUPS_DOC`, `UNHIDDEN_MAX` 8000, and a long paper cut at
  `GROUPS_DOC` keeps its base, its later pages unwrapped; checked by `delta-wire.mjs wrapWhy` on both sides for their shape and
  that the counts are at least the lists' (that a unit with a group and no list entry is the reader's to hide is `wrapFinal`'s
  word: no head reader knows the groups). A page merged for its bounds makes a unit with a placeholder or a label there `bounds`. A unit is the reader's to hide iff the config holds `axt:u<id>` and it is in neither
  list. A head without them is an unwrapped base. The cell rules the add-on manifest carried are each part's `rules` now (§11.8).
- **Measured** (2026-10-23, the gate pack's 7 papers in Chinese and 2602.23285v2, the sources' units): every page wrapped
  (290/290, 0 refused, the proof passing on all); `spell` 1 unit of 1,806 (2608.04322v1 u0: its journal header over-taken),
  `marks` 38 (24 the title block's authors and `\thanks` notes the marker does not mark, the engine lane's item; 14 cells that
  open with an unmarked macro), `across` 0, labels kept 0 (the earlier 9 were each a label and a lead macro, now split); ownership equal to today's geometric ownership on 1,740 of 1,806 units (96.3 %: the rest the marks' own over
  today's residue, a table's row header today calls a cell's label, a babel name, the unmarked authors); 54 shows split; 230 to
  981 groups a paper. The wrap 0.4 to 1.9 s a paper in Node with PDF.js's lite worker (the 147-page thesis 1.9 s), +165 MB
  at most beside what the maker holds (the 46 MB pair); the wrapped base 0.4 % to 23 % larger (the thesis 3.08 to 3.79 MB);
  the deltas 2,561,390 bytes over 83,666,965 of originals (3.06 %; 2,139,403 unwrapped, 2.56 %: 1.08x to 1.53x each; layers
  matched by identity cost 1706.03762v7's figures, whose forms name arXiv's layers, 61 KB either way), the largest 0.87 MB
  (2307.16209v1), the delta proof passing on 8 of 8. The lab gate (`lab/pdf/spikes/ocg-gate.mjs`, its run in
  `lab/pdf/records/ocg-gate.md`) in Chromium, GPU and CPU canvases, every page of the 8: all groups ON is our page, 0 px
  outside split glyphs and image edges, 0 px inside the split glyphs; text and labels OFF equal the remover's cut of the same
  ownership on 247 pages (measured at 85fdc442, while the remover was still there; that comparison ended with its deletion), 0 px outside image edges, and the image-edge pixels the two change equal (72 on GPU, 31 on CPU).
  Chromium differs from itself on two pages in earlier runs of one long-lived browser (2608.04322v1 p9 GPU, 2609.26457v1 p2
  CPU: our unwrapped page against itself), 0 px from fresh documents.

### 19.10 Content classes and the ledger (stage 1 of `docs/route/orphan-text.md`)

Every text glyph of our final pass belongs to exactly one content class, and each class has one translation path, made once on
the server, and one reader toggle (the owner's rulings of 2026-10-25: always, heads and feet, tables, figure text, references,
names, never). The one table is `rules/content-classes.mjs` (`CLASSES`, `TOGGLES`; a unit's class by its kind, `unitClass`, the
same on the server and in every reader, from what the bundle's units already carry). The maker child's `wrapFinal` returns each
paper's ledger (`layout/ledger.mjs` `ledgerOf`, `ledgerSummary`: each class's glyphs and letters, the document's letters, its
orphan letters), read from facts alone: a glyph's owner (own.mjs), its region (in a column's body or not, a float's depth), the
babel names' points that open a list or the bibliography, stream order on the page (the head before its first mark, the foot
after its last, on one baseline, as `folioOf` reads a folio), whether it is inside a form XObject (an included PDF: pageInk's
`form` with `indices`), and its face's family (math, typewriter). No layout file and no version changes: nothing on the wire,
nothing in the compile. What no class explains is an orphan: the sweep's invariant (o) is no orphan letters (`orphanRows`, rows
in the sweep's shape), run in the lab by `lab/pdf/spikes/ledger.mjs` (record `lab/pdf/records/ledger.md`). The class `figures`
is built (§19.12): a glyph a figure unit owns (`f<k>`) is the ledger's `figures`, cut before the ink units, so that none of them
takes a figure's text.

**The ink units (stages 2 and 3, BUNDLE5 `'10'`, LAYOUT `'21'`, REMOVAL `'11'`).** Text no source unit owns — the running heads and
feet, the contents and the lists, a note with no unit, prose the front end did not cut — is made units of our own glyphs in the
wrap (`layout/ink-units.mjs`), from the ledger's lines: a head's line one, a contents entry or a block one paragraph of TeX's (the
layout compile's point `q<n>` at LaTeX's para/begin, inside the paragraph's indentation box so that no paragraph's list
changes, which pageInk keeps apart from the marks' points as `paras`; a paragraph with no indentation carries none and reads
as the one before; a paragraph's next line is followed at the paper's own leading, `PARA_DY` 3 of its size at most, where
`BLOCK_DY` 1.75 falls short, when it starts an indent from the paragraph's first line, more than `EDGE` 0.75 of its size
across and no more than `INDENT` 6 (a hanging line, or the run after an indented first), measured only from a block whose first
line holds its paragraph's point (the ledger's `opens`, PIPELINE 32: a block that begins at a column's or a page's top where a
paragraph runs on begins at a line of that run, and REVTeX's bibliography, whose entries set no point and so read as one
paragraph, had every next entry's label an indent from it: 2610.21770v1's and 2610.20595v1's orphan entries joined over each
entry's link line, a column one unit), LAYOUT 25: a thesis's list of
figures set double was cut line by line, each line translated alone, 2610.19274v1 pp67–69; a list's items, which no point of
their own tells apart, start at its edge, a right-aligned label's digit (half a size) aside, and stay apart at their skip,
single-line or not, and a list after a centred heading starts further across than any indent (2610.20266v1 p21's
bibliography, its labels [9] and [10] half a size apart, its "REFERENCES" 20 sizes in); a script a text face sets after a formula's run is that run's placeholder, C_n²'s "2"; the ink
units, as the figure units, are units of the paper's for PIPELINE: a translation is stored for them and found again by an output
identity that names PIPELINE, so their cut moving raises it, PIPELINE 31, and the unit-cut golden holds their cut), each of its
class's kind (`inkheads`, `inkcontents`, `inknotes`, `inkorphan`, after the source kinds in UNIT_KINDS; `inknames` a block
most of whose letters are an author unit's words, of the names toggle as that unit is, and so one that echoes a unit of the
author block, an affiliation REVTeX or ACM prints from its own lists, PIPELINE 74), its numbering, leaders
and page number left the original's ink (a leader dot a word a word's gap from the word before it, `WORD_GAP`, as
`\@dottedtocline`'s `\mkern\@dotsep` sets it: a stop that abuts a formula, a word of its own by its face alone, is the entry's,
PIPELINE 34, 2610.19274v1's list of figures, "… strength $C_n^2$." had its stop left beside the drawn entry; two words of its line
are joined by a space only where a gap stands between them), its numbering and page number where a number stands apart from the line's text (`APART`, half its size: a folio, a
section number's `\quad`, a page number after leaders) or is a running head's folio (the head's other words recur on another
page with another number there: amsart's `\llap{\thepage}` after a title as wide as the line sets two digits nearer its last
word than its words are to each other, 2610.21884v1), a number in the text's own words the unit's, translated in its flow
(LAYOUT 25: 2010.11929v2's running head "Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2021", the same on every page, had its year
left the original's and drawn apart from its line), its math and typewriter runs (and a web address in any face) kept placeholders (the
rebuilt reader's copy of the maker, `packages/engine` `locate/today/ink-units.mjs`, keeps an e-mail address in a word one too, the
address alone and the word's other characters text, by the front end's own pattern, `latex-front.mjs` `EMAIL_ADDRESS`: in colour
groups no translation kept, 2609.36054v2 p1's grey addresses were drawn black, #28; and a group of local parts before their one
domain, `ADDRESS_GROUP`, one kept run over its words and over the break of lines TeX set one right after the other, every glyph
of it whatever its face: 2611.00342v1 p1's two rows, braces in the symbol font's math face, the first broken after a comma, had
their local parts sent under the names toggle and drawn back capitalised with full-width commas; now lines of addresses alone
are no ink unit's but a kept block, and a group inside a note one element of it; and it gives each kept run its own ink, which
today's file draws by its own segments and the copy had given the unit's first placeholder: 149 of the 88 corpus papers' 185 ink
members of two elements or more drew every run at the first one's place; and it writes a kept formula's TeX specials by the tokens
that set them in a formula, `\{`, `\}`, `\$` and `\backslash`, where today's file strips them: a run of a brace alone, the closing
brace of `\{0,\dots,J-1\}` between upright digits, 2610.21377v1 p42, or a bibliography title's `$\{$Intra-Operator$\}$`,
2608.06007v1 p17, was `$$`, which every reader takes as a display, and once drawn in its own ink each was a kept display row in
the middle of its line: 15 runs in 3 members; over the 88 corpus papers 10 ink units of 3 papers change their id, the copy text
of 25 other runs gains the braces it had lost; and it reads a script by its glyph, whatever its face (`scriptsOf`): a glyph TeX
set smaller than its line's text and off its baseline (the size most of the line's glyphs have, the baseline most of those stand
on, each on the hundredth of a point, as locate reads one box's baseline: no threshold) is a kept run's, where the face alone made
a script in a text face the unit's text, drawn flat at the line's size — Times sets `$^{1,2}$`'s digits in its text face and
Computer Modern a formula's digit or a footnote's mark in CMR7, so 2610.30854v1 p1's names read "Jiang1,2"; a run of scripts of one
sign is written as TeX writes one, `$^{…}$` or `$_{…}$`, so that every reader of the source reads it as a source unit's mark (a
mark of one symbol drawn raised, `sym`, where `$*$` drew it on the baseline at the line's size); a unit's label is its first
line's leading run of raised scripts, in any face (`labelLength` without today's 0.85 and a fifth: 2610.40394v1 p1's "*", 7.77
pt on its note's 7.97 and raised 0.20 pt, was a placeholder, its note no longer echoing its source footnote), its glyphs the
text's as before; and no run is joined over a line's break where a script stands at the break, as TeX sets a script on its line
after its atom and breaks a formula only after a binary operation or a relation (2610.20030v1 p1's "Krajnc¹" and "¹Jožef Stefan
Institute" one element on two lines, drawn as text): over the 88 corpus papers 79 ink units of 21 papers move and one more
states its label, 69 runs written as scripts (50 raised, 19 lowered), 4 display lines in a text face of 2608.08481v1 no longer
translated, no source unit; and a line of no text word — an address, a URL TeX broke onto a line of its own — is the next line of
the unit its line before belongs to in one of TeX's paragraphs as the compile marked them, never by the lines' places alone, and
starts no unit (round 8 B2, rebuild/block-residue): left out of every unit since an address became a kept run, JCAP's
`E-mail: \the\email@toks`, broken before its last address, was the block's names unit on its first line and a kept block on its
second (2609.20976v1 p1, lost in the differential, the block's rule taking the one and not the other). Over the 88 papers 59 such
lines stand in a class made units; 3 join, the e-mail line and ACM's permission note's DOI after "ACM ISBN …" (2402.10294v1,
2610.22214v1), each a kept block before; the other 56 stay apart, each beginning its paragraph or another than the line before's
(addresses under their affiliations, footnotes' URLs after their marks, 3 typewriter words, a table's figures): no line of code
joins a unit of prose, and 2610.19159v1's transcripts, code its regions keep, hold none), and
each run of its words in another weight, slant or colour than most of its glyphs hold a group of the commands that set it
(`\textbf{`, `\textmd{`, `\textit{`, `\textup{`, `\textcolor[HTML]{…}{`, rule 9, LAYOUT `'23'`), as a source unit's groups are,
so that its translation keeps each run's style (the release sweep of 2026-10-25, (d): a theorem's bold head before its regular
note, a reference's italic title, a coloured term, all drawn in the unit's one style). Its text is its glyphs' characters, a spacing
accent TeX's `\accent` set over its letter joined to it (`layout/accents.mjs`, the reader's table, `joinAccents`: the accent and its
letter next in the stream, in one font, the accent's advance centred on the letter's, its baseline the letter's or above it by at
most the letter's height; only the move back over the accent puts it there, never an apostrophe's or a quote's advance, nor a
formula's `\hat` in its own font: "F´ısica" for Física, "Cande`s" for Candès, "PE´REZ" for PÉREZ, read left to right before,
13 ink units of the 87-paper sweep in 7 papers, whose "M. Bru¨ckner" Microsoft's zh spelled as "Bru·ickner"; PIPELINE 74), and its label
is none of it (`labelLength`: the glyphs of no letter its first line begins with, each smaller than `SCRIPT` of the line's size and
raised over its baseline by more than a fifth of it, as the reader keeps a label, up to three digits or marks, or up to three
marks of no digit: the reader breaks its words at that baseline and kept the original's, so a text that said it drew it twice,
"¹ 1Instituto de Física …" on 2610.20716v1 p1; its glyphs stay the unit's, claimed, erased, in its line's box; PIPELINE 74). The
reader keeps that label as the original's ink, the first line laid after it; where the line is not laid from where TeX set it,
centred (by the file's flag, LAYOUT 37, or by the door's reading of its lines) or flush right, the label goes with it, its ink
copied as the line's first item and erased where it stood (`run.mjs` `carried`, as a source unit's label group was carried on a
centred line before): an ink unit has no label group, and its label's ink is its text's, hidden with it. The copy stands as high
over the line's baseline as TeX set it (the baseline the line's own characters give), so that a raised mark stays raised: set by
its own baseline, it had stood on the translation's, 3.8 pt low, and so had every raised label carried before (2610.20848v1's
seventeen affiliations' letters). Left where it stood, the
shorter translation centred alone stood up to 118 pt from it (12 lines of 7 of the 87 papers, all the author block's: 2610.20716v1's
"1" 93 pt left of its translated place, 2610.21765v1, 2610.21770v1, 2610.22065v1 among them). A label the wrap left the
original's ink (`labelKept`) stays where it stands. One
whose letters and placeholders are a source unit's (a heading first), else an earlier ink unit's (a running head), echoes it: its pieces that unit's, its row that unit's row under its own id, never translated
itself (`rows.mjs` `echoRows`, `layerIds`). Its glyphs are claimed under its own groups, `u<id>` and `u<id>.p`, so the reader
hides it as any unit; one the wrap could not hide alone (its page not wrapped, its placeholder's group merged: `ink.off`), or on a
page not drawable, keeps its id (which names its groups and which an echo names) and is laid nowhere. The page pass carries them (`pipeline/ink-pass.mjs`, from the host's `ours.ink`): in the bundle's units
after the source units', in a chunk of their own (`INK_UNITS_FORMAT` `'2'`, a seventh element, the echo; the source units' chunks
byte for byte as before), on the left by arXiv's tokens on their lines, in the layout by the wrap's rows. An ink unit's text is
its own alone (LAYOUT `'23'`): a source unit's label row that meets it goes from the layout (`layoutWithInk`), and so does one
that meets a figure unit's run (PIPELINE 49, §19.12). The maker reads a
label off the glyphs left of a unit's start mark, and the wrap leaves one with no label's form in no group (`labelKept`), where
an ink unit then claims it; the reader shows a label row its unit does not draw again from render C, every group shown, so that
row put the original back under the ink unit's translation (the release sweep of 2026-10-25, (c): SIAM's "AMS subject
classifications." before its codes, 2610.20266v1 p1; a theorem's head whose note is a citation, "Definition 1 ([TT])", whose
body's label it was; 2610.11256v1's bold heads before a table's cells). Such a head and its body's first row share one of TeX's
lines, and the body is laid from where the head's translation's ink ends there, the original's separation after it (a shared line,
`need.mjs` `rowLeadOf`, which takes its lead by K's order alone wherever the order is given: an ink unit is numbered after every
source unit, and by the ids the head came after its body, which was laid where the English head had ended, a blank of its
width less the translation's after the translated head: 2610.40645v1 pp14-15's "Theorem 3.3 ([Ang, Theorem 1.1])." and
"Proposition 3.2 ([Ang, Proposition A.1])." in Japanese, the owner's report of 2026-11-01). Two rows are one of TeX's lines where the
file's baselines are at most one hundredth apart: the file writes each row's baseline to a hundredth on its own (its glyphs' y
rounded, `layout/make.mjs` `baselineOf`), so that float noise on either side of a half splits one line in two (a drawing rule, no
version, §18.3). 2610.40645v1 p34's "Proof of Proposition 4.4." is placed by `Td` at 539.605 and its text by `Tm`, which PDF.js
reads as a float32, 539.60498: written 539.61 and 539.60, the two were no shared line, and the text was laid where the English head
had ended, 5.14 em after the translated head in Chinese against 0.55 em in the original (the owner's report of 2026-11-04). Over
the release sweep's corpus (b6586f7c, 1,308 shared lines) the rule finds three more: two heads, 2610.40645v1 p34's (zh, ja) and
2610.20266v1 p26's (zh, 3.39 em), which go to the original's gap, and 2609.20976v1 p1's line of names (ja), drawn as before; the
gate pack's layout files hold no such pair, and its cut is byte for byte the same. The body starts where the head's ink ends,
not its last advance (`layer2.mjs` `shareOf`'s `ink`: the last drawn item's own right edge, TextMetrics' `actualBoundingBoxRight`
of its text in its face, measured as its width is and cached apart (one more number on every width's entry grew the heap 2.8 KB a
laid page, the speed check), with its tracking and an oblique face's slant): a full-width closing mark keeps a blank half
in its advance, an ideographic full stop's ink ending 0.34 em into its em in Source Han Serif, and that blank stood on the
original's separation (2010.11929v2 p4's "Inductive bias." in Chinese, 1.71 em to its text against the original's 1.05: the
owner's report of 2026-11-04; a drawing rule, no version). One rule for every face and language, from what the face draws, with no
list of marks: it takes the full-width colon too, whose ink a Chinese face sets in its left half. The page fill keeps a head's row
only where its ink there ends no further right than its fit's (`keepsShare`). Over the corpus's 1,022 run-in heads (the sweep's
rows, both panes measured ink to ink, each in its own em; the diagnosis's census), the 598 Chinese heads in 37 of 55 papers and the
27 Japanese whose last advance held a blank of over a quarter em went from +0.64 em wider than the original (Chinese, the median;
+0.44 to +0.81) and +0.69 (Japanese) to −0.03 (−0.16 to +0.13) and 0.00 (−0.07 to +0.29); the three heads above to −0.08 and
−0.04; the 361 Chinese
heads that were as the original from +0.02 to −0.05 (−0.25 to +0.19), the 15 Japanese and 5 Polish to −0.03 and −0.05; no head
changed state. The original's separation stays the layout file's, advance to advance (its rows' x1 and x0): neither the file nor
the parts hold the ink of the original's glyphs, and the door's own read of a page's glyphs is bounded by a clock and absent on a
page drawn from data, so a gap comes out the English last glyph's right bearing and its text's first glyph's left bearing tighter
than the original's ink to ink, 0.05 em at the median and 0.25 at most (2610.16663v1 p45, a head ending ")." at 12 pt); the
owner ruled on 2026-11-04 that it stays (no ink-level precision: a gap of the original's spaces is the rule). **A head the left
does not hold stands in K before its text (PIPELINE 65).** The lead is chosen among the entries before its text in K, and a unit
only the layout file holds (no left unit, so no stream of its own: a heading the left found no place for) took its slot after
the largest stream of a left unit with a smaller id over the whole paper. A float or a note numbered before the head and
streamed after its text put the head after its text, which then found no lead and was laid where the English head had ended:
2610.21547v1 p16's "Label flipping." after a caption of page 17 (1.66 em more than the original), 2610.21924v1 p21 (16.04),
2610.21884v1 p13 (6.94), 2610.37668v1 p21's "Initialization." (1.61). Such a unit now stands beside the left unit it shares one
of TeX's lines with (`need.mjs` `lineAfterOf`, in the cutter's K and the door's own): right after the unit whose last row its
first row continues, else right before the units whose first row continues its last; through the units the file alone holds
between them on the line, each one past the one before it within the room before the next left unit's stream, so that a chain
A (the left's), B, C (the file's alone) stands A, B, C whatever its ids (a review's finding on #579); any other as before. TeX's line is the
one fact that says where in the stream such a unit stands, whatever its id: ids are the source's order, which floats, notes and
ink units (numbered after every source unit) do not keep. Over the sweep's 87 papers it moves 7 of 5,241 such units (rules by
the ids over the left units up to its own page, or by the next unit's stream, moved 998 or 2,347 and lost two shared lines
each): the four heads, and three lines of amsart's keywords after "Key words and phrases.", an ink unit, which shared their line
before only where an affiliation of the last page stood before them by id; every other paper's K is the same, slot for slot. Over
the census's 1,022 heads (the sweep's rows, the six papers whose K moved cut again) exactly the four move, to the original's
gap: from +1.66, +16.04, +6.94 and +1.61 em more than the original to 0.00, -0.07, -0.09 and -0.08; no other head moves by
more than 0.05 em, and none changes state. The page stream closes a part only where no slot of it is past the stream right below the least
left unit whose line such a unit may still share (`frontier.mjs` `partClosable`): a chain of them before that unit stands down to
there (with streams 10 and 12, two before 12 stand 10.5 and 11.5; half a step below 12 alone let a part close at 10.5 that the
first of them sorts before by its id: a review's finding on #579), and a unit told keeps in the stream, beside the pages K
reads of it, its first and last lines whole (`make.mjs` `stubOf`), what a shared line reads: with its pages alone, a unit only
the file holds, told beside its line's other unit, took its slot by the ids in the parts after its own, and 2610.21884v1's parts
from page 4 on were not the whole's. Its streamed and whole prepares now give the same head, parts and left parts, as
2610.37668v1's do (the lane's offline prepare). One head of the census was still after its text, 2610.37668v1's "Surface
losses." (below).

**The rest of the run-in heads' cases (PIPELINE 68, LAYOUT 34).** A unit only the layout file holds and no line of TeX's places
stands after the largest stream of a left unit with a smaller id among those first framed on pages up to its own first row's
page (`cut.mjs` `entriesOf`, `need.mjs` `pagedBefore`; the door's own K the same). Over the whole paper by the ids, a float or
a note numbered before it and set pages later put its slot at that float's, and the frontier of its own page reached there:
2610.21884v1's first part (pages 1 to 3) told entries reaching page 31, 254,889 B, where it now reaches page 3, 20,722 B. The
page stream bounds the slot of such a unit not in K for good by the units placed up to the page after the pages done
(`frontier.mjs` `leftBoundsOf`: every such unit has its rows past them); past the pages the maker let go instead, a unit made
whose left anchor is not final, on a page let go, was bounded by units placed after its own page, and a part closed that it
sorts into. Over the sweep's 87 papers 991 such slots move and no lead on a shared line changes; 9
papers' parts differ, 443 pages read fewer bytes before them and none waits on a later page; 5 pages read 74 to 76 B more, every
byte in their paper's last part (the font names the units moved there bring into its own table, less the views the part before
no longer carries). On 2610.21884v1 the stream still cuts every part at the end: its ranged anchoring of page 1 waits for its
affiliation's marks on page 31 (where a unit is searched, below: PIPELINE 70). The layout maker takes no label
where a unit's own text begins (`make.mjs` `headLabel`): where the line read from the head's first glyph spells more of the
unit's text, past the head, than the line read from after it, its case and compatibility forms aside, the head is that text
(a label "1" before "11 apples" spells two characters of it from the label, all of it from after: a label). 2610.21377v1 sets `49\textsc{k}20
(primary)` in its subject classes: the source's words parted at the small capital, its text's start fell to the "k", and "49"
was read as an item's number, kept as the original's before a line laid from the "k": "49 49k20". Over the left lane's 65
papers 9 units are laid again, each a text that opens with what reads as a label (that line; 2610.19159v1's paragraphs that
begin with an agent transcript's "**"; an author line that begins with "*"); the gate pack's 32 layout files are the ones
before but for their version. And the left's heading rule (`anchors.mjs` `matchUnits`): a unit with no marks found by its
words in a row at the last of several places in the gap between its marked neighbours is searched again between its nearest
neighbours whose place is certain (found by their text, or by their words where they come once in the gap), floats aside.
2610.37668v1's "Surface losses." had taken a figure's panel title of page 22 with its words, the last of eight places in the
gap (no mark of the 29 units around it is carried on arXiv's PDF), and "Initialization." another; each now stands right
before its text. A neighbour found by the same rule at one of several places is no bound: 2610.16663v1's two headings of one
title both took the gap's last place, and one bounded by the other was put on the other's page. Over the left lane's 65
papers 5 units move on 2 papers, each to its own place (2307.16209v1's four, which a running head of the same words had put
four pages on, out of TeX's order), none lost. Located, "Initialization." showed a rule of the layer's: a unit's line grows over
what no other unit holds, and a located unit's rectangles are its left ones, arXiv's page's, which stand where ours do but on a
page drawn through drift. 2610.37668v1's page 21 is set 9 pt lower on ours, the head's left rectangle stood over its own line,
and its text's first line grew over the head's word, which its source holds, to the head's start (0.05 em to the head where
the original has 0.71). A neighbour's line now grows over no unit's own lines of the file either (`run.mjs` `growOn`), a
drawing rule, so no version (§18.3).

**Where a unit is searched, known from the head (PIPELINE 70, LAYOUT 35).** The owner's first problem is how soon a new paper's
first page shows. The page stream tells a part once everything it reads is final, and the first page's left read every unit whose
search could reach it. A unit whose marks did not bound it was searched between its nearest *bounded* neighbours by number: known
only once their marks were read, and until then a window from the last bounded unit to wherever the next one stood, to the paper's
end where no later one was marked yet. The stream held every page such a window could meet, on both sides (the left, arXiv's
page; the maker, ours). On 2610.21884v1 the affiliation u2, a float numbered among page 1's units, has its marks on page 31, where
TeX set the affiliations: its window was page 1, so page 1 waited for page 31. The units' number says only the source's order,
which a float, a note or a unit numbered after the text (an affiliation, a title, a figure's text, a table's cells set pages on)
does not keep; the head says, before any page is read, the pages each unit's own marks stand on. One rule for the matcher
(`anchors.mjs` `matchUnits`) and the stream (`left-part.mjs` `rangedAnchors`, `leftReach`), both anchorings under it
(`searchHead`). A unit with marks is searched within its bounds; where they do not bound it, first in the part of its gap between
its neighbours on its own pages and a page beside (`DRIFT`: a mark TeX writes before a page break stands a page from its words,
and our compile and arXiv's drift), by the gap's rules, then on those pages alone; where its stretch meets them nowhere, on them
alone, never waiting for its neighbours. A unit without marks is searched in its gap between its nearest neighbours with marks in
the text, within their stretch (the page before the last of the earlier one's own pages to the page after the first of the later
one's; a float's on to the pages of the float with marks before it, its table's caption, TeX setting a float with its own units
and never before its source): its edges the first neighbour that bounds it within the stretch, or, for a unit in the text, where
an unbounded one's own text stands on its own pages (`ownPlaces`); a float of K words or more then by its match over the whole
document, as before. So a unit's match is final once it and the units its gap's walk meets are marked, its reach is fixed from the
head until then, and once final a unit without bounds is matched at once and reaches where its match stands. Each step was
measured against #584 over the sweep's 78 papers on disk and kept where it lost nothing: a float without marks by its
whole-document match alone lost 22 figure texts of 2610.37818v1 and took 2610.19159v1's cells from a table 42 pages on; in its
whole stretch a table's cells took a neighbouring table's; a unit whose marks do not bound it on its own pages alone lost short
texts whose words come twice there (2608.06007v1's "Stepfun", 2307.16209v1's "Expansion for :"); a gap bounded at an unbounded
neighbour's pages put two paragraphs a page on; a float's gap edged where its text neighbours' words stand lost two figure texts
of 1810.04805v2's page 16; and without its caption's pages a table set two pages on lost 8 cells (2610.30854v1). Measured over the 78
papers (the production pass offline, an instrumented copy of the engine that records each page's read time and each part's
close): the first part is told sooner on 38 of 77 (2610.20030v1 refuses its layout), on the same page on 35, a page later on 4
(a unit not yet marked may still reach the page beside its own pages); sooner by a median 2 pages (1 to 111) and 0.16 s
of the page pass on the base run's own timeline (0.04 to 4.34 s; 13.2 s over the 38); told only at the paper's last page on 13
against 19. 2610.19159v1 (163 pages) tells pages 1 to 4 at page 48, at 159 before, 4.34 s sooner. The left over the 78: 32,499
units located before, 32,515 now: 16 gained (12 footnotes of 2307.16209v1 found on their own pages, 2610.30854v1's two cells and
two references), none lost, none moved; the maker lays 2610.17024v1's title, keyword list and 29 references, and 2610.30769v1's
title, units numbered after the text that it did not lay. Streamed equals whole on all 78 papers. What still holds a first part
is no search: the cut's slot of a unit the left may not locate (2610.21884v1's affiliation, after units 0 and 1 by its id) and a
table's cells whose whole-document match stands pages on (2610.19159v1's, page 46: their left anchor is final only there).

A run-in head its own row cannot hold uses the
rest of its line (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-03; a drawing rule, so no version, §18.3). Laid in its row alone, beside the
paragraph's first words, which are ink the fit may not widen over (`widenOverPaper`), a head whose translation is much longer
than the English fitted only below its floor, or not at all: 2610.19159v1 p7's "Node-level grading still separates agents."
needs 34 em of Japanese on a row of 170.6 pt, past what `floorMin` 0.6 reaches, and stayed English beside its Japanese paragraph
(`unfit`). Where a head's fit in its row is clipped at its floor, its last block now runs on to the end of the paragraph's first
line (`run.mjs` `overFollower`), taken where it fits there at the floor or above; the paragraph is laid from where the head's
translation ends, its first line shorter, or given way to its next row. A head its row holds only by shrinking takes the rest
of its line too, where it is set larger there (the owner's report of 2026-11-10 on round 8's staging, 2611.03178v1 page 16 in
Chinese: "ML Coding." in seven characters shrunk to 0.85 of the body in its own 62 pt, and the size tie of the 2026-11-08 ruling,
one paragraph's text at one scale, set its whole paragraph at 0.85 among paragraphs at full size, a hole under it; laid over its
row the head is at full size, 73 pt, and so is its paragraph, its first line from the head's end). Before the tie a head that
fitted its row at the floor or above kept it, since its paragraph paid for the room (1810.04805v2's Russian p4, a paragraph from
0.73 to 0.70 for a head from 0.85 to 1); under the tie the head's shrink is its paragraph's, and over the corpus's 90 pairs with
stored rows (part A's bundles) 29 heads in 14 pairs take their row (34 in 18 with every toggle on), from 0.80-0.975 to 1 (two to
0.9 and 0.975), 68 units on 24 of 2,564 pages move (77 on 27), and no paragraph comes out smaller: 27 larger, 2 the same.
The two are decided together (`settleLeadOf`, `relay`): where the paragraph is left the original's, is not laid from the head's
end (`ledBy`), or fits from there only below its own floor, the head is laid again in its row alone, as before, and the
paragraph again from where the head then ends; no unit goes under its floor to lift another. This runs as the paragraph's lay
ends, or as it is refused unlaid for a page that failed, before their page passes; on a row three units share it settles from
the last back. A head of several lines, one with something kept between it and its text (`keptAfter`), and one that begins on an
earlier page (that page's pass paints it on the row's page before the paragraph is laid, past taking back) are laid as before.
On 2610.19159v1 in Japanese (staging's rows) ten run-in heads move:
nine from 0.62 to 0.80 of the body's size to 0.96 to 1, and "Node-level grading…" from English to 0.97; three paragraphs lose up
to 8 % of their size to a shorter first line, seven only reflow. In Chinese, over the corpus's 462 pages with a shared line (57
papers, the sweep's rows), two heads move: 2610.21026v1's "Part I." and 1810.04805v2's "QNLI", English before. In Korean on
19159, none. Every other unit is drawn as before. The reader's toggles
are an option of the layer's open (`classes`, `TOGGLE_DEFAULTS`); a change of them is an open again over the same documents, parts
and rows (`layer-side.mjs` `setClasses`), each laid page kept until the new door's commits: 81 to 384 ms to the two pages in view
over 14 page pairs (the layer gate's jump, `--perf`). The web's half is `docs/route/orphan-text.md` §8.

**An item's label on a shared line, and a shared line where the translation before it ends (the owner's report of 2026-11-05).**
2610.21085v1 p2 in Chinese, "Our contributions are fourfold. (1) … (2) … (3) … (4) …": an inline list (enumitem's `enumerate*`,
`label=(\arabic*)`), each item a unit of its own whose first row TeX set on the line where the item before ends. The file holds
each "(n)" as its item's label (`make.mjs` `labelOf`: the glyphs TeX set before the unit's start mark, whatever command set them:
paralist's `inparaenum`, an `\item[(1)]` by hand), kept as the original's ink where TeX set it; `keptBetween` saw it between the
two units and refused the shared line, so each item was laid from TeX's English x: a blank of several em after the paragraph's
first sentence, "(2)" and "(3)" alone at the column's right edge, "(4)" mid-line. Where the only thing between the two, from the
unit before's end to the next unit's first word, is that unit's own label (`run.mjs` `ownLabelOnRow`: its label row on the row,
after the unit before's end, its group one the layer hides; the glyphs it carries aside, nothing of the page there, so that a mark
between the label and the word, another unit's or no unit's, keeps both where TeX set them), the label goes with its unit: its ink copied as the first line's start, set by the row's baseline so that a raised mark
stays raised, its first word glued to it, and erased where it stood; the unit before still ends its text on the row where TeX did.
A shared line that holds the label and not its first word is left as a sliver is (`layer2.mjs`, the breaker's `ownLabel`), never
the label alone at the line's end (2610.21098v1 p2's "(2)" was, its text a line under it). And where the unit before ends its
translation above TeX's shared row (a Chinese translation at its own leading, 16.9 pt a line against the original's 14.45), its
last line is the shared line (`shareOf`'s `above`, or its `at` within an em of the row): the next unit goes on on it after its
ink, the original's separation kept, and its lines flow on from there at its own pitch (`slotsAt`, `onLead`), one paragraph read
straight through as the original reads. Its lines laid over the rows the unit before left, down to the shared row, are that
paragraph's: each takes the measure TeX set at its height (`flowX`, `flowMeasureAt`), the unit before's rows' and on the row both
units' (the row's start the one's, its end the other's), not the next unit's first block's, which holds only its own rows there:
where TeX set a float right after the shared row, the row's remainder alone, and 2608.16117v1 p19's u59 ("The increasing-" at the
end of the line before Figure 9) laid "and" and "MacKintosh," each on a 79 pt line at the column's right edge, its text going on
after the figure. Nor a block's outer bounds, which take in rows further down: beside a wrapfigure whose rows around the shared
row end before it and whose rows under it run on to the column's edge, a flowed line laid at those bounds ran on over the figure
(the review of #595). Laid on TeX's row under it, it stood a line's height under the line before (12 pt at 11.95
pt type); laid from TeX's row after a first line on the line over it, its second line stood a pitch and that distance under the
first (2610.21098v1 p2's item (3): 26.4 pt at a pitch of 16.9). The page fill keeps that line (`keepsShare`: still the unit's
last, on its baseline, no further right), so that a unit before it whose fill would spread its lines over more of its frames keeps
its fit's pitch where spreading moves the line: 2608.16117v1's u57, the paragraph a float splits from u59, 18.8 pt a line on pages
18 and 19 where its fill set 23.1, its frame on page 18 ending 17.4 pt higher (the rules gate's three pages that move, pages 17 to
19 of that paper in Chinese: its blank lines a frame a little worse, its wide paragraph gaps fewer); where none of the next unit's
text fits after it, its first line stands a pitch under it, unless its last line then ends lower than laid as before, where it is
laid as before. Lower is read across pages, a line on a later page lower than any of the page before. And where that leaves none of
the unit on its first row's page while laid as before it has a line there, it is laid as before (2026-11-06; the release sweep of
e4be8723, its first follow-up): 2501.14787v1 p57's u423 ("So here, we aren't thinking of a, b as numbers…") shares p57's last line
with u422 ("…as seen in the diagram below:"), whose Chinese ends on the line over it, 14.9 pt up, with no room after it. A pitch
under that line stood 0.6 pt under the row at u423's leading of 1.3, past the foot of its block on p57, the row alone. So none of
u423 was laid on p57, its row was erased and drawn empty, and all its text went to p58, ending where it ends laid from the row.
The check read its first line, on p58, as higher than the line before on p57 (its baseline the greater number). It is laid from
TeX's row again, as production drew it: 27 characters on p57, p58's two lines as production's. Over the release sweep's 88 pass-papers (1,308 shared rows): `keptBetween` refused 83 rows and refuses 52, the 31
that go each a unit's own label between it and the unit before (11 inline items of 2610.21085v1 and 2610.21098v1, a sub-caption's
"(d)", 3 paragraph footnotes' marks, and 16 author lines' affiliation marks, which are drawn pixel for pixel as before); 28 next
units are laid anew (their lines in reading order): 15 go on on the line before, the translation before them ending over the row;
3 move on the row with their label; 6 kept their first line on the line before, within an em over the row, and now flow on from it
(2610.37668v1 p5's u45, 2610.21377v1 p43's u592 among them); 2 keep their first line and move with their page's fill; and 2 are
laid from TeX's row where a pitch under the line before would end them lower (2610.21098v1 p1's u9 and p2's u14, 13.6 and 16.3 pt
under that line, at their pitches of 13.5 and 17.6); no label stands alone on a line. 9 of them end lower than before, by 0.1 to
17.9 pt, each within its block's foot (`slotsAt` never passes it): under 3 no unit stands, 3 have the next unit going on on their
last line, and the 3 others come nearer the unit under them, none nearer than a line's pitch (2610.20808v1 p26's u730 by 0.4 pt,
to 18.6; 2608.25210v2 p11's u212 by 0.1, to 16.1 at a pitch of 14.1; 2608.16117v1 p19's u59, which takes a line more after the
float that split it, by 17.9, to 22.5). 18 other units on those pages are laid anew by their page's fill, each in as many lines,
none lost. The run-in census (1,043 heads, every pass of the sweep): every measured head's gap as before; the two that change are
headings whose translation ends a line over their shared row (2610.20808v1 p26's u729, 2608.23393v1 p13's u159), which the census
does not measure, their text now on that line after the original's separation. A drawing rule, no version (§18.3).

**A group TeX set as a paragraph of its own (2026-11-06; the release sweep of e4be8723, its item 2).** The front end ends a unit
where the source ends a paragraph (a blank line, `\par`), never inside a command's argument; so a box a command makes of its
argument under a paragraph's text is the same unit as that text. 2608.25210v2 p3's prompts are such units (55 to 57): an item's
text, "response_equal_llm.: [sentence_1] and [sentence_2] are placeholders for two test sentences.", then `\mypython{…}`, the
prompt in a frame at 7.97 pt where the item is 8.97, its lines 8.3 pt further in. Laid as one paragraph, one block of all its
lines, the translation ran on from the item's short last line to the column's edge, over the frame's top border and past its right
edge, and the frame's first row stood empty. The units had stayed English (their item's label a placeholder whose ink was not
known) until PIPELINE 73 moved the start mark past `\topic{\code{…}}` (#596), which drew them. TeX's file and the alignment tell
where the paragraph ends (`tex.mjs` `paragraphBreaks`). In a unit TeX set justified (UNIT_FLAG.JUSTIFIED: none of its lines ends
short of its measure but a paragraph's last and a forced break's), a line of the file that ends short of its own measure
(`forcedBreaks`' SHORT) ends a paragraph where the next line holds first the words of a group the source opens after the words
the short line holds last. Its own measure is the one TeX set at its height as the door lays it (`layer2.mjs` `measureOf` over
its block: `measuresOf`' runs, else the block's edges), never the frame's widest edge: a full row of a narrower measure beside a
wrapped figure is no paragraph's end, and a group on the row after it is no paragraph of its own (the review of #603). A wrapped
paragraph too short for `measuresOf` to read its measures (under four lines) is read as one measure here, as its slots are. The alignment reads each source piece's first and last line (`layer2.mjs` `pieceLinesOf`, over the
words it pairs). There must be no forced break of the source nor a display between the two lines, and the group must close after
those words. The group's open piece, where the row holds it between texts of its own, breaks the translation there
(`finishUnit`'s `openBreaks`, `tokensOf2`), and the text after it starts on the line TeX set the group's from, in a block of its
own: its measure and pitch its own lines', its first line at its indent (`blocksOf2`: a line such a paragraph opens starts a
block, `paraAt`, `opens`). An ordinary forced break's region still splits its block later, keeping the measure the unit's lines
share: a unit of two lines ended by `\\` after its first lays its first part on to the second line's measure, as before (the review
of #603; a line a forced break opened had started a block too, its own measure the first line's 20 to 130 where the two shared 20
to 280, which the door's widening of a one-line block mostly hid). A centred or flush
unit, and one whose alignment the file does not tell, is laid as before: its short lines may end no paragraph. The unit is still
laid at one size, the group's where it holds most of the lines (the item's text at 7.97 pt on p3). Over the 83 of the release
sweep's 87 papers whose layers and rows staging's cache holds (2,267 pages, next's door against this one): 5 pages move. They are
2608.25210v2 p3 (its three prompt boxes, and the page's fill, which evens its other units' leading by about a point a line),
2501.14787v1 p57 and p58 (u423, the shared line's rule above), and two SIAM title pages, 2610.20266v1 and 2610.20285v1. There
`\funding{…}` sets its own paragraph under "Submitted to the editors …" in the same note, and the translation had run the two
on one line; the funding now starts on TeX's next line, at its indent.

**What TeX sets after a bibliography, and an appendix's own contents (PIPELINE 64, LAYOUT 33, REMOVAL 23; the owner's report of
2026-11-03 on 2610.42112v1 p16).** The references' zone that a bibliography's entries open ends with its last entry: on the line
its end mark stands on and the lines right below it at an entry's leading (`ledger.mjs` `lastEntriesOf`, `ENTRY_DY`: what a style
sets past the mark, a DOI), never a line that ends as a list's entry does (a list set right under it), not at the next unit's
start; the page's end ends it too, where a thebibliography, which sets no mark at its end (biblatex's `bz<n>` is one), leaves no
fact to tell a tail TeX broke onto the next page from that page's own first lines. Where no unit started before the next text — an appendix's own title
and contents list after the bibliography, titletoc's `\printcontents` under the paper's centred "Appendix" — every line between
was a bibliography line with no entry and kept as the original's, the list English. A line that ends as a list's entry does —
its page number its last word, after leaders or two of its size clear of the text, or the next word past it on its baseline in
its column (`stream.mjs` `columnsAt`, the maker's columns), two of its size clear of what follows (the ledger cuts a number set
that far as a line of its own); a page number at the text's size, never where the page sets numbers past its units' lines too
(`marginNumbers`: lineno's line numbers in the margin) — is a contents line wherever it stands where it would be an orphan, no `\contentsname` heading it (`listedOf`), and ends its entry:
the ink units cut it an entry a unit, its numbering, leaders and page number the
original's ink, and an entry that repeats a heading is drawn with that heading's translation (the echo). And the counter TeX sets
after a babel name on its line where the name leads no unit — IEEEtran's `\appendixname\nobreakspace\thesection`, "APPENDIX A"
centred over its title and "Appendix A:" in that list — is the name's (`names.mjs` `counterAfter`: its first glyph within 1.1 of
the name's size after it, each later one within a word's space of the last, a letter, a number or a numeral, its parts after stops
or dashes, a stop or a colon, then a space or the line's end; in the name's column; no unit's once the units have let go of what
is not theirs): in its group in the wrap (`own.mjs` MR 6b) and in its row in the layout file (`make.mjs` `nameAt`), its width at
the row's end in the row's slot 12, which a name leading no unit left 0 (a RUN_IN name's glue there), so that the line is centred
whole where it is, and the layer splits the counter off where the maker did, never reading the gaps again (`run.mjs`
`counterOf`: a thin space before it, a name letter-spaced, a stop after a space), and sets it after the name's word instead of
leaving it at its own place past a gap of the English word's width less the target's. A unit whose first line follows such a
name on its line in the name's column (the entry's title, an ink unit) is laid from where the name's word and counter end, the
original's separation after them. A name that leads its unit (RUN_IN: 2608.16117v1's "Appendix A." before its heading's
title) was drawn so already, its number the unit's label after the name's word. Over 63 local papers prepared on both sides, 4 move, each as meant: 2610.20484v1's "APPENDIX" and 2610.21106v1's authors'
addresses after the bibliography translated where they were kept; 2610.21201v1's etoc list in its appendix (orphans before: 12
entries, 5 drawn with their headings' translations) and 2610.37668v1's appendix contents after the bibliography (kept before: 11
section lines and 14 sub-entries, every one drawn with its heading's translation) cut an entry a unit; no source unit's class and
no name's row moves, before the review's fixes and after them (the margin's numbers, the line's column, the counter's split). On 2610.42112v1 p16 the title, the 8 lines and the
19 sub-entries are units (25 drawn with their headings' translations, 3 translated), their numbering, leaders and page numbers the
original's ink, and the headings "APPENDIX A" to "H" centred whole.

**The number a class sets right before a babel name (the owner's report of 2026-11-10 on 2610.20967v1 p5; the decision
of the same day: the number is the name's label).** A class that sets a heading itself and numbers it sets the number before the name: ICASSP's `spconf.sty`
defines thebibliography as `\section{References}`, and its `\@sect` sets `\@svsec` ("9." and `\hskip 0.6em`) and the word,
centred whole. The number was no unit's: a stay beside the name, the name's alignment read off its word alone (its middle 6 pt off
the column's: justified), and the target's word set from the word's start after the number, the line left of the column's middle
where the original's two sections before it were laid centred. The number is now the name's label, as a section's number is its
heading's (`own.mjs` MR 6c, `names.mjs` `counterBefore`, the mirror of `counterAfter` and narrower: every glyph before the name on
its line in its column, one word, a counter's form with a digit in it, ending within 1.1 of the name's size before it, no unit's,
TeX's stream setting nothing between it and the name's first glyph): its group `n<occ>.l` in the wrap, ROLE.label of the name's
unit in the instrument (`instrument.mjs` `nameGroupOf`), the part's Label of the name (kind `head`, its number and stop), so that
the alignment is read from the label on, as a section's is; S.names draws its crop before the target's word, the original's
distance between their starts kept, the whole centred where the name is centred, at its own place where the name keeps its left
edge, its label group off with the text's (on a page whose labels the add-on folded into the text's group, hidden with the word,
its crop drawn all the same). Over the 88 corpus papers one name gains a label, this one: its line 152.33-200.30, its middle the
column's 176.31 (before, 140.12-188.10); every other object of the 88 the same, the prepare dumps the same.

### 19.11 Structural names: a head's, a reference's, in the target's words

A theorem's head, a proof's name and the names cleveref and `\autoref` generate are TeX's text, not the author's sentences:
the translator never sees them, so the layer sets them itself, in the names TeX's own packages give the target, never in a
table written by hand (the owner's ruling of 2026-10-25). The names are `rules/tex-names.json`, which
`lab/pdf/spikes/tex-names-make.mjs` writes from the compile image's TeX Live files (each file's digest in it; `--check` makes
it again and compares): translator's theorem dictionaries (beamer's; ctex's `ChineseUTF8` for Chinese) for a theorem-like
name, cleveref's language definitions (`\Crefname` and `\crefname` by counter type, number and branch, and the conjunctions)
and hyperref's `\HyLang@<language>` for a reference's, ctex's own names (`ctex-name-utf8.cfg`) for Chinese, and babel's (the
layout rules' labels) for a float's or an appendix's in a target that has neither; TeX's text decoded by LaTeX's own tables
(`t1enc.dfu`, `t2aenc.dfu`, read backwards). A name no package gives in the target is left the original's (`rules/tex-names.mjs`).

- **A label is what the head macro set** (`layer2.mjs labelOf`, `tex.mjs`): whether a unit begins with text is its source's
  (`unit.source`, rows.mjs `unitOf`), never its translation's. A paragraph that opens with a reference, "\Cref{prop:lbCs}
  below shows how …", whose Chinese begins with "below" and sets the reference second, had cleveref's "Theorem 5.1" read as a
  theorem's label: kept as the original's ink at the line's start and drawn again inside the translation (2610.18513v1 p19
  u156). The code is production's (699b4aea's `labelOf` reads the translated pieces alike), not #460's or #462's.
- **A theorem-like head** (`layer2.mjs headLabelInTarget`, `run.mjs headOf`): the layout file's label of a theorem's body
  or its note, read from the page's characters in its box (the unit's own part of the page may leave a head's first letters
  to the unit before: "finition5.1("), its name in translator's word for the target, its number and punctuation the
  original's, the name and number in the style of its first character and its punctuation in its last's; after an opening
  bracket the note follows with no space ("Definition 5.1 (s-conductance)." in Chinese: ctex's word for
  "Definition", " 5.1 (", the note's translation, ")."). The wrap gives it a group to hide (REMOVAL 11, §19.9): a note's head ends in the bracket its head opens the
  note with, and the joint after a babel name that leads its unit (amsthm's "." after "Proof") is that unit's label, so that
  the name's lead is drawn (§11.8, `jointOf`) where the original's "Proof." stayed English.
- **A generated reference** (`layer2.mjs renameRefs`, `GENERATED_REF`; `renameRuns` in `tokensOf2`): a `\cref`, `\Cref` (and
  their page and name forms) or `\autoref` drawn as its page's text (`orig-text`) has each name and conjunction it prints
  replaced by the target's, its numbers and punctuation kept, each run in its own colour (cleveref's black "Theorem", its
  linked blue "A.17"); a theorem-like name as its head reads, so that a reference and the head it names agree; one any part of
  which has no word in the target is the original's whole, never half in either language ("Section A.7", "Sections 5.2.1,
  5.2.3 and 5.2.4" in zh: no package gives Chinese a section's name or an "and"). A citation's note ("[Ascolani et al., 2026,
  Lemma 1]") is a name and its number the same way, the cited work's own text as it is. A name the source writes itself
  ("Theorem~\ref{…}") is the translator's text: over the 58 papers in Chinese of the sweep's cache, 564 of 567 such names were
  translated, against 0 of 981 generated ones before this rule.
- **Measured** (2026-10-25, base `next` 37d84180, the 25 local papers whose zh rows the sweep's cache holds, each paper's
  bundle made by both engines on the production path, TL2025): the units' hashes are every one kept (168 local sources); the
  wrap's `labelKept` 298 → 96 and its groups 11,126 → 11,328, `unhidden` the same on every paper, every page of every group
  shown our page (the ocg gate's G1, CPU canvas: the same 4 pages differ on both sides, from run to run); the sweep's checks
  in Chromium, no unit gained or lost (`a` 41 → 41), `c` 10 → 8 violations (2610.21376v1 p4 u30, u31: a note's head now its
  label), `e` 15 → 9, `m` 25 → 24, `j` reviews 148 → 139. 2610.18513v1 in zh: p18 u150 and p19 u157's heads, p19 u156's
  "Theorem 5.1" drawn once, its and p18 u153's "Theorem A.17", the citation's "Lemma 1" and p7's "Proof." in Chinese;
  "Section A.7" and "Sections 5.2.1, 5.2.3 and 5.2.4" as the paper prints them.
- **Limits.** Japanese, Korean and Traditional Chinese have no theorem dictionary in TeX Live (translator has none, ctex's are
  Simplified Chinese), and no target outside cleveref's languages has a section's or an equation's name or an "and": those
  heads and references stay the original's. A name translator's dictionary lacks ("Assumption", "Conjecture", "Claim") stays
  English in every target, until the paper's own name units give it a word (§19.14), and a head of such a name is its unit's
  label where the paper defines the name (§19.14, REMOVAL 19).

### 19.12 The text inside vector figures (the content class `figures`, stage 5 of `docs/route/orphan-text.md`)

The labels, axis titles, legends and annotations a figure draws as glyphs are units of their own, made from our final pass's
glyphs, translated with the paper's units whatever the reader's switch, and drawn in each original run's box; the switch shows or
hides what was made. The owner's rulings of 2026-10-25 bind it: the format is ours (exact positions from our compile's glyphs,
each original's ink owned and hidden by its own optional-content group, the text in its original's box, no double ink, no overlap
with the figure's lines), the translation's quality the provider's; translated once into the shared cache, shown or hidden by
the toggle with no prepare again; bitmap figures (OCR) are another lane.

- **Which glyphs** (`layout/figure-text.mjs` `figureUnitsOf`, in `wrapFinal`, after `ownOf`): those no unit owns inside a figure
  our compile set — an included PDF's (shown inside a form XObject: pdfTeX includes a PDF, and an EPS made one, as a form), or a
  TikZ or pgfplots picture's (between the points `zs` and `ze` the layout compile now sets inside pgf's `\pgfsys@beginpicture`
  and `\pgfsys@endpicture`, in the picture's own box: `marks.mjs POINTS_TEX`, LAYOUT 21; pageInk keeps them apart, `pictures`,
  so that no reader of the marks or the ownership sees them). A glyph set turned is read too (pageInk's `turned`: its baseline,
  direction, size and band), so that a y-axis title keeps its turn. Never a glyph of a code region (§19.7, PIPELINE 63): the
  code and terminal output of 2610.19159v1's agent transcripts, set in an environment of the paper's own (`trajectoryCode`,
  typewriter type with its lines obeyed) inside mdframed boxes TikZ draws, were a picture's text, cut into figure units word by
  word and translated ("echo" a word in Japanese); they are code, kept as the paper has it. Such a run is counted under the caps as
  any run (`FIGURE_UNITS_DOC`), so that where the cap falls does not move: past it, as before, the transcripts' heads are the ink
  units' lines.
- **Cut** into runs, one a label or a line: in stream order, one family (its font's name past a subset's tag, PIPELINE 69, and
  past its style, neither a math face, PIPELINE 71, below; TeX's own line in a picture over its faces and colours, below),
  size, colour, direction and figure (one form painted, one picture: pageInk's `fid` and `pid`, so that two figures side by side never make one label), in a code region or out of every
  one (a run kept whole for a code glyph would leave the prose beside it English: none of the 14 code papers has such a run, a
  rule of the cut, not a case), one baseline (`RUN_DY`
  0.05 of the size across), at most `RUN_GAP` 0.6 of the size past the run's end; a run spelling a word (two letters together)
  in no math face is a unit, its text the glyphs' Unicode (NFKC), a space at a gap of `SPACE_GAP` 0.15 em. A number, a tick's
  label, a letter alone or a formula stays the original's; so does a run a glyph of which is not wholly inside the clip in force
  (an included figure's viewport: pageInk's `clipped`; 1706.03762v7's cropped attention figures held two such titles) or inside
  its page's box (a row's origin off its page is one no part's reader takes, `checkFigures`). A glyph is wholly inside where its
  own ink is: its outline (else its font's ascent and descent) up and down, its outline (else its advance) across, a glyph set
  turned with that box turned (PIPELINE 46, the release sweep of 2026-11-01; its advance no longer since PIPELINE 62, below). The box of a turned glyph's whole size on both
  sides of its baseline, read before, passed a form's BBox wherever matplotlib's tight box set a y-axis title, a colour bar's
  title or a slanted tick label at the figure's edge, and once our final pass gave its included figures no group (PIPELINE 44,
  §19.7) the form's box clipped them: 45 figure units of 9 of the sweep's papers, 40 translated before, stood English though
  arXiv's page shows them whole (2610.35877v1 p8, 2610.22065v1 p3, 2610.17108v1 p4's slanted bar labels). Measured by the
  production pass on the 16 papers the sweep and PIPELINE 44 name (ba433da8's engine, 6e0a8d1c's and this one): every figure unit
  44 lost is back, drawn as before; the only units beside them are two titles 44's clip uncrowded (2610.22195v1 p8: the ink past
  a neighbour panel's box that had crowded them is cut away); and the three deltas 44 gained are byte for byte 44's
  (2610.30034v1 196,579 bytes, 2610.30875v1 304,787, 2610.31506v1 248,653). Over arXiv's PDFs of the 108 papers on disk, which
  carry no group (81 with figure text): 327 units on 47 papers that 44's reading cut are units again, none lost, and the 236 on
  16 papers whose glyphs a clip does cut stay the original's (2610.21312v1 p12's "Spearman(lr_std, bulk1)", its tops 1.7 pt
  past its box; 2610.22065v1 p3's "Relative Accuracy Drop (%", its parenthesis past it; a multi-panel figure drawn once a panel,
  each clipped to its own: 2608.12606v1 p5). Nor is a run a glyph of which stands past `BAND_MAX` (4) of its size from its
  baseline, by its own ink (a level glyph's outline; a turned one's, pageInk's `up` and `down`, its font's band where it has no
  outline): its size is not its glyphs' (`outsized`, PIPELINE 47, the release sweep of 5514953c). 2608.08481v1's figures are

  89 units own no group; 5 of them the maker had laid by their text alone, never drawn for want of one. An ink unit that repeats such a text (a running head, a contents entry of the same words: `layout/ink-units.mjs`'s
  echo, rule 5) takes no echo of it and is translated itself (on those 6 papers none does, of their 101 ink units). No constant
  moves: every bundle is byte for byte as it was, and every unit's cut, its wire and each request's shape; only the plan, the
  units `toTranslate` and `layerIds` name, is smaller (`pipeline/versions.mjs`, under PIPELINE 31).
- **A label no group holds** (PIPELINE 49, the owner's report of 2026-11-01 on 2501.14787v1): a unit's label the wrap leaves the
  original's ink in no group (`labelKept`: no label's form) is no unit's glyphs to the figure text, which cuts it where it stands
  in a figure our compile set. mdframed's `framemethod = TikZ` sets a whole thmtools theorem inside a picture, its head "Recall 7
  (" before its note's unit ("Recall" is the paper's own name, no label's form), and the head's "Recall 7" was a figure unit,
  drawn translated over its hidden ink; but the note's label row stayed in the layout, and the reader shows a label row its
  unit does not draw again from render C, every group shown (`hide.mjs`): the original's "Recall 7" came back under the
  translation, both legible at once, on every such box of the paper (pp10-11's "Recall 7", "Recall 8", "Notation 9"). As for
  the ink units (§19.10), a label row that meets a figure unit's run — its band from its origin along its direction for its
  length, across from its descent to its ascent, the box the reader hides when it draws it, met along and across the run as
  well as on the page's axes, so that a slanted run's empty corners meet nothing — goes from the parts' layout
  (`pipeline/ink-pass.mjs` `layoutWithInk`, given the page pass's figure rows by page, in the whole and the streamed cut
  alike): the figure unit's translation stands alone over its hidden ink, and where the reader leaves the unit the
  original's, its group stays shown, and its ink with it. Over 66 local papers the three label rows of that paper's boxes go,
  and no other; no figure unit and no unit laid changes (`lab/pdf/spikes/figure-gate.mjs` on the pack, the rules gate: the
  same).
- **Drawn** (`run.mjs paintFigures`, once a page's figures' rows are in: the page waits for them as for its units', `rowsFor`
  ranks them with its page): its translation's text in runs by script (`layer2.mjs figureRuns`: its CJK characters, by the
  rules' class, in the target's CJK face, every other, a Latin word, a digit, a space, in its font's family's Latin face, as a
  unit's words are; the CJK faces the web serves hold no Latin letter or digit, so that one CJK face for the whole text was
  refused, `served`, and 2010.11929v2's "Width MLP", "Head 2" and Figure 7's title stayed the original's, Microsoft's
  translations of them keeping "MLP", "2" and "RGB" beside their Chinese), of its font's weight and slant, in its fill, on
  its run's baseline, turned by its angle (`layer2.mjs svgOfFigure`), by the fit rule (`layer-proto/figure-fit.mjs` `fitFigureSet`), set
  by set: each translation from its anchor's edge (a start one from the original's start, an end one to its end, a middle one
  about its middle), into its room on the side its anchor grows to (a middle one the same either side); every unit of a set at
  one size, the original's where each fits, else the one factor its tightest translation needs, to the rules' last floor
  (`floorMin`, 0.6) at most; a translation that would need less is the original's (`unfit`), and the rest of its set keeps the
  factor the others need. Its group set OFF in render A. Left the original's: no row (`untranslated`), a translation that says its source again (`same`), no group in
  the document (`unhidden`), a face's refusal, `unfit`; a label of names (`kept`). The run's `figures` lists each. A page is
  ready once its figures are painted, not while a face they wait for loads.
- **The switch** is the toggle `figures` of the reader's toggles (§19.10: `openLayer({ classes })`, the layer side's `classes`
  and `setClasses`, which opens the door again over the same documents with every row held, so that nothing is prepared, fetched
  or translated again): a figure unit's row is taken, and its figure drawn, where it is on; off, it is the original's, as any
  unit of a class not shown. Its default, `TOGGLE_DEFAULTS.figures`, is on (the owner's, 2026-10-25, having seen the web's
  settings: a figure's text is shown translated, and a label that does not fit stays the original's). The extension's reader passes

  lands, from the reading options or the settings page; until configuration v21 it passed the image switch, which the HTML
  page's figure text shares, as `classes.figures`. A form one page wrote again and another paints: the other
  page's figures in it are `shared`, the original's, and its render shows the form's groups ON, since each render sets the
  visibility of its own page's drawn groups alone (visibility.mjs).
- **Measured** (2026-10-25, `lab/pdf/spikes/figure-gate.mjs`, record `lab/pdf/records/figure-gate.md`): on the gate pack's 7
  bases (the pack `09208b43`, LAYOUT 21: 1810.04805v2's pgfplots axis between its points), 846 of 1,030 figure units drawn, 184

  (`lab/pdf/spikes/figure-final.mjs`; five of them TikZ or pgfplots papers), 1,216 of 1,469 drawn, 253 crowded, 99 forms; none
