  zh the labels drawn go from 589 to 830 of 846 on the pack and from 905 to 1,177 of 1,216 on the set, and the sets of mixed
  sizes from 16 and 43 to 0; over Microsoft's answers on three papers (1512.03385v1, 1810.04805v2, 2010.11929v2) from 107 to
  265 of 265, 80 to 224 at their full size, 6 sets of mixed sizes to 0.

### 19.13 References and names, and the reader's toggles (stages 4 and 7 of `docs/route/orphan-text.md`)

The owner's rulings of 2026-10-25: we own format correctness (positions from TeX, the original's ink owned and hidden by its own
groups, line fit, no double ink, structure kept) and the provider owns translation quality; every class is translated once, on the
server, into the shared cache, and a reader's settings only show or hide it. And of 2026-10-28, the references and the author names
decoupled, each toggle's duty its own: "references" governs the bibliography alone, each entry whole, the names inside an entry
its own; "names" governs the author names under the title alone; the affiliations, addresses and the e-mail line are always
translated. And of 2026-10-30, which reverses that last part: "names" governs the whole author block under the title, its names,
affiliations, institutions, addresses and e-mail line, translated together or the original's together (the row "Authors and
affiliations"; the key `names` and its default, off, kept, so that by default the whole block is the original's). The toggle
moves no version: a unit's class is the reader's, read from the kind the bundle carries (`UNIT_CLASS`), so a paper prepared
before it is read so as it is; every class was already translated whatever the toggles say. What moves PIPELINE 39 is the
block's units, below: whatever TeX sets an author block in, its units are the block's. And of 2026-11-09: the toggle governs the
author block under the title, the whole of it, and affects nothing else: what a class prints from the author data elsewhere
(acmart's reference format, a running head, amsart's addresses at the paper's end, an author's biography) is ordinary text of
no toggle, and everything under the title that is the block's (its connectors, its notes, its correspondence and e-mail
lines) follows it, the original's with it off, translated with it on (the author block under the title, below).

- **Entries are units, each whole** (`source/latex-front.mjs` `bibliography`; PIPELINE 29, and PIPELINE 30 one unit an entry). The
  ground truth is the bibliography's TeX the compile reads: the paper's `thebibliography`, or the job's `.bbl` where
  `\bibliography` reads it (BibTeX's output, which the package holds or the prepare's first pass makes, below; never biber's data,
  which is biblatex's and no text). Each `\bibitem`'s entry, from its key to the next `\bibitem`, is one unit of kind `reference`
  (class references), its names its own: never set in two pieces styled apart, and no guess of where its names end, which
  PIPELINE 29's `refnames` made (a committee's name in the authors' block taken for its names up to the title's words; a title
  with a comma taken for its authors). A `.bbl` is read in the encoding the paper declares, as its own TeX is. The
  label (`\bibitem`'s optional argument, set in the list's label box) and the key are no piece; what a style writes before the
  first entry is no unit, nor REVTeX's `\BibitemOpen` and `\BibitemShut`. In an entry a number (a year, pages, a volume and its
  issue: a token of a digit and no letter, white space or a piece that sets none on each side) or a DOI written out, letters and
  all (`10.1007/s00125-020-05190-9.`, after `doi: ` or `doi:`) is a placeholder of the class `number` (`layout/marks.mjs`, both
  marks, MARKS_SCHEMA 11), the original's ink as a web address and a formula are. An entry is marked as the body's units are, in
  the bibliography's own TeX (the `.bbl` written back marked: no BibTeX runs over it), so its place, its ink and its groups are
  TeX's (LAYOUT 22: UNIT_KINDS `reference`; `refnames` kept at its index, so that a file of 22 reads as it was). The entries' units
  are numbered after every other unit of the source (`entriesLast`), so that no other unit's number moves: a translation held by a
  unit's number (the gate pack's frozen ones) is still its unit's. The probe asks about an entry's commands after every other
  unit's, so the body's marks are what they were. A bundle of 29 a reader still reads keeps its `refnames` units: their class is
  the references' (`UNIT_CLASS`), the entry's two halves shown or hidden together, and "names" the author block's alone.
- **backref's lists travel with their entries** (`source/latex-front.mjs` `BACKREF_LIST`, `layout/marks.mjs` `BACKREF_TEX`;
  PIPELINE 35, LAYOUT 29, REMOVAL 16, TRANSLATE_VERSION 7). Under hyperref's `backref` or `pagebackref` (or backref.sty itself), each entry is
  followed by the pages or sections that cite it, each a link back (2610.37668v1's grey "2, 25"). With its default parscan
  backref reads the whole entry as an argument (`\bibitem` redefined as `\BR@@bibitem#1#2\par`), sets it, then the list
  (`\BR@backref`, through `\backrefalt` or `\backref`): TeX's own text, after the entry's end mark, in none of its pieces. Its
  ink was no unit's, left on the page where the entry was drawn translated over it (the owner's case of 2026-10-29, References
  on). Where a command of the package's files (its classes too) that loads a package or sets its options (`\usepackage`,
  `\RequirePackage`, `\PassOptionsToPackage`, `\documentclass`, `\LoadClass`, `\hypersetup`) names backref or the option, never
  `=false`, and none says `\backrefparscanfalse`, the unit that ends each entry's first paragraph (where the parscan stops and
  sets the list; a later paragraph, a paper's `\mbibitem` macro, is TeX's next entry) ends in a placeholder of no source
  (`\axtbackref`: patch writes nothing for it, the probe never asks about it). It goes on no wire (TRANSLATE_VERSION 7,
  `mt.mjs` `listOf`): it is no word of the entry's sentence, and on the wire Microsoft's Chinese read it as a page number and
  wrote the character for "page" (U+9875) before it, between the year and the list (2610.37668v1). It comes back after the translation, an en space before it: the `\enspace`
  backref sets is a kern, no ink of the list's, and without it the list stood against the year in a CJK translation
  ("2025.3, 5, 26"); what TeX sets there is `\newblock`'s glue, which `\BR@backref` begins with. The rebuilt reader states
  it on its element (`el.after`, the en space its gap: the front half's adapter, `pipeline/instrument.mjs`), and
  `packages/translate`'s chain asks every translator for the entry without it and puts it back after the translation, on
  every wire and the runs floor. Until 2026-11-09 it went as a marker: over the 88 corpus papers 314 entries of 5 papers, 147
  a marker alone at the wire's end, 167 in one marker with the year before it, read back against the year with no gap;
  stated, 147 markers wires and every one of the 314 tags wires change, and 300 of the markers wires are today's byte for
  byte (the rest differ before the list, by the package's own rules). In the marked original the entry names
  its marks after its end mark (`\axtbrname{p<i>.<k>}`, an assignment), and LAYOUT_TEX wraps both printers where the document
  begins (begindocument/end, after the class's own `\backrefalt`), so that the list has that piece's opening mark before it
  and its closing mark after it; `\backrefalt` only where a package or the paper defined one (backref calls `\backref` while
  `\backrefalt` is its own unused one, which it tells by `\ifx` at `\thebibliography`). The list is then the piece's ink: its
  group's (`u<id>.p`), hidden with the entry, and drawn after the entry's translation as its page text, in its colour, its
  links with it. An entry TeX sets no list for (an option that turns nothing on, a package not loaded) has no point of the
  piece's: EMPTY, drawn as nothing, as the entry was before. The marks change no item on the page (the invariant test's two
  documents: the class's `\backrefalt` under natbib, and backref's own printer). Measured against #501's head on the eight
  local papers whose source names backref (2026-10-29): seven turn it on (eccv.sty's `\@ifpackagewith{hyperref}{pagebackref}`
  is a test, no setting); 377 lists found, each its entry's own (2610.37668v1 41 of 41, 2609.26457v1 122 of 122, 2608.13505v1
  111 of 112, 2608.08876v1 28 of 30, 2608.10322v2 29, 2608.28692v1 29, 2608.29782v1 17), 3 EMPTY (an entry no page cites);
  no unit changes class, every unit drawn before is drawn, and 198 of 198 base pages are pixel-identical. On 2610.37668v1's
  pages 13 and 14 every list's link (58 and 8) is moved with its entry's translation, where none was. The gate pack's
  2609.26457v1 gains its 122 rows, every other output's layout file its version alone, every other base page byte-identical;
  the maker's time on it is the same (3 runs each, 449 to 467 ms both), the front end's within noise (+1 %)
- **A bibliography BibTeX makes is a shipped one** (`layout/paper.mjs` `madeBibliography`, `bibliographyKept`; the owner's ruling of
  2026-10-28). A paper that names `\bibliography{…}` over `.bib` files its package holds, loads no biblatex and ships no job's
  `.bbl` (102 of the local sources) had no entry unit: the units were cut before any compile, and the `.bbl` was first written
  inside the marked compile, unmarked. The host now asks, before it tells the paper's units, one pass of the unmarked original
  (`guard.mjs` `unmarkedFiles`: the paper's own files) as a draft with the bibliography step (`bibtex`, CM's first draft's
  request: BibTeX on the job's aux), its files returned; the `<job>.bbl` it wrote, a `thebibliography` with a `\bibitem`, is the
  job's `.bbl` the paper is opened again with (`live.mjs openPaper`), and from then on it is a shipped one (`meta.bbl`): written
  back marked, no BibTeX in the marked compile. No pass is made, and the paper stays as it was, where it ships its `.bbl`, names no
  `\bibliography`, loads biblatex, or lacks a `.bib` it names (latexmk -norc runs no BibTeX then, nor does the marked compile; a
  `.bib` the pass wrote itself is no lack, on the disk latexmk decides by: REVTeX 4.x's `<job>Notes.bib`, its notes as entries,
  named in `\bibdata` before the paper's own, read as missing until PIPELINE 32, so that every REVTeX paper that ships no `.bbl`
  had its bibliography no unit's, ink units cut a column long, 2610.20595v1 and 2610.21770v1);
  nor is its `.bbl` taken where the pass does not run through or returns no files, writes another job's bibliography beside the
  main one's (chapterbib, multibib, bibunits), writes a `.bcf` (biber's), or writes no `\bibitem`; nor where an entry of the paper opened again
  runs over another `\bibitem` it wrote (one at each entry's first line, as every style writes it), or the entries outnumber
  them (`entries`: a URL's `%3F` in an entry's `\href`, a character to TeX and read as a comment by the front end until PIPELINE
  33, left that entry's group open over the 18 after it, 2610.21770v1, whose marked `.bbl` no longer defined their citations:
  "[41? ? ? –43]" on our page). An entry of no words is no unit, and no reason to keep the others (PIPELINE 33: ACM's entry of a
  web page alone, `\bibinfo{year}{2025}\natexlab{}. \newblock \bibinfo{booktitle}{\emph{\url{…}}}`, read before as an entry
  missing, kept 2608.25210v2's 64 others the text no unit owns). The paper's other units must be
  the same with the `.bbl` and without (every unit before the entries and every name after them, the bundle's byte for byte,
  their spans too), else it stays as it was (`moved`): so `\bibliography` ends the paragraph before it whether the `.bbl` is there
  or not (TeX's `thebibliography` is a heading's paragraph end, and a `\bibliography` with no `.bbl` sets nothing), which moved 7
  paragraphs of the local sources by one placeholder, their ids kept. The units the host tells are then a shipped `.bbl`'s:
  the source's, the entries, the paper's names; nothing is announced twice, and no contract between the host's children changes
  but the `.bbl` handed to the one that opens the paper again (the web's prepare: the hand-off's `bbl`). The host decides the
  paper's TeX Live tree before the pass, so that the entries are the `.bbl` of the tree that compiles it. Measured: below.
- **A `\bibliography` inside a group is read where TeX reads it** (`source/latex-front.mjs` `bibliographiesIn`). The walk reads
  every group next to a command the role table does not know as that command's arguments, kept whole as one placeholder (some
  prose stays untranslated, nothing breaks), and never met a `\bibliography` inside one: 2608.06007v1's
  `\balance{ \bibliographystyle{unsrt} \bibliography{ref} }` (balance.sty's `\balance` takes no argument, the group is TeX's)
  named no bibliography, so BibTeX made no `.bbl`, and 2610.37818v1's `{ \small … \bibliography{main} }`, read as a fourth
  argument of the `\iftoggle{…}{…}{}` before it, never visited its shipped one. Their printed entries, text no unit owns in the
  references' zone with no entry number, were kept blocks (§17.1, the owner's ruling of 2026-10-30: a bibliography the front end
  did not cut into entries), never translated: the References toggle reached nothing there (round 8: 7 blocks over 06007's pp. 15-18, 4 in
  37818). Such a call's `\bibliography`, outside comments, is now read as a bare one is: its names recorded, the job's `.bbl`
  visited there, the paragraph before ended; the call is then no unit's, as `\bibliography`'s own source is none, and nothing
  of ours is written in its groups (the entries are the `.bbl`'s units). Not the whole group walked: our marks would go into an
  argument whose use the walk cannot know. Over the 88 papers the front end changes these two alone: 06007's 88 entries and
  37818's 40, units of kind `reference` under the toggle; the 4 biblatex papers' 223 entries were units already.
- **A biblatex bibliography: one unit an entry, of kind `inkreferences`** (`marks.mjs` POINTS_TEX, `ledger.mjs`, `ink-units.mjs`,
  2610.35877v1 on staging: its entries translated with the references off, its heading drawn into the first entry). biblatex
  prints its entries from biber's fields (`\printbibliography`), no TeX of the source the front end could mark, and they were
  orphan text, always translated. The marked compile now sets a point before each entry (`bi<n>`: biblatex's per-entry hook, the
  entry's paragraph begun there so that a numeric style's label, which the list's `\item` sets, stands before it; a count in a
  macro), and one after each bibliography's last entry (`bz<n>`: biblatex's `\blx@endbibliography`, the entry's last glues taken
  before it, as `\endtrivlist` and the paragraph's end would take them), and the ledger cuts the printed bibliography by them:
  from each point to the next, to the bibliography's end or to the next unit's start, one entry (one unit over a column's or a
  page's break, a running head between its parts a unit of its own; the next bibliography's heading of a title of its own,
  `\printbibliography[type=book,title={Books}]`, no entry's), of the references' class, so that the references toggle governs it as it governs a `\bibitem`'s; its names its own; its
  label the original's ink; every line of an entry is its unit's whatever it holds (a URL alone in a typewriter face, as `\url`
  breaks it, or numbers alone: left out, it stood the original's where the drawn entry ran over it), an entry of no text word
  none. What stands before the first point (biblatex's heading) is a unit of its own. No `.bbl` is read (biber's is a file of
  fields), and nothing of the source changes. Measured over 59 papers (the sweep's 54 and every biblatex paper of the local corpus,
  six of 185): 378 entries now units of their own in the six, under the toggle (141 `inkorphan` units of the entries gone; in
  three of the six the entries had been no unit's at all, never translated), 236 more units laid and none fewer, units left
  LOST 163 → 160 (none new), every base page pixel-identical (1606).
- **Not units:** a `.bib` the TeX tree holds rather than the package (a style's IEEEabrv): no pass is made.
- **The author block: names apart from places** (`source/latex-front.mjs` `frontBlock`, PIPELINE 30, LAYOUT 23). An author block's
  affiliations, institutions, addresses and its e-mail line are units of their own, kind `affiliation`, its names kind `author`,
  both of the class names, the names toggle (2026-10-30; the places were the body's, always translated, from 2026-10-28).
  Whatever environment TeX sets a block's text in, a unit cut there is the block's, of its row's kind (`blockKind`, PIPELINE
  39): a tabular inside `\author` is cut at its `&` and `\\` as a table's cells are, so that no unit spans an alignment's
  cell, but its units are names or places, placed in no table's grid and never a table's kept name (2610.35877v1's
  `\author{\begin{tabular}{cc} Ayush Mittal & Dhruv Gupta\\ …}`: its names were cells, of the tables' toggle, translated with
  the block's off; 2608.06007v1's row of places and 2610.22214v1's whole block too: 3 of the 190 sources on disk, 8 units,
  each at its number with its text, every other unit and every kept name as it was; compiled, each located, none left the
  original's by the wrap, their layout rows next's). A block in a center, a minipage or a theorem keeps its kind as well. Read from the TeX the source holds: the command (`\author`
  and its kin names, `\affil`, `\affiliation`, `\institute`, `\address` and their kin places), the rows of the tabular LaTeX sets an
  `\author` in (its first row names, the rest places, but a row that holds an author's note, sets an affiliation's mark after a
  name, opens with "and", or stands before a numbered list of places is names: 2608.14893's and 2610.21880v1's second rows of
  names), a numbered list of places; IEEEtran's, acmart's, REVTeX's, elsarticle's (each key's value), llncs', ICML's and AAAI's
  forms; a row set in a `\centerline` of its own (FRONT_BOXES, ICLR 2021's block, 2010.11929v2: its argument the row's text, read
  through for the row's mark, its block before PIPELINE 32 no unit and its names, notes and places one orphan's ink unit, always
  translated and set in the names' bold; outside an author block `\centerline` is one placeholder as before). A later row with
  none of these is a place, as the classes set it: a name alone there cannot be told from a place by its
  TeX. An e-mail, a web address and an ORCID written out stay placeholders, the original's ink; so does an e-mail whose
  local part TeX escapes (`goh\_siong\_thye@…`, one placeholder with its `\_`, 2608.11884, 2608.29778); and so does a group of
  local parts written once before their one domain, in braces, parentheses or brackets, separated by commas and/or white space,
  whatever space TeX writes between them (`\{kahe,~v-xiangz\}@…`, `\{mph,\,lmb\}@…`, `[first name]@…`: `ADDRESS_GROUP`,
  `keepGroups`, one placeholder as the paper writes it; read from one text between `\{` and `\}` alone, a tie parted the list
  into words sent one by one, 1512.03385v1, and a bracket's was text, 2610.21085v1). A row of addresses alone is then no unit,
  and the ink side keeps it whole too (below, the ink units' rule 4): its lines a kept block, the original's whatever the names
  toggle (2611.00342v1, the owner's 2026-11-10: 「翻译或者不翻译都可以，关键是不能乱翻」). Every author block's
  unit keeps its number: what PIPELINE 29 cut the text between two notes into (one unit of kind author, a unit the walk flushed
  inside it one more: `olderUnits`, a walk of the old cut in a shadow of the walk's context) keeps it in the first unit cut inside
  its range, of either kind, and every other unit cut there is numbered after every other unit of the source, before the entries
  (`later`, `entriesLast`): over the local sources no source unit's number moves for it. A place is searched on arXiv's page as a float is
  (`make.mjs`, `page-pass.mjs` FLOATING: a class sets it where it likes, amsart's addresses at the paper's end). Each row is
  marked in the layout compile as the block's one unit was (`frontMarks`), the duplicates a class compares left unmarked by the
  command's whole argument as TeX reads it, its comments, line breaks and runs of spaces aside (two equal `\affiliation{…}`
  of revtex's, set once: 2610.21770v1's third, broken over two lines, had been marked and set again), never two rows of one block (article sets
  1706.03762v7's three "Google Brain" rows each where it stands: all 15 of its block's units laid); a row that opens with its
  first letter as a command in a group (`{\L}ukasz`) has its start mark before the group (`patch`), so that the letter is its

### 19.14 The paper's own names, units of their own (PIPELINE 29)

A name no package gives the target is the paper's to name, and the translator's to translate: each paper's structural names
are units of their own, sent to the translator once with its units, cached by their text as any unit is, and read by the
layer wherever such a name is drawn (the owner's other ground truth of 2026-10-25, after §19.11).

- **Which names** (`source/paper-names.mjs paperNames`, over every `.tex`, `.sty` and `.cls` file the paper ships, comments
  dropped, in the order its files are read): a theorem-like environment's printed name (`\newtheorem` and its starred form,
  llncs's `\spnewtheorem`, elsarticle's `\newproof`, mdframed's `\newmdtheoremenv`, thmtools' `\declaretheorem`, its `name=`
  or else its environment's name capitalised, as thmtools prints it); the reference names the paper gives (cleveref's
  `\crefname` and `\Crefname`, thmtools' `refname=` and `Refname=`, a redefined `\<type>autorefname`); and, where the paper
  calls cleveref or `\autoref` at all, the words no package names in some target the readers offer
  (`rules/tex-names.json` `gaps` and `conjunctionGaps`, which `tex-names-make.mjs` derives from the same files: each counter
  type's English singular, "Section", "Equation", "Theorem" …, nineteen, and the conjunctions' one word, "and"; a range's
  " to " is no word of one sense alone, and a conjunction of punctuation is every target's). A name is plain words alone
  (one holding a command or a brace is the original's), each once, at most 96 a paper.
- **Where they are**: after the source's units in the bundle (`layer-proto/units.mjs bundleUnitsOf`, kind `name`, one text
  piece), so that every source unit keeps its id and its hash; the prepare child writes them in the source units' chunks, and
  the ink units (§19.10) follow them: the wrap numbers its ink units from the bundle's count before them
  (`wrapFinal`'s `inkFrom`, which the host gives as `bundleUnitsOf(paper).length`; `page-pass.mjs inkOfHost` takes no ink
  unit numbered otherwise). A name unit is no page's ink: the maker, the anchors and the wrap never see it (`paper.units` is
  the source's alone), the page pass settles it from the start and lays it nowhere, the door awaits it on no page.
- **Sent only where read** (TRANSLATE_VERSION 10): a name the target's packages answer wherever it would be read — its head's
  word, which headName reads and refName reads first, a conjunction's, and in a target whose names do not inflect no other form
  of its type falling back to it (`rules/tex-names.mjs nameAnswered`) — is not sent for that target (`rows.mjs toTranslate`):
  zh's "Theorem", "Lemma". A name a reference's word alone answers is still sent, since a paper's own head may print it (its
  `\newtheorem{algorithm}{Algorithm}`, whose head zh's packages do not name: Codex on #581). Over the 53 sweep papers 191 of
  379 name units for zh, 200 for de and fr, none for ja, ko and zh-TW, for which tex-names.json holds no word; a babel name the
  layout rules give is not counted either.
- **Translated first**: a language's batches carry the names first (`rows.mjs batchesOf`, `runRows`), so that the first page
  drawn has them; their class is `generated`, always translated (`rules/content-classes.mjs`). A row of one is the run's
  word for that name (`layer2.mjs nameOfRow`: its translation's text, an ideographic full stop the translator ends a word
  with dropped), taken at the open or with any rows (`run.mjs take`), never laid; one that comes after a page is drawn
  changes no drawing.
- **Read where a name is drawn** (`rules/tex-names.mjs`): a package's word first, as §19.11 has it; else the name unit's
  translation: a theorem-like head's name (`headName`), a generated reference's name (`refName`: the form itself, a name the
  paper defines, or in a target whose names do not inflect its type's singular, so that zh's "Sections 5.2.1, 5.2.3 and
  5.2.4" reads its section's word once), its conjunction's word with the English spacing (`conjunctionOf`). A reference any
  part of which has no word yet is still the original's whole. In a target that inflects, a plural no package and no name
  unit gives stays English whole ("Assumptions 1 and 2" in de).
- **Measured** (2026-10-25, the 168 local sources): 923 name units in 85 papers, 32 at most (19 of them call cleveref or
  `\autoref`); every source unit's hash the bibliography's 29 gives it (§19.13), 168 of 168 papers the same. The paper's own
  names besides the gaps: "Conjecture" in 26 papers, "Assumption" and "Claim" in 14, "Question" and "Fact" in 8, "Proof"
  and "Problem" in 7 (a class's own among them: acmart's Conjecture, llncs's Claim), a Portuguese paper's "Teorema",
  "Lema" and "Corolário", a Chinese paper's own Chinese names (each file read in its own encoding, as the units' text is,
  and held in the bundle as a text piece is). The gates' fixtures hold no name unit's row yet (their records are of an
  earlier pipeline): their drawing is unchanged until the records are made again.
- **Its heads are labels** (PIPELINE 50, REMOVAL 19, the coordinator's follow-up of #541, 2026-11-01): a head TeX sets of a
  theorem-like name the paper defines (\newtheorem's and its kin's printed name, thmtools' `name=`: `theoremNames`, the
  theorem names among `paperNames`) is a label's form as a standard name's is (`own.mjs` `labelFormOf`), so that the wrap gives
  it its unit's label group and the layer draws it in that name unit's word, one word a name on every head of it
  (`headLabelInTarget`). It was left the original's ink in no group (`labelKept`), and where a figure unit or an ink unit then
  took it, it was translated alone each time: 2501.14787v1's thmtools boxes in mdframed's TikZ frame read "Recall" one way on
  p10's first box and another, a sense of "recall" no reader wants, on its second. Over the 216 local sources, 96 define theorem
  names and 44 a name the standard form does not take (Conjecture 29, Question 9, Fact 9, Notation 8, Observation 5, Axiom 4,
  a Portuguese and a Chinese paper's names). Over 66 local papers prepared by both engines, 34 define names and 4 change: 9
  heads are labelled where they were the original's (2501.14787v1's six, "Recall", "Notation" and "Question"; one each of
  2610.21312v1's "Setting", 2610.21884v1's "Notation", 2610.35877v1's "Result"), 3 figure units and 6 ink units that had taken
  them go (the ink units after them numbered one on), their 9 label rows stay in the layout (#541's rule had dropped them under
  those units), and no source unit's text group moves; 216 of 216 local sources keep every unit's hash.
- **Waited for where drawn** (2026-11-13, round B16, the coordinator's ruling on design-display row F6). The reader's typesetter
  read every name's row on every page of a paper with names (`ownNamesOf`, 29,522 reads on 1,890 pages of the 90 pairs) and
  waited for none, so a page committed before a name's row came drew the original's head or reference and was laid again once
  it came. Now a name's row is read only when a member's head or reference asks it (`unit/rename.ts` ownNamesOf: a lookup that
  reads a row when asked), and one predicate (`lay/wait.ts` drawsName) says which members can: a theorem's or a heading's head
  name (Label.name), or an element whose source a cross-referencing package generates or a citation's note (U.rename's
  sources). Such a member waits, beside its own row, for every name of its paper; no other member is given them. What it costs a
  reader: the server asks for the names first (the website's windows: the name units lead the first window whether or not the
  layer's catalog is known), and over the 90 pairs' 83 papers every name stands in that first window (47 papers name their own,
  610 names, at most 330 characters against the first window's 2,500); the reader orders them first too
  (`session/rows.ts` ranked). A refused row ends the wait, as any row does. Where a page's own rows come from before and a name's
  does not (asked again), the page waits for the first window, which holds the names and the page in view. A name's row that
  comes after a page's own now lays that page once, where it laid it twice, the head first drawn as printed
  (`packages/reader/tests/composer.test.ts`); the reads gate counts no name read outside a page's wait set (§18.63). Nothing a
  page draws moves: over the 90 pairs, on the door's rows and Google's, the lay draws every page as before but the highlight
  boxes of members a toggle leaves (no longer read by sentence from rows the reader answers refused: what the reader draws).
- **Limits.** The translator sees a name alone, with no sentence around it: a word of two senses may come back in the other
  ("Note", "Line"). A name only a macro of the paper's prints (`\newcommand{\thmname}{Satz}`) is not read.

### 19.15 One person, one translation (the block's names elsewhere)

The owner's ruling of 2026-11-10: one person, one translation per paper. With the names toggle on, a name of the author block
that the paper prints elsewhere is drawn with the block's translation of that name. "Elsewhere" covers an ACM reference format,
a correspondence line, an acknowledgement, an author's biography and a self-citation. With the toggle off, that other text is
ordinary text, translated and drawn as before: the same unit, the same wire and the same row, with nothing keyed by the toggle.
The toggle still governs the block under the title alone (§19.13, the ruling of 2026-11-09), and since 2026-11-13 the notes the
source ties to it (§18.71): such a note keeps its variant, drawn with the names on; with them off it is left the original's and
neither its row nor its variant's is read.

- **Why.** A name is translated again wherever it stands. Today's stored rows (the sweep cache, Microsoft) compare a name
  translated alone with the same name in other units: outside references 12 differ, 5 agree and 4 stay English; in references
  11 differ and 22 agree.
  - 2610.22065v1's block line has 周文勇, its reference format 文永周 and its footnote 周文勇.
  - 2604.14228v3's block has 申志强; its correspondence line came back 沈志强（ in one run and 申志强（ in another.
- **A stretch.** A stretch is a unit's text between two of its pieces that set something, or its edges.
  - A piece that sets something is an element that is not a tie, states no glue, is no forced break and is not silent, or a
    nested unit's mark.
  - A tie reads as a space, and an element that sets nothing reads as nothing.
  - A group's edges are no cut: Microsoft returns a group that travelled on no wire hollow, with its words outside it. Of
    today's stored replies, names cut at the group edges failed 73 of 293 times; cut at the elements alone, 0 of 242.
- **A name.** A name is a stretch of the source's author declaration (a unit of kind `author`). It is trimmed of Unicode
  punctuation, white space, symbols and controls at both ends, and holds two words or more: a given name and a surname as the
  block writes them.
  - A single word is not a person's name. 2609.36054v2 writes its places inside `\author` through its own `\formataffil`, and
    its "Institute for Law \& AI" gives "AI", which stands in 99 of its paragraphs.
- **The anchor.** A name's anchor is the first member of the block, by ord, one of whose stretches is the name. The block is
  the names toggle's member kinds: author, affiliation and inknames.
  - The anchor's row, cut at the same elements, gives the name's translation.
  - A block that lists names with nothing between them has no anchor and changes nothing (IEEEtran's
    `\IEEEauthorblockN{A, B and C}`).
- **An occurrence.** An occurrence is the name's text inside one text piece of any other unit that a member lays and that is not kept. A unit no member lays is never drawn, and no variant is made for it.
  - Any white space may stand between its words; no letter or digit may stand beside it.
  - The longest name is taken first, and the anchor's own stretch is not an occurrence.
  - A unit whose every occurrence is a whole stretch is resolved in its own row: its stretch's letters become the block's and
    its own punctuation stays. These are 2610.22065v1's reference format names, each its own unit, and 2604.14228v3's
    "Zhiqiang Shen (", which becomes 申志强（.
  - Any other unit has a **variant**, a unit of kind `named` written right after it in Units. The variant is the unit with each
    occurrence an element of kind `person`, whose `src` is the name as the unit writes it.
  - The variant has its own id and wire, and so its own row and store key. The server translates it as any unit.
- **The part** (Part.paper):
  - `named`: each unit of the page's members that names a person elsewhere, its variant or '', and each name. A name is
    stated as its element and its length and offset, for the sentences, or as its stretch.
  - `persons`: each person's anchor, the anchor's member kind and its stretch.
  - `splits`: how the anchors' rows, and the rows resolved in place, are cut.
- **The lay** (`packages/typeset/src/lay/named.ts`, one view of the rows at layPage's top; every caller lays the page alike). With
  the names shown (the anchor's kind not left):
  - **The variant's row:** each `person` element becomes the block's translation. Its `src` sentences map back onto the unit's
    projection and its `tr` sentences onto the text as drawn, so that both panes light by sentence (§17).
  - **A whole-stretch unit's own row:** its stretch's letters become the block's translation.
  - **Cutting the block's row:** each cut must come back once and in order, and the row's stretches must hold a letter exactly
    where the source's do. A row cut otherwise gives no name. The tags wire's element moved across a name would give the
    neighbour's name between the same two elements, and the letters' places tell it.
  - **Fallbacks:**
    - where a name has no translation, a variant's member takes its own row as it came (its names cannot be told apart in
      it);
    - a whole-stretch unit keeps its own translation of that name.
  - **Waiting:** a page waits for the variant's row and the anchors' rows besides the unit's own, while rows may come. Nothing
    committed is laid again; a toggle lays every page again.
  - **What a page reads is what it waits for** (2026-11-13). One test, the persons of the unit the toggles show (`shownOf`),
    decides both. Where none is shown (the names off) the unit is its own row as it came, and neither the variant's row nor an
    anchor's is read. Before, the variant's row was read first: with the names off and that row not in yet, the unit read as
    still to come, though its page waited for nothing more, so the page committed with it the original's, and a toggle turned
    and turned back drew it from its own row (staging round B14, 2611.03953v2-zh p1: the ICML correspondence footnote, the
    original's at the first lay, its own row's translation after the names on then off). Over the round's bundles with the Google store (each variant's
    row made from its unit's), a page laid over only the rows it waits for against over every row: 6 of 90 first pages and 11
    of the 60 pages that hold a variant differed by default, all 60 with the references on; none after.
- **Measured** (stage 1a over the 88 at this change, against the base's run):
  - 29 papers state 117 units naming 192 persons elsewhere, every other object the same:
    - 96 references (self-citations);
    - 8 reference format units (2610.22065v1's), resolved in their own rows;
    - 5 paragraphs (acknowledgements, biographies);
    - 4 footnotes and 4 ink units (correspondence lines, a reference format paragraph).
  - 13 units are resolved in their own rows and 104 have a variant: 23.6K characters, 0.40 % of the corpus's.
  - On page 1: 15 units in 8 papers, 5 of them variants (487 characters).
  - 2604.14228v3's correspondence line, at this engine one ink unit of its block (the tcolorbox's rest), has a variant: it is
    drawn 申志强 with the names on and the original's with them off, as the block is.
- **The block's translation wins.** The block's translation is the person's, whatever it is. 2610.22195v1's block translates
  each ICML name alone (延辰邓) where its acknowledgement, in a sentence, had 邓彦晨: the acknowledgement now reads the block's.
  The block's own quality (names translated one by one rather than in a list) is a separate matter.
- **Not covered.**
  - Forms the block does not write: initials (152 references in 27 papers), surname first (42 in 12), running heads in
    initials or in capitals (18 units in 7 papers), and a name across a tie outside the block (4 in references).
  - A shorter name inside another person's longer one ("Jun Yang" in "Jun Yang Li") where the longer is no block name.
  - The anchors' cuts are measured on Microsoft's replies alone. The tags wire's readings (Google, Chrome's built-in
    translator) are tested on shaped replies (`packages/translate/tests/names-wire.test.ts`).
